The overhaul went through commissioner study sessions in August and September and a Planning Commission hearing on Oct. 22. The county also adopted its 2025 Official Zoning Maps on Oct. 6.

adams-county/6.title: Battery storage, substation and large solar proposals
adams-county/6.summary: The Planning Commission heard conditional use permit requests for a battery energy storage facility and utility substation near 12500 Cavanaugh Road. It also heard a major energy facility with solar and a transmission line near 6301 Manilla Road.

adams-county/7.title: Zoning violation penalties and graduated fine schedule
adams-county/7.summary: On Aug. 25 commissioners adopted a penalty payment process and a graduated fine schedule for civil infractions of zoning and land use rules. An amended fine schedule came back on the Oct. 27 agenda.

adams-county/8.summary: The county approved agreements with Brothers Redevelopment for the Homelessness Resolution Program and with Village Exchange Center for transformational homelessness response. A study session on Oct. 28 covered acquisition of the Irondale Mobile Home Park.

adams-county/9.summary: The county approved hangar leases, a $385,385 taxilane rehabilitation contract, and a hangar development lease. A CASP strategy update and 2027 budget presentation were also on the schedule.

adams-county/10.summary: The Planning Commission considered a comprehensive plan amendment to add the Water Master Plan and statutory water supply element. Strategic Growth Element compliance for the comprehensive plan was also discussed.

adams-county/11.title: Ballot question referral and Ordinance 19
adams-county/11.summary: On Aug. 25 commissioners referred a ballot question to county voters. Ordinance 19 had first reading on Sept. 8 and was adopted on second reading on Sept. 29. The documents do not give details.

akron/0.title: Washington County Housing Authority agreement and subdivision water review
akron/0.summary: Council reviewed a County Housing Authority request for water review of a Title 13 subdivision, then discussed a proposed MOU with the Washington County Housing Authority (Sept. 8 draft). The topic returned in October and November, with the November agenda noting negotiation.

akron/1.title: Proposition 123 expedited review for affordable housing
akron/1.summary: Council took up Resolution 26.09, which would set an expedited review process for qualified affordable housing projects as part of the town's Proposition 123 commitment. Special meetings on a housing project were also held in August and September.

akron/2.title: Sanitary sewer collection system replacement and WPCRF loan
akron/2.summary: A public hearing covered replacing aging sewer lines, including a badly deteriorated cast iron line under the railroad. A DOLA CDBG grant of about $700,000 is already awarded, with principal forgiveness and a CDPHE loan to follow. The average sewer bill would need to reach about $55, a $13 increase.
akron/2.where: Townwide, sewer line under the railroad

akron/3.title: Water system improvements project, DWRF loan and DOLA grant
akron/3.summary: A hearing reviewed the town's water system, which has arsenic, nitrate and uranium issues requiring treatment upgrades. Rates would need to rise an estimated $13 to $18 per month. Council also considered a new DOLA-EIAF grant application of up to $1,000,000.

akron/4.title: Town manager settlement and funding of the position
akron/4.summary: Council considered a settlement with the Town Manager in executive session and possible action in August, and appointed a successor to a vacated trustee seat. In November DOLA said the Energy Impact grant funding the manager position phases down from 75% to 25% and expires in June, and asked for a plan to sustain it. The mayor said the council needs more time to address a succession plan.

akron/5.title: Title 14 Planning and Zoning rewrite (Ordinance 614)
akron/5.summary: Ordinance 614 adopting a new Title 14 Planning and Zoning had first reading in September and second reading in October.

akron/6.title: 2027 budget and employee compensation
akron/6.summary: Council reviewed the 2027 budget in October and discussed employee compensation in November.

akron/7.title: E-bike ordinance discussion
akron/7.summary: Council discussed a possible ordinance on e-bikes at its October meeting.

akron/8.title: Scott hangar lease at the airport (Ordinance 613)
akron/8.summary: Council gave second reading to Ordinance 613 approving a hangar lease to Scott.

alamosa-county/0.title: La Puente/PALS major site plan at 240 Price Ave
alamosa-county/0.summary: The commissioners held a public hearing on October 14 on a major site plan for La Puente/PALS at 240 Price Ave. The hearing minutes were up for approval on October 28. The documents do not state the outcome.

sources.body: Alamosa County Board of County Commissioners

alamosa-county/1.title: Onsite wastewater treatment system (OWTS) regulation
alamosa-county/1.summary: The commissioners held a public hearing on October 14 on a county regulation for onsite wastewater treatment systems (septic). The hearing minutes were on the October 28 agenda for approval. The documents do not give the details of the rules.

sources.body: Alamosa County Board of County Commissioners

alamosa-county/2.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing
alamosa-county/2.summary: An item on Proposition 123 affordable housing was on the commissioners' October 28 agenda. The documents give no detail on what action was proposed.

alamosa-county/3.summary: A VOCA (Victims of Crime Act) grant was on the commissioners' October 28 agenda. The documents give no amounts or decisions.

arapahoe-county/0.summary: Commissioners got an overview of data centers (types, water and cooling, 57 in Colorado) ahead of a Sept. 25 tour, then on Oct. 19 voted 5-0 for option 3, directing staff to establish a permitted and/or special use for data centers. The current code does not define "data center"; noise, air quality, water use and Xcel energy costs were raised.

arapahoe-county/3.title: Gun Club Road widening and CORE transmission line relocation
arapahoe-county/3.summary: The Board considered a relocation agreement with Rippey Commercial, Copperleaf Metro District and CORE for moving the transmission line on the west side of South Gun Club Road between the E-470 ramps and East Belleview Avenue. Right-of-way would grow from about 89 feet to 141 feet, and the county would pay design and construction costs. The item continued in executive session and was on the Oct. 27 consent agenda.

arapahoe-county/4.summary: The Board voted 5-0 to authorize submitting the county's 2027-2029 Proposition 123 commitment to the state, set at 231 affordable housing units over three years.

arapahoe-county/5.title: Rezoning study and group homes code amendment
arapahoe-county/5.summary: The Planning Commission took up proposed county rezonings (Federal Enclave, Dry Creek, 4 Square Mile, Belleview areas, with Dry Creek survey results and public comments) and a presentation on group homes code amendment LDC 26-002. A public land dedication amendment (LDC 26-003) was scheduled in October.

arapahoe-county/6.title: Joint water pipeline use-by-special-review
arapahoe-county/6.summary: On Aug. 11 commissioners heard a request for a joint pipeline project, asking about the route, CDOT approval, Colorado Parks and Wildlife referral comments and the Bennett Watkins Fire Department's future water infrastructure. No public comment came in at planning commission.

arapahoe-county/7.title: Onsite wastewater cease-and-desist hearing at 23900 E. Ohio Ave.
arapahoe-county/7.summary: The Board of Health held a hearing on a cease-and-desist over a failing onsite wastewater system at 23900 E. Ohio Ave. The homeowner did not attend, and the board discussed options to gain compliance. An update was on the September agenda.

arapahoe-county/8.title: Swimming pool and aquatic venue regulations
arapahoe-county/8.summary: Public Health asked the Board of Health to adopt the existing state code as the local pool standard and to start a stakeholder process on local aquatic rules based on the CDC Model Aquatic Health Code. The resolution does not adopt the code, create licensing or set fees.

arapahoe-county/9.title: Federal and state legislative agenda and ballot measures
arapahoe-county/9.summary: The Board reviewed federal funding and appropriations, drafted 2027 state and federal legislative priorities (including a data center land-use priority), and was briefed on statewide measures such as Propositions 136-137 and Amendments 81-87.

arapahoe-county/10.title: Payment Error Rate costs for human services
arapahoe-county/10.summary: Staff briefed commissioners on the state's SFY 2026-27 Payment Error Rate, under which the state would cover 60% of the allocation reduction and counties the rest. They discussed how Arapahoe County DHS could reduce errors.

arapahoe-county/11.title: Open space grants and High Line Canal leases
arapahoe-county/11.summary: Staff recommended keeping the 2027 Open Space grant allocation at $5.5 million while raising the standard maximum award from $600,000 to $750,000. Open Spaces also sought to extend High Line Canal recreation leases with local government partners.

arapahoe-county/12.title: Detention Facility Medical Expansion funding
arapahoe-county/12.summary: Staff asked to transfer $250,000 of unallocated capital funds to finish the Detention Facility Medical Expansion, since a missed smoke control airflow requirement left funds insufficient.

archuleta-county/0.title: Archuleta County Comprehensive Plan update
archuleta-county/0.summary: Consultant HRGreen briefed the Planning Commission on the purpose, timeline and status of the County's Comprehensive Plan update. Commissioners asked about having only one public outreach meeting and about meeting state deadlines for water supply and strategic growth elements. Resident David Laufer urged that the plan focus on strategizing for growth rather than preservation, citing low incomes compared to housing costs.

archuleta-county/1.title: Cloman Blvd administrative rezoning (PLN-REZ-26-050)
archuleta-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission heard a staff report from Development Director Eva Kruse on an administrative rezoning request for Cloman Blvd. The documents provided do not state the outcome.

archuleta-county/2.title: LPEA transmission line to Trujillo Substation (PLN-26-028)
archuleta-county/2.summary: La Plata Electric Association applied for a Board Conditional Use Permit for about 2,700 feet of 115 kV double-circuit transmission line (initially operated at 69 kV) with seven poles up to 75 feet tall. It would serve the approved Trujillo Substation, on Agricultural Ranching parcels at 2140 County Road 500. A public hearing was set for the Oct. 27 commissioners meeting.

archuleta-county/3.title: Housing Action Plan and multijurisdictional housing coordination
archuleta-county/3.summary: The Multijurisdictional Housing Coordinator, Jeff Sams, was scheduled to brief officials on the Housing Action Plan at the Sept. 28 meeting.

archuleta-county/4.title: Upper San Juan watershed and water presentations
archuleta-county/4.summary: Officials scheduled briefings from the Upper San Juan Watershed Enhancement Partnership and, at an Oct. 27 work session, a water presentation from the San Juan Water Conservancy District and the Partnership.

archuleta-county/5.title: 2026 flood discussion and 2027 draft budget
archuleta-county/5.summary: The Oct. 28 Town agendas include a 2026 flood discussion, a strategic planning retreat report and a draft 2027 budget discussion. The documents give no details of what was decided.

archuleta-county/6.title: Transportation grant awards
archuleta-county/6.summary: Andrew Mylroie was scheduled to present transportation grant awards at the Oct. 27 commissioners work session.

archuleta-county/7.title: County fair and rodeo planning
archuleta-county/7.summary: A planning committee approved entertainment bookings and accepted an LPEA STEM program, though LPEA cannot give a cash sponsorship this year because of wildfire mitigation. It also worked on a rodeo contractor RFP, beer garden applications with Rotary, and sponsorships, with about $57.1k of a $58.5k contractual services budget estimated.

arriba/0.title: Wastewater permit compliance and facility study
arriba/0.summary: Arriba is working with GMS Inc on an engineering study of its wastewater facility under new state permit rules, with half the costs covered by DOLA grants (a $16,428.06 reimbursement; $19,250 in invoices paid in July 2026). The facility has had BOD and ammonia violations, flooding and infiltration problems, and board members are looking at cheaper alternatives to evaporative ponds. In September 2026 CDPHE let the Town revert to its old permit compliance; the permit expires in 2027.
arriba/0.where: Town wastewater facility and sewer lines

arriba/1.title: RV park sewer and water rates
arriba/1.summary: Residents, notably Beverly Langley, have complained that campgrounds like Big Ben's RV Park use more water and sewer than they pay for. In January 2026 the board raised the monthly RV sewer rate per hookup (a $2 increase from $5 was moved after a $10 motion failed for lack of a second), and the RV park's heavy use has affected BOD levels at the wastewater pond. Residents asked again in August and September 2026 for a rate review.

arriba/2.title: Base water rate increase
arriba/2.summary: To stay in compliance with its drinking water loan covenant, the Town adopted a resolution raising the in-town and out-of-town base water rates by $5.50, to $55.00. It takes effect August 1, 2026.

arriba/3.title: Mandatory trash service ordinance and Rob's Trash Service contract
arriba/3.summary: The board negotiated a contract with Rob's Trash Service and adopted an ordinance requiring every occupied residential household to have trash service, with an option for residents to use their own approved 3-yard dumpster emptied monthly for $45. The contract can be renegotiated at the end of 2026.

arriba/4.title: 2026 budget and mill levy cut
arriba/4.summary: After a public hearing, the board adopted the 2026 budget and a 2025 supplemental sewer fund budget, which raised sewer spending from $116,940 to $229,440 for wastewater permit costs. The mill levy was certified at 14.509, down from 25.948, to stay under the property tax revenue limit.

arriba/5.title: Sales tax ballot question for 2026
arriba/5.summary: The board placed a question on the 2026 ballot asking voters to let the Town keep 2025 sales tax revenue above its estimate. The Town had estimated $14,000 but projected about $30,000. The 2026 election will be by mail ballot.

arriba/6.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption (Ordinance 159)
arriba/6.summary: The state-required wildfire code was tabled for months over concerns about enforcement, with the Town Clerk as code official. In July 2026 the board adopted Ordinance 159 adopting the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code, after discussing its effect on residents' insurance rates and a state affidavit requirement.

arriba/7.title: Time capsule event and park improvements
arriba/7.summary: The Town held a July 4, 2026 time capsule event funded by a $7,500 grant and a $2,500 tourism grant, with a beer garden on the park basketball court. Volunteers painted the park building. A $2,500 donation from Big Ben's RV Park and Conservation Trust funds are earmarked for a park sprinkler system that staff and volunteers plan to install.

arriba/8.title: Pine Street drainage and speeding on College and Lincoln Avenues
arriba/8.summary: Resident Beverly Langley reported rainwater from Pine Street flooding her house, and the board agreed to a ditch on the west side of Pine Street. Residents also raised truck speeding, and the board discussed speed bumps on College Ave and Lincoln Ave, plus a missing stop sign at Grant and Lincoln.
arriba/8.where: Pine Street, College Ave, Lincoln Ave, Grant St

arriba/9.title: RV and manufactured home permits
arriba/9.summary: The board approved a manufactured home permit at 521 Lincoln Ave and an RV permit for Troy McCue at 214 Main Street. The board decided under the RV ordinance that no tap fee applies, only the permit fee and backhoe use.

arriba/10.title: Hooved animals ordinance (Ordinance 113)
arriba/10.summary: A request to allow hooved animals in Town or on lots over 5 acres was considered in July 2026. The board agreed not to change Ordinance 113, which bans them except by variance for 4-H.

arvada/0.title: Data center moratorium
arvada/0.summary: Council discussed a temporary moratorium on data center applications at an Aug 11 study session, citing water, energy and land-use questions and moratoriums in neighboring jurisdictions. On Sept 15 it saw first reading of CB26-029, a moratorium on primary-use data center applications, with a public hearing set for Oct 6, 2026.

arvada/1.title: City water treatment plant annexation at 6809 SH 93
arvada/1.summary: The city is annexing and rezoning a 25.257-acre site at 6809 SH 93 (two parcels, 17.885 and 9.016 acres) from Jefferson County PD to Arvada Open Space for a new water treatment plant. It also needs a comprehensive plan amendment and exceptions on fencing, roofline and windows. Planning Commission heard it Aug 5, Council accepted petitions Aug 18, and the Council hearing was set for Oct 6, 2026.

arvada/2.title: 2027-2028 budget, mill levy and pay plan
arvada/2.summary: The City Manager presented a proposed two-year budget, with a 2027 appropriation of $412,447,446 and 32 requested new positions. Council set first reading for Oct 6 and a Oct 20 hearing on the 2027 budget, capital budget, pay plan and 2026 mill levy certification.

arvada/3.title: 2027 water, wastewater and stormwater rates and drought surcharges
arvada/3.summary: Council reviewed 2027 water, wastewater and stormwater rates, with ordinances on rate changes set for hearing Oct 20. Staff pulled the drought surcharge ordinance CB26-018 and plans to bring surcharges back in spring 2027, after a March 24, 2026 drought declaration and water use restrictions.

arvada/4.title: Hibernia Gold Strike Apartments, 4800 W 60th Ave
arvada/4.summary: A conditional use permit for 240 apartments in a five-story building on 3.47 acres, with a roughly 1,000 sq ft coffee shop near the RTD station. Planning Commission reviewed it Sept 16, and Council first reading was set for Oct 20 with a hearing Nov 17. About 20 residents attended the 2025 neighborhood meeting.

arvada/5.title: Proposition 123 zoning changes and affordable housing
arvada/5.summary: Planning Commission considered Land Development Code text amendments related to Proposition 123, and Council's Sept 15 agenda included an ordinance repealing and reenacting the residential land use table. Council also took up a resolution committing to Prop 123 obligations for 2027-2029, plus private activity bond assignment for Maiker Housing Partners.

arvada/6.title: Paid parking in Olde Town
arvada/6.summary: Council held a study session on parking demand in Olde Town, where studies from 2010, 2016 and 2025 show demand outpacing supply. Staff reviewed paid parking options under the Olde Town Strategic Reinvestment Plan and stakeholder feedback.

arvada/7.title: Wildfire early detection system
arvada/7.summary: Council approved an IGA with the Urban Renewal Authority for up to $300,000 for cameras and chemical sensors to detect wildfires in the Urban Renewal Area. Staff gave an Oct 27 update after data ownership concerns were raised in public comment.

arvada/8.title: Restricting residency of registered sex offenders
arvada/8.summary: Council asked Legal to draft an ordinance regulating where registered sex offenders may live. At a Sept 8 study session, attorneys summarized the law and asked Council for direction, recommending distances no further than 1,000 feet.

arvada/9.title: Comprehensive Plan update
arvada/9.summary: The city finished Phase 1 of the Comprehensive Plan update with consultant Metta Urban Design and is starting Phase 2, with adoption targeted for Q3 2027. Presentations covered how growth eras and zoning affect housing attainability.

arvada/10.title: Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan update and Gold Strike Park
arvada/10.summary: Council reviewed the process to update the 2016 Parks Master Plan, including public engagement. Council also considered a contract up to $9,596,751.06 with Arrow-J Landscape and Design for redeveloping Gold Strike Park.

arvada/11.title: Homelessness response and Navigation Center funding
arvada/11.summary: Council recognized faith leaders in the homeless response program, and took up an IGA on operational funding for the Navigation Center. A Homelessness Action Plan was on the Oct 27 agenda.

arvada/12.title: Scenic Heights West Metropolitan District service plan
arvada/12.summary: Council held a Sept 1 public hearing on a resolution approving the proposed service plan for the Scenic Heights West Metropolitan District.

arvada/13.title: City Attorney turnover and leadership contracts
arvada/13.summary: Council amended employment agreements for the City Attorney, Presiding Judge and City Manager, then later approved an employment agreement for Nora Steenson as Interim City Attorney after personnel executive sessions.

aspen/0.title: Entrance to Aspen (CO 82) reevaluation and historic mitigation
aspen/0.summary: Council and the Historic Preservation Commission are reviewing the refined preferred alternative for the CO 82 Entrance to Aspen project, including a historic mitigation discussion and a CDOT historic resources survey. An amended information update was prepared at Council's request.

aspen/1.title: Drought, Stage Three water restrictions and Ruedi Reservoir supplies
aspen/1.summary: With low flows and regional fires, the city is working on a drought response partnership using Ruedi Reservoir water, continuing Stage Three water restrictions, and reviewing water use at special events such as a snow polo request. Council is also weighing the purchase of Twin Lakes water right shares and talking with the Ruedi Water and Power Authority.

aspen/2.title: 2027 city budget work sessions
aspen/2.summary: Council held four budget work sessions covering fund overviews, the capital budget, supplemental requests and fees, and open items. The sessions included presentations on ACRA and CORE budgets, and a community development fee update with a consultant report.

aspen/3.title: Affordable housing fee-in-lieu update and locals fee deferral program
aspen/3.summary: Council reviewed the five-year affordable housing fee-in-lieu study (Phases I and II), and Planning & Zoning is making a recommendation on it. P&Z also considered Ordinance #11, a fee deferral program for qualified locals, and the West Mountain Regional Housing Coalition gave an update.

aspen/4.title: Marolt housing redevelopment with Aspen Music Festival and School
aspen/4.summary: Council discussed redevelopment concepts for Marolt housing in collaboration with the Aspen Music Festival and School, based on a redevelopment study.

aspen/5.title: Conner Park stage and amplified sound
aspen/5.summary: Residents raised concern at public comment that amplified sound from a proposed stage in Conner Park would harm the Armory Hall redevelopment, with a church of about 500 weekly participants nearby. Council scheduled a Conner Park stage discussion.

aspen/6.title: E-bike and e-moto rules and Rio Grande Trail safety
aspen/6.summary: A resident asked Council to align e-bike and e-moto rules along the valley, with licensing, permitting and a minimum age of 16. The mayor said other towns face the same issues and locals no longer feel comfortable walking on the Rio Grande Trail.

aspen/7.title: 121-123 East Hyman Avenue special review (Good Thunder Condos)
aspen/7.summary: Planning & Zoning held repeated hearings on a special review for 121 and 123 East Hyman Avenue, with a reduced application and public comment submitted. A third hearing was scheduled in October. Also on the October agenda was a residential design standards review for 1005 Waters Avenue.

aspen/8.title: Water treatment plant improvements and bond ballot question
aspen/8.summary: Council considered an early work package amendment for the Water Treatment Facility Improvements Project and Holy Cross Electric easements and conduit contracts. It also considered resolutions supporting a water treatment plant bond question and ballot issue 1A.

aspen/9.title: Armory Hall redevelopment and Main Street inlet project change orders
aspen/9.summary: Council took up change order #4 for builders risk on the Armory Hall project with Shaw Construction and an interior update. It also considered supplemental funding and an expanded culvert-lining scope for the Main Street Inlet and Pedestrian Improvements Project.

aspen/10.title: Short-term rental program guideline amendments
aspen/10.summary: Staff reported forthcoming amendments to the short-term rental program guidelines, referencing a 2024 resolution and 2025 ordinance.

aspen/11.title: Golf clubhouse area master plan and West End mobility
aspen/11.summary: Council reviewed a concept design for the golf clubhouse and campus master plan with a follow-up report. Staff also gave a status update on West End mobility improvements and a signage plan.

aspen/12.title: Fire fuel mitigation and Parks and Open Space strategic plan
aspen/12.summary: Council and county commissioners got a fire fuel mitigation update amid regional wildfires, and Council reviewed the Parks and Open Space Strategic Plan and forestry programs.

aurora/0.title: Data center moratorium and zoning standards
aurora/0.summary: Council took up a data center moratorium resolution (R2026-111) that would pause acceptance or processing of development applications with a data center as the primary use, with a waiver of reconsideration requested as time-sensitive. Council also held standards discussions and a public hearing on ordinance 2026-51, a Unified Development Ordinance text amendment to the permitted use table for data centers. An earlier agenda paired this with an evaporative cooling ordinance from Aurora Water.

aurora/1.title: 2027 city budget deliberations, fees and rates
aurora/1.summary: Council held a full-day budget session on Oct. 3 covering department budgets, the capital projects fund, proposed 2027 service fees, a 2026-2027 pay table, and 2027 budgets for several general improvement districts. On Oct. 12 it considered 2027 proposed rates and fees and a new fund to self-fund United Healthcare employee coverage.

aurora/2.title: Homeless services funding awards
aurora/2.summary: Council considered a series of Homeless Services Notice of Funding Opportunity applications, with recommendations including Advance Pathways and Aurora Housing Authority grants (Emergency Solutions Grant, HOME tenant-based rental assistance, marijuana funds). The items moved from the Oct. 12 study agenda to the Oct. 26 consent calendar.

aurora/3.title: Affordable housing: Mercy Housing ground lease and bond allocation
aurora/3.summary: Council considered a ground lease with Mercy Housing Mountain Plains for an affordable housing project (R2026-107), with an outside speaker listed. Council also considered assigning the city's 2026 private activity bond allocation to the Aurora Housing Authority.

aurora/4.title: Nine Mile Station and urban renewal redevelopment agreements
aurora/4.summary: The Aurora Urban Renewal Authority board considered amendments and agreements for The Point Crossing and Tempo at Nine Mile Station apartments in the Plaza 3 area, plus a restated finance agreement for Plaza 1. An IGA between the city and the Authority followed to council on Oct. 26.
aurora/4.where: Nine Mile Station, Plaza 1 and Plaza 3 urban renewal areas

aurora/5.title: Water restrictions on turf and ornamental water features
aurora/5.summary: Council finalized ordinances on new turf and ornamental water features, including one prohibiting certain permits, as part of Aurora Water conservation efforts. An evaporative cooling ordinance was also on an earlier agenda.

aurora/6.title: Water agreements: Lake County IGA and Westerly Creek storm sewer
aurora/6.summary: Council considered an amended and restated IGA with Lake County on water deliveries and storage, with a waiver of reconsideration requested to assist Lake County. It also took up an IGA for the Akron storm sewer and outfall to Westerly Creek for flood control improvements.

aurora/7.title: Regis Jesuit High comprehensive plan amendment
aurora/7.summary: Council held a public hearing on ordinance 2026-44 to amend the 2018 Comprehensive Plan placetype map for the Regis Jesuit High site, north of East Arapahoe Road and west of S. Olathe Street.
aurora/7.where: North of E. Arapahoe Road, west of S. Olathe St.

aurora/8.title: Fire and police labor contracts and public safety grants
aurora/8.summary: Council considered 2027-2028 collective bargaining agreements with IAFF Local and Fraternal Order of Police Lodge #49. It also considered police grant applications, including a state peace officer mental health program and a Department of Justice cybercrimes grant, plus mutual aid agreements with fire districts.

aurora/9.title: Industrial zoning and food truck rules
aurora/9.summary: Council considered a Unified Development Ordinance amendment for industrial zone districts and a text amendment to food truck standards and definitions.

aurora/10.title: Bethel Lutheran Church historic designation
aurora/10.summary: Council held a public hearing on ordinance 2026-52 designating Bethel Lutheran Church as a historic landmark.

avon/0.title: Flock license plate reader cameras
avon/0.summary: Residents repeatedly urged Council to end the Town's Flock Safety automated license plate reader program, citing privacy concerns and petitions with 1,544 to over 1,900 signatures. Town Manager Eric Heil said the Town has not renewed its Flock agreement and is reviewing contract terms and data security. Council is scheduled to discuss the program on October 6, 2026.

avon/1.title: Avon Whitewater Park and Bob the Bridge improvements
avon/1.summary: Residents asked Council to consider improving the Bob the Bridge area and redeveloping the Avon Whitewater Park, including a standing river wave. Speakers also asked for better river access amid low water this year and for skate park funding.
avon/1.where: Avon Whitewater Park / Bob the Bridge

avon/2.title: Piedmont Apartments trash and wildlife concerns
avon/2.summary: Residents raised property management and code enforcement concerns at the Piedmont Apartments, including trash drawing wildlife. Deputy Chief Cosper reported that police had received 27 calls about the trash.

avon/3.title: Community housing outreach
avon/3.summary: A resident asked for more opportunities for neighborhood participation and input on a recent community housing project. Town Manager Heil said the referenced meeting was not the final step and that further public comment would be available at future Town Council public hearings.

avon/4.title: Pedestrian crosswalk safety at Avon Road and Highway 6
avon/4.summary: A resident asked for flashing pedestrian beacons on both sides of Avon Road near Highway 6, after a near-miss involving his father in the crosswalk. He noted beacons exist on Highway 6 near Avon Road. Earlier, another resident said the Town had quickly made requested crosswalk improvements.

avon/5.title: Lot B (The Summit) redevelopment and tree removal
avon/5.summary: A resident asked about trees that could be removed during future redevelopment and site excavation of Lot B (The Summit). Town Manager Heil responded that trees would likely be removed as part of that work.

avon/6.title: Third 2026 budget amendment
avon/6.summary: Council's consent agenda on September 22 included a resolution for the Town's third budget amendment of 2026, renumbered as Resolution No. 26-14.

basalt/0.title: Public Works/Police facility and 0.5% sales tax ballot measure
basalt/0.summary: The Town plans a shared Public Works and Police facility on the town-owned lot at the end of East Valley Road by Highway 82, estimated at $25-26 million. Voters will see a 0.5% sales tax with a 20-year sunset on the November ballot (Ballot Issue 3A), and the Town has applied for a USDA loan. Staff say the police department is cramped, with one bathroom and no secure parking, and Council considered a resolution supporting the measure.

basalt/1.title: 218 E. Valley Road (former Movieland) Residence Inn hotel
basalt/1.summary: Planning and Zoning has held repeated hearings on a revised 93-key Residence Inn by Marriott with three deed-restricted affordable units on the former Movieland site, including PUD, site plan and annexation agreement amendments. Staff added conditions limiting the use to the approved hotel, and Council scheduled a site visit.

basalt/2.title: Jadwin/Black Mountain development and annexation
basalt/2.summary: Council continued the second reading of the ordinance approving 64 dwelling units, 12 short-term rental cabins and annexation with initial zoning for the property at 431 Emma Road.

basalt/3.title: Town-owned affordable housing: BCC units, COP financing and Parcel 9
basalt/3.summary: The Town closed on six deed-restricted units in the BCC project on August 5, 2026, for $2.38 million. Council considered Ordinance 21 to finance them with Certificates of Participation, and BACH is setting rents. The Finance Committee also reviewed the pro-forma for the Parcel 9 housing project, with a funding stack of about $5 million identified.

basalt/4.title: Short-term rental rules and fees
basalt/4.summary: A resident living on East Sopris Drive said the 2025 STR ordinance's 60-day cap and fees unfairly hit full-time residents who rent a spare room, and asked that on-site hosted primary residents be exempt. Council scheduled a work session on STR regulatory fees for October 22.

basalt/5.title: Tobacco tax ballot request
basalt/5.summary: Speakers urged Council to refer a tobacco tax increase to the ballot, noting Basalt's $2 per pack cigarette tax is below the $4 rate in Pitkin and Eagle counties and neighboring towns.

basalt/6.title: 2027 budget and town finances
basalt/6.summary: Staff reported sales tax is tracking above budget, with year-to-date sales tax through May at $4.22 million. Cash generated in the first six months was about $450,000, versus $2.2 million a year earlier, and lower tap fees hit the Water Fund. A Two Rivers Road CDOT grant was deferred to 2027. Council held a budget work session on September 17 and the proposed 2027 budget was presented on September 22.

basalt/7.title: Zoning, annexation and subdivision code rewrite
basalt/7.summary: With consultant Design Workshop, the Town is reorganizing its Annexation, Zoning and Subdivision codes (Chapters 15, 16 and 17) to make them more user-friendly, with some substantive changes. Planning and Zoning continued the hearing to October 20.

basalt/8.title: Midland Avenue streetlights and Southside traffic concerns
basalt/8.summary: Residents complained that the new catenary streetlights on Midland are not bright enough. Staff said the lights are at maximum output and they are working with the contractor. Residents also raised the single egress from Southside, a stop sign at Alexander and Fiou Lane, and a roundabout on Willits Lane for access to Crown Mountain Park.

basalt/9.title: Green Team: building benchmarking, CORE and lawn equipment
basalt/9.summary: The Green Team reviewed building energy benchmarking, regional IMPACT Accelerator grant funding of over $4 million, and CORE energy projects such as heat pumps. It also discussed extending the 2025 ban on combustion leaf blowers beyond town property.

basalt/10.title: Cliff's Hillside Park design and trail wayfinding funding
basalt/10.summary: The Parks, Open Space and Trails committee reviewed the 90% design for Cliff's Hillside Park, including play elements and furnishings. It also discussed a Mid-Valley Trails/RFTA funding request for wayfinding signs, which missed the 2027 budgeting cycle.

basalt/11.title: Winter snow removal on Midland Avenue streetscape
basalt/11.summary: Public Works presented three options for snow removal on the new streetscape, including continued use of a contracted service, as the main challenge is clearing before parking spaces fill and plowing begins.

berthoud/0.title: Data center moratorium and land use rules
berthoud/0.summary: After trustees asked on Aug. 25 for a possible moratorium, the Board adopted Ordinance 1391 on Sept. 22, an emergency measure temporarily suspending applications for large data centers. Discussion focused on the size threshold for a large data center. A Sept. 29 work session looked at a technical criteria guide and code amendments covering noise, heat and water, and staff plan to budget for a noise consultant in 2027. A study session summary was on the Oct. 27 agenda.

berthoud/1.title: Legacy Park final plat and development agreement
berthoud/1.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on the Legacy Park final plat (south of Mountain Ave, east of Meadowlark Dr, west of S. Berthoud Pkwy) and moved to approve it. The Town Board held a hearing on Sept. 8 on the development agreement with revised vesting and phase-by-phase improvement guarantees. The silos on the site are to be removed because of asbestos.
berthoud/1.where: South of Mountain Avenue, east of Meadowlark Drive, west of S. Berthoud Parkway

berthoud/2.title: Heron Lakes Marina neighborhood master plan
berthoud/2.summary: The Planning Commission heard the Heron Lakes Marina Neighborhood Master Plan in September and recommended it to the Town Board. The Board took up a continued hearing on Resolution 2026-25 approving it on Oct. 27.

berthoud/3.title: Rewrite of Chapter 30 land use code
berthoud/3.summary: Staff introduced amendments to Chapter 30 of the Municipal Code covering impact fees, annexation, zoning, flood mitigation and other sections, including a technical guide for zoning amendments. The Planning Commission was to hold a hearing on Oct. 22 and the trustees on Nov. 10. The Planning Commission also considered the annual Three Mile Plan.

berthoud/4.title: November 3 ballot measure and bond financing
berthoud/4.summary: The Board approved intergovernmental agreements with Larimer County for the Nov. 3, 2026 coordinated election and reviewed ballot language in Ordinance 1390. Trustees worried the language did not clearly say taxes would not increase, and bond counsel suggested adding wording to that effect. A resident spoke in favor of a bond to finance Mountain Vista Park.

berthoud/5.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and wildland-urban interface
berthoud/5.summary: After a continuance in September, the Board held a hearing and approved Ordinance 1389 adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. A cooperative agreement with the Berthoud Fire Protection District for administering the code was also considered. Trustees asked for a map of the wildland-urban interface boundary.

berthoud/6.title: 2027 preliminary budget
berthoud/6.summary: Administrator Kirk introduced the preliminary 2027 draft budget on Oct. 13 and a public hearing was to be set. The Board also approved a 2026-2028 strategic plan in September and a new supplies and equipment purchasing policy.

berthoud/7.title: Boards and commissions ordinance 1388
berthoud/7.summary: The Board adopted Ordinance 1388 consolidating rules for town boards and commissions into a new Section 4.9, with term limits and appointment procedures. Trustees added a requirement that each board review it in October and update bylaws. Committees such as Tree, Parks and Historic Preservation discussed the change and recruitment.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Recreation, and Trails Committee

berthoud/8.title: Historic preservation grants and water tower sign
berthoud/8.summary: The Historic Preservation commission pursued a survey plan grant and a water tower interpretive sign. Funding for the elevated water tank interpretive sign was received. Residents asked the Board in September to support historic preservation.

berthoud/9.title: Welch Avenue and 9th Street road improvements
berthoud/9.summary: The Board authorized a request for proposals for design of Welch Avenue roadway and drainage improvements. Staff also gave an update on challenges and planned improvements to the 9th Street crossing. A resident asked for a speed limit adjustment.

berthoud/10.title: Parks and open space projects
berthoud/10.summary: Trustees handled Jaskowski Open Space construction bids, Mountain Vista Park design changes, bike park bids, and an Eagle Vista/Front Range Trail grant letter of support. The Board also discussed an arboretum design reduction contract.
berthoud/10.where: Jaskowski Open Space, Mountain Vista Park, Eagle Vista

berthoud/11.title: Affordable housing and Ordinance 1355
berthoud/11.summary: The Board scheduled a discussion of Ordinance 1355 and possible expansion of affordable housing. The Planning Commission also held a work session with the regional housing director.

berthoud/12.title: Tree program and memorial trees
berthoud/12.summary: A resident asked the Board and the Tree Advisory Committee to start a memorial tree program in Fickel Park. The committee is also pursuing grants and a fall planting plan.

berthoud/13.title: Flock cameras discussion
berthoud/13.summary: More than three trustees supported scheduling a future agenda item on Flock cameras.

black-hawk/0.title: Education Enhancement Tax and the proposed Gilpin County sales tax
black-hawk/0.summary: Black Hawk's 1.5% Education Enhancement Tax for the Gilpin school has raised about $16.9 million since 2009 and ends automatically if a countywide sales tax is adopted. Council discussed the County Commissioners' possible November 2026 sales tax and passed Resolution 17-2026 on March 25 reaffirming that the tax would terminate.

black-hawk/1.title: Water supply: Four Mile Gulch Well #6 and Army Corps reservoir permit
black-hawk/1.summary: The city is pursuing an Army Corps of Engineers permit for a reservoir and approved a reimbursement agreement (CB12) covering review costs. Residents of unincorporated Aspen Springs and Chalet Park spoke on Sept. 9 against drilling Well #6 near Dory Hill Road, saying it could harm neighbors' water, and asked the council to pause additional wells.
black-hawk/1.where: Four Mile Gulch / Dory Hill Road

black-hawk/2.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption and fire restrictions
black-hawk/2.summary: Council adopted the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code into the municipal code on March 25 by a 5-1 vote. In July the city manager issued an administrative order imposing fire restrictions. The city also contracted Good People Tree Service for fire mitigation work.

black-hawk/3.title: City-owned land purchases and sales, including Resolution 48-2026
black-hawk/3.summary: Council approved a contract to buy land on Gregory Hill in June and accepted a property conveyance in July. A vacant land sale agreement (Resolution 48-2026) was repeatedly continued from August into September, with discussion of Central City's roadway permitting and traffic study.

black-hawk/4.title: Leadership turnover: new City Manager and Police Chief
black-hawk/4.summary: Police Chief Moriarty announced her retirement after 31 years, and the council met in executive session on City Manager matters. Lance Hillis's employment agreement as City Manager took effect May 2 (Resolution 22-2026), and Ely Reyes was introduced as the new Police Chief in July.

black-hawk/5.title: Capital projects: Bobtail Mine, Highway 119 culverts, Red Dolly electrical, Ballard House
black-hawk/5.summary: Council approved a $949,307 change order for Bobtail Mine Improvements Phase 2 and a $160,400 Bobtail wall excavation contract. It also approved relining two storm culverts under Highway 119 after a failure at Gregory Street, the Red Dolly Casino electrical relocation, storage sheds, and Ballard House renovation with a barn shed addition (Roche Constructors). Also streamlined the capital project approval process (CB10).

black-hawk/6.title: Historic preservation and Lace House designation
black-hawk/6.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission is working on the Lace House designation, a phased reconnaissance survey and an intensive survey property list. Council accepted the reconnaissance survey and the Five-Year HPC Work Plan in August to meet Certified Local Government requirements.

black-hawk/7.title: Rick Thomas Distillery trademark license and water fee waiver
black-hawk/7.summary: Council approved a trademark license agreement with Rick Thomas Distillery and extended a waiver of water fees for another year for its site on Lot 7 of the Black Hawk Park Subdivision.

black-hawk/8.title: Fee schedule update and 2025 audit
black-hawk/8.summary: Council accepted the 2025 audit and amended the fee schedule, aligning commercial electrical fees with state fees and moving SAFEbuilt's hourly rate to consultant fees, plus City Clerk fee changes.

black-hawk/9.title: Sanitation district agreement and ballot measure positions
black-hawk/9.summary: Council approved an amended and restated service agreement with the Black Hawk/Central City Sanitation District. The mayor also spoke against a County Commissioners property-tax measure (Initiative 1A) and proposed a resolution supporting Initiative 177 on natural gas purchases.

blue-river/0.title: Short-term rental caps, zones and moratorium exceptions
blue-river/0.summary: The Board has been working through a new short-term rental policy: a six-zone framework with license caps by zone, a draft ordinance effective Jan. 1, 2027, and licensing set to begin May 1, 2027. Ordinances 2026-10, 2026-11 and 2026-12 would let some owners hurt by the moratorium (Ordinance 2026-03) apply, with a Nov. 1, 2026 application deadline, and change renewal and enforcement processes. Residents urged enforcement against unlicensed operators and fair treatment for recent buyers.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/1.title: Transition Zone District lot size and setback rules (Ordinance 2026-06 and 2026-07)
blue-river/1.summary: The Board held a hearing on Ordinance 2026-06, which sets minimum lot size, lot width and setbacks in the Transition Zone District. Ordinance 2026-07 would put a Development Code in effect Oct. 1, 2026, on the condition that 2026-06 is in effect. Discussion covered consistency with R-1 standards and wetland and topography limits.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/2.title: Proposed 2027 budget and town finances
blue-river/2.summary: The Board was scheduled to hear a presentation and discuss the proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 20. Financial reports show a 10.459 mill levy after a temporary credit, and 2026 general property tax is projected at about $930,583.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/3.title: Porch, deck and roof project at 6871 Highway 9 and wildfire code review
blue-river/3.summary: The Planning Commission found the application incomplete in August because it lacked wildfire-code measurements, a current survey and parking and second-access information on Highway 9. In September it found the revised materials adequate and approved the application. The Town Attorney advised on how far the Highway 9 Access Control Plan applies to minor projects.

blue-river/4.title: 1253 Indiana Creek Road residence: height, garages and carriage house
blue-river/4.summary: The Commission held a pre-application session on a proposed home. Topics were the 35-foot height limit, whether recessed garage entrances count as basement entries, the 25% garage area limit, two separate living areas and a carriage house. The applicant was asked for revised exhibits showing existing and proposed grades.

blue-river/5.title: Sewer and septic concerns along Blue River Road
blue-river/5.summary: Residents raised aging septic systems and environmental concerns on Blue River Road. They asked the Town to explore grants, financing and partnerships for future sewer infrastructure.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/6.title: Goose Pasture Tarn boat dock rules repealed
blue-river/6.summary: The Board considered Resolution 2026-10, repealing Resolution 13-05, which set rules and permits for private boat docks at Goose Pasture Tarn. The Town Attorney gave background and the Board moved to adopt it.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/7.title: Speeding and traffic calming on Indiana Creek Road
blue-river/7.summary: Residents raised speeding on Indiana Creek Road and asked for traffic-calming measures.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/8.title: Summit School District mill levy override presentation (Measure 4A)
blue-river/8.summary: District representatives presented Ballot Measure 4A, a local mill levy override raising up to $5.9 million a year, and the statewide Proposition NN. About 76% of the 4A money would go to staff pay, and the district cited turnover and cost of living.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/9.title: Summit County Hazard Mitigation Plan 2026 adoption
blue-river/9.summary: The Board was to consider Resolution 2026-13 adopting the Summit County Hazard Mitigation Plan 2026.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/10.title: Board policy on agenda item placement
blue-river/10.summary: Trustees discussed a draft bylaw policy setting a clear process for bringing items before the Board and supported moving it forward for formal consideration.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

boone/0.title: New water treatment facility startup, leaks and draws
boone/0.summary: Boone's new water treatment plant moved from operator training (March) toward startup in early May 2026, with periodic loan/grant draws and a 2-year warranty. By August the council said a leak in the GreenSands room and chlorine pump problems needed further investigation, and a bottled water advisory was lifted by the state health department in July.

boone/1.title: Water/sewer billing procedure ordinance and landlord-tenant section
boone/1.summary: The council spent months drafting an ordinance on water bill dates, late, reconnect and disconnect fees. The tenant/landlord responsibility section (Section 9) was repeatedly reworded, and the ordinance was approved and signed on Oct 14, 2026, with 30 days of posting before it takes effect. A new utility billing system with card and ACH payments was also approved.

boone/2.title: Water and sewer tap fee ordinance
boone/2.summary: A tap fee ordinance was in the works from January, read and accepted in June, and finalized, signed and posted by July 29, 2026. In October the council also discussed a sewer tap for a resident, who is responsible for issues up to the tap.

boone/3.title: Fire protection IGA with Edison Fire Protection District
boone/3.summary: Boone worked out an intergovernmental agreement and lease with the Edison fire district to cover fire service. Council accepted the IGA in April and adopted a resolution approving the IGA and contracts on May 7, 2026.

boone/4.title: Adopting Southern Colorado Building Department codes and amended IGA
boone/4.summary: The town worked with the Southern Colorado Building Department (SCBD/SOCOBD) attorney to update ordinances based on Pueblo regional codes for code enforcement. The ordinances were reviewed, finalized and posted Oct 14, 2026 (one was missed), while the amended IGA was tabled until Nov 18 so Rockvail can be added.

boone/5.title: Refuse rate increase
boone/5.summary: A 3% trash fee increase under the town's contract was discussed in June. Council approved a resolution for the refuse rate increase on July 29, and all members signed it Aug 19, 2026.

boone/6.title: Park playground equipment, mower and sprinklers
boone/6.summary: Council discussed the town park needing new playground equipment, and the Edison fire chief suggested USDA and GOCO grants. Eight sprinkler heads were replaced after mowing damage and council approved buying a new mower. A park memorial re-dedication for the 250th anniversary was also on the June agenda.

boone/7.title: Town administrator appointment and employee handbook
boone/7.summary: Council approved a resolution appointing a town administrator in August 2026, with a follow-up completed in September. An employee handbook workshop was set.

boone/8.title: Internet service change and 2026 budget
boone/8.summary: Council discussed switching the town from CenturyLink to Starlink at a $280 flat monthly fee. Separate budget meetings were held in March and April 2026.

boulder-county/0.title: County rules for data centers and detention centers
boulder-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled on Oct. 21 to consider Land Use Code text amendments (DC-26-0003 and DC-26-0004) that would define data centers and detention centers as specific uses and set where and at what scale they could be permitted in unincorporated Boulder County. The data center item and the detention center item each go to the commissioners as a recommendation.

boulder-county/1.title: 2027 Boulder County budget and general fund reductions
boulder-county/1.summary: Commissioners discussed efficiencies and general fund budget reduction recommendations in August, held a town hall in Superior on the 2027 budget, and heard department presentations on Oct. 13, 15 and 22. Public testimony was taken at the Oct. 22 hearing, with a work session Nov. 5 and adoption set for Dec. 8.

boulder-county/2.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing Aug. 19 on the ten-year BVCP update, including Rural Lands text amendments, and took public comment. The commissioners conditionally approved it Aug. 13, and the resolution (2026-059) was adopted Oct. 13.

boulder-county/3.title: Ballot measure to expand the Board of Commissioners from 3 to 5
boulder-county/3.summary: On Aug. 25 the county fixed ballot titles for an initiative petition to increase the Board of County Commissioners from 3 to 5 members on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot. The clerk confirmed the petition was sufficient. Commissioners also considered taking positions on other 2026 ballot measures.

Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/4.title: Amicus brief supporting Cook County's ban on semiautomatic firearms
boulder-county/4.summary: The County Attorney asked commissioners to ratify Boulder County's participation with other jurisdictions in a U.S. Supreme Court amicus brief in Viramontes v. Cook County. The brief supports Cook County's ban on certain semiautomatic firearms, including AR-15-style rifles.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/5.title: Housing authority funding, grants and annual plan
boulder-county/5.summary: The county pursued homelessness and housing money, including a $300,000 youth housing grant application, a $571,307 application, reallocation of state funds to Family Bridge Housing and a $1.08M grant for Willoughby Corner Phases II and III at 928 Canterbury Drive, Lafayette. Commissioners also approved the Housing Authority's 2027 Annual Plan and Moving to Work Supplement after a public hearing, and assigned private activity bond cap. A work session covered the Affordable and Attainable Housing Tax Innovation Fund.

boulder-county/6.summary: The Eldorado Springs Public Improvement District board referred a multiple-year debt question to the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot to pay for wastewater treatment plant improvements required by the state health department.

boulder-county/7.title: Longmont 1st & Main urban renewal tax increment agreement
boulder-county/7.summary: Boulder County agreed to share tax increment financing with the Longmont Urban Renewal Authority for redevelopment of the 1st & Main corridor, including a regional transit center, environmental cleanup and public infrastructure.

boulder-county/8.title: Riverside Cabins Lodge special review revocation
boulder-county/8.summary: Staff recommended revoking the Riverside Cabins Lodge special use approval for violating conditions. Commissioners declined to revoke and continued the hearing to Jan. 7, 2027, so the owners can finish the work and meet conditions.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/9.title: Apahapa LLC Flagstaff Road boundary line appeal
boulder-county/9.summary: Commissioners heard an appeal of a decision on a boundary line adjustment between parcels at 6808 and 7022 Flagstaff Road, which also denied recognition of 6808 Flagstaff. The hearing was tabled to Dec. 3 at 1 p.m., when public comment will be taken.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/10.title: Mental and behavioral health tax funding for schools and services
boulder-county/10.summary: The county signed $800,000 contracts each with Boulder Valley and St. Vrain Valley school districts from the 1B Mental and Behavioral Health Tax for school-based services. A tax advisory committee and bylaws were discussed, and an opioid abatement grant passes through to Clinica for a treatment facility.

boulder-county/11.title: Wildfire mitigation grants and fire restrictions
boulder-county/11.summary: Commissioners funded $191,350 for Superior's grazing program and about $990,263 for Watershed Center work at Conifer Hill, plus a wildfire awareness campaign contract. Stage 1 fire restrictions in the mountain area were rescinded effective Oct. 15.

boulder-county/12.title: Open space water share purchases and Tucker Complex management
boulder-county/12.summary: Parks and Open Space proposed buying 20 ditch company shares for $450,000 (Copley) and one James Ditch share for $120,000 (Buckner) to keep water on agricultural open space. Commissioners also discussed interim management for the Tucker Complex and easements for the 120th Street shoulder reconstruction.
