boulder/0.title: November 2026 city ballot measures (bonds, vacancy tax, firefighter bargaining, downtown authority)
boulder/0.summary: Council gave second reading to ordinances sending several questions to the November 3, 2026 ballot. They cover general obligation bonds for recreation and safety infrastructure, a Vacancy Excise Tax on homes occupied 183 days or less, a charter amendment for firefighter collective bargaining, and formation of a Boulder Downtown Development Authority with tax increment financing. Council later set the order of the ballot measures and discussed supporting a county ballot measure.

boulder/1.title: Annexation of 1275 Cherryvale Rd. and 5995 McSorley Ln.
boulder/1.summary: A petition would annex about 5.43 acres at these two properties with initial RR-2 residential-rural zoning. The item was removed from the August 20 agenda and came back October 1 for first reading, with a public hearing set for November 12, 2026.

boulder/2.title: North 30th and South 30th Street projects: eminent domain property acquisition
boulder/2.summary: Council considered ordinances 8771 and 8772 authorizing acquisition of property interests for the North 30th Street Project and the South 30th Street Multimodal Improvements Project, by negotiation or by eminent domain if needed.

boulder/3.title: Affordable housing financing for Harvest34 and Boulder Housing Partners
boulder/3.summary: Council considered assigning $7,333,256 of 2026 private activity bonds to Boulder Housing Partners for permanently affordable rental housing. It also considered approving a public approval certificate for BHP to issue multifamily housing revenue bonds for the Harvest34 project.

boulder/4.title: 2027 city budget and special district budgets
boulder/4.summary: Council held a study session on the 2027 Recommended Budget on September 10. On October 15 it took up 2027 budgets, mill levies and appropriations for the Central Area GID, University Hill GID, Boulder Junction Access GID (TDM) and the Municipal Property Authority.

boulder/5.title: Frasier and Naropa campus redevelopment proposals
boulder/5.summary: Council considered a Site Review Amendment to redevelop the Frasier campus into a joint campus, including a new 55-foot, four-story independent living building with 96 apartments and underground parking. A Site Review application to redevelop the Naropa campus was also on the October 1 agenda.

boulder/6.title: Rezoning and right-of-way vacations at 2106 and 2130 Arapahoe Ave. and Marine Street
boulder/6.summary: First reading of Ordinance 8774 would rezone about 3.72 acres at 2106 and 2130 Arapahoe Ave. and adjacent land to RH-5. Ordinance 8775 would vacate part of the Marine Street right-of-way next to 2130 Arapahoe. A related land exchange with Canal Avenue Park, LLC for about 1.0 acre of city land was also on the agenda.
boulder/6.where: 2106 and 2130 Arapahoe Ave. and Marine Street

boulder/7.title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan 10-year update
boulder/7.summary: Council took up first reading of Ordinance 8784 adopting the 2025 major 10-year update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan.

boulder/8.title: Wildfire resilience and home hardening program
boulder/8.summary: Council held study sessions on August 27 and October 22 about a wildfire home hardening implementation hub and an assessment of current and planned city wildfire programs. It is a council priority project.

boulder/9.title: Power reliability and resilience forum
boulder/9.summary: The city held a Community and Council Forum on October 8 on the council priority project for power reliability and resilience. A concept plan to expand the Xcel Energy service facility at 2655 N. 63rd Street was also reviewed.

boulder/10.title: Civic Area East Bookend development partnership RFP
boulder/10.summary: Council discussed a request for proposals for a development partnership on the Civic Area East Bookend in an August 13 study session. The summary was accepted September 17.

boulder/11.title: Pedal cab licensing and alcohol permit changes
boulder/11.summary: Ordinance 8757 creates pedal cab agency and driver licenses with fees. Ordinance 8773 allows expanded alcohol beverage permits for spirituous liquor manufacturers and adds a related tax and fee.

boulder/12.title: Restaurant and small business task force
boulder/12.summary: Council discussed whether to form a restaurant and small business task force.

breckenridge/0.title: Flock license plate cameras and the automated license plate reader program
breckenridge/0.summary: Residents spoke at the Aug. 25 Council meeting against Flock license plate cameras, citing broad data-use rights, no federal or state oversight, and no opt-out, and asked for better communication on camera placement and contracts. The Flock contract comes up for renewal in March 2027, and an automated license plate reader program presentation was scheduled for the Oct. 13 Council meeting. A later public commenter asked whether police policies and training comply with Colorado law.

breckenridge/1.title: Comprehensive Plan underutilized parcels and workforce housing density
breckenridge/1.summary: As required by state comprehensive plan rules, the Planning Commission reviewed maps of underutilized parcels that could be developed or redeveloped for housing, such as the North Gold Rush lot, the Breckenridge Elementary parcel and the Park Avenue corridor. Staff recommended allowed workforce housing densities, including 30 units per acre along Park Avenue. Commissioners worried about views of the Carter Park pavilion and about a parking study being done with Vail.
breckenridge/1.where: Townwide, including Carter Park, North Gold Rush lot and the Park Avenue corridor

breckenridge/2.title: 2027 budget, mill levy and capital improvement plan
breckenridge/2.summary: Town Council held a Budget Retreat on Oct. 13 and was scheduled to take up the 2027 mill levy (Council Bill 11), the 2027 budget (Resolution 22) and the 2027-2030 Capital Improvement Plan on Oct. 27. Open space staff described a conservative budget built on flat sales tax projections.

breckenridge/3.title: Housing Helps program and employee housing
breckenridge/3.summary: Residents thanked Council for the Housing Helps program, which buys homes from locals and resells them with restrictions, and urged continued robust funding. Council also moved on a first reading to remove employee housing mitigation requirements for exterior food and beverage uses, and a landowner at 10944 Highway 9 asked to partner with the Town on water service for housing units. The Oct. 27 agenda included a housing update and an accessory dwelling unit policy discussion.

breckenridge/4.title: Trails at Berlin Placer development, water service and bonds
breckenridge/4.summary: Council went into executive session on Sept. 8 to discuss a water service agreement for the Trails at Berlin Placer development and instructed the Town Attorney to begin negotiations on bond money for the project. A related executive session discussed acquiring real property in the Upper area.

breckenridge/5.title: City Market fuel center at 430 N. Park Avenue
breckenridge/5.summary: The Planning Commission held preliminary hearings on a new City Market #430 fuel center (PL-2026-0171). It includes future demolition and environmental remediation of the existing fuel center, tree removal at Airport Road and Park Avenue, and a mountain-style design with a red sign reviewed separately. Commissioners asked for more evergreen screening, snow storage coordination and a less conspicuous color palette.

breckenridge/6.title: Little Red Schoolhouse expansion town project
breckenridge/6.summary: The Town's expansion of the Little Red Schoolhouse at 600 Reiling Road went through a Planning Commission work session on Sept. 15 and a hearing on Oct. 6, then a Town Council hearing on Oct. 27.

breckenridge/7.title: Mamba Trust retaining wall variance at 219 Glen Eagle Loop
breckenridge/7.summary: The Planning Commission heard a request to let part of an unpermitted retaining wall remain beyond the platted disturbance envelope. Staff said about 75 feet would need to be removed to comply, and the property's architect presented in support of the application.

breckenridge/8.title: Open space trails workplan, Tiger Road Rec Path and downhill trails
breckenridge/8.summary: The Open Space Advisory Commission refined a trails prioritization matrix and scored a proposed Phase 1 of the Tiger Road Rec Path. Residents asked for more hand-built downhill trails, such as near Little Mountain, to ease user conflicts. Commissioners named new trails Bald Barber and Chasing Mystic and kept the Little Daisy access road name McCain Drive.
breckenridge/8.where: Tiger Road, Little Mountain, Little Daisy Open Space

breckenridge/9.title: Quandary Peak trailhead improvements and Aspen Alley shuttle
breckenridge/9.summary: The Town pledged $400,000 in matching funds for a Summit County Outdoor Coalition grant for Quandary Trailhead improvements, with results expected at year-end. Staff also hired SGM for design studies needed for a County PUD parking expansion. A free seasonal shuttle and police parking enforcement manage crowding at Aspen Alley.
breckenridge/9.where: Quandary Peak trailhead and Aspen Alley

breckenridge/10.title: Wellington-Oro and French Gulch water treatment plant
breckenridge/10.summary: Staff updated the commission on optimizing the French Gulch water treatment plant for cadmium and zinc, including budgeting for engineering consultants and pilot-testing an aeration pond. The Town and County are working toward a critical 2029 Water Quality Control Commission hearing, with specialized legal counsel.

breckenridge/11.title: Ballot measures: Summit schools mill levy 4A and Proposition NN
breckenridge/11.summary: Council adopted resolutions supporting Summit County's referred measure 1A (Strong Futures) and the Summit School District Mill Levy Override, added to the Sept. 22 agenda as Resolution 19. Council also took up Resolution 21 supporting statewide Proposition NN, which would increase public education funding 2% per year for 10 years without raising taxes.

breckenridge/12.title: Refunding of 2016 certificates of participation
breckenridge/12.summary: Council approved Council Bill 10 on first and second reading to refund Series 2016 certificates of participation, with $4.6 million outstanding. The refunding will proceed only if potential savings justify the costs.

breckenridge/13.title: Worker and resident parking permits
breckenridge/13.summary: A resident told Council that permitted parking for workers and residents is hard to find despite holding a permit. She suggested gated access for permit lots, towing enforcement, and expanding parking into the South Gondola lots or the parking structure. Council also revised the delivery zone program in Council Bill 9, updating fees and penalties.

brighton/0.title: 180-day data center moratorium
brighton/0.summary: Council took up an ordinance pausing acceptance, processing or approval of permits, licenses, zoning or other land use applications where a data center is a proposed use. It was introduced Oct. 6 for 180 days and came back in amended form for final consideration on Oct. 20.

brighton/1.title: Case Farms zoning map amendment (232 acres)
brighton/1.summary: Council held a public hearing on a zoning change for about 232 acres of the Case Farms PUD, to R-2 and open space and parks zoning. The ordinance came back for further consideration on Sept. 1.

brighton/2.title: 2027-2028 budget, mill levy, fees and 2026 budget amendments
brighton/2.summary: Council reviewed the proposed 2027 and 2028 budgets and a Q2 2026 financial update in August. A 2027 rate and fee proposal followed on Sept. 8, and a third amendment to the 2026 budget was heard Oct. 6. The Oct. 20 agenda lists the 2027 budget, mill levy and fees.

brighton/3.title: Water revenue refunding bonds and 2016 bond refunding
brighton/3.summary: Council reviewed refunding the 2016 revenue bonds, then considered the Water Activity Enterprise Revenue Refunding Bonds, Series 2026. The bond ordinance had initial consideration Sept. 15 and final consideration Oct. 6.

brighton/4.title: Bromley Park PUD amendments (38th and 39th)
brighton/4.summary: Council considered the Bromley Park PUD 38th Amendment for land near the I-76 frontage road and North 60th Avenue, hearing it Sept. 15 and Oct. 6 before an ordinance on Oct. 20. A 39th amendment for about 5.92 acres near Bromley Business Parkway and the BNSF railroad also had a hearing Oct. 20.
brighton/4.where: I-76 frontage road and North 60th Avenue; Bromley Business Parkway

brighton/5.title: Land Use and Development Code changes, floodplain rules and Bridge Street land
brighton/5.summary: Council worked on Land Use and Development Code amendments: Articles 1 and 11 on administration (hearing Sept. 15, then Oct. 6) and Article 10 floodplain rules (Oct. 20). It also discussed a Comprehensive Plan 80% draft and land use scenarios for city-owned property on Bridge Street.

brighton/6.title: North 40th Avenue construction and 27J agreement
brighton/6.summary: Council considered a roughly $2.7 million contract for building the North 40th Avenue roadway segment. It also considered an intergovernmental agreement with School District 27J covering a regional detention pond, easements and maintenance.

brighton/7.title: Lawsuit over contaminated city drinking water well
brighton/7.summary: Council approved filing an amended complaint to add defendants in litigation over contamination of a city drinking water well. The resolution also covers filings in opioid litigation.

brighton/8.title: Police JAG grant and Flock cameras
brighton/8.summary: Council reviewed accepting an Edward Byrne Memorial JAG grant and authorizing the police chief to sign it and other public safety grants. Attached presentations reference Flock.

brighton/9.title: Water treatment chemical supply contracts
brighton/9.summary: Council reviewed and then approved master price agreements for water treatment plant chemicals, with awards to Univar Solutions USA and PVS DX.

brighton/10.title: Lupton Meadows reservoir and Cherry Meadows pond maintenance
brighton/10.summary: Council reviewed Cherry Meadows pond maintenance and the Lupton Meadows reservoir design project. It considered Change Order No. 3 with Engineering Analytics for the reservoir design.

brighton/11.title: Prairie Center Metropolitan District No. 7 service plan amendment
brighton/11.summary: Council held a public hearing on a second amendment to the service plan for Prairie Center Metropolitan District No. 7.

broomfield/0.title: Broomfield Town Square site plan revocation / Notice to Show Cause
broomfield/0.summary: On Sept. 22 Councilmembers Twiss and Peterson asked Council to consider starting a revocation hearing for the Broomfield Town Square Site Development Plan. On Oct. 13 Council took up a Notice to Show Cause (Resolution 2026-133). The documents do not state an outcome.

broomfield/1.title: 2026 revised and 2027 City and County budgets
broomfield/1.summary: Council reviewed the draft 2026 revised and 2027 operating and capital budgets, the long range financial plan and department budget presentations. A public hearing was set for Oct. 13 and budget resolutions for the City and County, BURA, Arista Local Improvement District and Flatiron Improvement District were scheduled for Oct. 27. The library was told its 2027 budget is flat.

broomfield/2.title: Hospital developments in North Park and Northlands (AdventHealth and UCHealth)
broomfield/2.summary: The Land Use Review Commission recommended approval, 6-0, of the North Park Filing No. 8 Replat A final plat and site plans, including the AdventHealth hospital. It also recommended the UCHealth hospital site plan in Northlands Filing No. 1 Replat C, with an added condition. An Anthem Ranch resident spoke at the hearing.

broomfield/3.title: November 3 ballot: lodging tax and Xcel franchise agreement
broomfield/3.summary: Council referred a lodging tax question to the Nov. 3, 2026 election and later considered resolutions supporting Ballot Item 1A (lodging tax) and 1B (Broomfield-Xcel franchise agreement). Council also approved election IGAs and heard an update on 2026 ballot measures, including a proposed DA term-limits question.

broomfield/4.title: Housing: needs assessment, inclusionary housing and Proposition 123
broomfield/4.summary: Council heard the Broomfield Housing Alliance annual update and a youth housing presentation. A study session covered the 2026 Housing Needs Assessment and inclusionary housing ordinance status. Council also considered opting in to Proposition 123 Cycle 2 and a Prop 123 fast-track review ordinance (first reading Oct. 27).

broomfield/5.title: Enterprise utility ordinance and water items
broomfield/5.summary: Council took up Ordinance 2308 on an enterprise utility (first reading Oct. 13, second reading Oct. 27). It also approved a Mile High Water license, and the FLOW water advisory committee met.

sources.body: Fiscal Leadership on Water (FLOW) Advisory Committee
Fiscal Leadership on Water (FLOW) Advisory Committee

broomfield/6.title: Electronic bike enforcement ordinance
broomfield/6.summary: Council held first reading of Ordinance 2311 on electronic bike enforcement on Aug. 25.

broomfield/7.title: Protecting outdoor recreation facilities in site plan amendments
broomfield/7.summary: Ordinance 2305 would require a public hearing for site development plan amendments that reduce or eliminate outdoor recreation facilities. It had first reading Aug. 25 and second reading Sept. 22.

broomfield/8.title: EV charging fees and zoning
broomfield/8.summary: Council set a fee structure for EV charging stations on city property. It also held a public hearing and second reading on Ordinance 2301, allowing EV charging as a primary permitted use in non-residential districts.

broomfield/9.title: Rail, transit and regional transportation
broomfield/9.summary: Council considered a Rail District station narrative for joint service and Front Range Passenger Rail. Councilmember Ward also asked for a resolution supporting H.R. 5356 (National Infrastructure Bank Act) and a study session on Regional Transportation Authorities. The transportation forum met Aug. 14.

broomfield/10.title: Palisade Park Chipotle and Nordstrom Silo landmark
broomfield/10.summary: Council and BURA held public hearings on the Chipotle final plat and site plan at Palisade Park. Council also considered a landmark nomination for the Nordstrom Silo.

broomfield/11.title: Parks, recreation and senior services 2027 fee schedule
broomfield/11.summary: Council considered the 2027 Parks, Recreation and Senior Services fee schedule (Resolution 2026-92). It also considered the Markel Wottge Open Space Plan implementation agreement.

buena-vista/0.title: R-2 OT zone change to allow duplexes and small multifamily (The Crossing)
buena-vista/0.summary: A developer at The Crossing and a resident asked the Planning & Zoning Commission to amend the R-2 OT zone to allow small multifamily and attached duplexes. The commission discussed party walls, a 3-foot side setback, articulation and possibly requiring a special use permit for larger lots, and planned a formal code amendment for consideration on 11/4/26. The Historic Preservation Commission was also asked for feedback on over/under duplexes.
buena-vista/0.where: R-2 OT zone district, including The Crossing

sources.body: Planning and Zoning Commission - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)
Planning and Zoning Commission - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/1.title: Short-term rental ordinance (Ordinances 2026-14 and 2026-16)
buena-vista/1.summary: The Board of Trustees discussed and considered amending the short-term rental rules in Chapter 6 of the municipal code over several meetings. Ordinance 2026-14 was on the August agendas and Ordinance 2026-16 followed on September 22.

buena-vista/2.title: 2027 Town budget and fee schedule
buena-vista/2.summary: Department heads and advisory boards presented 2027 budget requests in work sessions, followed by public hearings. The Board was scheduled to adopt the 2027 budget, appropriations and fee schedule on October 27. Requests included $12,700 from Beautification and $3,000 for Historic Preservation.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/3.title: Boys & Girls Club facility at 710 Cedar Street
buena-vista/3.summary: The Planning & Zoning Commission reviewed a major site plan for a new Boys & Girls Club building on a 0.729-acre town-owned lot. The Trustees were also asked to amend the ground lease and consent to assigning it to Great Futures BV, Inc. A neighbor wrote in support and asked about on-street parking.

buena-vista/4.title: Rustic Haven cohousing site plan
buena-vista/4.summary: The Planning & Zoning Commission held a hearing on a major site plan to convert a 2.2-acre cabin lodging property into a cohousing community of 11 units. The applicant must complete a water audit. Supporters spoke in favor, and a neighbor raised fence and livestock concerns.

buena-vista/5.title: Data center moratorium discussion
buena-vista/5.summary: The Planning & Zoning Commission placed a general discussion of a data center moratorium on its October 21 agenda.

sources.body: Planning and Zoning Commission - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/6.title: Water rate study and water efficiency planning
buena-vista/6.summary: The Water Advisory Board reviewed technical memos for the utility rate study, including 10-year financial planning. The Trustees heard a rate study update and an Urban Land Institute presentation on water-efficient development and landscaping.

buena-vista/7.title: Housing Needs Assessment and Proposition 123 commitments
buena-vista/7.summary: Buena Vista is part of a regional Housing Needs Assessment with Chaffee County and Salida, due to DOLA by the end of 2026. The Trustees were also asked to approve a regional Proposition 123 affordable housing memorandum and the town's 2027-2029 commitment.

buena-vista/8.title: Transportation Master Plan update
buena-vista/8.summary: KLJ Engineering introduced the new Transportation Master Plan to the Planning & Zoning Commission and the Trustees. Top priorities include safe crossings of major roads and the railroad, paved multimodal trails and a parking strategy.

buena-vista/9.title: Airport projects: AWOS, safety plan and Aspen closure
buena-vista/9.summary: The Airport Advisory Board tracked the AWOS weather system bids, which came in high but were later brought within available funding. It also followed the North Apron close-out, the draft safety plan, prairie dog hazards and planning for the 2027 Aspen airport closure. Both meetings lacked a quorum for formal action.

buena-vista/10.title: Wildfire resiliency code amendments and fire district Ballot Issue 6A
buena-vista/10.summary: The Trustees held a hearing on Ordinance 2026-15, local amendments to the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. They were also asked to support Ballot Issue 6A to include all town property in the Chaffee County Fire Protection District.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/11.title: Law enforcement agreements and co-response program
buena-vista/11.summary: The Trustees considered intergovernmental agreements with the Chaffee County Sheriff's Office for a regional tactical response team and law enforcement mutual aid, and ending the town's participation in another special team agreement. They also heard an update on the county co-response program.

buena-vista/12.title: Sangre de Cristo Electric tree permit
buena-vista/12.summary: The Tree Advisory Board reviewed a tree inventory along primary power lines with removals and pruning identified. The Trustees were to hear the electric association's right-of-way tree work permit application.

buena-vista/13.title: Historic Pearl stabilization and St. Rose of Lima roof
buena-vista/13.summary: The town is stabilizing the damaged Pearl building, with staff hoping to step away by year-end. The Historic Preservation Commission also approved an asphalt shingle roof replacement at the historic St. Rose of Lima church, with recommendations including a closer cedar match and a State Historical Fund grant.
buena-vista/13.where: The Pearl; 343 St. Rose of Lima

burlington/0.title: Proposed 2027 city budget
burlington/0.summary: City staff and department heads were scheduled to present the proposed 2027 budget to the City Council at the Oct. 26 meeting. The presenters included the city administrator, police, activities, treasurer, Old Town and economic development.

burlington/1.title: City administrator executive search
burlington/1.summary: The City Council scheduled a closed-door session on a personnel matter about the search for a city administrator. No outcome is stated in the documents.

burlington/2.title: Our Hometown Charitable Foundation fundraiser at The Midway Theater
burlington/2.summary: Council was asked to consider a special events permit for a fundraising event by Our Hometown Charitable Foundation on Saturday, Nov. 21. The event would be at The Midway Theater, 446 14th St.

campo/0.title: Triangle Bikeway East Design alignment and opposition
campo/0.summary: The TCC and Executive Board were asked to endorse a technical alignment for the Triangle Bikeway East Design Project to carry forward to 30% design. At the November 2025 board meeting, a resident spoke against the project, citing mining regulations, zoning and active lawsuits on the property.
campo/0.where: Triangle Bikeway East corridor, Wake County

campo/1.title: Capital Boulevard/US 1 North (U-5307) project and tolling
campo/1.summary: The board discussed accelerating the Capital Blvd./US 1 North project, including its earlier action authorizing tolling. The 2055 transportation plan was recommended for approval subject to removing U-5307 as a tolled project. An outside speaker praised NCDOT and CAMPO for speeding it up.
campo/1.where: Capital Boulevard / US 1 North, Raleigh area

campo/2.title: 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan adoption
campo/2.summary: The Executive Board approved the draft 2055 MTP/CTP project list in November 2025 and held public hearings, with final adoption planned for February 2026. A resident at the January hearing called the plan good and asked that safety be emphasized.

campo/3.title: Wake Transit Plan 2035, Bus Plan and annual work plans
campo/3.summary: CAMPO committees reviewed the Recommended 2035 Wake Transit Plan, which aims for routes running 365 days a year, plus quarterly amendments and the FY 2027 Wake Transit Work Plan. The board approved a Wake Bus Plan 2035 contract with Nelson\Nygaard, and a public hearing on the FY 2027 work plan was held in May 2026. A vehicle rental tax revenue footnote was debated.

campo/4.title: Triangle Mobility Hub preferred alternative
campo/4.summary: GoTriangle sought approval of the Locally Preferred Alternative for the Triangle Mobility Hub. After a public hearing where comments generally supported the project, the Executive Board moved to approve it in June 2026. The Triangle West board approved it the day before.

campo/5.title: Project cost estimates and delivery deadline for NCDOT-funded projects
campo/5.summary: NCDOT now requires a certified cost estimate (CSCE) for prioritized projects, with a September 30, 2027 target for all projects. CAMPO has 27 projects needing plans, and officials tracked Division 4 and 5 projects such as the Western Boulevard tunnel and NC 42. The chair asked for more frequent updates.

campo/6.title: Local roads and greenways funding (LAPP) including Crabtree Creek Greenway
campo/6.summary: Raleigh requested additional funding for the Crabtree Creek Greenway at Lassiter Mill, requiring a 50/50 match, with bids due February 10, 2026. The FFY 2027 LAPP funded 19 submitted projects, including Rolesville, Holly Springs Road and Smith Creek Greenway, and planning began for the FFY 2028 call for projects in August 2026.
campo/6.where: Crabtree Creek Greenway at Lassiter Mill, Raleigh; other Wake County sites

campo/7.title: Bonus allocation projects and TIP amendments (NC 540, RDU interchange)
campo/7.summary: The board selected 16 NC 540 bonus allocation projects, including a new two-lane Neuse River bridge and the Benson Road and Poole Road work, and added them in TIP Amendment #3. The amendment also added an RDU-funded interchange at Aviation Boulevard and National Park, and removed a Cary trails project. Amendment #4 had a hearing in August 2026.
campo/7.where: Johnston and Wake counties; Aviation Blvd at National Park Drive, RDU

campo/8.title: NCDOT resurfacing and safety improvements in Johnston County
campo/8.summary: NCDOT Division 5 briefed the TCC on resurfacing, bridge replacements and the Angier Bypass (scheduled April 2028). CAMPO staff asked whether local funds could widen FY 2028 resurfacing projects to add intersection improvements, and were told it was possible but timing was unclear.

campo/9.title: Regional Transit Technology Plan
campo/9.summary: The TCC and Executive Board approved the Regional Transit Technology Plan as a guiding document for future technology investment, covering real-time passenger information, integrated payments and open data. No public comments were received.

canon-city/0.title: Pool ballot question and sales tax agreement with the Recreation and Park District
canon-city/0.summary: Council met jointly with the Cañon City Area Recreation and Park District on ballot language and a revised pool project. Resolution 12, Series 2026 asks voters to let the city keep previously collected tax and continue the temporary 0.30% sales and use tax for the community pool. The related intergovernmental agreement with the District caps bonds at $18 million and would end collection if the question fails.

canon-city/1.title: 2027 city budget and budget workshops
canon-city/1.summary: Staff began 2027 budget planning in August and held committee workshops on police, the Parks Improvement Fund, stormwater and raw water. Council held the 2027 budget public hearing on October 21 and continued it on November 2. The budget includes street, water, stormwater and park projects. The committee also discussed 2026 underspending and a compensation study.

sources.body: Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee

canon-city/2.title: 2A street program and pavement management
canon-city/2.summary: Staff reported 40 roadway projects completed under the 1% 2A street sales tax, which was renewed through 2036. Projects include N 9th Street segments and a Griffin Avenue design slated to bid in October 2026. Staff recommended delivery methods for 2027 projects, updating the pavement plan in 2028, and continued magnesium chloride on gravel roads. Ordinance 14 amends code on the 2A tax.

sources.body: Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee

canon-city/3.title: Water quality, drought, bills and rate increases
canon-city/3.summary: Council and the Water Committee discussed water quality, water bills, drought availability and which tier of shortage response plan to adopt. The committee reviewed a 7% water rate increase and a 3.9% stormwater rate increase. Ordinances 19 and 20 on water and stormwater rates were on the November 2 agenda.

canon-city/4.title: Ditch and culvert maintenance rules
canon-city/4.summary: Draft code language defines culverts, ditches and obstructions and puts maintenance of private culverts and stormwater ditches on property owners. It was before Council on October 7 and the Water Committee on October 28 under a Title 19 discussion.

canon-city/5.title: Royal Gorge lease termination and Royal Gorge Mountain Park trails
canon-city/5.summary: Council held closed sessions on negotiation strategy for terminating the Royal Gorge lease agreement with Royal Gorge Company of Colorado. Council also considered a state grant resolution for Royal Gorge Mountain Park, which was removed from the October 5 agenda. The Trails Committee planned to walk the contemplated South Rim Trail.

sources.body: Royal Gorge Mountain Park Trails Committee
Royal Gorge Mountain Park Trails Committee

canon-city/6.title: City attorney resignation and search
canon-city/6.summary: Council discussed next steps after the city attorney resigned. A relationship study committee and a search committee have met repeatedly, with a search committee update on November 2.

canon-city/7.title: Centennial Park plaza and parking design options
canon-city/7.summary: Council weighed two design options for a public plaza and about 17 parking spaces. The first uses bids from April 2026 of $939,559.78 and $971,290.03, with Gordon Construction asking a $10,000 adjustment. The second is a basic plaza with the stage, restroom and electrical removed, needing $57-94K to design and possibly stormwater work. Funding is 100% city dollars.

canon-city/8.title: Western Gateway Park Framework Plan
canon-city/8.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on a resolution adopting the Western Gateway Park Framework Plan, which fulfills the 2021 Comprehensive Plan's riverfront vision. It then went to Council on November 2.
canon-city/8.where: West of South 1st Street, north of the Arkansas River

canon-city/9.title: Police impound lot fence variances
canon-city/9.summary: The Board of Adjustment heard a request for four variances from fence standards to build security fencing around the expanded police impound lot at 161 Justice Center Road. Staff had received no public comment letters as of September 30.

canon-city/10.title: Urban renewal grants and 4-Mile Ranch development
canon-city/10.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority held a pre-budget grant discussion, a building systems grant for 320 Main Street, and a special project grant application for 111 N. Cottonwood. Council also held a closed session on revenue sharing agreements and a Master Development Agreement for 4-Mile Ranch.

canon-city/11.title: Sales tax on food for home consumption
canon-city/11.summary: The Economic Development Committee heard a presentation from Ken Rief on Sally's Bakery about whether city sales tax should apply to food for home consumption. A sales tax item also appeared on the November 2 Council agenda.

canon-city/12.title: Public restroom design recommendations
canon-city/12.summary: The Public Safety and Quality of Life Committee reviewed recommendations for public restrooms, including local metal-frame construction, preventing gutter clogging with trash and needles, police opening and closing, and backup skylight lighting.

sources.body: Public Safety and Quality of Life Committee

castle-pines/0.title: Annexation Policy and charter ballot measure requiring voter approval for annexations
castle-pines/0.summary: Council adopted an Annexation Policy (Resolution 26-49, with a minor three-word addition) after continuing it on Aug. 11. It also passed Resolution 26-53 opposing a citizen-initiated charter amendment that would require voter approval for certain large annexations, and set ballot title for that measure. The Chamber of Commerce spoke on the issue, and a resident asked for a public meeting timeline.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/1.title: Site Improvement Plan zoning amendment (Ordinance 26-06)
castle-pines/1.summary: Council amended Section 27 (Site Improvement Plan) of the zoning ordinance, with first reading Aug. 11 and a public hearing and second reading Aug. 25. Speakers asked for a holistic review and an amendment, while another said it gives a clear and predictable process. Later commenters asked for adjacent-owner notification, a central online page for development information, and HOA inclusion in referrals.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/2.title: Happy Canyon Road/I-25 interchange project agreements
castle-pines/2.summary: Council approved a series of intergovernmental agreements with the State and CDOT, professional services amendments, and funding (BTE) and maintenance agreements for the Happy Canyon Road/I-25 interchange. It also considered construction management with Alfred Benesch and constructability services with Stanton.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/3.title: Proposed 2027 budget and strategic projects 2027-2029
castle-pines/3.summary: Council discussed 2027 budget policy and a 2027-2029 strategic project list, then the City Manager presented the proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 20. Projections include 104 new home permits, a 3% property tax increase, a 36% drop in construction use tax after a 26% rise in 2026, and a 28% decrease in development-related permit revenue. Priorities include the Road Solutions Plan, Spring Tributary at Lagae Road, a second Parks foreman, the Trails Master Plan and lodging/admissions tax research.

castle-pines/4.title: Canyonside plans and South Havana Street vacation
castle-pines/4.summary: Council heard a public hearing on the Canyonside Preliminary Plan No. 1, 2nd Amendment (Resolution 26-62), then took up the Canyonside Filing No. 1, 3rd Amendment replat and an ordinance vacating part of South Havana Street. A Castle Pines North Filing No. 27 replat was also on the Oct. 27 agenda.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/5.title: Expedited review for affordable housing (Proposition 123)
castle-pines/5.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-63 adopting an expedited review process for qualified affordable housing development as part of the city's Proposition 123 commitment.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/6.title: Transfer of recreation properties and tracts to Castle Pines North Metropolitan District
castle-pines/6.summary: Ordinances 26-08 and 26-09 approve conveying certain recreation properties and tracts of land under an intergovernmental agreement between the city and the Castle Pines North Metropolitan District. They passed first reading Sept. 22 and went to public hearing on second reading Oct. 13.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/7.title: Soaring Hawk Park phasing, Coyote Ridge renovation and trail signage
castle-pines/7.summary: The Parks and Recreation Advisory Board reviewed Soaring Hawk Park Phase 1 and phasing options, a Coyote Ridge Park renovation update, and trail signage for 35 trail segments, including kiosks, directional signs and mile markers. Council also awarded a construction contract (Project 2026-PR-003) on Aug. 25.
castle-pines/7.where: Soaring Hawk Park, Coyote Ridge Park and city trails

Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting

Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting

castle-pines/8.title: City council redistricting (Ordinance 26-10)
castle-pines/8.summary: Council amended the boundaries of the city's three districts, with first reading Oct. 13 and a public hearing on second reading Oct. 27.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/9.title: Axon camera discussion and I-25 interchange monument
castle-pines/9.summary: The Oct. 27 study session included a discussion of Axon cameras. The regular agenda included a design and engineering services agreement for a northbound interchange monument at Castle Pines Parkway and I-25.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

centennial/0.title: Elevation Volleyball annexation and initial zoning
centennial/0.summary: Council considered a petition to annex the Elevation Volleyball property from Arapahoe County, with initial zoning (Ordinances 2026-O-11 and O-12). Planning and Zoning reviewed the zoning on Sept 9, first reading was Sept 15, and annexation hearings were set for Oct 6.

centennial/1.title: Rezoning of business park and industrial land (Fremont/Potomac, Nichols/Akron, Chester)
centennial/1.summary: Ordinance 2026-O-14 would rezone land north of East Fremont Avenue and east of Potomac Street from PUD to Employment Center – Light Industry 50. Further rezonings south of East Nichols and east of South Akron, and west of South Chester, from Business Park to Employment Center were on first reading Nov 2. Council also held a legal-advice session on regulating industrial and business parks and discussed legislative zoning opportunities.
centennial/1.where: East Fremont Ave/Potomac St; East Nichols Ave/South Akron St; South Chester St

centennial/2.title: 2027/2028 biennial budget
centennial/2.summary: The Budget Committee and Council held work sessions and budget workshops on revenues, fund balance and the City Manager's proposed 2027/2028 budget. Committee also reviewed a fee and cost analysis for general improvement districts.

centennial/3.title: Sales and use tax rate increase and election
centennial/3.summary: Resolutions in August covered an intergovernmental agreement for election administration and authorization to increase the sales and use tax rate. Ordinance 2026-O-21 amending Chapter 4 on a tax rate increase was set for hearing Nov 17.

centennial/4.title: Opting out of the state graywater program
centennial/4.summary: Ordinance 2026-O-15 would opt Centennial out of the state graywater program and prohibit graywater treatment works and use. It had first reading Sept 1 and a public hearing Sept 15.

centennial/5.title: Land Development Code amendments
centennial/5.summary: Planning and Zoning and Council study sessions discussed proposed amendments to the Land Development Code in October.

centennial/6.title: Livable Streets residential collectors next phase
centennial/6.summary: Council discussed the next phase of the Livable Streets program for residential collector streets on Oct 20.

centennial/7.title: Changes to Investment and Budget Committees
centennial/7.summary: Ordinance 2026-O-17 would amend the rules for the city's Investment and Budget Committees, including member appointment dates, with a hearing set for Nov 17.

centennial/8.title: Grant funding agreement and housing bond allocation
centennial/8.summary: Council considered amending the 2026 budget to accept grant funding, and assigning private activity bond ceiling to the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority.

centennial/9.title: Westray Business Improvement District 2027 plan and budget
centennial/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-R-32 approving the Westray Business Improvement District's 2027 operating plan and budget.

chaffee-county/0.title: Corrigan Rezone in Garfield (22420 and 22435 Hwy 50)
chaffee-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission heard a request to rezone several parcels in the historic Garfield townsite from Residential Rural to Mixed Use Rural so the properties could apply for commercial lodging. Staff said the rezone would remedy a land use code violation. Neighbors raised spot zoning, noise, unpermitted structures, wastewater and fire-safety concerns, and the owner spoke in support. A public hearing was on the Commissioners' October 20 agenda.

chaffee-county/1.title: Housing needs assessment, River Village Mobile Home Park and affordable housing funding
chaffee-county/1.summary: Commissioners reviewed the final 2026 Regional Housing Needs Assessment done with Buena Vista, Poncha Springs and Salida. They agreed to serve as applicant and fiscal sponsor for a DOLA asbestos-removal grant for River Village Mobile Home Park, with Chaffee Housing Trust. A $25,000 lodging-tax reimbursement for the park's planning and building fees was also on the agenda. The Planning Commission scheduled an affordable housing work session.
chaffee-county/1.where: River Village Mobile Home Park; Countywide

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/2.title: 2027 county budget hearings
chaffee-county/2.summary: Commissioners held budget hearings in late August and a Sheriff's Office budget hearing in September. The Fair Committee presented its FY27 budget request on October 6. The airport and tourism boards were also working on their 2027 budgets.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/3.title: Airport land lease, new development area and 2027 projects
chaffee-county/3.summary: The airport board discussed a new land lease at length, with members of the public commenting. The 2027 budget requests include removing the old fuel farm (about $48,000 eligible), a well for the new development area, a master drainage plan and Taxiway A rehabilitation design. The terminal roof has been leaking during rainstorms.

chaffee-county/4.title: Tourism marketing budget and Colorado Tourism Office conflict-of-interest memo
chaffee-county/4.summary: The tourism board worked on the 2027 tourism budget, a five-year strategic plan and a memo responding to the Colorado Tourism Office's "perceived conflict of interest." Lodging tax is up 18% in unincorporated Chaffee County for January to July. Commissioners were to discuss the Destination Management Council's recommendation for website and AI enhancements.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/5.title: Wildfire response and forest health grants
chaffee-county/5.summary: Chaffee County helped Lake County with the Willow Fire and the emergency council reported dry conditions. Commissioners wrote support letters for Forest Restoration and Wildfire Risk Mitigation grant applications from Chateau Chaparral, Colorado Firecamp, Chaffee County Fire Protection District and Salida Fire Department. A work session item covered a letter to the Public Utilities Commission on Xcel and Black Hills wildfire mitigation.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/6.title: County archery range ground lease with Colorado Parks & Wildlife
chaffee-county/6.summary: Commissioners considered a ground lease for Colorado Parks and Wildlife to manage the Chaffee County Archery Range. A motion was made directing staff to finalize terms with CPW.

chaffee-county/7.title: EMS medical director and regional tactical team agreement
chaffee-county/7.summary: Commissioners moved to contract Dr. Michael Mandrell as Chaffee County EMS Medical Director. They also considered an IGA with the Town of Buena Vista for a Regional Tactical team. The E911 board also took up Motorola console replacement.

chaffee-county/8.title: Water court opposition and Monarch Mountain Lodge water
chaffee-county/8.summary: The county ratified a statement opposing water court case 2026CW3107, a change of water rights application by Colorado Parks and Wildlife and the Wildlife Commission. Commissioners also said they would help people relying on water at Monarch Mountain Lodge get their water turned back on. Closed-door legal discussion covered Monarch Mountain Lodge, Forest Service Road 295 litigation and 7856 County Road 152.

chaffee-county/9.title: Planned development rules training and building code appeals
chaffee-county/9.summary: The Planning Commission held a work session on how planned developments work under the county land use code. The Board of Review denied a window variance for emergency escape and rescue. Another appeal concerned permit extensions, and the building code amendments were also on a board agenda.

chaffee-county/10.title: Public health: retail food fees and safe firearm storage grant
chaffee-county/10.summary: Commissioners were asked to approve an updated retail food fee schedule for Public Health after an October 19 work session. Public Health reported its gun violence prevention grant ended, noting local firearm retailers were already approached by multiple initiatives and the required safe-storage messaging did not align with local views.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/11.title: Electric vehicle fleet study and electric transmission discussion
chaffee-county/11.summary: A CSU fellow presented on replacing county vehicles with electric ones, covering costs, grants and the Colorado Charge Ahead application. Commissioners also planned to meet the Colorado Electric Transmission Authority on September 14.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/12.title: Chaffee County archery range ground lease with Colorado Parks & Wildlife
chaffee-county/12.summary: On September 1, 2026, the Commissioners considered a ground lease with Colorado Parks & Wildlife to operate the Chaffee County archery range. Commissioner Armstrong moved to approve the lease and direct staff to work with CPW to finalize terms.

cherry-hills-village/0.title: 2027 budget and temporary property tax mill levy cut to zero
cherry-hills-village/0.summary: The draft 2027 budget temporarily cuts the Village property tax mill levy to 0 mills for 2027, with the levy able to return in 2028. This is expected to give about $8.5 million in relief, roughly $3,800 for the average homeowner, including about $4.5M that the General Fund would transfer to the Parks Fund. Council held a study session on October 20 and the budget ordinance public hearing is scheduled. The draft also assumes a 10% compensation placeholder and adds a Planner I position.

cherry-hills-village/1.title: Ballot Question 2C: home rule charter amendment on zoning and land use
cherry-hills-village/1.summary: Council passed Resolution 29 supporting Ballot Question 2C, a Charter amendment going to voters on November 3, 2026. It affirms the City's home rule authority over zoning and land use against state land use legislation. Council asked for stronger wording and approved the resolution subject to an added whereas clause.

cherry-hills-village/2.title: Council opposes Front Range Passenger Rail District Ballot Issue 7A
cherry-hills-village/2.summary: Council took up Resolution 30 opposing Ballot Issue 7A, a tax increase for Front Range Passenger Rail District voters on the November ballot. Discussion focused on how the district was structured for taxing purposes and on a planned stop near Santa Fe, across from the City in unincorporated Jefferson County.
cherry-hills-village/2.where: Citywide; planned rail stop near Santa Fe

cherry-hills-village/3.title: Planning commission study sessions on rezoning, lot frontage, and Master Plan sustainability
cherry-hills-village/3.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission scheduled a study session on legislative rezoning and lot frontage. It also discussed Master Plan sustainability and resiliency, including electric police and public works vehicles, electronic permitting, and stormwater drainage along roadside ditches and South Holly Street. The land use and zoning Master Plan discussion was deferred partly because of recent legal and legislative developments, including a lawsuit filed by Northglenn.

cherry-hills-village/4.title: Día de los Muertos art exhibit and family event
cherry-hills-village/4.summary: Council approved a loan of eight calavera sculptures and bases for up to $10,000. The Art Commission is planning a free family event on Saturday, October 24, 2-4 p.m., and has worked through food, activities, a guitarist, and a children's author or storyteller. About $4,800 remains in the public art display budget after the loan.

cherry-hills-village/5.title: Parks, Trails & Recreation 2027 work plan, including trail safety and bike lanes
cherry-hills-village/5.summary: The commission is building its 2027 work plan, adding a Trail Passport Program, Parks & Trails Visioning with safety improvements, a Recreation Reimbursement Program, bike lane improvements on Colorado, Quincy and Mansfield, park signage, and e-bike/e-moto rules. Members raised concerns about crosswalks at the High Line Canal.
cherry-hills-village/5.where: High Line Canal; Colorado, Quincy and Mansfield

cherry-hills-village/6.title: 2027 Sculpture-on-Loan project, Art Commission work plan and branding
cherry-hills-village/6.summary: The Art Commission is deciding whether to start a project brief for the 2027 Sculpture-on-Loan program, with about $4,687.50 available and $5,000 anticipated in the 2027 work plan. It is also considering a brighter cherry-red logo color, the Snow Plow Painting Program, and a revised meeting schedule.

cherry-hills-village/7.title: Possible expansion of municipal parks and Fair Housing Act discussion
cherry-hills-village/7.summary: The October 6 Council agenda lists items on the potential expansion of municipal parks within the City and on the operation of the federal Fair Housing Act alongside Village rules. The documents give no detail on outcomes.

clear-creek-county/0.title: Lodging tax increase ballot question (R-26-55)
clear-creek-county/0.summary: The commissioners considered Resolution R-26-55 to put a question to voters in unincorporated Clear Creek County and its municipalities, except Georgetown, on raising the county's lodging tax. Proceeds would go toward road maintenance or improvements, public safety, childcare and housing tied to tourism. Lodging tax was also on an August intergovernmental agenda, and a tourism bureau website and messaging presentation was scheduled.

clear-creek-county/1.title: 2026 budget check-in and 2027 proposed budget
clear-creek-county/1.summary: The board held work sessions on the 2026 budget and the 2027 budget process in August, then took up 2027 budget requests in September. A 2027 proposed budget workshop was set for October 20. Also on the agenda: restoring a Deputy Clerk position as permanent full-time, and a Sheriff's Office staffing and compensation matter.

clear-creek-county/2.title: Open fire ban ordinance (Ordinance No. 20) and wildfire preparedness
clear-creek-county/2.summary: The board held a second reading and public hearing on Ordinance No. 20, which repeals and replaces Ordinance No. 16 and sets regulations for banning open fires. It also heard a Public Safety Power Shutoff presentation, and reviewed the county's 2026 wildfire mitigation plan. A Wildfire Preparedness Workshop was announced for August 26 at Dumont Fire Station.

clear-creek-county/3.title: Housing: Prop 123 credits and regional housing action plan
clear-creek-county/3.summary: The county committed to join the Clear Creek Regional Housing Authority's Housing Action Plan and considered an intergovernmental agreement on sharing Proposition 123 affordable housing credits. It also amended an agreement in support of childcare in the county.

clear-creek-county/4.title: Alvarado Open Space Park, Glass Memorial and open space rules
clear-creek-county/4.summary: The Open Space Commission followed up on the Glass Memorial at Alvarado Open Space Park and reviewed a concept for it. It also began a discussion of updating its rules and regulations using Jefferson County's park rules as a model. Other items included a legal question on adding a gate to an access road, grant projects, and parking on county roads to reach open space.

clear-creek-county/5.title: Georgetown purchase of Waldorf inholding parcel
clear-creek-county/5.summary: The Open Space Commission and commissioners discussed a possible purchase, lease or sale involving Parcel No. 2091-034-00-645 in unincorporated Clear Creek County, with the Town of Georgetown seeking to buy. The matter was handled partly in executive session.

clear-creek-county/6.title: Sale of county real property (Resolution R-26-54)
clear-creek-county/6.summary: The board considered Resolution R-26-54 authorizing the sale of real property and granting signature authority to sign the real estate documents.

clear-creek-county/7.title: CDOT I-70 Floyd Hill reporting and Condition 9 requirements
clear-creek-county/7.summary: The board held work sessions on CDOT reporting on the I-70 Floyd Hill project and on CDOT requirements for Condition 9. It also accepted Forest Service public road easements for several county roads, including Little Bear Creek Road and Sinton Road.

clear-creek-county/8.title: Public health agreements and Jefferson County partnerships
clear-creek-county/8.summary: The board rescinded and replaced earlier agreements with Jefferson County Public Health for referral clinical services and with Arapahoe County Public Health for clinician preceptor services. It also approved state public health contract amendments for emergency preparedness and Vaccines for Children.

clear-creek-county/9.title: Clear Creek Fire Authority and emergency services district appointments
clear-creek-county/9.summary: The board considered nominating Bruce Hohne to the Clear Creek Fire Authority board, along with a letter of support for ambulance nomination and USFS grant support. Items also included wildfire watershed and forest health grant support.

clear-creek-county/10.title: Strong Start Scholarship administrative rate
clear-creek-county/10.summary: The Clear Creek Schools Foundation asked to adjust the administrative cost rate for the Strong Start Scholarship Program. The board asked for full financials in a few weeks before amending the agreement. The board also considered support for a school district ballot measure in October.

colorado-springs/0.title: Project Taurus data center appeal at 1565 High Tech Way
colorado-springs/0.summary: Planning Commission held a 15-hour hearing on Project Taurus, a data center on Corporate Ridge Filing No. 1 Lot 4. City Council scheduled a special September 17 appeal hearing at the Pikes Peak Center, limited to 120 public speakers, on the administrative approval of the development plan modification, with noise monitoring and acoustic impacts a focus. Planning staff advised against discussing data centers generally while next steps are uncertain.

colorado-springs/1.title: 2027 budget, tax levy and mid-year finances
colorado-springs/1.summary: Council reviewed 2026 revenue running over budget and how that shapes the 2027 budget, including police and fire turnover and retail marijuana tax funding. It used the extra revenue to cancel a November furlough day, held 2027 budget work and markup sessions, and scheduled a 2027 tax levy of 3.209 mills and the 2027 salary schedule.

colorado-springs/2.title: Homelessness Response Action Plan and car-camping ban
colorado-springs/2.summary: Council got an update on the Homelessness Response Action Plan, the Safe Parking program model, and enforcement of the ordinance banning sleeping in vehicles, with 335 vehicles cited or addressed since it took effect. A councilmember asked whether the Chief Housing and Homelessness Officer role should be split in two. Council also heard on the downtown Clean and Safe program.

colorado-springs/3.title: 501 N Wahsatch Ave conversion to multifamily
colorado-springs/3.summary: The Planning Commission considered a development standards adjustment to allow 13.33 dwelling units per acre to convert an existing commercial building to residential. Neighbors raised parking concerns and opposed losing commercial use; staff said the request met all criteria and the site has six parking spaces.

colorado-springs/4.title: Rezonings and land use plans: Wagner Equipment, Lowell, Creekbend, Cherokee water tank
colorado-springs/4.summary: Several rezones moved through Planning Commission and Council: 22.37 acres for Wagner Equipment at East Platte Ave and Wooten Road, the Cherokee Metro District water tank at Tamlin and Marksheffel, Creekbend, and the Lowell site on East Las Animas Street seeking 184 units per acre and 65-foot height. Council set second readings for several in late October.
colorado-springs/4.where: East Platte Ave and Wooten Rd; Tamlin Rd and N Marksheffel Rd; 202-252 E Las Animas St

colorado-springs/5.title: Banning Lewis Ranch Village B2 rezone
colorado-springs/5.summary: Council took first reading of a rezone for Banning Lewis Ranch Village B2 near Tamlin Road and Dublin Boulevard to a planned development zone with 3.5-7.99 units per acre and 35-foot maximum height.
colorado-springs/5.where: Banning Lewis Ranch, Tamlin Rd and Dublin Blvd

colorado-springs/6.title: Kettle Creek metro district, setbacks and road vacation
colorado-springs/6.summary: Council approved a service plan for the Kettle Creek Metropolitan District north of Old Ranch Road. Planning Commission reviewed a garage setback adjustment at 2060 Old Ranch Road, and Council set a vote on vacating about 2.42 acres of Kettle Creek Road.

colorado-springs/7.title: Annexation petitions
colorado-springs/7.summary: Council accepted annexation petitions for Peacock Ranch South, Sellers Addition, Huber Road, Klein Additions 1-3 and Crow Foot Addition No. 1. Council also took on approving authority for the Southern Colorado Railyard Metropolitan Districts.

colorado-springs/8.title: Height allowances for accessory dwelling units
colorado-springs/8.summary: A proposed ordinance would amend the Unified Development Code to change height allowances for accessory dwelling units. It went through Planning Commission and a Council work session.

colorado-springs/9.title: Business license code rewrite and 2027 fee increases
colorado-springs/9.summary: Council passed ordinances 26-52, 26-53 and 26-54 repealing and reordaining business licensing, sales of goods and adult use business code. A resolution sets 2027 general business license fees rising toward full cost recovery by 2029, with annual CPI adjustments after, raising about $81,000 in year one.

colorado-springs/10.title: Sale of Meadows Park and Wilson Ranch Park
colorado-springs/10.summary: Council went into closed session on negotiating the sale of Meadows Park Community Center, and later on a property interest in part of Wilson Ranch Park.

colorado-springs/11.title: Utilities bonds and electric rates
colorado-springs/11.summary: Council advanced Colorado Springs Utilities bonds, refunding outstanding revenue bonds and issuing new Series 2026A/B improvement bonds, plus a wastewater treatment agreement with Garden Valley and a resolution setting electric rates.

colorado-springs/12.title: New Fire Construction Services Enterprise and ethics code update
colorado-springs/12.summary: Council considered an ordinance creating a Fire Construction Services Enterprise split from the Development Review Enterprise, and updated the Code of Ethics and Internal Audit Charter.

columbine-valley/0.title: E-bike and e-scooter ordinance
columbine-valley/0.summary: Trustees raised concerns about electric bikes in January, and in April the police chief described the current approach to e-bikes and e-scooters. The Board directed staff to draft an ordinance. A resident spoke in support in June, and the mayor later reported positive support for it.

columbine-valley/1.title: Platte Canyon Road sidewalk project
columbine-valley/1.summary: The Board approved extra spending on the sidewalk in June. In August a required design change was discussed and the Trustees directed staff to proceed. In September staff said the sidewalk would not proceed because the design had changed too much.

columbine-valley/2.title: 2027 Town Budget
columbine-valley/2.summary: Staff presented a first draft of the 2027 budget in September, including several special projects and initiatives. A second draft and a required public hearing were scheduled for the October and November meetings. A long-range financial forecast was also presented in August.

columbine-valley/3.title: Housing Needs Assessment
columbine-valley/3.summary: The town is conducting a Housing Needs Assessment. A community survey is underway and staff expects the response to exceed the 20% target. A first draft was scheduled for the October 20 meeting.

columbine-valley/4.title: Annexation of 8 Hunter Run
columbine-valley/4.summary: The Board approved Resolution #14 in August concerning the annexation of 8 Hunter Run. Trustee Bill #11 on the annexation was set for a public hearing on October 20. Earlier, the town had also discussed an HOA about annexing into the town.

columbine-valley/5.title: Pickleball noise and Columbine Country Club development
columbine-valley/5.summary: A resident at 7 Fairway raised concerns about pickleball noise and asked the Trustees to act before future development of the Columbine Country Club Villas. Pickleball discussions came up again in May.

columbine-valley/6.title: Fee schedule and permit fees
columbine-valley/6.summary: The Board approved Resolution #13 in August adopting a town-wide fee schedule. Trustee Bill #9 on permit fees was on the October 20 agenda.

columbine-valley/7.title: Jake brake ordinance
columbine-valley/7.summary: Trustee Bill #8 on engine compression (Jake) brakes passed first reading in July and second reading in August.

columbine-valley/8.title: Smoking and vaping ban in Town Park
columbine-valley/8.summary: Trustee Bill #4 prohibiting smoking and vaping in the Town Park passed first reading in March and second reading in April.

columbine-valley/9.title: Building and fire code updates
columbine-valley/9.summary: The Board adopted updated building codes in November 2025 and the 2024 Fire Code in June 2026 after a public hearing. A Building Commissioner ordinance was tabled indefinitely in March. Land use and zoning updates (Trustee Bill #10) were set for a November hearing.

columbine-valley/10.title: Graffiti in Platte Canyon Road culvert
columbine-valley/10.summary: The Town took steps to mitigate graffiti in a culvert under Platte Canyon Road, and updates continued into April.

commerce-city/0.title: Data center moratorium and study
commerce-city/0.summary: Council voted to schedule a data center topic for a study session, in response to a request for a data center moratorium ordinance. The Environmental Policy and Innovation Commission is discussing data centers and preparing a recommendation, and public feedback is encouraged.

commerce-city/1.title: Shamrock Foods rezoning to I-3 and food oil conditional use at 5199 Ivy Street
commerce-city/1.summary: Planning Commission recommended approval of rezoning the site at the southwest corner of East 52nd Avenue and Ivy Street from I-2 to I-3 heavy industrial, plus a conditional use permit for food oil storage tanks. Commissioners noted the Sand Creek Regional Greenway, about 1,100 feet north, was not notified. Council approved the rezoning on first reading October 5.
commerce-city/1.where: 5199 Ivy Street (SW corner of E 52nd Ave and Ivy St)

commerce-city/2.title: 2027 city budget, fees and mill levy
commerce-city/2.summary: Council and its related districts (Urban Renewal Authority, E-470 Commercial and Residential GIDs, Northern Infrastructure GID) reviewed 2027 preliminary budgets, with mill levy options for NIGID. Budget adoption and tax levy hearings are set for October 19 and November 2. Parks and golf fee increases for 2027 were also presented.

E-470 Commercial Area General Improvement District
