E-470 Commercial Area General Improvement District
E-470 Residential Area General Improvement District

commerce-city/3.title: Reunion Filing 39 final plat (84 lots)
commerce-city/3.summary: Oakwood Homes requested final plat approval for Reunion Filing 39, creating 84 lots and six tracts on about 22.5 acres near Chambers Road and Heartland Drive within the Reunion PUD. It went to Planning Commission September 1 and Council October 19, with public comment submitted.
commerce-city/3.where: Chambers Road and Heartland Drive, Reunion PUD

commerce-city/4.title: Land Development Code rezoning and amendments
commerce-city/4.summary: The city is updating its 2025 Land Development Code, including a legislative rezoning project with proposed zoning maps, Ordinance 2795, Ordinance 2803 and a joint Tier 2 study session on land uses, procedures and approval criteria. Public comment was included in the rezoning materials.

commerce-city/5.title: Annexations: Third Creek East, South Platte Crossing Phase 2, surrounded enclaves
commerce-city/5.summary: Council found substantial compliance on the Third Creek East annexation petition (September 21) and the South Platte Crossing Phase 2 petition (October 19), setting eligibility hearings. Council also discussed annexing surrounded enclaves, and approved the 88th and Tower annexation earlier.
commerce-city/5.where: Third Creek East; South Platte Crossing; 88th and Tower

commerce-city/6.title: Housing Action Plan and Commerce City Housing Authority
commerce-city/6.summary: Outreach for the Housing Action Plan launched with public surveys, and a consultant presented to Council and Planning Commission on October 26. Council also scheduled a discussion of the Commerce City Housing Authority and its affordable projects.

commerce-city/7.title: Chambers Road widening and road impact fees
commerce-city/7.summary: Council moved to use road impact fee funds for road widening Phase I projects, awarded a contract to Lighthouse Transportation Group for the Chambers Road and Heartland Drive project, and scheduled a project update.

commerce-city/8.title: Oil and gas development north of the city, Suncor study session
commerce-city/8.summary: A Chevron-hosted meeting reviewed proposed oil and gas development north of the city, and a Council request sought a study session with Suncor.
commerce-city/8.where: North of Commerce City; Suncor refinery

commerce-city/9.title: Police mobile command unit and Axon agreement
commerce-city/9.summary: Council considered an ordinance (2796) for the Police Department to purchase a mobile command unit from SACFD, and approved a first amendment to the Axon master services agreement.

commerce-city/10.title: Municipal court, noise ordinance and code enforcement changes
commerce-city/10.summary: Court staff presented draft ordinances 2806 and 2807 on jury trials and compliance and enforcement, while Council also discussed options for the municipal noise ordinance.

commerce-city/11.title: Hogan Property PUD amendment
commerce-city/11.summary: Council adopted on second reading an ordinance amending the Hogan Property PUD to consolidate development standards and expand the boundary, on 16.82 acres near 101st Way, with written public comment.

commerce-city/12.title: Riverdale Animal Shelter fees and outdoor vendor rules
commerce-city/12.summary: Council reviewed Riverdale Animal Shelter fees and services, and introduced an ordinance amending restrictions on outdoor vendors.

cortez/0.title: Park Village on 7th affordable rental development
cortez/0.summary: Council was asked on Oct. 13 to authorize the Mayor to sign CHFA's notification form for Park Village on 7th, a proposed affordable rental development on city-owned land at the former high school property. A 7th Street property update was also presented at an Aug. 25 work session.

cortez/1.title: Lodger's Tax increase on the November 2026 ballot
cortez/1.summary: Council held a public hearing on Ordinance No. 1375 to set ballot language asking voters to approve a 4% increase in the city's Lodger's Tax at the Nov. 3, 2026 general election.

cortez/2.title: Comprehensive Plan update and Water System Master Plan
cortez/2.summary: Council considered adopting the 2026 Water System Master Plan (Resolution 16) and awarding the Comprehensive Plan update covering Strategic Growth and Water Supply elements to SE Group. Council also toured the Cortez Water Treatment Plant in August.

cortez/3.title: Cortez Municipal Airport contracts and FBO lease termination
cortez/3.summary: Council took up a notice of termination of the Fixed Base Operator lease, an asbestos abatement project bid, extension of the TSA terminal lease through June 30, 2031, and a five-year engineering services contract starting Dec. 1, 2026. A youth seat on the Airport Advisory Committee was also filled.

cortez/4.title: Historic designations: Garland Home and 209 West Main
cortez/4.summary: Council moved through readings of ordinances adding the Garland Home at 120 East North Street (Ord. 1376) and the building at 209 West Main Street (Ord. 1377) to the City Register of Historic Resources. Council also accepted a CLG grant award and a $50,000 supplemental state grant amendment.
cortez/4.where: 120 East North Street; 209 West Main Street

cortez/5.title: Land Use Code changes (Ordinance 1374)
cortez/5.summary: Staff presented an ordinance revising various sections of the Cortez Land Use Code, with first reading on Aug. 25 and second reading on Sept. 8.

cortez/6.title: Site plan and permits at 127 N. Market St and 1411 Montelores Ave
cortez/6.summary: Planning commission reviewed a major site plan for 127 N. Market St, which went to Council as Resolution 15 on Aug. 25. A conditional use permit and minor deviation for a carport encroaching into setbacks was heard by planning on Sept. 1 and Council on Sept. 22.

cortez/7.title: Mobile food vendor licensing rules
cortez/7.summary: Council discussed and then took up Ordinance 1371 revising the annual licensing process for mobile food vendors in Cortez, appearing on agendas Oct. 13 and Oct. 27.

cortez/8.title: Parks and Recreation Master Plan and ash tree beetle
cortez/8.summary: Council picked a representative for the Parks and Recreation Master Plan committee and held a community engagement update and listening session on Oct. 27. Parks staff also briefed Council on the green ash beetle's impact on park ash trees.

cortez/9.title: Montezuma-Sligo drainage improvement project
cortez/9.summary: Council considered awarding Phase 2 of the 2026 Montezuma-Sligo Drainage Improvement Project to D&L Construction.

cortez/10.title: City Attorney and Municipal Judge contracts, spending limits
cortez/10.summary: Council considered an amendment increasing the City Attorney's compensation and held executive sessions on the Municipal Judge's contract. Council also considered Resolution 14 updating spending authority limits.

cortez/11.title: Fiber Express Line negotiations
cortez/11.summary: Council went into executive session on Sept. 22 for negotiations about the Fiber Express Line.

craig/0.title: Water and wastewater rate increase (Ordinance 1187)
craig/0.summary: The City Council was set to take up on first reading Ordinance No. 1187, which would raise water and wastewater rates in the Municipal Code so the Water and Wastewater Enterprise Funds keep a sufficient balance. Another ordinance (No. 1188) amending section 8.04.250 of the code was listed alongside it.

craig/1.title: 2027 city budget and property tax (Ordinance 1186)
craig/1.summary: Council scheduled introduction and first reading of Ordinance No. 1186, which adopts the 2027 budget, sets appropriations and fixes the property tax levy. The item was on the October 27 public hearing agenda.

craig/2.title: Meadows Apartments HUD and DOLA grant agreements
craig/2.summary: Council was asked to approve Resolution No. 34 (2026), covering subrecipient agreements for HUD and DOLA grant funding tied to the Meadows Apartments project.

craig/3.title: Craig Sports Complex bond counsel
craig/3.summary: The Parks and Recreation director recommended Butler Snow LLP as bond counsel for the Craig Sports Complex, which points to bond financing for the project. Council was to consider the selection on October 27.

craig/4.title: Craig Master Plan update awarded to SE Group
craig/4.summary: Council was asked to award the Craig Master Plan Update to SE Group for $195,000. The Planning Commission notes mention a master plan proposed to be completed by early 2028.

craig/5.title: Craig Business and Industrial Park sketch plan
craig/5.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission reviewed a major subdivision sketch plan for the Craig Business and Industrial Park on West 1st Street. Commissioners raised concerns about vagueness, infrastructure capacity and sidewalks, and discussion pointed toward recommending approval to Council on the condition that sidewalks be added to meet the Land Use Code.

craig/6.title: Local Marketing District grants and business plan competition
craig/6.summary: On September 22 Council approved Economic Development Advisory Committee recommendations for Local Marketing District dissolution funds, including $15,000 for the Moffat County Balloon Festival, $4,000 for the Bear River Young Life car show and $15,000 for Powder Mountain Ventures. On October 13 the 2026 Business Plan Competition winners were announced.

craig/7.title: Site plan for hobby shop at 791 Industrial Avenue
craig/7.summary: Mike Thompson's site plan for a personal hobby shop in Green Tree Business Park went from the Planning Commission to Council. Council approved it on October 13.
craig/7.where: 791 Industrial Ave, Green Tree Business Park Lot 6, Block 1

craig/8.title: Tunatua RV Resort deferred amenities agreement
craig/8.summary: The Planning Commission was to consider recommending to Council a Deferred Recreational Amenities and Certificate of Occupancy Agreement for the Tunatua RV Resort.

craig/9.title: Timberg vacant land plan at Pine and East 12th
craig/9.summary: Bruce Timberg was scheduled to present a tentative plan for his vacant land east of Pine Street and East 12th Street to the Planning Commission. Staff also mentioned possible upcoming annexations.
craig/9.where: East of Pine Street and East 12th Street

crawford/0.title: Water rate overhaul and Water Rate Committee
crawford/0.summary: A committee formed in spring 2026 is building a new water rate structure. Current rates of $35-$41 are well below sustainable levels, and the operating need is projected at $238,800 by 2027. Consultant Rita Trick (RCAC) recommended $125/month. Options include tiered overage rates, bulk water at $2-$3 per 100 gallons (now $1.50), a higher tap fee (now $5,000) and doubled conservation rates. A single proposal is headed to a public hearing, and sewer rate analysis was authorized on June 8.

crawford/1.title: Crawford State Park water and sewer rate structure
crawford/1.summary: The committee is reviewing how the state park is billed. The park has about 76-78 points of use, modeled as roughly 31 equivalent taps, and is billed as a rural commercial tap. Council questioned whether that still fits given the park's growth since the 1990s. The park rate was on the October 12 agenda.

crawford/2.title: Spring water project and potable water tank replacement
crawford/2.summary: The spring project is substantially complete and came in under $400,000 of a $537,000 grant, with final reimbursement received by June 2026. Replacing the potable water tank awaits CDPHE approval of the final design, and bidding is expected around July. Crews logged about 150 overtime hours on the project, and council deferred a decision on comp time pending grant guidance.

crawford/3.title: 2026 budget, fee schedule and sewer deficit
crawford/3.summary: Council held the 2026 budget hearing on Nov. 24, 2025. The proposal included a $10/month water increase per meter and a $21,000 sewer deficit split between rate increases and reserves. It also budgeted $10,000 for new billing software and a wastewater jetter. Resolution 6-2025 would update the town fee schedule, but discussion was deferred. Lagoon liner deterioration needs planning for the 2027 budget.

crawford/4.title: Fire-damaged properties on Dogwood and Elm
crawford/4.summary: Council raised concerns about two properties left from earlier fires. In March, letters went to the owners requesting cleanup plans.

crawford/5.title: Cemetery District land purchase and plat
crawford/5.summary: The Cemetery District plans to buy land from Ann Landreth, requiring a boundary adjustment and final plat. Survey and title work indicate the historic cattle-drive easement was abandoned decades ago. Town staff will process the amended plat, set for June 22, 2026. A separate A Street property closing was also noted in November 2025.

crawford/6.title: 2026 municipal election
crawford/6.summary: Three council seats are up for election. Petitions were due January 26, and the town is working with the County Clerk under an intergovernmental agreement.

crawford/7.title: Region 10 partnership and campus master plan
crawford/7.summary: Region 10 pitched regional economic development help, including broadband fiber links, small business consulting and Enterprise Zone credits ($19,000 reinvested locally last year). Council discussed a campus master plan for town-owned property and grants from DOLA and USDA.

crawford/8.title: Unauthorized excavation on K Street and building permit enforcement
crawford/8.summary: The town is pursuing a resolution over unauthorized excavation on town property on K Street. Resident Cameron Clark raised concerns about inconsistent building permit enforcement and was allowed to renew his permit for $50. Council also discussed the need for clearer permit requirements and formal variance procedures.

crawford/9.title: Public access to meeting packets and Town Hall concerns
crawford/9.summary: Resident Marty Durlin reported difficulty accessing agendas online and asked for packets to be public. The clerk will work on providing water rate reports. Fire Auxiliary member Cathy Cheatham raised kitchen cleanliness, grease trap and pest issues at Town Hall.

crested-butte/0.title: Zoning and subdivision code rewrite (Chapter 16) with affordable housing incentives
crested-butte/0.summary: Council and the Board of Zoning and Architectural Review worked through a full rewrite of the town's zoning and subdivision code from Nov 2025 to Aug 2026. The work covered residential and commercial districts, Belleview Avenue and Sixth Street incentives tied to deed-restricted space, and the Resident Occupied Affordable Housing (ROAH) program. A final draft was reviewed June 15, with a proposed effective date of September 1, 2026. Ordinances 12-16, including a new official zoning map, went to first reading Aug 4 and second reading Aug 17.

crested-butte/1.title: Non-primary home excise tax and long-range financial planning
crested-butte/1.summary: Staff described structural budget pressures from heavy reliance on sales tax and asked Council about an excise tax on vacant or underused homes and a resident property tax rebate. Council reviewed revenue options of $1.0M and $1.5M. Draft ballot language was discussed Aug 4, and a resolution calling a November 3, 2026 election was on the Aug 17 agenda along with a 2027 Budget Advisory Committee.

crested-butte/2.title: Affordable housing strategy and town home purchases
crested-butte/2.summary: Council reviewed the town's affordable housing portfolio and adopted a 5-year Housing Strategy, with amended 2026 housing guidelines. The town authorized purchases of homes on Gothic Avenue (816, 818, 810, 806 #5A) and 16 Ninth Street, and moved to sell a unit at 16 Ninth Street. It also handled the Whetstone and Paradise Park housing projects.
crested-butte/2.where: Gothic Avenue, Ninth Street, Whetstone and Paradise Park

crested-butte/3.title: Red Lady Avenue and Sixth Street roundabout
crested-butte/3.summary: The town is designing a roundabout at Highway 135/Sixth Street and Red Lady Avenue, where the intersection runs at level of service E at peak hours. In June the Gunnison Watershed School District asked for a cost-sharing discussion on the project.
crested-butte/3.where: Red Lady Avenue and Sixth Street (Highway 135)

crested-butte/4.title: Gunnison to Mt. Crested Butte Corridor Plan
crested-butte/4.summary: Council worked on its values and priorities for the Gunnison County-led Corridor Plan and Transportation Strategy. It held a listening session with the county on Aug 4 and discussed an MOU with the county.
crested-butte/4.where: Gunnison to Mt. Crested Butte corridor (Highway 135)

crested-butte/5.title: Drought water restrictions and water/sewer penalties
crested-butte/5.summary: In June Council discussed changes to water restrictions to address drought. On July 6 it took up Emergency Ordinance 10, amending the violations and penalties for water and sewer regulations, and it ratified the ordinance July 20.

crested-butte/6.title: Mt. Crested Butte Water and Sanitation District biosolids dispute and loan
crested-butte/6.summary: Council held legal discussions about the district's failure to pay for biosolids, and considered a loan agreement with the district in January.
crested-butte/6.where: Mt. Crested Butte Water and Sanitation District

crested-butte/7.title: Parks, Recreation, Open Space and Trails (PROST) plan
crested-butte/7.summary: Council reviewed the PROST plan in work sessions covering the open space definition, success measures, cost recovery philosophy and a parks decision framework. The plan was scheduled for adoption May 4, 2026.

crested-butte/8.title: Single-use plastics reduction
crested-butte/8.summary: Staff sought feedback on a Plastic Pollution Reduction Act ordinance after a survey in November. Council later discussed single-use plastic policies for special events.

crested-butte/9.title: Trash bin fees and wildfire code
crested-butte/9.summary: Council examined 2026-27 Save-As-You-Throw bin fees to fund sanitation. It also adopted the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code as a new article of the municipal code and reviewed the Wildfire Ready Action Plan update.

crested-butte/10.title: Food trucks, parklets and special event rules
crested-butte/10.summary: Council considered The Hideout's request to use a trailer or food truck, extended a suspension on food trucks, and discussed expanding parklets along Elk Avenue at the request of Sherpa Café. It also amended special event permitting rules.
crested-butte/10.where: Elk Avenue and downtown Crested Butte

dacono/0.title: Emergency moratorium on data centers (Ordinance 1023)
dacono/0.summary: On Aug. 24, 2026 City Council considered Ordinance 1023, an emergency ordinance imposing a temporary moratorium on building permits, special use permits, business licenses and land use applications for any business that includes a data center. The documents do not state the vote.

dacono/1.title: Police Advisory Board complaint investigations and process overhaul (Ordinance 1024)
dacono/1.summary: The Police Advisory Board met in August, September and October to review an investigation into a complaint filed July 28, 2026 and to discuss a proposed ordinance revising its process. Council took up Ordinance 1024, which repeals and reenacts Section 2-75 of the municipal code on the board, on first reading Aug. 24 and set a Sept. 14 public hearing.

dacono/2.title: Northern Lot CNS annexation and zoning
dacono/2.summary: Council found an annexation petition in substantial compliance on Sept. 14. Planning and Zoning reviewed initial zoning on Oct. 13. On Oct. 26 Council considered eligibility (Resolution 26-62) and first reading of Ordinance 1026 (annexation) and Ordinance 1027 (zoning).

dacono/3.title: Water supply planning, efficiency plan and water dedications
dacono/3.summary: Council received a Water Supply Master Plan and Water Efficiency Plan presentation Aug. 24 and held a closed session on the city's water supply and a potential land purchase. It then took up Resolution 26-58 adopting the 2026 Water Efficiency Plan on Oct. 12. On Oct. 26 it considered a water dedication agreement for Strata Filing 2, and council toured the United Water and Sanitation District on Oct. 15.

dacono/4.title: 2027 city budget
dacono/4.summary: Council discussed the 2027 budget on Oct. 7 and on Oct. 12 acknowledged receipt of the draft 2027 budget and set a public hearing. The Urban Renewal Authority also set its own 2027 budget hearing date. A Sept. 26 council retreat listed budget and capital improvement planning as a topic.

dacono/5.title: City Center Park design and urban renewal funding
dacono/5.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority heard a City Center Park presentation from Wenk Associates on Oct. 7 and considered a first amendment to Wenk's design services agreement. It also considered a third amendment to the reimbursement agreement with the city for capital projects, which Council took up Oct. 12.

dacono/6.title: Sales tax credit agreement near Colorado Boulevard (Ordinance 1025)
dacono/6.summary: Council considered Ordinance 1025 on first reading, which would give a sales tax credit for taxable transactions on a property along Colorado Boulevard. It appeared Sept. 28 and again Oct. 26 with an agreement attached.

dacono/7.title: Silver Peaks Warehouse industrial use application
dacono/7.summary: Planning and Zoning held a hearing Oct. 13 on a site plan and industrial use for Silver Peaks Warehouse. On Oct. 27 it considered a resolution recommending denial.

dacono/8.title: Strata Dacono Subdivision Filing No. 3
dacono/8.summary: Planning and Zoning considered the preliminary plat and development plan Aug. 25. Council held a hearing on Resolution 26-51 approving them on Sept. 14.

dacono/9.title: Changes to PUD and subdivision approval process, and impact fees
dacono/9.summary: Council discussed a PUD ordinance Sept. 28, and Planning and Zoning considered Oct. 27 an amendment allowing administrative approval of final documents that conform to approved preliminary plans. Council also held an impact fee discussion Oct. 26.

dacono/10.title: Repeated deadline extensions for Ridge Lands and Sendero subdivisions
dacono/10.summary: Council repeatedly considered extending deadlines for meeting approval conditions: a fourth extension for Ridge Lands Filing No. 1, a third for Ridge Lands Filing 2, and extensions for Sendero Filing Nos. 1A and others.

dacono/11.title: Colorado Blvd and 6th Street roadway improvements; QuikTrip development
dacono/11.summary: Council considered accepting right-of-way and a temporary construction easement at Colorado Boulevard and 6th Street for city roadway improvements. It also considered a subdivision improvement and master development agreement for the QuikTrip #4224 development.

dacono/12.title: Cancellation of the November 3, 2026 election
dacono/12.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-49 canceling the Nov. 3, 2026 election on Sept. 14.

de-beque/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center development
de-beque/0.summary: On the October 27, 2026 agenda, the Council is set to discuss and give direction on a temporary moratorium on data center development within the town. The documents give no details on the outcome.

de-beque/1.title: Pivot Energy solar farm proposed in unincorporated Mesa County
de-beque/1.summary: The Council is continuing to discuss a Pivot Energy solar farm proposed in unincorporated Mesa County that borders the town. It is on the October 27 agenda for further discussion and direction to staff.
de-beque/1.where: Unincorporated Mesa County bordering De Beque

de-beque/2.title: Water, wastewater, irrigation and trash fee schedule
de-beque/2.summary: Resolution 2026-30 would adopt a fee schedule for water, wastewater, irrigation and trash services. It was scheduled for discussion and action on September 22, 2026.

de-beque/3.title: 2027 preliminary budget
de-beque/3.summary: Staff presented the preliminary 2027 town budget on September 22. An updated preliminary budget was submitted on the October 27 agenda.

de-beque/4.title: CDBG grant application for housing abatement and demolition program
de-beque/4.summary: The Board held a public hearing on an application to the state Department of Local Affairs, Division of Housing, for a Community Development Block Grant for a housing abatement and demolition program. Resolution 2026-32 would authorize staff to apply.

de-beque/5.title: Automated license plate readers
de-beque/5.summary: The Council is scheduled to discuss automated license plate readers on October 27. The documents give no details on what is proposed.

de-beque/6.title: Homeward Bound of the Grand Valley funding request
de-beque/6.summary: Marvin Duarte of Homeward Bound of the Grand Valley gave an operational update and made a funding request to the Council on September 22.

de-beque/7.title: Sanitary sewer agreement and dedication
de-beque/7.summary: Resolution 2026-34 would authorize the dedication and acceptance of a sanitary sewer agreement between the town and another party. Resolution 2026-33 would direct staff to enter a contract. Both were on the October 27 agenda.

de-beque/8.title: Animal Assistance Foundation grant and Title 9 code change
de-beque/8.summary: Resolution 2026-31 approves the town's application for a grant from the Animal Assistance Foundation. Ordinance 576 amends Title 9 of the municipal code.

de-beque/9.title: Change to council meeting time
de-beque/9.summary: The Council continued discussion and direction on a new meeting time at both the September and October meetings.

del-norte/0.title: Outdoor Entertainment Overlay District and Ordinance 789
del-norte/0.summary: The town set a public hearing for an Outdoor Entertainment Overlay District that defines district boundaries and amends the Use Chart (Table 16-4A). The hearing was scheduled for Sept. 9, then Ordinance 789 appeared again on the Oct. 14 agenda with another hearing.

del-norte/1.title: Moratorium on Flock Safety cameras
del-norte/1.summary: Council discussed a temporary moratorium on Flock Safety license-plate cameras on Sept. 9. Resolution 13-2026 for a moratorium on Flock cameras was on the Oct. 14 agenda.

del-norte/2.title: Police Department policy manual
del-norte/2.summary: Council discussed adopting Police Department policies and procedures in September. Resolution 12-2026 to adopt the Police Department Manual as a stand-alone policy was on the Oct. 14 agenda.

del-norte/3.title: 2027 town budget
del-norte/3.summary: Council was to accept the proposed 2027 town budget, set a public hearing for Nov. 11, 2026, and schedule a work session.

del-norte/4.title: Lookout Mountain annexation and GOCO grant
del-norte/4.summary: Gary Blakley addressed council on annexing the Lookout Mountain property and on GOCO grant funding.

del-norte/5.title: Water fund allocation for South Water Well and water plant property
del-norte/5.summary: Council was to consider allocating water fund balance to approve the South Water Well expense. Aaron Woodke also raised the town's Water Treatment Plant property on County Road 14.

del-norte/6.title: Master Print web and print contract
del-norte/6.summary: Council weighed signing a contract with Master Print with specific monthly price and deliverable expectations, or starting an RFP to find another firm.

del-norte/7.title: Nuisance violations and civil abatement process
del-norte/7.summary: Council discussed how the town handles nuisance violations and civil abatement.

del-norte/8.title: Council rules of order and virtual meeting policy
del-norte/8.summary: Council considered amending regular meeting provisions in the Town Code, the rules of order (Resolution 11-2026), and the virtual meeting procedures policy (Resolution 9-2026).

del-norte/9.title: Rio Grande County comprehensive plan meetings
del-norte/9.summary: The town and Rio Grande County planned an open house on Oct. 27 and a town board stakeholder meeting on Nov. 4 on the county comprehensive plan.

del-norte/10.title: River Park changing stall request
del-norte/10.summary: Patti Kelly of D Mountain Recreation presented to council about a changing stall at River Park.

delta-county/0.title: Clear Water Enterprises rezone (PLN26-022) for 378.5 acres of homes
delta-county/0.summary: Peter Edwards/Clear Water Enterprises asked to rezone about 378.5 acres from A-35 to RES-1 for residential lots that would be served by Golden Eagle Water Company taps. The Planning Commission heard it Aug 12, and the commissioners held a public hearing Sept 15. A water attorney's opinion in the packet says the water rights and augmentation plan are adequate.

delta-county/1.title: Land Use Code amendments: battery storage, natural medicine and general cleanup
delta-county/1.summary: The county held public hearings on Land Use Code changes, including rules for battery energy storage systems (BESS) and natural medicine businesses. Adopting them would repeal earlier moratorium resolutions. Public comments covered temporary special events, intensive agricultural setbacks and site plan review. The Planning Commission reviewed the amendments and the commissioners moved to submit them on Oct 6.

delta-county/2.title: Concentrated animal feeding operation (CAFO) regulations working group
delta-county/2.summary: On Sept 15 the commissioners considered forming a working group to review and draft changes to county land use rules for CAFOs.

delta-county/3.title: Proposed 2027 county budget
delta-county/3.summary: The commissioners received a presentation of the proposed 2027 Delta County budget at a special meeting on Oct 13. The Assessor also presented the 2026 property assessment study, and the county is updating mileage and per diem rates starting Jan 1, 2027, which had not risen since 2008.

delta-county/4.title: Fire Mountain speed limit change and road right-of-way dedications
delta-county/4.summary: The commissioners considered a speed analysis and a resolution to change the speed limit on Fire Mountain. They also took dedications of road right-of-way for Fire Mountain Road (2.03 acres), Barrow Mesa Road, H Road and Surface Creek Road, and discussed a School Bus Ahead sign on G Road west of the railroad tracks.
delta-county/4.where: Fire Mountain Road, G Road, Barrow Mesa Road

delta-county/5.title: Hotchkiss skate park request
delta-county/5.summary: Hotchkiss resident Tanner Wilson asked the commissioners to consider a skate park in Hotchkiss, possibly at the fairgrounds, and offered to fundraise. He said families currently have to drive to other towns.

delta-county/6.title: Comment letter on the 2001 Roadless Rule and Forest Service road agreement
delta-county/6.summary: The commissioners discussed a county comment letter on the 2001 Roadless Rule on Sept 15. On Oct 6 they discussed a road agreement with the U.S. Forest Service.

delta-county/7.title: Property tax appeals and Board of Equalization
delta-county/7.summary: Acting as the Board of Equalization, the commissioners heard 2026 valuation appeals, including Lannie Yeager's property at Fruitland Mesa Road in Crawford (the value was retained at $449,341) and a stipulation for Meadow Brook Boulevard LLC. They also reviewed senior exemption applications.

delta-county/8.title: Portable chemical toilets policy and septic variance
delta-county/8.summary: The Board of Health planned to discuss a public health policy on portable chemical toilets and a variance request for an on-site wastewater treatment system.

delta-county/9.title: Resolution supporting Amendment 83
delta-county/9.summary: The commissioners considered a resolution in support of Amendment 83, a proposed constitutional right on the 2026 ballot.

delta/0.title: Massano rezone (Ordinance #7, 2026)
delta/0.summary: Council took up Ordinance #7, 2026, a rezone for the Massano property, on second and final reading on Aug. 4. The agenda provided for staff and applicant presentations and public comment. The documents do not state the outcome.

delta/1.title: Unified Development Code (Ordinance #9, 2026)
delta/1.summary: Ordinance #9, 2026, which covers the Unified Development Code, came to Council on first reading on Aug. 4. It returned as a discussion item on Oct. 6.

delta/2.title: Homelessness grant and Unhoused Task Force
delta/2.summary: Council considered Resolution #15, 2026 for a homelessness resolution program grant on Aug. 4. On Sept. 15 it appointed Carrie Boyd to the Unhoused Task Force, which met on Oct. 7 at the Police Department with public comment on its agenda.

delta/3.title: Housing role, 7th Street property and Proposition 123
delta/3.summary: Council discussed the city's role in housing and the 7th Street property with Proposition 123 grant funding on Aug. 4. It scheduled Resolution #20, 2026 on Proposition 123 for Oct. 20, with public comment.

delta/4.title: Data centers discussion
delta/4.summary: Council set aside time on Aug. 4 to discuss data centers. No packet materials were provided.

delta/5.title: 2027 budget, TABOR projections and capital plan
delta/5.summary: Council reviewed historical budget trends in August, a 2026 financial update in September, TABOR projections and the 5-year Capital Improvement Plan on Sept. 29. It held 2027 budget discussions on Oct. 6, 13 and 20.

delta/6.title: South Main Street gateway traffic and Main Street discussion
delta/6.summary: Council scheduled a South Main Street Gateway traffic conversation for Sept. 15 and Sept. 22, and a Main Street discussion on Oct. 13.

delta/7.title: Litter and junk code amendments (Ordinance #8)
delta/7.summary: Council considered Ordinance #8, 2026, amending litter and junk codes, on second reading on Aug. 4.

delta/8.title: Water and wastewater projects
delta/8.summary: On Oct. 6 Council was to accept construction of the wastewater treatment facility digester improvements. It was also to consider awarding the North Delta Waterline Project contract.

delta/9.title: Subdivision approvals: Stone Mountain, Quintana and O'Connor
delta/9.summary: Council considered the Stone Mountain Filing No. 10 final plat on Sept. 15, the Quintana Minor Subdivision on Oct. 6, and an O'Connor Subdivision extension request on Aug. 18.

delta/10.title: Comprehensive planning DOLA grant
delta/10.summary: Council took up a DOLA grant for comprehensive plan elements on Oct. 20.

denver/0.title: Mayor's proposed 2027 budget and council amendments
denver/0.summary: Council held the public hearing on the Mayor's Proposed 2027 Budget on Oct. 19 and set a Nov. 2 agenda with many amendments from members Lewis, Gonzales-Gutierrez, Watson, Alvidrez, Kashmann, Romero Campbell and Torres. Budget committees also reviewed the Finance budget book and sales tax initiative changes.

sources.body: Operations Meeting of the City Council

denver/1.title: Data center moratorium update
denver/1.summary: The Community Planning and Housing Committee heard an update on Denver's data center moratorium on Aug. 18. The documents give no details on what was reported.

denver/2.title: Failed votes on Citibot, Slalom and city video contracts
denver/2.summary: Council defeated resolutions adding $3.89 million to the Citibot contract and $5 million to the Slalom contract on Oct. 13. An earlier $600,000 addition to the Sunny Side Up Solutions video contract (26-1116) also failed on Aug. 10, and a later $250,000 amendment passed.

denver/3.title: Homelessness shelter and rapid rehousing contracts
denver/3.summary: Council approved a stream of contracts for rapid resolution and rapid rehousing (St. Francis Center, Salvation Army, Volunteers of America, Delores Project, Colorado Coalition for the Homeless). It also approved Colorado Village Collaborative licenses for pallet and micro-community shelters, including at 3815 N Steele St, and changed the scope of emergency shelter funding at the Sand & Sage/Westerner Motel on East Colfax.
denver/3.where: Citywide; 3815 N Steele St; East Colfax

denver/4.title: Rezonings and landmark designation
denver/4.summary: Council committees advanced several map amendments, including 3418 W. 14th Ave and 1371 N Julian St (G-RH-3 to G-MU-5), 3343-3351 N Mariposa St, and a 76 N Hazel Ct rezoning that had a public hearing. A landmark designation for 740 N. Washington St also advanced.
denver/4.where: West Colfax; N Mariposa St; 740 N Washington St; N Hazel Ct

denver/5.title: Affordable housing agreements and strategic plan
denver/5.summary: Council approved Denver Housing Authority agreement changes, loans for income-restricted housing (1371 Xenia, 1600 Pearl, a 118-unit project), Loretto Heights row homes, and a one-year 2027 continuation of the Housing Stability strategic plan.

denver/6.title: Denver Health sales tax spending
denver/6.summary: Council moved a contract amendment with Denver Health to implement the .34% sales tax passed in 2024 and heard a spending update. Related contracts also advanced.

denver/7.title: Rules against spending tax revenue on alcohol
denver/7.summary: Ordinances were filed to bar Caring for Denver, Denver Preschool Program and college affordability tax revenues from paying for alcohol and other administrative costs, including staff wellness programs.

denver/8.title: Broadway Station stadium site and pedestrian bridge
denver/8.summary: Council advanced an amended 2025 IGA for the stadium site project with Broadway Station Metropolitan District No. 1 and a state grant for the Broadway Station Pedestrian Bridge linking RTD to the NWSL stadium and Santa Fe Yards.

denver/9.title: Minority and small business contracting ordinance overhaul
denver/9.summary: Bill 26-1216 revises Chapter 28 to advance equitable access to public contracting for minority-, women-owned and small businesses. It passed final consideration Sept. 21.

denver/10.title: Downtown Development Authority boundaries and project funding
denver/10.summary: Council amended Denver Downtown Development Authority boundaries several times and took up funding agreements for the Midland Condominiums (444 17th St), University Building (900-918 16th St) and 101 W. Colfax, including a lease of 64,654 sq ft there.

denver/11.title: Airline lease agreements at Denver International Airport
denver/11.summary: Council approved use and lease agreements with Air Canada, Air France, Alaska, Lufthansa, WestJet and others, plus large contracts such as $135 million for North Terminal expansion project management.

denver/12.title: Automated vehicle identification and ShotSpotter changes
denver/12.summary: Council filed an amendment to the ordinance covering the Automated Vehicle Identification System and cut ShotSpotter contract capacity by $147,421. Council also considered a proclamation opposing Colorado Amendment 81.

denver/13.title: Civic Center Park and Welton Street projects
denver/13.summary: Council added $1.63 million to Studio Gang's Civic Center Park Next 100 contract, approved a $3 million design contract for a cultural plaza and shade structure at 2401 Welton, and heard a Welton Street study.

dolores/0.title: Broc's Development PUD and rezoning of 206 and 207 South Third Street
dolores/0.summary: Neighbors raised concerns about density, three-story buildings, parking, roads, lighting and infrastructure at the KKV/Broc Smith project on South Third Street. The Board approved the PUD concept plan on May 11, held hearings on Ordinance 592 rezoning the parcels from Downtown Mixed Use in August, and approved it on second reading on Sept. 14. Residents also raised spot-zoning and traffic study concerns.

dolores/1.title: 2026 fee schedule, business license fees and Ordinance 591
dolores/1.summary: The Board reworked town fees, including the business license, short-term rental permits, parks and building fees. Ordinance 591 gives authority to set fees by resolution and sets renewal, late fee and enforcement procedures; it passed on second reading Aug. 10. On July 27 the Board set the business license fee at $30 with a $50 late fee, and a business owner later objected to a late fee she was charged.

dolores/2.title: Phase 2 water project and main line replacement funding
dolores/2.summary: The town is funding water main replacement and the Phase 2 water project through a DOLA award of about $700,000 and Drinking Water Revolving Fund loan agreements (Resolutions 700 and 719). Phase II construction is expected to start in spring 2027.

dolores/3.title: Comprehensive Plan update
dolores/3.summary: The town is updating its comprehensive plan with a consultant, biweekly team meetings and community questionnaires. Public outreach events ended July 10, comments closed July 31, and a draft plan is expected in October.

dolores/4.title: Sheriff's Office contract
dolores/4.summary: The Board held workshops on the town's law-enforcement contract with the Sheriff's Office, discussing metrics to evaluate the value and level of service. Sheriff Steve Nowlin reported to the Board in May, and a draft contract was reviewed Aug. 24.

dolores/5.title: 2027 budget and Community Center funding
dolores/5.summary: Staff began 2027 budget planning in August and presented a preliminary budget Oct. 12, with a public hearing to follow. The Community Center Advisory Board asked for funding direction, and residents urged prioritizing unfinished park projects.

dolores/6.title: Public comment rules and public records policy
dolores/6.summary: After personal attacks on staff during public comment, the Board discussed limits, signage and adding a comment period before workshops. A resident argued the Board cannot limit comment under the First Amendment. A public records request policy and form were also reviewed.

dolores/7.title: Town Attorney resignation and new legal services
dolores/7.summary: Town Attorney Ethan Sumrall announced his resignation, and the Board accepted it by Resolution 723 on Oct. 12. It approved a legal services agreement with Holligan Westendorff, PLLC. In July the Board also agreed to hire a water law attorney for town water rights.

dolores/8.title: Adoption of 2024 International Codes and wildfire code
dolores/8.summary: Ordinance 594 adopting the 2024 International Codes passed first reading Oct. 12. A resident thanked the Board for not adopting the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. Fire hazard mitigation, such as tree cutting along the escarpment, continues.

dolores/9.title: Dog licensing ordinance 589
dolores/9.summary: The Board rewrote dog licensing rules to be more enforceable. Ordinance 589 passed first reading March 9, with a second reading hearing held April 13.

dolores/10.title: Hemp and THC beverage policy and marijuana tax changes
dolores/10.summary: The Board considered Resolution 698 on a hemp-derived and THC beverage policy in April. In September the attorney discussed HB 26-1409 and its effect on marijuana tax distributions.

dolores/11.title: Housing grant pass-through and housing needs assessment
dolores/11.summary: Resolution 714 makes the town the pass-through agent for a housing project funded by federal and state grants. In October the Board discussed the SB24-174 Housing Needs Assessment from Region 9 EDD.

douglas-county/0.title: Ballot measure to expand the Board of County Commissioners from 3 to 5
douglas-county/0.summary: In late August the commissioners fixed the ballot title for a measure expanding the BOCC from 3 to 5 members and approved an amended resolution referring it to voters on Aug 31 after a continuance. A ballot title protest administrative hearing was scheduled for Sept 3 and 4. Dozens of residents spoke on Aug 31.

douglas-county/1.title: Flexential tax incentive agreement
douglas-county/1.summary: The commissioners approved a Business Personal Property Tax Incentive Agreement between Douglas County and Flexential Corp (ED2025-002) on Aug 11 after pulling it from the consent agenda. Several residents from Parker, Highlands Ranch and Castle Rock spoke on it. The documents do not describe the facility.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Business Meeting

douglas-county/2.title: Private activity bonds for Ponderosa Pines and another project
douglas-county/2.summary: A $50 million private activity bond authorizing resolution for Ponderosa Pines was continued on Aug 11 to a later business meeting. A $37 million private activity bond resolution appeared on the Sept 22 agenda.

Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/3.title: Zoning changes: nonfunctional turf and non-owned animal training
douglas-county/3.summary: The county is drafting zoning amendments to regulate nonfunctional turf and artificial turf (DR2026-001) and animal training lessons and exercising sessions for non-owned animals (DR2026-004). Planning Commission work session and hearings were in September, with BOCC hearings set for Oct 27.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/4.title: New metro districts: Bloom, Castle Pines North, Roxborough Village
douglas-county/4.summary: The commissioners approved a new service plan for Bloom Metropolitan District on Aug 4. The Planning Commission is set to review the Castle Pines North Metropolitan District service plan on Oct 5 and a Roxborough Village Metropolitan District service plan amendment on Nov 2.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/5.title: Special use permits at 6685 S. Highway 83 and 2485 S. Russellville Road
douglas-county/5.summary: Two Use by Special Review applications went to the Planning Commission in October and to the commissioners on Oct 27. They cover 6685 South Highway 83 (US2023-011) and 2485 South Russellville Road (US2025-010).
douglas-county/5.where: 6685 S. Highway 83 and 2485 S. Russellville Road

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/6.title: Trinity Substation and Peaking Facility location review
douglas-county/6.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled on Aug 17 to review the location and extent of the Trinity Substation and Peaking Facility (LE2026-009). It was on the agenda alongside a Highlands Ranch Filing 159 review.

douglas-county/7.title: Road projects and transportation planning
douglas-county/7.summary: The county approved easements and contracts for the Highlands Ranch Parkway reconstruction, Pine Drive and Pine Lane improvements, and the Dakan Road bridge replacement. It also funded a University Blvd and Post Office traffic signal, a Waterton Road design contract of $2.15 million, and a $279,320 Transportation Safety Action Plan. The commissioners vacated Pine View Circle on Aug 25.

douglas-county/8.title: Rueter-Hess reservoir recreation and budget
douglas-county/8.summary: The Rueter-Hess Advisory Board considered recreation requests for sailing and e-foil use, budget updates, a budget reallocation and Incline Trailhead improvements.

douglas-county/9.title: Parks funding and grants: Gold Crown, Wildcat Regional Park, Mark Weston memorial
douglas-county/9.summary: The commissioners approved a parks funding agreement with the Gold Crown Foundation and up to $30,000 in open space funds to name a Mark Weston Open Space Memorial. A Great Outdoors Colorado grant request for Wildcat Regional Park was on the Sept 22 agenda.

Board of County Commissioners Business Meeting

douglas-county/10.title: Homelessness and human services grants
douglas-county/10.summary: The county applied for a $125,000 Homelessness Resolution Program grant, including a $62,500 match. It also handled older adult services grants and a Homeless Initiative meeting.

Board of County Commissioners Business Meeting

dove-creek/0.title: Sewer usage fee ordinance replacing Section 24-85
dove-creek/0.summary: On Oct. 27 the council scheduled a public hearing and first reading of an ordinance replacing Section 24-85 of the Dove Creek Code of Ordinances on sewer usage fees. Residents could comment for or against. The same agenda lists a Sinclair sewer item.

dove-creek/1.title: Town Manager hiring and contract
dove-creek/1.summary: In August the council reviewed applications for town manager, then on Aug. 25 held an executive session on the manager's contract and offer, with possible action afterward.

dove-creek/2.title: Town Clerk/Treasurer recruitment and contract
dove-creek/2.summary: The council took up a contract for the treasurer on Sept. 29, reviewed Town Clerk/Treasurer applications on Oct. 13, and planned discussion and possible action on the selection on Oct. 27.

dove-creek/3.title: Town Attorney legal services RFP
dove-creek/3.summary: The council is reviewing responses to a request for proposals for town attorney legal services and planned to schedule interviews with candidates.

dove-creek/4.title: Foundational ordinance draft and proposed ordinance changes
dove-creek/4.summary: On Sept. 22 the board was to review a foundational ordinance draft and approve its public release. In October the council held an ordinance overview, presentations, discussion and proposed changes.

dove-creek/5.title: Preliminary budget, capital plan and DOLA meter grant
dove-creek/5.summary: The council began with a preliminary budget on Oct. 13. The Oct. 27 agenda lists a DOLA meter grant and a capital improvement plan.

dove-creek/6.title: Enforcement order project update and trench box purchase
dove-creek/6.summary: The council received a project update on an enforcement order on Aug. 25 and on Sept. 22 considered buying a trench box for worker safety.

durango/0.title: Fire protection district inclusion on April 2027 ballot
durango/0.summary: Council is considering a resolution directing the City Manager to start the steps to include the City of Durango in the Durango Fire Protection District on the April 2027 election ballot.

durango/1.title: Land Use Code changes responding to 2025 Housing Needs Assessment
durango/1.summary: Council is introducing an ordinance amending the Land Use and Development Code in response to the 2025 Housing Needs Assessment and 2026 state requirements. The Community Development Commission also gave a quarterly report on housing and economic development.

durango/2.title: 2027 proposed budget and lodgers' tax changes
durango/2.summary: Council is requesting a public hearing on the City Manager's 2027 proposed budget. It is also giving final reading to an ordinance amending the lodgers' tax in the city code. The Financial Advisory Board is touring public works sites, including water plants and a street project.

durango/3.title: Noise rules in the Land Use and Development Code
durango/3.summary: The Community Development Commission is holding a public hearing on text amendments to the Land Use and Development Code regarding noise (PR-26-68), after a study session on October 22.

durango/4.title: City Hall/Police Station site plan early design guidance
durango/4.summary: The Community Development Commission is reviewing early design guidance for the major site plan for a new City Hall and Police Station (PR-26-52).

durango/5.title: Neighborhood parking permit options
durango/5.summary: Council is considering a resolution giving staff direction on neighborhood parking permit options.

durango/6.title: Old Hire firefighter and police pension cost-of-living adjustment
durango/6.summary: A resolution would direct the City Manager to start an annual cost-of-living adjustment equal to the prior year's national inflation rate for the Old Hire Firefighter and Police pension.

durango/7.title: Organic waste management feasibility analysis
durango/7.summary: Council is considering a resolution directing the City Manager to analyze the feasibility of organic waste management ordinance and policy options, submitted by Sustainability.

durango/8.title: Camino Crossing underpass presentation
durango/8.summary: The Community Development Commission is hearing a presentation on the Camino Crossing underpass from Lily Oswald.

durango/9.title: Section 106 permitting reform and historic preservation code changes
durango/9.summary: The Historic Preservation Board is discussing Section 106 permitting reform and an ordinance amending the Land Use Code chapter on lots, buildings and structures.

durango/10.title: Drone delivery discussion
durango/10.summary: The Community Development Commission chair proposed a discussion of drone deliveries.

eagle/0.title: Proposed pickleball courts at Town Park
eagle/0.summary: Neighbors near Town Park, including residents 68 feet from the proposed courts, oppose the pickleball courts over noise, cost and loss of park space. The Town held an August 25 open house and online survey, and residents kept raising it at the September 22 meeting.

eagle/1.title: 2026 supplemental and 2027 town budget
eagle/1.summary: Council reviewed the 2026 supplemental budget and the 2027 draft, which shows a General Fund operating surplus of $466,340 before transfers and includes $350,000 in assumed vacancy savings. Work sessions covered capital priorities and grant funding, and a public hearing was set for October 27.

eagle/2.title: Eagle River Park funding and engineering
eagle/2.summary: The Eagle River Park Coalition asked Council to include maintenance and development funding for the river park in the 2027 budget, including an engineering project to improve safety. Residents also asked Council to work with the Coalition rather than a third-party contractor, and Council planned a site visit at 200 Fairgrounds Rd.

eagle/3.title: Eagle Bike Park 2027 maintenance funding
eagle/3.summary: Staff asked Council to set the Town's 2027 contribution to Bike Park maintenance. The Town approved $44,500 for 2026 and moved the funding to the Sales Tax Capital Improvement Fund, while the Vail Valley Mountain Trails Alliance operates the park under a 2023 license and has submitted a 2027 maintenance budget.

eagle/4.title: Variance and appeal/call-up rules in the Land Use Code
eagle/4.summary: Council passed amended Ordinance 13 overhauling variance rules in Title 4, chapters 17 and 20, after deleting a provision that would have prohibited call-ups of decisions. Council directed staff to draft appeal and referral language, and the Planning & Zoning Commission was set to consider the appeal, referral and call-up amendments on October 20.

eagle/5.title: Mixed-use building step-back standards (LUDC26-04)
eagle/5.summary: Planning & Zoning reviewed proposed changes to Section 4.10.050 on mixed-use and commercial design, including step-back requirements for taller buildings. It was on the September 1 agenda and was presented on October 20.

eagle/6.title: West and East Eagle sub-area plan updates
eagle/6.summary: Staff asked Council and Planning & Zoning whether to update the 2011 West Eagle Sub Area Plan and the 2021 East Eagle Sub Area Plan, looking at density, connectivity, traffic and housing. Staff noted Eagle County is not currently pursuing its earlier land use application in the West Eagle area.

eagle/7.title: Red Mountain Ranch Metropolitan District service plan
eagle/7.summary: Council held a public hearing on Resolution 52 approving the consolidated service plan for Red Mountain Ranch Metropolitan Districts 1 and 2. Discussion covered financial risks and utility ownership and maintenance responsibilities.

eagle/8.title: Downtown Development Authority: inclusions, boundary and 2027 budget
eagle/8.summary: The DDA approved Resolution 05 to include 212 E. Third Street and discussed reaching out to owners of 214 Capitol Street and the Big Bear building. It also reviewed its 2027 draft budget, including a commercial activation rebate program, and Council scheduled Ordinance 16 to add a vacated alley in Block 13 to the DDA boundary.

eagle/9.title: Town purchase of 215 Capitol Street and St. Mary's Church
eagle/9.summary: Council took up Ordinance 14 authorizing a real estate purchase at 215 Capitol Street, and the Mayor recused himself. The Economic Vitality Committee heard the Town is under contract to buy St. Mary's Church, which can keep operating until January 2028, and an executive session on property negotiations was scheduled October 27.
eagle/9.where: 215 Capitol Street and St. Mary's Church

eagle/10.title: Right-of-way parking rules and enforcement
eagle/10.summary: Council asked about parking in the public right-of-way. Police reported the Town Code does not specifically prohibit parking there, though vehicles left 24 hours or more can be treated as abandoned and the Model Traffic Code bans parking near driveways, hydrants and crosswalks.

eagle/11.title: Haymaker Trailhead restroom and open space capital plan
eagle/11.summary: The Open Space committee reviewed the Haymaker Trailhead restroom, whose cost grew from $90,000 to about $160,000 against a single bid of about $380,000, and discussed a relocatable vault toilet as an interim option. It also backed the Open Space Fund operating budget and took up the 5-year capital plan.

eagle/12.title: Council support for school district Ballot Issue SB
eagle/12.summary: Council passed Resolution 61 supporting Eagle County School District Ballot Issue SB on the November 3, 2026 ballot, after a motion to deny failed. Several residents and teachers urged support, citing school budget cuts, and Council agreed to work out how to handle future ballot-issue requests.

eagle/13.title: Merging the Economic Vitality and Marketing & Events committees
eagle/13.summary: The Economic Vitality Committee and the Marketing and Events Advisory Committee discussed merging, with a joint pilot project on event marketing and business engagement. The committees also looked at Eagle Airport traffic during the Aspen Airport closure and at permitting reform.

edgewater/0.title: Zoning Code Update and rewrite (RLI, RMLI, RMHI districts)
edgewater/0.summary: The city is rewriting its zoning code with a Technical Focus Group. The group's June 8, 2026 meeting reviewed proposed residential districts (RLI, RMLI, RMHI), rear-lot intensification, building heights and floor area limits, balancing more housing against Edgewater's cottage-scale character. The code update is also tied to HB24 state housing requirements and the Edgewater 2040 Comprehensive Plan.

edgewater/1.title: Transit-Oriented Communities housing study (HB 24-1313)
edgewater/1.summary: Consultant Matrix Design Group is running a Transit-Oriented Communities planning project and presented existing conditions, housing market and economic feasibility findings to Planning and Zoning on Aug. 12, 2026. The work is meant to shape Edgewater's response to HB 24-1313 housing capacity requirements and to guide housing, land use and transportation strategies.

edgewater/2.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing fast-track review policy
edgewater/2.summary: Staff proposed a resolution adopting an expedited review policy for qualifying affordable housing, with a 90-day review period. Adopting it by June 30, 2026 makes Edgewater eligible for about $45,000 in state incentive funding, which staff would use for affordable housing tools in the zoning code update.

edgewater/3.title: Sheridan Boulevard safety improvements with CDOT
edgewater/3.summary: Planning and Zoning was briefed on the updated Sheridan Corridor Multimodal Plan, coordinated with CDOT, for Sheridan Boulevard between 17th and 26th Avenues, a high-injury corridor. The design adds ADA improvements and signal timing changes, and construction is expected to begin in late 2026.

edgewater/4.title: 2026 budget, tax levy and audit findings
edgewater/4.summary: Council reviewed department budget presentations, set the 2025 tax levy, and scheduled adoption of the annual budget in December. The City Manager called next year's budget very tight. The 2024 audit presentation prompted talk of water, sewer and trash losses, segregation of duties and rate increases.

edgewater/5.title: Local minimum wage ordinance 2025-23
edgewater/5.summary: Council took up an ordinance amending the local minimum wage and tip provisions of the municipal code, effective January 1. First reading was Nov. 25, 2025 and second reading was scheduled Dec. 16.

edgewater/6.title: Right-of-way funding sales tax ballot measure
edgewater/6.summary: A sales tax ballot measure for right-of-way funding was presented to city boards, including the HARP board and the Board of Adjustment, in August and September 2026.

edgewater/7.title: Rezonings at 2525 Harlan St. and 2403 Fenton St.
edgewater/7.summary: Planning and Zoning held public hearings and recommended approval to City Council of a rezoning of 2525 Harlan Street to Residential 2, and of 2403 Fenton Street from R-1 and R-3.

edgewater/8.title: Accessory dwelling unit ordinance and home rule dispute
edgewater/8.summary: Planning and Zoning recommended an ordinance amending Chapter 16 on accessory dwelling units, driven by state legislation. Resident Larry Welshon objected, citing home rule authority. Council tabled Resolution 2025-14 affirming home rule authority.

edgewater/9.title: Foothills Animal Shelter intergovernmental agreement
edgewater/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-02 approving an amended intergovernmental agreement with Jefferson County, Arvada and others on animal sheltering, licensing and funding for the Foothills Animal Shelter.

edgewater/10.title: Accessory structure height variance
edgewater/10.summary: The Board of Adjustment heard a variance request for a 20'2" accessory structure, over the 15-foot limit. It also approved a variance allowing rear-lot parking access closer than five feet to the side lot line.

el-paso-county/0.title: 2027 county budget hearings
el-paso-county/0.summary: The Board of County Commissioners held Budget Hearing #1 on Sept. 29 for the preliminary balanced 2027 budget and Hearing #3 on Oct. 27 for department and office critical needs presentations. The Regional Building Department's 2027 budget was also taken up Oct. 13.

el-paso-county/1.title: Triple H Ranch preliminary plan and other land use plats
el-paso-county/1.summary: The commissioners were set to consider a 752.68-acre Triple H Ranch Preliminary Plan from P760 Land, LLC creating 244 single-family lots in the RR-2.5 zone. They also had a Final Plat for Hardy Road Properties, a 19.34-acre site that would create two lots, and set a Nov. 17 hearing on the Bent Grass Commercial Metropolitan District Service Plan.
el-paso-county/1.where: Triple H Ranch site; 1054 Hardy Road area; Bent Grass Commercial district

el-paso-county/2.title: Road and bridge projects: Mesa Ridge Parkway condemnation, US-24 and Commerce Road
el-paso-county/2.summary: The county considered condemning property for the Mesa Ridge Parkway Improvements Project between Powers Blvd and Marksheffel Rd. It also took up an agreement with CDOT on maintenance after the US-24 & Judge Orr Road intersection work and easements for the Commerce Road Bridge Replacement. Design work on North Calhan Highway and a multi-year paving contract of up to $948,543 also came up.
el-paso-county/2.where: Mesa Ridge Parkway; US-24 & Judge Orr Road; Commerce Road; North Calhan Highway

el-paso-county/3.title: New county courthouse construction contract
el-paso-county/3.summary: The commissioners considered a trade contractor agreement with Adolfson and Peterson Construction for the courthouse construction project at up to $3,633,791.

el-paso-county/4.title: Sugarbowl Urban Renewal tax increment agreement
el-paso-county/4.summary: The board considered a Tax Increment Revenue Agreement with the Colorado Springs Urban Renewal Authority for the Sugarbowl Urban Renewal Plan.
el-paso-county/4.where: Sugarbowl Urban Renewal area, Colorado Springs

el-paso-county/5.title: Weed, rubbish and unsafe structure ordinances
el-paso-county/5.summary: First readings of Ordinances 26-02, 26-03 and 26-04 update enforcement procedures and legal remedies for weed and brush removal, rubbish accumulation and unsafe structures. The changes comply with Colorado House Bill 26-1239.

el-paso-county/6.title: Sheriff's Office grants and safety funding
el-paso-county/6.summary: The commissioners considered accepting a $500,000 federal Byrne grant and a $299,021 impaired driving enforcement grant for the Sheriff's Office. A $213,137 dishwasher for the detention facility was also on the agenda.

el-paso-county/7.title: Paint Mines Interpretive Park grant
el-paso-county/7.summary: The county considered a $200,000 grant contract from Lyda Hill Philanthropies for Paint Mines Interpretive Park.

el-paso-county/8.title: Resolution on November 2026 ballot initiatives
el-paso-county/8.summary: The board considered a resolution supporting or opposing various statewide ballot initiatives on the November 2026 General Election ballot.

elizabeth/0.title: Gold Creek Commons Sketch Plan (Resolution 26R28)
elizabeth/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on Sept. 15 on the Gold Creek Commons Sketch Plan and considered recommending approval of Resolution 26R28. The Board of Trustees took up a public hearing and possible action on the same resolution on Oct. 13.

elizabeth/1.title: 2027 Town Budget and budget workshops
elizabeth/1.summary: The Board of Trustees reviewed the 2027 draft budget on Oct. 13. It also held budget workshops on Sept. 26 and Oct. 17, and discussed 2027 budget modifications on Oct. 27.

elizabeth/2.title: Accessory building size and permit rules (Ordinances 26-11 and 26-12)
elizabeth/2.summary: The Planning Commission considered Ordinances 26-11 and 26-12, which amend town code on the size of accessory buildings and permit requirements.

elizabeth/3.title: Extending town water restrictions
elizabeth/3.summary: On Oct. 13 the Board of Trustees was to discuss and possibly act on extending the town's water restrictions. Public Works presented the item.

elizabeth/4.title: E86 Annexation Agreement (Resolution 26R29)
elizabeth/4.summary: The Board of Trustees had the E86 Annexation Agreement, Resolution 26R29, on its Oct. 13 agenda.

elizabeth/5.title: Housing Planning Grant for Comprehensive Plan elements
elizabeth/5.summary: The Board of Trustees was to consider Resolution 26R32 on Oct. 27, a grant agreement with the Colorado Department of Local Affairs for a Housing Planning Grant (HPLN-H26084). The grant would fund the Elizabeth Comprehensive Plan Elements Project.

elizabeth/6.title: Main Street Station site plan agreement amendment
elizabeth/6.summary: On Oct. 27 the Board of Trustees considered Resolution 26R31, a first amendment to the site plan agreement with Main Street Station Elizabeth, LLC. The amendment extends the agreement.

elizabeth/7.title: Town fire regulations and metropolitan district discussion
elizabeth/7.summary: At its Oct. 27 workshop the Board discussed town fire regulations with Chief TJ Steck and Chief Jeff Engel. It also held a metropolitan district discussion led by Corey Hoffmann.

elizabeth/8.title: Town infrastructure contracts: Hillside Village paving and Depot restrooms
elizabeth/8.summary: On Oct. 27 the Board was to discuss a change of scope on the Hillside Village paving project. It was also to consider Resolutions 26R33 and 26R34 amending trade contractor agreements, including one with NexCivil Engineering and Construction, and to discuss the Depot parking lot restrooms.
elizabeth/8.where: Hillside Village and the Depot parking lot

elizabeth/9.title: Main Street events and Friday Night Markets
elizabeth/9.summary: The Main Street Board of Directors planned to discuss recent events on Main Street and a possible communication plan on Sept. 14. The Board of Trustees heard a 2026 Friday Night Markets recap from Elizabeth Brewing Company on Oct. 13.

erie/0.title: Town mineral rights, SM Energy Draco pad and lease offer
erie/0.summary: Council approved Ordinance 26-028 on June 23 to sell Town-owned minerals to SM Energy. SM Energy terminated the contract on Aug. 19 and Council repealed the ordinance on Aug. 25. On Sept. 1 staff sought direction on leasing the minerals (an offer of $12,000 per net mineral acre, about $1.36M) and on the state ECMC process for the Draco drilling and spacing unit.

erie/1.title: 2027 Town budget and work plan
erie/1.summary: Council held budget study sessions on Aug. 18 and Oct. 6 on forecast assumptions. Sales tax growth is below 2% and use tax and building permits are down over 40%, so staff are minimizing new positions. The first reading of the 2027 proposed budget was set for Oct. 27. Advisory boards, including Sustainability (reduced to $9,928) and Tree (reduced to $4,750), are working with trimmed budgets.

erie/2.title: Trees removed for new water meters
erie/2.summary: Several residents, including Bradley Beck, Chad Schroeder, Brian Plymell and Christine Welker, spoke to Council on Sept. 8 about the Town digging up trees to install new water meters. Council also approved temporary water meter standards on Sept. 22.

erie/3.title: Oil and gas regulations update (Title 10, Chapter 12)
erie/3.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed proposed changes to the Town's oil and gas rules. These include doubling inspection fees, per-well fees, notification periods, legacy wells, noise, and air quality. A resident spoke on the fee proposals.

erie/4.title: Page property rezoning and open space protection
erie/4.summary: The Open Space and Trails board recommended rezoning land west of the Cottonwood Extension Irrigation Ditch on the Page property as Reserved Open Space. Council discussion is set for Nov. 10, and a rezoning application for 1025 Weld County Road 1½ was on a Sept. 14 agenda. The Planning Commission and the board are planning a joint study session on Oct. 21 about open space zoning and protection.

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/5.title: Vista Ridge golf course PD Amendment No. 9
erie/5.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing Aug. 19 on the Vista Ridge Planned Development Amendment No. 9 for the golf course. Council held a public hearing on the ordinance on Oct. 13 with a presentation by Gauge Land Development and the golf course manager.

erie/6.title: Comprehensive Plan amendments and Prop 123 affordable housing
erie/6.summary: The Planning Commission and Council discussed Comprehensive Plan amendments. They also discussed Erie's request to reduce its Prop 123 unit requirement to 30 units and how affordable housing will figure in the Unified Development Code update. Residents including the Gonzales family spoke against Comp Plan changes on Sept. 8.

erie/7.title: Short-term rental regulations and permit fee
erie/7.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a new UDC chapter on short-term rentals on Oct. 7. Council also took up a fee for short-term rental permit applications on Oct. 27.

erie/8.title: Urban Renewal: Colliers Hill tax increment and downtown projects
erie/8.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority amended the tax increment agreement with Weld County for the Colliers Hill plan area. The amendment removes the requirement that revenue between $10M and $14M go to Weld County Road 5 and adds parks and recreation facilities. The Authority also approved $30K more for FHU design work on a bridge project and took up a disposition agreement for 150 Briggs. Council approved a related agreement with the URA.

erie/9.title: Airport noise, hangar leases and through-the-fence fees
erie/9.summary: A resident asked for more regulation of early-morning touch-and-go flights. The airport board discussed residential through-the-fence fees (a staff proposal goes to Council in December), a hangar presentation to Council on Oct. 13, and a charter change to allow land leases longer than 20 years. It is also looking at modernizing the airport fund code.

erie/10.title: New Town Manager appointed
erie/10.summary: Council considered a resolution appointing Kelli Johnson as Town Manager effective Jan. 4, 2027, with an employment agreement. Staff and a review committee interviewed finalists after applications opened in August.

erie/11.title: Compass Park and safe sidewalks
erie/11.summary: Members of the Fargo family spoke in favor of Compass Park and safe sidewalks during public comment on Oct. 6.

erie/12.title: Business licensing and economic incentives policy
erie/12.summary: Council scheduled discussion and direction on business licensing updates and revisions to the Economic Incentives Policy on Oct. 20.

estes-park/0.title: Housing definitions, density bonuses and parking in the draft Development Code
estes-park/0.summary: The Town Board reviewed the 50% draft Development Code's housing definitions, base densities, density and height bonuses, and lower parking minimums for qualifying projects. The Estes Park Housing Authority said 1.2 to 1.4 spaces per unit would work for its properties, while some board members worried about going below two cars per unit. Related housing needs were also raised in public comment and the Housing Assessment and Action Plan.

estes-park/1.title: Fall River Village II PUD and subdivision plats
estes-park/1.summary: Resolutions 87-26, 88-26 and 89-26 on the Fall River Village II PUD and subdivision plats were continued from July 28, and the public hearing was re-opened on August 11. Staff noted the Development Code and state statute require action within 30 days or the application is deemed approved.

estes-park/2.title: Annexation of Fawn Valley and Highway 7 enclaves
estes-park/2.summary: Staff reported costs and benefits of annexing two enclaves, including a $50,000 consultant cost for the map and legal description, about $12,750 a year in added sales tax and $1,900 in property tax. Neighbors surveyed on Highway 7 responded four against and one in favor. Staff will research who owns an unannexed gap parcel that would first need to be annexed.
estes-park/2.where: Fawn Valley and Highway 7 enclaves, including Chalet Ridge Court

estes-park/3.title: Parking license plate recognition policy
estes-park/3.summary: Staff presented a draft policy for license plate recognition at Town-owned paid parking, with data kept one day unless tied to a citation. Prohibited uses include enforcing federal immigration law and monitoring First Amendment activity. The Board asked for the policy to come back for consideration and discussed limiting private LPR use.

estes-park/4.title: Parks and Open Space Master Plan
estes-park/4.summary: The final draft plan covers 11 parks, 2 natural areas and 2 town parcels, and found 76% of households are within a 15-minute walk of a park. About 890 people gave feedback, including students. Board members asked for an urban forestry element and more dog parks, and staff said implementation depends on funding.

estes-park/5.title: Dark Sky lighting ordinance and certification
estes-park/5.summary: Visit Estes Park presented on pursuing International DarkSky Community Certification and a draft Lighting Ordinance. Board members questioned requiring residential properties to comply with Dark Sky fixtures within ten years and how Rocky Mountain National Park's status affects certification.

estes-park/6.title: Water administrative penalties, Windy Gap units and Colorado-Big Thompson subcontract
estes-park/6.summary: Water staff proposed administrative fines to enforce repair of leaking surface lines. The Board declined its right of first refusal to buy Windy Gap water units from Platte River Power Authority, which would have cost nearly $10 million for two units. A Colorado-Big Thompson subcontract extension with the YMCA of the Rockies and Northern Water was pulled for discussion of incorporating Town water customers into the district.

estes-park/7.title: Rezoning review criteria amendments
estes-park/7.summary: Staff proposed amending Development Code Section 3.3 so rezonings must be consistent with the Future Land Use Plan of the Estes Forward Comprehensive Plan, replacing the 'change in conditions' criterion, along with a second new criterion.

estes-park/8.title: Feather flag temporary sign rules
estes-park/8.summary: The Board reviewed Ordinance 15-25, which temporarily allowed feather flags without permit or fee, limited to one per lot up to 12 feet tall, and not in residential zones or downtown. Members were split on whether to charge a fee and require a permit or make the rules permanent.

estes-park/9.title: Youth tobacco and vaping policy request
estes-park/9.summary: A speaker urged the Town to consider policies on tobacco and vape products to protect youth, citing Larimer County's survey results and concerns about Estes Park schools.

estes-park/10.title: Utility purchasing policy non-compliance
estes-park/10.summary: An audit found Power and Communications and Water divisions accepted competitive quotes for inventory purchases instead of following the $30,000 bid process. Staff said this will be addressed in the ongoing revision of purchasing policies.

estes-park/11.title: Events Center storage building contract
estes-park/11.summary: The Board approved a $424,350 contract with Kinley Built to design and build a new storage building at the Events Center Complex, and accepted a $100,000 state DOLA grant toward design of a project.

fairplay/0.title: Gemenskap development sewer dispute and lawsuit
fairplay/0.summary: The Board has repeatedly gone into executive session on the sewer system at the Gemenskap development in Park County, including mediation with the developer on July 27, 2026, a joint session with the Park County commissioners on Sept. 15, and by November a lawsuit the developer filed against the Town. The documents also mention settling Sallie Williard's potential claim; no outcome is stated.

fairplay/1.title: Park County use of Fairplay water for landfill-area wells
fairplay/1.summary: The Board discussed Park County's use of Town water for wells contaminated by the landfill, and in November took up fees for Park County's use of Town water on parcels outside Town limits.
fairplay/1.where: Outside-of-town parcels near Park County landfill

fairplay/2.title: Land swap with Park County (Ordinance 5)
fairplay/2.summary: The Board held first reading of Ordinance No. 5, 2026, authorizing a land swap in which the Town conveys Park County Parcel No. 32670 to Park County in exchange for county property.

fairplay/3.title: 2026 amended and 2027 budget
fairplay/3.summary: Staff presented preliminary 2027 staffing, salaries, police and events budgets. The proposed FY2026 amended and FY2027 budgets were submitted Oct. 19, with a first budget hearing Nov. 2.

fairplay/4.title: Police Department matters: station assessment and personnel review
fairplay/4.summary: The Board reviewed the proposed 2027 police budget and paid for a structural assessment of the police station. Executive sessions covered legal advice and personnel matters involving Chief Jeff Worley and an officer in an investigation.

fairplay/5.title: Water conservation, source water protection and capital planning
fairplay/5.summary: The Board discussed a water conservation plan, heard a Colorado Rural Water Association presentation on the Source Water Protection Plan, and held a work session on Town water rights and the utilities capital improvement plan. Wastewater lagoon liner and new lagoon projects are underway.

fairplay/6.title: Property Improvement Incentive Program (PIIP) agreements
fairplay/6.summary: The Town considered incentive agreements for exterior and window projects at 711 Front Street (Andrew Schofield, with a Certificate of Appropriateness), 305 4th Street and 402 Hathaway Street (Greg Johnson).

fairplay/7.title: Funding requests from nonprofits and community groups
