fairplay/7.summary: The Board weighed funding requests from the Park County Senior Coalition, Rocky Mountain Rural Health, the Boys & Girls Club of the High Rockies and others, and donated $1,000 to a South Park High School football fundraiser. It also picked a Mardi Gras fundraiser beneficiary and considered Burro Days and Halloween event requests.

fairplay/8.title: Automated vehicle identification system ordinance
fairplay/8.summary: First reading of Ordinance No. 6 to repeal and re-enact rules on the Town's automated vehicle identification system.

fairplay/9.title: Fee schedule changes and records request policy
fairplay/9.summary: Resolutions amend the Town's schedule of fees; the November version adds a policy on responding to Colorado Open Records Act and criminal justice records requests.

fairplay/10.title: Fireworks show and special events
fairplay/10.summary: The Board discussed whether to hold a 2026 fireworks show, and staff reviewed 2027 events budget items including a tire recycling fee grant.

firestone/0.title: Comprehensive Plan update before Planning Commission
firestone/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on Resolution PC-26-03, which would approve an update to the town's Comprehensive Plan, at its October 1, 2026 meeting. The outcome is not stated in the documents.

firestone/1.title: Barefoot Lakes Filing 5, 2nd Amendment preliminary plat
firestone/1.summary: At its July 16, 2026 hearing, the Planning and Zoning Commission considered Resolution PC-26-02 recommending approval of the Barefoot Lakes Filing 5, 2nd Amendment preliminary plat. Resident Steve Trunk raised concerns about impacts on neighboring properties, including views and buffering.

firestone/2.title: Parks and trails priorities and 2027 budget recommendations
firestone/2.summary: The Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission discussed priorities and 2027 budget recommendations. Ideas included trail connections to St. Vrain Park via the Legacy trail, improvements at Birch and Firestone Blvd. and Cotton Hollow and Sable, and repairing rotting bridge boards south of Gateway Park. Members also suggested looking into adding pickleball courts, and a proposed PTROC projects list is on the October 7 agenda.
firestone/2.where: Townwide, including Gateway Park and St. Vrain Park

sources.body: Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission

firestone/3.title: Arts in Public Places program discussion
firestone/3.summary: The Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission discussed the Colorado Arts in Public Places (AIPP) program on July 1, 2026, and staff were asked to collect further input.

sources.body: Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission

firestone/4.title: Summer Hours pilot program for town operations
firestone/4.summary: The Board of Trustees has a discussion item on its October 14, 2026 agenda about a Summer Hours Pilot Program. Details are not given in the documents.

florence/0.title: SUMO Golf Course water rates
florence/0.summary: The manager of the SUMO Golf Course asked City Council to revert the course's water rates, stressing its importance to the community. Another resident worried about losing the golf course amid vacant buildings on Main Street.

florence/1.title: FY 2027 city budget public hearing
florence/1.summary: Council held a public hearing to take input on the proposed FY 2027 budget. Residents spoke during the hearing, including about golf course water rates.

florence/2.title: Florence Pioneer Museum trust termination and property conveyance at 100 East Front Street
florence/2.summary: Council passed Ordinance 11-2026 on first reading, authorizing the end of a 1964 trust agreement and conveyance of the property at 100 East Front Street, home of the Florence Pioneer Museum. The City Manager described the museum's history.

florence/3.title: Volunteer firefighter personnel policy
florence/3.summary: Council considered Resolution 12-2026 establishing a volunteer firefighter personnel policy. The city recently hired several Florence Fire Protection District volunteers, and staff want their rights and responsibilities as firefighters respected while they work for the city.

florence/4.title: Negotiations on water rights, utility service and PUD compliance
florence/4.summary: Council went into a session to instruct negotiators on water rights, municipal utility service and billing, and PUD compliance. The documents give no further detail or outcome.

fort-collins/0.title: Downtown paid-parking pilot at Oak & Remington lot
fort-collins/0.summary: At an Aug. 11 work session, staff presented a paid-parking pilot at the Oak & Remington surface lot, and the delay in the College Avenue Waterline gives the City more time to weigh alternatives. Council asked staff to return with revised pilot options, including on-street paid parking, and more downtown employee parking ideas. A Code update is planned ahead of an on-street pilot. A resident also spoke about messaging on downtown parking fees.
fort-collins/0.where: Oak & Remington lot, downtown Fort Collins

fort-collins/1.title: ELCO wholesale water agreement for Montava development
fort-collins/1.summary: Staff reviewed a proposed wholesale water deal with East Larimer County Water District (ELCO) to supply Montava, a 4,000+ unit mixed-use development in northeast Fort Collins. Councilmembers voiced support, while asking about fee differences, utility revenue, long-term supply under climate change and the non-potable system. A capital project of about $2.5M was mentioned.

fort-collins/2.title: Joining the Northern Integrated Supply Project and dropping Halligan enlargement
fort-collins/2.summary: The Water Utility Enterprise board was to consider agreements letting the City join the Northern Integrated Supply Project (NISP) and store some of its own water rights in Glade Reservoir. Staff say NISP looks more certain than enlarging Halligan Reservoir, which has permitting uncertainty, and would likely mean lower rate increases. The City would notify the Army Corps and withdraw its Clean Water Act Section 404 permit application for Halligan.

fort-collins/3.title: 2027-2028 biennial budget
fort-collins/3.summary: Council held a series of work sessions (Sept. 15, Sept. 22, Oct. 13) on the City Manager's Recommended 2027-2028 Budget, the first under a new Priority Based Budgeting approach. The City faced a gap between ongoing revenue and expenses, and service areas were asked to find 8% in ongoing cost reductions. Council was to give direction on additions and offsets before adoption in November. A Lincoln Center theater group objected to higher rental rates and user fees, and a pause on the new rates was set up.

fort-collins/4.title: North College urban renewal projects: 1505 and 1630 N. College, Bristlecone, community coalition
fort-collins/4.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority handled several North College items: grant funding of roughly $1M for façade, infrastructure and community-use improvements at 1505 N. College; a $250,000 appropriation to acquire 1630 N. College; and a $2M loan term sheet for Bristlecone Affordable, a 112-unit income-restricted community. It also discussed a draft community Coalition charter with 15 voting seats for redevelopment starting with 1636 N. College, and the plan's finances before TIF collection ends. Approval of the full Charter is planned for December 2026, and a closed session on possible property purchase including eminent domain was held.

fort-collins/5.title: College and Drake urban renewal plan amendment
fort-collins/5.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority considered funding an existing conditions study around College and Drake and directing staff to prepare an amendment to the College and Drake Urban Renewal Plan, since changing conditions mean the original intent no longer works. It would evaluate adding more properties. A separate appropriation would satisfy a stipulation so the Authority can take possession of a property for redevelopment.

fort-collins/6.title: Safe Parking pilot program
fort-collins/6.summary: At a Sept. 8 work session, staff outlined a possible Safe Parking program pilot for people living in vehicles. Council gave mixed input on whether to pursue an ordinance to ensure neighbors are heard, and discussed code updates and enforcement. Homelessness response strategy and funding returned in an Oct. 27 work session.

fort-collins/7.title: Economic Development Investment Program
fort-collins/7.summary: Council gave broad support at a Sept. 8 work session to a new Economic Development Investment Program, suggesting it support community vitality and micro-business proof-of-concept rather than jobs or sales tax. Members discussed after-the-fact review, discomfort with ongoing annual commitments, and whether added staff is needed. The program is to be built into the 2027-28 budget.

fort-collins/8.title: Affordable housing: 314 N. Howes land conveyance and housing funds
fort-collins/8.summary: Council took up Ordinance 098 conveying city-owned land at 314 North Howes Street for affordable housing, which a resident called a large giveaway. Other items directed leftover 2016-2025 CCIP sales tax reserves to the Affordable Housing Capital Program, and a Housing Action Plan was discussed in October. A speaker also criticized funding delays for the EcoThrift site project, which a councilmember attributed to competitive subsidies.

fort-collins/9.title: Platte River Power Authority rollback of 100% non-carbon electricity goal
fort-collins/9.summary: Several residents told Council they oppose the Platte River Power Authority board's discussion of rolling back its goal of 100% non-carbon electricity by 2030.

fort-collins/10.title: Land Use Code Ordinance 118 and RP3 parking permit change
fort-collins/10.summary: Residents spoke in support of Ordinance No. 118 amending the Land Use Code, which Councilmember Nelsen pulled from consent for more discussion. Another resident opposed an RP3 change to charge for the first vehicle parked in front of a home, and a councilmember said she requested a pause on implementing the new rates.

fort-collins/11.title: Election code and campaign finance changes
fort-collins/11.summary: The Election Code Committee reviewed the 2025 election (final cost about $176,300), campaign finance reporting and 36 complaints. It considered code changes including letting the City Clerk issue fines directly for late reports, precinct boundary changes, and long-term ideas like public campaign funding.

fort-collins/12.title: Ethics rules and board residency requirements
fort-collins/12.summary: Council considered an ordinance on reporting contacts with staff about non-routine city mailers, amendments to the Code of Conduct policy recommended by the Ethics Review Board, and a change to residency requirements for board and commission members. A resident raised ethics concerns about the first two.

fort-collins/13.title: Wastewater septage receiving facility and utility projects
fort-collins/13.summary: Council considered bond-related financing intent and grant and reserve appropriations for the Wastewater Utility Septage Receiving Facility Project, noting out-of-city customers use it. Other items covered stormwater and the North Mason Street project funding and pedestrian intersection improvements at five locations.

fort-lupton/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center applications (5 MW or more)
fort-lupton/0.summary: On Oct. 20 the City Council took up an ordinance (AM 2026-158) imposing a temporary suspension on submitting, accepting, processing and approving applications to establish or expand data center facilities with a demand of 5 megawatts or more. The documents do not state the final vote.

fort-lupton/1.title: Housing Action Plan, Strategic Growth Element and Comprehensive Plan update
fort-lupton/1.summary: The Planning Commission and City Council reviewed the draft Housing Action Plan, the draft Strategic Growth Element and proposed Future Land Use Categories in October. The council also amended the Ayres Associates contract to add a water supply element to the Comprehensive Plan update, and approved a DOLA planning capacity grant application.

fort-lupton/2.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment
fort-lupton/2.summary: The council directed the Planning Department to file the local government affordable housing commitment for 2027-2029 so the city can take part in Proposition 123 state funding programs.

fort-lupton/3.title: Water and sewer plant investment (tap) fee changes
fort-lupton/3.summary: Council approved a resolution revising the water and sewer infrastructure investment fee schedule effective Dec. 1, 2026, after staff surveyed regional tap fees. METRO Water Recovery is raising its tap fee to $6,290, up $220 per single-family home, and the city has several water and wastewater plant upgrades underway.

fort-lupton/4.title: Water tower project contracts and easement
fort-lupton/4.summary: Council considered a Burns & McDonnell construction management contract amendment, a change order with HPM and the Murray Farms easement for the water tower project. Council also approved the 2027 Colorado-Big Thompson assessment of up to $191,000.70.

fort-lupton/5.title: Street reconstruction design contracts funded by CR 12 UPRR money
fort-lupton/5.summary: The city hired engineers for added street projects: JVA for 5th Street and Broadway Avenue (up to $143,095, later amended by $16,585), IMEG for Homestead Drive and Columbine Avenue, and HKS for 3rd and 5th Streets. The 9th and Northrup/9th Street extension and dust control on County Road 21 ($28,282.80) also came up.
fort-lupton/5.where: 5th St & Broadway Ave; Homestead Dr & Columbine Ave; 3rd & 5th Streets

fort-lupton/6.title: Ewing Annexation Agreement amendment
fort-lupton/6.summary: Council took up the first amendment to the Ewing Annexation Agreement, which was originally approved April 16, 2024. It was adopted by ordinance on first reading Sept. 1 and came back for second reading Sept. 29.

fort-lupton/7.title: New metropolitan district service plans
fort-lupton/7.summary: On Sept. 29 council reviewed the resubmitted Lancaster Crossing Metropolitan District Nos. 1-5 service plan and the 277 Metropolitan District service plan.

fort-lupton/8.title: Western Midstream buried gas gathering pipeline permit
fort-lupton/8.summary: The Planning Commission heard a Western Midstream request for a special use permit for a buried gas gathering pipeline through I-2 industrial and agricultural parcels. Nearby residents asked about pipe size, property access and effects on their land.
fort-lupton/8.where: South Denver Ave and County Road 10 area

fort-lupton/9.title: 2027 budget and urban renewal finances
fort-lupton/9.summary: Council received the 2027 requested budget Sept. 29 and a preliminary budget at an Oct. 17 retreat, and considered an application to exclude revenue from the 5.5% assessed valuation limit. The Urban Renewal Authority reviewed its 2027 draft budget, TIF reimbursements, and a grant extension request from El Rey Del Taco.

fort-lupton/10.title: Koshio Park renovation and Parks and Trails planning
fort-lupton/10.summary: Council handled Koshio Park change orders for temporary irrigation and a second change order, plus a park update and gazebo discussion. It also heard the Design Workshop Parks and Trails Vision Plan update.

fort-lupton/11.title: Police K-9 program
fort-lupton/11.summary: Council considered and approved a police K-9 program supported by donations, bringing it up Oct. 13 and on the Oct. 20 consent agenda.

fort-morgan/0.title: Electric rate increase (Ordinance No. 1338)
fort-morgan/0.summary: Utilities Director Doug Linton presented a rate study and an ordinance raising electric rates. Notices went out July 31 and the first reading was approved Aug. 18. After a Sept. 1 public hearing where resident Cynthia Ruppel opposed the increase, council approved the second reading. The city said it buys power and passes the cost on to customers.

fort-morgan/1.title: Police chief departure and interim chief appointment
fort-morgan/1.summary: At the Oct. 6 meeting, many residents criticized how the former police chief left and the council's handling of it. Some praised the police department and urged hiring a new chief. The Oct. 20 agenda includes appointing Steve Brown as Interim Police Chief and an executive session personnel check-in with him.

fort-morgan/2.title: 2027 city budget and labor contract adjustments
fort-morgan/2.summary: Council has been reviewing 2027 department budgets since August. After Cargill and the Teamsters agreed on a labor contract, the city changed its budget timeline to give departments time to adjust. Police are seeking a records technician, and the Oct. 20 agenda covers the capital improvement, conservation trust and perpetual care funds plus the schedule of fees.

fort-morgan/3.title: Aquatic facility design and certificates of participation financing
fort-morgan/3.summary: Council received an update on the aquatic facility design, with budget and timeline unchanged and excavation set to begin this fall. An ordinance authorizing certificates of participation to fund it had its first reading Oct. 6. The second reading and public hearing on Ordinance 1339 are set for Oct. 20.

fort-morgan/4.title: Historic landmark designations on Main Street
fort-morgan/4.summary: Council approved local historic landmark designations for 325, 327 and 329 Main Street, the 329 building being the 33rd local landmark. The former Fort Morgan Times building was among those designated. The Historic Preservation Board also filled seats and is tracking changes to federal Section 106 rules and the state residential tax credit program.

fort-morgan/5.title: Sale of Pointe Village Commercial Park lots for grocery store
fort-morgan/5.summary: Council approved selling three lots totaling 1.5 acres in Pointe Village Commercial Park subdivision to K&M LLC and approved the development agreement. The lots are intended for a grocery store.

fort-morgan/6.title: Special use permit for upstairs apartment at 305-307 Main Street
fort-morgan/6.summary: Council approved a special use permit for a new residential living space above a tattoo shop in the downtown overlay district. State health rules require a separate outdoor entrance. No public comments were received.

fort-morgan/7.title: Water leases, pipeline contract and NCHD agreement
fort-morgan/7.summary: The Oct. 20 agenda includes resolutions to extend the riverside irrigation and quality water lease, amend the Southern Water Supply Project pipeline allotment contract, and amend and extend the development agreement with NCHD.

fort-morgan/8.title: Airport apron expansion naming and obstruction light project
fort-morgan/8.summary: The Airport Advisory Board repeatedly discussed naming the aircraft parking apron expansion in honor of a person named Kyle. It also has an obstruction light project update.

fort-morgan/9.title: Economic incentive negotiations in executive session
fort-morgan/9.summary: Council twice met in executive session with the economic development specialist and outside parties to discuss economic incentives. No details or decisions were stated.

foxfield/0.title: Speeding and traffic calming: radar speed signs and traffic study
foxfield/0.summary: The town has reviewed speed data from engineer SEH, looked at options such as radar feedback signs, speed humps and enforcement, and put $120,000 toward traffic work in the 2026 budget. In July trustees moved to buy four solar radar signs for Hindsdale and Waco, with a total cost of about $22,373. In September trustees questioned the purchase and favored a resident speeding-report tool on the town website, and Trustee Pakanati asked to revisit it with all trustees present.
foxfield/0.where: Townwide, including Hindsdale and Waco streets

foxfield/1.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption and fire prevention
foxfield/1.summary: Trustees considered Ordinance 2026-03, which adopts the state-recommended Wildfire Resiliency Code by reference. After public hearings with no public comments, the Board approved it on August 6. Trustees also worked with South Metro Fire on outreach, a wildfire prevention training and a fire prevention meeting, and discussed the 6-inch versus 12-inch grass rule and evacuation planning.

foxfield/2.title: Land Use Code rewrite (Ordinance 2026-02)
foxfield/2.summary: Ordinance 2026-02 amends Articles 1-6 of Chapter 16 of the municipal code, the Land Use Code. The public hearing was continued several times and trustees reviewed the draft, including with an AI review. The Board approved the ordinance unanimously on August 6, 2026.

foxfield/3.title: Home Rule exploration and charter timeline
foxfield/3.summary: The town attorney presented on becoming a home rule town. Trustees debated next steps, with one saying the process was being rushed. A timeline was laid out for an ordinance initiating the process and special elections that could put a charter before voters in 2027. The Board also discussed home rule authority and land use regulation in July.

foxfield/4.title: 2026 town budget and finances
foxfield/4.summary: The Board held a study session and a public hearing on the 2026 budget, then adopted it. General Fund spending rose about 25%, largely for speed and traffic work. The mill levy stayed at 4.982 and the property tax levy was approved. Trustees later noted sales tax had dropped over four years and discussed vacancies at Foxfield Village Center.

foxfield/5.title: Road maintenance: crack seal and pavement program
foxfield/5.summary: The town approved the SEH engineering fee estimate for the 2026 pavement repair and surface treatment program. Terracare asked to bid on the work, and Vance Brothers was the bidder in the earlier rounds. In October staff asked to approve an extra $6,300 for 2 more tons of crack seal, bringing the Vance Brothers bid to $11,800. Roads Maintenance Fund money remaining for 2026 is $19,047.

foxfield/6.title: Waco Street drainage and culvert repair
foxfield/6.summary: Engineering recommendations described erosion and roadway deterioration near Waco Street and Arapahoe Road. Trustees weighed seeding versus riprap rock. In September they approved a revised Terracare quote that dropped the culvert cleanout but kept seeding and watering, with work to be scheduled for fall.

foxfield/7.title: Streetlight and tunnel light repairs
foxfield/7.summary: Trustees followed several broken streetlights and tunnel lights, including on S Lewiston Way and Parker Road. They approved a CLI Services proposal to replace three roadway light fixtures and a fuse kit at Lewiston Way and Parker Road, with not-to-exceed pricing.

foxfield/8.title: Short-term rental litigation
foxfield/8.summary: In July trustees discussed a Summary Judgment ruling in the town's short-term rental litigation and future steps.

foxfield/9.title: Law enforcement and code enforcement contracts
foxfield/9.summary: The Board approved the 2026 law enforcement services agreement and a new SafeBUILT code enforcement contract with changed rates, asking that an 8-hour rate be added. Trustees also asked for a ride-along with code enforcement.

foxfield/10.title: Foxfield Trustee vacancy and canceled April 2026 election
foxfield/10.summary: The Board canceled the April 2026 election and declared candidates elected. A trustee vacancy was expected and applicants were interviewed, with Trustee Hodge applying. Doug Hodge was sworn in as an appointed trustee in May, and trustee compensation and rules of procedure were revised.

fraser/0.title: St. Louis Landing workforce housing and NMTC financing
fraser/0.summary: The Board and Fraser Housing Authority approved resolutions authorizing New Markets Tax Credit (NMTC) actions for the St. Louis Landing project, with financing going toward the playground and buildout of the early childhood space. In October the Housing Authority took up the project's housing regulations, community documents, and initial rents and fees for the workforce housing development.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/1.title: Chapter 18 & 19 code amendments (Ordinance 340)
fraser/1.summary: The Planning Commission has been workshopping rewrites of Fraser's zoning and subdivision codes, aiming to have them in effect by Jan. 1, 2027 to meet the Proposition 123 fast-track requirement for affordable housing. Changes include plat-before-site-plan sequencing, proof of water and sewer service before building permits, fee waiver criteria, and drought and fire-resilient landscaping standards. Ordinance 340 went to the Planning Commission on Oct. 28 for a recommendation. Annexation policy will be handled separately.

fraser/2.title: Cornerstone v. Fraser mediation and conservation dispute
fraser/2.summary: The Board met in executive session about upcoming mediation in a dispute with Cornerstone and then considered a resolution approving a mediation submission agreement on Oct. 21. The documents give no details of the claims or any outcome.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/3.title: Water and sewer tap fee reassessment
fraser/3.summary: The Board held executive sessions to get legal advice on reassessing water and sewer service fees on properties whose water use has expanded or changed since the original tap fee was issued. The item was pulled from one September agenda and returned on later agendas, with no decision reported.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/4.title: Mandatory watering restrictions and water protection permits
fraser/4.summary: The Board unanimously approved Resolution 2026-09-05 amending the town's mandatory watering restrictions. It also approved a Water Supply Protection District permit for the Public Works fuel station at 150 Grand County Road 72, and in October considered a Windy Gap Environmental Fund application and a Upper Colorado Watershed Environment Team groundwater study.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/5.title: Regional wastewater plant expansion and discharge permit appeal
fraser/5.summary: The Joint Facilities Oversight Committee, made up of Fraser, Grand County Water & Sanitation District #1 and Winter Park Ranch Water and Sanitation District, reviewed capital projects and plant expansion with Tetra Tech. It also heard an update on the appeal of the plant's new discharge permit and considered a contract with Tetra Tech and regional wastewater alternatives.
fraser/5.where: Upper Fraser Valley Wastewater Treatment Plant

fraser/6.title: 2027 town budget
fraser/6.summary: The Board held budget workshops in October on the 2027 draft budget, presented Oct. 7 by the finance director. The Downtown Development Authority also reviewed its own 2027 preliminary budget in late September.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/7.title: Transit budget and service options
fraser/7.summary: On Sept. 2 the Board discussed the transit budget and service options and a motion approving one of the options was made and seconded. The documents do not say which option was chosen.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/8.title: Grand Kids Learning Center lease and child care funding
fraser/8.summary: The Board considered a lease for the Grand Kids Learning Center on Aug. 5, with the center's budget and projections in the packet. In September it authorized a Grand County child care strategic resolution.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/9.title: Public art: Mural Fest expansion and Fire & Ice 2027
fraser/9.summary: The Public Arts Committee reviewed Mural Fest, where all 30 murals sold. It discussed moving toward building wall murals, which would need roughly $50,000 more on top of the ~$91,000 Art in Public Places budget. It is also planning Fire & Ice 2027, including shuttles, EMS and fire staging, fire artists, and a possible sledding hill at Lions Ponds.

fraser/10.title: Meyer Lot No. 1 preliminary plat
fraser/10.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled a public hearing on Oct. 28 for the Meyer Lot No. 1 preliminary plat, with public comment included in the packet. An encroachment license agreement was also up for a recommendation in September.

fraser/11.title: Pole Yard development community wishlist
fraser/11.summary: The Board set aside 20 minutes on Aug. 5 to gather community wishes for development of the Pole Yard site. The documents do not record the outcome.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

frederick/0.title: Roads & Routes 1% transportation sales tax and debt ballot measures
frederick/0.summary: The Board scheduled ballot language for a sales and use tax for transportation infrastructure (Ordinance 1422) and authorization to issue debt for transportation projects (Ordinance 1423). A Roads and Routes Taskforce update was on the Sept. 2 agenda, staff ran a communications campaign with video and FAQs, and Resolution 26-R-46 in support of the road tax was on the Oct. 7 agenda.

frederick/1.title: Land Use Code bi-annual amendments (Ordinance 1425), including marijuana retail ban
frederick/1.summary: The Planning Commission recommended amendments to Articles 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 13 of the Land Use Code. The package creates a marijuana retail sales use and prohibits it in all zoning districts, changes the permitted animals list, and clarifies parking and loading language. The Board of Trustees scheduled a public hearing on Ordinance 1425 for Oct. 21.

frederick/2.title: Town water rights, leases and reservoir treatment
frederick/2.summary: Water Resources staff made a water lease agreement with the Wyndham Hill Metropolitan District, filed a Statement of Opposition in water court case 2026CW3081, and submitted the annual water audit. The Town also received a discharge permit (effective Sept. 1, 2026) to treat a reservoir with phosphorus inactivation to curb algae blooms. Payments included $198,000 in Central Weld County Water District tap fees and $25,314 for Lower Boulder change-of-use work.

frederick/3.title: Parks water, urban forestry and golf course management plans and design standards
frederick/3.summary: The PROST Commission reviewed final updates on the Parks Water Management Plan, Urban Forestry Management Plan and Golf Course Management Plan, which are headed for adoption this fall. The Planning Commission also held a work session on Parks, Open Space and Trails Design Standards.

sources.body: Parks, Recreation, Open Space & Trails Commission (PROST)
Parks, Recreation, Open Space & Trails Commission (PROST)

frederick/4.title: Public Works & Parks Campus construction
frederick/4.summary: Phase 1 (Building A and site improvements) of the new Public Works & Parks Campus is near completion. Phase 2, including the Fleet Shop and Warehouse, is underway with concrete footings starting.

frederick/5.title: Budget amendment, fee schedule and finance updates
frederick/5.summary: The Board held a quarterly finance update and budget introduction (Aug. 19), a budget work session and Ordinance 1424 for a budget amendment (Sept. 16 and Oct. 7), and a fee schedule review on Oct. 21.

frederick/6.title: Engineering Building mural and public art
frederick/6.summary: The Arts Committee is pursuing a mural on the Engineering Building and approved an RFP with a $19,000 budget covering all costs. It also approved new wood carvings in Centennial Park and Crist Park, and discussed hiring a balloon artist for Frights on Fifth.
frederick/6.where: Engineering Building; Centennial Park, 630 Eighth Street; Crist Park, 105 5th Street

frederick/7.title: Historic Preservation Plan, Miners' Museum and Certified Local Government status
frederick/7.summary: The Historic Preservation Committee worked on plan goals, museum open dates and cleaning, Music in the Park museum hours, and plaques for founding families. Staff plan to pursue State Historic Fund grants and are waiting on History Colorado about the Town's Certified Local Government application. A resident, Mike Sindelar, spoke to the Committee.

frederick/8.title: Wheatlands plat extension and Del Camino South property conveyance to KO Industrial
frederick/8.summary: The Board considered Resolution 26-R-43 extending the Wheatlands Preliminary Plat expiration date. It also considered Ordinance 1421 conveying Tract B of Del Camino South Replat of Outlot A to KO Industrial, LLC and vacating drainage, utility and access easements.
frederick/8.where: Wheatlands; Del Camino South Replat of Outlot A

frederick/9.title: Fire district maintenance facility agreement and Weld County agreement
frederick/9.summary: The Board considered Resolution 26-R-40, a notice of termination of the Maintenance Facility intergovernmental agreement with the fire district (FFFD), and Resolution 26-R-41, an agreement with Weld County.

frederick/10.title: Youth Commission funding, Youth Day and mental health discussion
frederick/10.summary: The Youth Commission's grant funding failed, so it must seek sponsors and plans presentations to Erie, Firestone and Dacono boards. Youth Day planning was postponed over budget limits, and the mental health and bullying discussion and minutes were repeatedly pushed back to October.

frederick/11.title: Community grant request for rent and utility assistance
frederick/11.summary: A nonprofit applied for a Town of Frederick Community Grant to support its rent and utility assistance program, citing support from other local governments and businesses. The application noted that requests above $500 require an explanation.

fremont-county/0.title: Cañon Dolomite Quarry truck traffic permit amendment
fremont-county/0.summary: Amrize asked the commissioners to amend Section K of Conditional Use Permit 11-001 for the Cañon Dolomite Quarry so the truck traffic limit uses "Annual Average Daily Traffic" wording, matching the original CDOT approval. The quarry operates only a day or two a month and wants room for sales surges on those days, not more operating days.

fremont-county/1.title: 152-lot Planned Unit Development at 1337 County Road 3A
fremont-county/1.summary: A Planned Unit Development with 152 lots at a minimum lot size was on the October 13 agenda for a hearing. It is at 1337 County Road 3A, Cañon City.

fremont-county/2.title: Outside consultant review fees billed to an applicant
fremont-county/2.summary: Planning & Zoning asked the commissioners to bill an applicant for review costs beyond the application fee. The excess came from an outside consultant hired after the applicant alleged staff bias. The request relies on Section 306 of the county resolution.

fremont-county/3.title: 2027 Fremont County budget
fremont-county/3.summary: A public hearing on the proposed 2027 county budget was scheduled for the October 27 meeting. The agenda also lists a 2027 MotivHealth employee health plan proposal and a bid award for the DHS building roof replacement.

fremont-county/4.title: Resolutions on state ballot measures (Amendment 83, Amendment 87, Proposition NN)
fremont-county/4.summary: The commissioners were to consider resolutions supporting Amendment 83 and opposing Amendment 87 (graduated income tax) and Proposition NN. Titles are partly cut off in the agenda.

fremont-county/5.title: Aspen Acres Fire and evacuation planning for veterans center
fremont-county/5.summary: Public Health reported on the Aspen Acres Fire, which came close to the Bruce McCandless Veterans Community Living Center before firefighters controlled the north side. Staff have planned and practiced evacuation since the 24 Fire. Fire danger in the county remains extreme, and DOT stopped mowing to avoid sparks.
fremont-county/5.where: Bruce McCandless Veterans Community Living Center

fremont-county/6.title: Colorado River shortage and water rights
fremont-county/6.summary: Commissioner McFall reported on Colorado Counties Inc. discussions about Colorado River negotiations. The Bureau of Reclamation decided the Lower Basin must cut use by 1.25 million acre-feet because the states could not agree.

fremont-county/7.title: Rezoning from Business to Residential (R1)
fremont-county/7.summary: A property owner asked for a zone change from commercial to Residential One so they can add a full bathroom to a unit for personal use. A public hearing was held August 25.

fremont-county/8.title: New liquor license for restaurant, bar and mercantile and CDOT highway access
fremont-county/8.summary: The commissioners considered a new malt, vinous and spirits-light license for a restaurant, bar and mercantile in a building with 134-person occupancy. The site's existing CDOT access permit allowed only 20 trips a day, so a traffic study was needed for a new permit using the West gate off Grant Street. The motion to approve was made.

fremont-county/9.title: RV roof repair business development hearing
fremont-county/9.summary: A hearing was scheduled for a proposed business that maintains and repairs RV roofs inside a building. Details are limited in the documents.

frisco/0.title: Fast-track affordable housing review (Prop 123) – Ordinance 26-18
frisco/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on August 20, 2026 on a fast-tracked review process for affordable housing to meet Proposition 123 state requirements. Council took up Ordinance 26-18, adding Section 180-2.8 to the Unified Development Code, on first reading September 8 and second reading September 22.

frisco/1.title: Unified Development Code changes to allowed uses, accessory structures and parking – Ordinance 26-17
frisco/1.summary: Amendments to the Unified Development Code would change the table of allowed uses, accessory uses and structures, and parking and loading rules. The Planning Commission heard it August 20, and Council considered it on first reading September 8 and second reading September 22.

frisco/2.title: Short-term rental cap and income-restricted housing
frisco/2.summary: Staff asked Council at the October 13 work session whether to change how the short-term rental license cap is calculated. Currently all residential units, including deed-restricted ones like The Scout, count toward the total. An ordinance amending the STR licensing code (Ordinance 26-14) was on the October 27 agenda for first reading.

frisco/3.title: 2027 budget, mill levy and appropriations
frisco/3.summary: Council discussed the 2027 budget September 8. It then took up Ordinance 26-22 (appropriations) and Ordinance 26-23 (setting the town mill levy) on first reading October 13 and second reading October 27, along with Resolution 26-24 adopting the 2027 budget and 2027-2031 plan. A 2026 investment review showed a portfolio market value of $21.2 million and a 3.96% weighted average yield.

frisco/4.title: Council strategic planning retreat
frisco/4.summary: On August 25 Council held a retreat at the Summit Fire & EMS building to set strategic direction. It reviewed the current plan, which covers infrastructure, public safety, finances, water rates, housing (90–100 more income-restricted units since 2023), the Arts and Culture plan and recreation. A strategic plan briefing followed on October 27.
frisco/4.where: Summit Fire & EMS Building, 0035 County Shops Road

frisco/5.title: Ballot measure support: Summit County Strong Future mill levy and school district 4A
frisco/5.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-19 supporting Summit County's referred question to continue the Strong Future mill levy in perpetuity; it is not a new or increased tax. On October 13 it considered Resolution 26-26 supporting Summit School District RE-1 Ballot Measure 4A, a mill levy override for teacher and staff pay, and heard a school district and teachers' association presentation.

frisco/6.title: Sixth Degree Town Homes at 121 E Main Street
frisco/6.summary: The Planning Commission conducted final review of a major site plan for a mixed-use building with six residential and two commercial units at 121 E Main Street. Commissioners asked about parking lifts, lighting compliance, and an unlocated water line and easement responsibility.

frisco/7.title: Eight townhomes proposed at 207 Granite Street
frisco/7.summary: A sketch plan review for eight townhomes at 207 Granite Street. Staff urged a sidewalk on Granite Street, and the project needs waivers for dumpster access and access from 2nd Avenue, a collector street. Commissioners noted the CC zoning allows residential by right, limiting the town's leverage, and that the site should blend with the historic park across the street.

frisco/8.title: Telecommunication facility at 101 W Main Street
frisco/8.summary: The Planning Commission was to consider a special use permit for a new freestanding telecommunication facility at 101 W Main Street, applicant BMF Development LLC.

frisco/9.title: Thermal energy network test bore at Town Hall
frisco/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-23, a revocable license and right of entry for a utility thermal energy network test bore on the Town Hall property at 1 Main Street. This ties to the town's geothermal partnership with Xcel.

frisco/10.title: Landscaping and revegetation code discussion
frisco/10.summary: Council held a code discussion on landscaping and revegetation requirements on August 11.

frisco/11.title: Downtown winter parking and grants
frisco/11.summary: On September 22 Council received a downtown winter parking update and 2027 Grant Award Committee recommendations.

fruita/0.title: Water Supply and Strategic Growth plan required by the state
fruita/0.summary: Colorado requires cities with a comprehensive plan to adopt a Water Supply Element and a Strategic Growth Element by December 31, 2026. Planning Commission and City Council discussed a community engagement strategy and a draft water survey, and the mayor noted the mandate is unfunded. The City has authorized a grant application and hopes to hire a consultant, and a draft submitted by the deadline counts as 'Compliance in Progress'.

fruita/1.title: 1925 J Road annexation and rezone (36.14 acres)
fruita/1.summary: The Planning Commission heard a request to annex about 36.14 acres at 1925 J Road and rezone it to Community Residential. A resident told Council that the development plan calls for at least 40 homes and raised concerns about irrigation water and the Encanto system, which lost water for over 24 hours in June. The resident asked for a long-term irrigation plan before approvals.

fruita/2.title: Fruita Co-op annexation and industrial rezone (40.16 acres)
fruita/2.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled public hearings on annexing about 40.16 acres for the Fruita Co-op and rezoning it from county AFT to Industrial.

fruita/3.title: Raptor Crossing PUD amendment
fruita/3.summary: A major amendment to the Raptor Crossing PUD Guide would allow certain residential and other uses. Council introduced Ordinance 2026-17 on first reading, with a public hearing set for September 15, 2026.

fruita/4.title: 2027 City Manager's recommended budget
fruita/4.summary: City Manager Shannon Vassen presented a 2027 budget with no big surprises and fewer, smaller capital projects. The largest is $2 million to build J Road from Wildcat Avenue to Skiff Road, with grant funding being sought. Other items include $100,000 for sidewalks, $320,000 for four police trucks, and pay increases for some positions such as wastewater plant operators.

fruita/5.title: CDOT US 6 West/SH 139 access control plan amendment
fruita/5.summary: CDOT presented an amendment to the access control plan for Highway 6 from 18 Road to 22 Road ahead of a future widening project. It includes right-in/right-out intersections with dedicated U-turns and alternate access for properties along the highway. An updated intergovernmental agreement is expected in January 2027.
fruita/5.where: US Highway 6 from 18 Road to 22 Road

fruita/6.title: Park conditions, Farmers Market location and drought watering
fruita/6.summary: The Parks and Recreation Commission discussed Civic Center Park grass wearing thin from heavy use and whether to move or alternate the Farmers Market with Reed Park, or close part of Aspen Street. Salt Wash soccer fields are turning to dirt as the city cuts water use during drought. Residents also asked for more lap lanes or longer hours at the Community Center.
fruita/6.where: Civic Center Park, Reed Park, Salt Wash fields

fruita/7.title: Museums of Western Colorado revitalization plan
fruita/7.summary: The Museums of Western Colorado presented a multi-phase, thirteen-year revitalization plan. Construction is estimated to begin in late 2028 or early 2029, and no capital campaign has been outlined yet. Council also approved a lease for the Old Fruita Museum.

fruita/8.title: Public sculpture selections for downtown pedestals
fruita/8.summary: The Arts and Culture Board reviewed artist applications for sculptures at sites including South Mesa Street, the Dinosaur Journey parking lot and the FARM. Board members visited the artists' pieces on August 17 and planned to confirm accurate representation before announcing selections.
fruita/8.where: South Mesa Street, Dinosaur Journey lot, FARM

fruita/9.title: Request for town halls and recording of workshops
fruita/9.summary: A resident asked for regular Council town halls to allow two-way conversation, not just public comment. Another resident asked the City to record workshop meetings to keep an accurate record, citing remarks by the police chief at a recent workshop.

fruita/10.title: Bee City USA designation
fruita/10.summary: Council heard a presentation on making Fruita Mesa County's first Bee City, which requires a $200 annual fee and a Council resolution. Staff suggested the Livability Commission or Parks and Recreation Commission take responsibility for the application.

fruita/11.title: Municipal judge hiring and court powers
fruita/11.summary: Council interviewed candidates for Municipal Court Judge in executive session and recommended that the City Manager negotiate a contract. Ordinance 2026-16 on municipal judges' powers was introduced on first reading.

garden-city/0.title: New Police Department building construction
garden-city/0.summary: The board repeatedly approved Mark Young Construction change orders (COR 002 through 010) and monthly invoices, including a $301,598.32 November 2025 invoice, and approved a June 2026 invoice. Staff also noted the PD floor will be entirely replaced.

garden-city/1.title: 2026 budget, 4% COLA and property tax levy
garden-city/1.summary: After a public hearing, the board was set to adopt the 2026 budget, appropriation and property tax levy (Resolutions 10, 11 and 12-2025) on Dec. 9. It also considered a 4% cost-of-living raise and a larger health insurance stipend for employees.

garden-city/2.title: Town Administrator/Clerk transition and alternate attorney
garden-city/2.summary: In July 2026 the board approved Town Administrator Cheryl Campbell's resignation letter and discussed handing the position over once Linda Blackston starts. It also discussed an employment agreement and alternate town attorney options.

garden-city/3.title: Speed humps on 27th Street Road
garden-city/3.summary: The board considered speed hump proposals for 27th Street Road in November 2025. In July 2026 staff were to check on an issue at the end of 27th Street Road.

garden-city/4.title: 2026 Greeley Transit contract
garden-city/4.summary: The board considered approving the 2026 contract with Greeley Transit for services.

garden-city/5.title: Building codes and 2026 building permit fees
garden-city/5.summary: The board considered adopting the 2026 building permit fee schedule. It also took up Ordinance 11-2025, adopting by reference building codes including the Electric and Solar Ready Code and Colorado wildfire resiliency code, with a hearing on Dec. 9.

garden-city/6.title: Award Alliance incentive
garden-city/6.summary: Paul Hlad of Award Alliance presented to the board in November 2025. On Dec. 9 the board was set to consider Resolution 13-2025, an incentive for Award Alliance.

garden-city/7.title: Marijuana business licenses and special review use
garden-city/7.summary: The board considered several retail marijuana store, cultivation and manufacturing licenses and renewals in November 2025. In July 2026 it considered a Star Buds license at 2502 8th Ave and adopted Resolution 10-2026 granting a use by special review.

garden-city/8.title: Commercial Revitalization Grant for El Rodeo Night Club
garden-city/8.summary: The board was to give final review and approval to El Rodeo Night Club LLC's Commercial Revitalization Grant.

garden-city/9.title: Coordinated election and community development grants
garden-city/9.summary: In July 2026 the board approved a memorandum of intergovernmental agreement for the coordinated election, discussed the election, and approved an IGA for the Weld County Community Development Block Grant program.

garden-city/10.title: Police department sells last Smith & Wesson
garden-city/10.summary: The board approved lowering the price of the last Smith & Wesson firearm held by the police department.

garfield-county/0.title: 2027 county budget hearings and Budget Supplement #4
garfield-county/0.summary: Commissioners held 2027 budget hearings in October, with department and elected office presentations, and a public hearing on 2026 Budget Supplement #4. A workforce analysis from MGT and requests from outside groups, such as the Early Childhood District and Forest Improvement District, were part of the budget talks.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session
Board of County Commissioners - Budget Hearings

garfield-county/1.title: Affordable housing: USDA programs, Housing Authority and Cavern Springs Mobile Home Park
garfield-county/1.summary: Commissioners heard from USDA Rural Development's state director on affordable housing programs and from the Garfield County Housing Authority, which presented its annual report and a $90,000 funding request for 2027. They were also asked for a letter of support for the Cavern Springs Mobile Home Park partnership request.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session

garfield-county/2.title: Library District tax extension on the November 2026 ballot
garfield-county/2.summary: The Garfield County Public Library District asked commissioners to place a ballot issue on the November 3, 2026 election. It would ask voters to extend a portion of the district's property tax levy.

garfield-county/3.title: Jail standards, overtime and Sheriff's Office funding
garfield-county/3.summary: The Sheriff presented on new jail standards, and a $267,000 supplemental request was made to cover jail overtime. The Sheriff's Office also sought grants for opioid treatment medication for inmates ($39,903) and bulletproof vests ($12,100), and renewed body camera contracts.

garfield-county/4.title: Development proposals: Mitchell Creek PUD, Lake Springs Ranch PUD, McClure River Ranch, Hogback View Estates
garfield-county/4.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled hearings on rezoning Mitchell Creek Community PUD at 50235 Highway 6/24 and on the Lake Springs Ranch PUD amendment near 4001 County Road 114. Commissioners signed resolutions approving McClure River Ranch amendments (12 lots on 48.96 acres) east of Carbondale and the Hogback View Estates preliminary plan at 24 County Road 138.
garfield-county/4.where: Mitchell Creek, Lake Springs Ranch, McClure River Ranch, Hogback View Estates

garfield-county/5.title: Xcel Energy Hopkins to Basalt transmission line rebuild
garfield-county/5.summary: The Planning Commission held a location and extent review for Xcel's Hopkins to Basalt Line 9256 rebuild, starting at the Hopkins Substation east of Carbondale. Xcel also gave a presentation to commissioners.
garfield-county/5.where: Hopkins Substation, Red Canyon Road and Fisher Cemetery Road

garfield-county/6.title: Senior transportation and meals: Traveler, RFTA IGA, congregate meals
garfield-county/6.summary: Commissioners discussed the Traveler transit service, reviewed a draft RFTA-Traveler agreement and a seven-party senior programs MOU. They also considered a sole-source contract with the City of Rifle for congregate meals in western Garfield County.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session

garfield-county/7.title: Parachute funding requests: 1st Street/US 6 reconstruction and PATS transit
garfield-county/7.summary: The Town of Parachute asked for $600,000 toward the Parachute MOVES 1st Street/US 6 reconstruction. It also asked for disbursement of $200,000 in 2026 funding and a 2027 funding request for the Parachute Area Transit System.

garfield-county/8.title: Madison AI assistant purchase
garfield-county/8.summary: The county considered a $43,200 supplemental appropriation and a Carahsoft contract for a 12-month Madison AI subscription, with a countywide assistant and a Community Development assistant.

garfield-county/9.title: Slaughterhouse Gulch mudslide landfill fee waiver and LoVa Trail support
garfield-county/9.summary: A request asked commissioners to waive landfill tipping fees after the Slaughterhouse Gulch mudslide. Glenwood Springs also sought a letter of support for a federal grant to advance the LoVa Trail through South Canyon.
garfield-county/9.where: Slaughterhouse Gulch; South Canyon, Glenwood Springs

garfield-county/10.title: Garfield Clean Energy funding and Colorado River District update
garfield-county/10.summary: Commissioners were asked to approve $150,000 in 2027 for Garfield Clean Energy membership. They also received an annual Colorado River District update including the Shoshone Water Rights preservation project.

gilpin-county/0.title: Rollinsville area fire-protection cisterns
gilpin-county/0.summary: The commissioners took up Resolution 26-085 to develop a community cistern for fire protection in the Rollinsville area, choosing between the East/Gold Dirt and West/Public Works cistern projects. By Sept. 8 the resolution covered coordinated procurement of both projects.

gilpin-county/1.title: Short-term rental regulations (Ordinance 26-01)
gilpin-county/1.summary: Ordinance 26-01 on rental regulations had a first reading on Aug. 25 and a second reading at a public hearing on Sept. 22. Community Development and the County Attorney presented it.

gilpin-county/2.title: Roadway design manual, road classification and county road inventory
gilpin-county/2.summary: The county reviewed a Roadway Design and Construction Manual and County Road Inventory. On Aug. 25 a public hearing covered Resolution 26-084, designating and classifying county roads, and Resolution 26-088, adopting the roadway manual.

gilpin-county/3.title: 2027 budget, employee benefits and compensation
gilpin-county/3.summary: A draft 2027 budget was presented on Sept. 22. Commissioners also considered the 2026 Compensation Plan (Resolution 26-089) and the 2027 employee benefits renewal (Resolution 26-097).

gilpin-county/4.title: Wildfire mitigation grants and fire restrictions
gilpin-county/4.summary: The county committed $51,000 over three years to the Clear Creek Watershed & Forest Health Partnership's grant application for forest restoration and wildfire risk mitigation. It also coordinated a Community Wildfire Defense Grant and supported fuels reduction projects. Stage 2 fire restrictions were lowered to Stage 1 on Sept. 8, and Resolution 26-099 removed the remaining restrictions in late October.

gilpin-county/5.title: Ballot issue referred to Gilpin County voters
gilpin-county/5.summary: Resolution 26-077 refers a ballot issue to county voters. It appeared on the Aug. 11 and Aug. 25 agendas. Upcoming ballot propositions were discussed on Sept. 8, and a November election resolution was also on the Aug. 25 agenda.

gilpin-county/6.title: Affordable housing: Proposition 123 credits and commitment
gilpin-county/6.summary: The county considered an intergovernmental agreement on Proposition 123 affordable housing unit credits (Resolution 26-086). It also considered Resolution 26-098 authorizing an affordable housing commitment filing.

gilpin-county/7.title: Parks and Recreation fees, equipment and youth programs
gilpin-county/7.summary: Commissioners discussed a fee structure and equipment purchase plan for Parks and Recreation. A youth programs status update followed in October. The county's comprehensive fee schedule was also updated (Resolution 26-093).

gilpin-county/8.title: Code enforcement policy and public records (CORA) process
gilpin-county/8.summary: A draft code enforcement policy was discussed on Aug. 18. The county amended its public records request policy (Resolution 26-090) and heard an update on the CORA process and fees.

gilpin-county/9.title: COMBA bike trail outside I-70 project
gilpin-county/9.summary: A bike trail project with COMBA outside the I-70 corridor was on the Aug. 18 agenda for discussion.

glendale/0.title: Xcel Energy franchise agreement (Question 2B)
glendale/0.summary: On the Oct. 6 agenda, Council considers a resolution tied to Question 2B, which grants a franchise to Public Service Company of Colorado (Xcel) and approves a franchise agreement.

glendale/1.title: 2026 city budget and tax levy ordinances
glendale/1.summary: Council is slated to introduce Ordinance No. 6 adopting the city budget and appropriating money, and Ordinance No. 8 levying taxes for 2026. Introduction is set for Oct. 6.

glendale/2.title: Four Mile Project legal advice
glendale/2.summary: Council planned an executive session on Oct. 6 to receive legal advice about the Four Mile Project. The documents give no further detail.

glendale/3.title: Entertainment Advisory Board events: car show, Music on the Plaza, Get To Know Glendale
glendale/3.summary: The advisory board's teams are working on a car show, Music on the Plaza and a Get To Know Glendale effort. They prepared presentations to City Council on 9/1 and are reviewing the budget and proposed activities in October.

glendale/4.title: Infinity Park discussion
glendale/4.summary: Infinity Park is a discussion item at the Oct. 6 City Council meeting, presented by Kieran Nelson. The agenda does not say what is being discussed.

glendale/5.title: Ordinance corrections to Ordinance No. 1 references
glendale/5.summary: Council is to introduce Ordinance No. 5, which amends and corrects reference numbers from Ordinance No. 1 of 2026.

glenwood-springs/0.title: Short-term rental and accessory tourist rental permit renewal rules
glenwood-springs/0.summary: The Planning & Zoning Commission reviewed a code amendment (CDA-000049-2026) requiring STR and accessory tourist rental permit holders to actually rent and remit lodging tax to renew. Council took up Ordinance 2026-22 on Sept. 17, and the amendment was changed to require a minimum of 20 nights and $150 in sales tax remitted over a two-year period. The ordinance was on the Oct. 1 consent agenda. Council also heard an appeal on a short-term rental at 319 Park Drive.

glenwood-springs/1.title: JG Housing Solutions enforcement at 100 Midland Avenue
glenwood-springs/1.summary: Council received an update on the special use permit that Planning & Zoning revoked for 100 Midland Avenue, Units 110 and 210, and discussed legal enforcement and injunctive relief against JG Housing Solutions for code, zoning and land use violations. A resident raised a complaint to Planning and Zoning on Aug. 20, and council held an executive session on the lawsuit in October.

glenwood-springs/2.title: Fire department funding and November 2026 property tax ballot question
glenwood-springs/2.summary: Council considered raising property taxes to fund the fire department on the November 2026 ballot. On Aug. 20 it took up a resolution certifying the ballot issue, setting the ballot title and content, and the mayor spoke in support of a resolution backing the fire tax.

glenwood-springs/3.title: Parking on Bennett Avenue and 1600 Bennett fee-in-lieu request
glenwood-springs/3.summary: Residents repeatedly told council about parking problems and tree stumps on Bennett Avenue in August and September. A parking fee-in-lieu request for 1600 Bennett was on the Oct. 1 agenda.

glenwood-springs/4.title: Canyon Vista affordable housing at 51993 Highway 6 & 24
glenwood-springs/4.summary: Planning & Zoning reviewed a preliminary plat to consolidate three parcels into one lot for Canyon Vista, an 80-unit affordable multifamily project on about 4 acres between Highway 6 and Donegan Road. Staff found the plat met all seven criteria with six conditions. It went to council on Oct. 15 along with a right-of-way encroachment license.

glenwood-springs/5.title: Affordable housing funding and housing policy discussions
glenwood-springs/5.summary: Council considered a funding request for the 130 Midland affordable homeownership project (Oct. 1, continued Oct. 15) and scheduled a housing policy work session. Councilors also called for an overarching housing conversation and discussed employee housing.

glenwood-springs/6.title: Xcel transmission line rebuild (6584 line)
glenwood-springs/6.summary: Xcel Energy applied for a Location and Extent permit and a 1041 permit to replace aging wood poles with weathered-steel monopoles on the 6584 transmission line through Glenwood Springs, widening easements to reduce wildfire risk. The Planning Commission decides the L&E permit and recommends on the 1041 permit to City Council.

glenwood-springs/7.title: 2027 budget and tourism fund
glenwood-springs/7.summary: Staff presented the 2027 budget on Oct. 1, with a 2027 Tourism Promotion Fund budget and a public budget hearing on Oct. 15. Council also amended the 2026 appropriation ordinance for carryovers and reallocations.

glenwood-springs/8.title: Transit and transportation: Hogback route, Ride Glenwood pricing, haul routes
glenwood-springs/8.summary: Council discussed the Hogback bus route, an IGA with Roaring Fork Transportation Authority, Ride Glenwood On-Demand pricing and a comprehensive transportation discussion. A councilor also asked to look at street weight limits and designated haul routes.

glenwood-springs/9.title: Mountain Waste and Recycling pay-as-you-throw contract
glenwood-springs/9.summary: Council held a work session and then considered a contract with Mountain Waste and Recycling for pay-as-you-throw trash service on Oct. 15. A resident also raised bear and trash enforcement.

glenwood-springs/10.title: Electric vehicle charging regulations
glenwood-springs/10.summary: Council considered Ordinance 2026-18 amending the municipal code on regulating and permitting EV charging projects, and it was approved on the Sept. 3 consent agenda.

glenwood-springs/11.title: Comcast franchise agreement
glenwood-springs/11.summary: Council approved Ordinance 2026-19, a franchise agreement with Comcast of Colorado IX, LLC, on first reading Sept. 3 and second reading on the Sept. 17 consent agenda.

golden/0.title: Fire Department incident, City Manager separation and interim appointment
golden/0.summary: After an incident at the Fire Department, residents spoke at several meetings and Council began an outside investigation. Council created a temporary subcommittee (Resolution 3344), appointed Carly Lorenz as Interim City Manager on Aug 11, and approved a City Manager Separation Agreement and an Acting City Manager Agreement on Aug 25. On Sept 15 Council approved a contract (Resolution 3357) after striking some clauses, and the REDI Task Force discussed racial profiling concerns and how to move forward.

golden/1.title: The Junction urban renewal plan and TIF request (Highway 93)
golden/1.summary: GURA is reviewing a new urban renewal area for The Junction, a 51.28-acre light industrial business park on the west side of Highway 93. A conditions survey found five blight factors. The developer (Evergreen) is asking for 100% of tax increment financing to cover about $59 million in public improvements, including a Highway 93 roundabout and a pedestrian bridge to the North Table Mountain trailhead. The board considered Resolution 172 recommending the plan, and the Planning Commission was to review the boundary.
golden/1.where: West side of State Highway 93, near North Table Mountain Park

golden/2.title: Nazarene urban renewal area at 17455 West 16th Avenue
golden/2.summary: City Council adopted the Nazarene Plan Area on July 14. The developer has secured key grant financing and staff are ready to negotiate tax increment financing. GURA reviewed a project update and a draft TIF agreement.

golden/3.title: Clayworks development: natural gas amendment, mobility and parking
golden/3.summary: Clayworks developers asked to amend their Official Development Plan to allow limited natural gas for pool and spa heating, fireplaces and communal grills. The Sustainability Board heard residents urge the project to keep its original all-electric commitments. The amendment must go through Planning Commission and City Council. The Mobility Board has also followed its transportation demand plan, traffic memo and parking.

golden/4.title: 2027-2028 city budget and revenue outlook
golden/4.summary: The Citizens Budget Advisory Committee, Council and advisory boards are reviewing the proposed 2027-2028 biennial budget under a more conservative revenue outlook. CBAC recommended more marijuana tax money for rent assistance and food insecurity. Council heard a financial report and revenue trends presentation, and the Sustainability Board sought a larger rebate budget.

sources.body: City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/5.title: Flock license plate camera contract
golden/5.summary: Council's Oct 13 study session had the Police Chief explain how Golden Police use Flock technology. Councilors Knecht and Kurzinski proposed reconsidering the Flock contract, which would go to a vote if three or more Councilors supported it.

sources.body: City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/6.title: 2122 Jackson Street cottage development and alley spur
golden/6.summary: Council called up approval of site plans at 2122 Jackson Street for Planning Commission review, focusing on the narrow alley spur. Neighbors raised concerns about the narrow alley, trash, parking and lighting. Staff said the site is overparked, with one space per cottage required.

golden/7.title: Historic preservation cases: 2024 Ford St, 612 10th St, 403 18th St
golden/7.summary: The Historic Preservation Board approved a new rear cottage and garage at 2024 Ford Street in the East Street Historic District. It also reviewed demolition requests, including 612 10th Street (the Schall Residence), where a developer weighed relocation or integrating the structure. On 403 18th Street the board must place a demolition stay of up to 190 days.

golden/8.title: Lions Park playground, GOCO grant and public art
golden/8.summary: Council supported a Great Outdoors Colorado grant application for the Lions Park nature play and outdoor area (Resolution 3340), and the Parks Board reviewed the playground redesign. The Arts and Culture Commission's jury narrowed 29 art entries to three finalists for more detailed renderings.

sources.body: Lion's Park Art Selection Panel Meeting - No Recording
Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting
ACC Lion's Park Art Selection Panel Meeting - No Recording

golden/9.title: Special events impacts, grants and Visit Golden marketing contract
golden/9.summary: A west 10th Street resident asked for a review of how events strain parking and street access. The Special Events Review Committee handles event grants, with a $40,000 program and revisions under discussion. Council considered a marketing contract with DVA Advertising (Resolution 3345), while the Community Marketing Board reviewed its 2027 strategic plan and 2027-2028 budget and a holiday sponsorship with KOSI.
golden/9.where: West end of 10th Street and Citywide

golden/10.title: Water conservation, drought response and wildfire planning
golden/10.summary: Staff gave a year-end report on 2026 drought response and water conservation, with a new weather-normalization model. Council's Oct 27 study session included a drought after-action review and a wildfire management update. Council also considered ordinances on water and wastewater regulations and wastewater pretreatment (Ordinances 2297 and 2298).

sources.body: City Council Study Session & Regular Business Meeting
City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/11.title: Commercial energy benchmarking and universal recycling ordinance
golden/11.summary: The Sustainability Board discussed a proposed Commercial Energy Benchmarking Program and heard comments urging clear goals and a voluntary pilot with incentives. Staff are also developing a universal recycling ordinance, possibly starting with hauler licensing, and the board discussed EV charging overnight fees.

golden/12.title: Downtown DDA projects and 807 13th Street grant
golden/12.summary: The DDA confirmed new priorities including 11th Street sidewalk and streetscape, legacy shade trees and 14 street trees on Arapahoe Street. It also considered a $7,500 holiday sponsorship, a holiday light contract extension, an emergency repair grant for 807 13th Street and Ford Street undergrounding. Police were to join a September meeting about downtown issues.

golden/13.title: Affordable housing and Prosper project
golden/13.summary: Demolition and site work are underway for the Prosper affordable housing project at 817 14th Street. Council approved agreements tied to Proposition 123 and regional housing, including assigning private activity bond allocation to Foothills Regional Housing.

sources.body: City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 6:30pm

golden/14.title: Makerspace study and economic indicator dashboard
golden/14.summary: The city contracted Artspace Consultants for a preliminary makerspace study. The Economic Development Commission also recommended the mySidewalk platform for an economic dashboard, and a 2027-2028 budget includes $20,000 a year for makerspace support and $15,000 for dashboard tools.

golden/15.title: Municipal Building and Heart of Golden public art
golden/15.summary: The Arts subcommittee planned artwork funded by the 1% for art, including a mural on the parking garage at 10th and Vasquez ($38,000 earmarked) and sculpture sites near Tucker Gulch and the Farmers Highline Canal. A call for artists is expected in fall 2026.
golden/15.where: Municipal Building, 10th and Vasquez; Heart of Golden

sources.body: ACC Art in Public Places Subcommittee Meeting - No Recording

granby/0.title: Town Manager separation and recruitment of an interim manager
granby/0.summary: The Board met in executive session on the Town Manager's employment, then took up ratifying a Town Manager separation agreement on Sept. 8. In October it discussed interim manager and permanent recruitment, and a transition. The documents do not state the terms or outcome.

granby/1.title: Data center workshop
granby/1.summary: The Board held a data center workshop led by the Town Manager on Aug. 25. The agenda does not say whether a specific facility or new rules are proposed.

granby/2.title: Zoning code rewrite and new zoning map (Ordinance 1041)
granby/2.summary: The Board held a public hearing on Aug. 25 and again on Sept. 22 on comprehensive amendments to Chapter 16 (zoning regulations) and a legislative update to the official zoning map.

granby/3.title: Ten Mile Crossing planned development plan
granby/3.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on Oct. 5 on the preliminary plat and plan for the Ten Mile Crossing Planned Development Overlay District, with conditions. The Board held a hearing on the preliminary plan on Oct. 13.

granby/4.title: Nuche Village apartments agreement, funding and contract
granby/4.summary: The Board dealt repeatedly with the Nuche Village apartments. It considered an agreement extension on Sept. 8, funding on Oct. 13, and the contract on Oct. 27. Hearing board appointments for Nuche Village also came up in August and September.

granby/5.title: Annexation proceedings and the GRCO annexation
granby/5.summary: On Sept. 22 the Board considered a resolution initiating annexation proceedings and setting a hearing on the eligibility of certain lands. On Oct. 27 it took up annexation consideration for GRCO.

granby/6.title: Grand Elk Ranch GID property conveyance and 2027 budget
granby/6.summary: The Grand Elk Ranch General Improvement District reviewed its 2027 budget on Oct. 13. On Oct. 27 it took up Ordinance 81 authorizing conveyance of real property related to the Village at Buckhorn.
granby/6.where: Grand Elk Ranch / Village at Buckhorn

granby/7.title: 2027 Town of Granby budget
granby/7.summary: The Finance Director presented the 2027 town budget for discussion on Oct. 13.

granby/8.title: Wildfire resiliency code workshop
granby/8.summary: The Board held a workshop on a wildfire resiliency code on Aug. 11.

granby/9.title: Peddler, mobile vendor and solicitor rules (Ordinance 1040)
granby/9.summary: The Board considered an ordinance amending Chapter 5.05 and adding Chapter 5.06 of the municipal code to regulate peddlers, mobile vendors, solicitors and canvassers.

granby/10.title: Granby Trails revegetation and parks planning
granby/10.summary: A resident and the Middle Park Conservation District presented revegetation and tree planting at Granby Trails using CSFS grants, with an update on Aug. 25. The Board also discussed Bark Park pond, parks planning and a parks and rec position in October.

granby/11.title: Police Chief contract and new Tahoes
granby/11.summary: The Board considered buying two Chevy Tahoes for the police department in August. A police chief contract was on the Sept. 22 agenda, and an oath of office for the police chief on Oct. 13.

granby/12.title: Alley traffic concerns
granby/12.summary: The Board discussed alley traffic concerns on Sept. 8.

grand-county/0.title: 2027 county budget hearings
grand-county/0.summary: Commissioners scheduled budget hearings for October 5-9, 2026, going department by department, including Road and Bridge, airports, Housing Authority, Community Development and Economic Development. The sessions include a 5-year budget projection and deliberations.

grand-county/1.title: Subdivision and PUD regulation amendments and Master Plan update
grand-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission's September 9 agenda included amendments to the county subdivision regulations and Planned Unit Development regulations, plus a Master Plan update. Commissioners set a public hearing on the subdivision regulation amendments for October 27.

grand-county/2.title: Devil's Thumb Ranch High Lonesome Lodge lot split
grand-county/2.summary: The Planning Commission unanimously recommended approval, with 14 conditions, of an outright exemption splitting a 44.33-acre parcel into an 8.82-acre lot with the existing lodge and a 32.60-acre lot for a possible single-family home. No public notice was required for this type of application.
grand-county/2.where: Devil's Thumb Ranch, Forestry and Open zone

grand-county/3.title: Good to Go portable toilet storage permit
grand-county/3.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a Special Use Permit request to store up to 200 clean, empty portable toilets on land in the Forestry and Open zone. Staff recommended conditional approval.
grand-county/3.where: Former Bergquist Outright Exemption property, Forestry and Open zone

grand-county/4.title: Building code appeals for two U.S. Highway 34 storage projects
grand-county/4.summary: The Board of Appeals was set to hear two appeals over how the county's adopted building code applies to Stillwater Storage and to the Storage at the Fort/Uplift Self Storage project.

grand-county/5.title: Departmental fee changes and Model Traffic Code amendment
grand-county/5.summary: Commissioners scheduled October 20 public hearings on changes to county departmental fees and on the second reading of Ordinance 23, amending the Model Traffic Code.

grand-county/6.title: St. Joseph's Foundation Retreat camping permit
grand-county/6.summary: Commissioners scheduled an October 20 public hearing on a Special Use Permit for camping at the St. Joseph's Foundation Retreat.

grand-county/7.title: Restoring Certified Local Government status for historic preservation
grand-county/7.summary: The Historic Preservation Board named restoring the county's Certified Local Government status an immediate priority, and the chair will contact History Colorado about requirements. The board also discussed historic inventories, landmark designations and a countywide preservation plan. A member of the public asked what properties qualify for designation.

grand-county/8.title: Water: drought preparedness MOU and water rights accounting
grand-county/8.summary: Commissioners were to consider a Drought Preparedness Memorandum of Understanding on October 20 and a water rights accounting contract with Rozaklis and Associates on October 27.

grand-county/9.title: Grand Lake Skijoring temporary use permit
grand-county/9.summary: A hearing on a temporary use permit for Colorado Skijoring, doing business as Grand Lake Skijoring, was continued from October 13 to October 27.

grand-junction/0.title: Temporary moratorium on large data centers
grand-junction/0.summary: Staff told Council on Sept. 14 that city code does not address data centers and their heavy power and water demands, with no applications pending. Council introduced a moratorium ordinance on Oct. 7 that would last until data center rules are adopted or 365 days pass, with a hearing set for Oct. 21.

grand-junction/1.title: 2027 budget and $6 million structural gap
grand-junction/1.summary: Staff reported a $6 million General Fund structural gap, with pressure from growth, rural fire/EMS costs and health insurance claims. The recommended 2027 budget is $317.4 million ($120.8 million General Fund), with about $2 million in personnel cuts, reduced Lincoln Park Pool hours, some housing programs moving to partners, and $2.7 million for six police officers and three fire battalion chiefs. Council continued review Oct. 26.

grand-junction/2.title: Significant Tree Ordinance removed from development code
grand-junction/2.summary: The Housing Affordability Code Task Force asked to remove the significant tree protections (sections 21.07.040 and 21.09.060(a)(1)) as a housing cost. Council heard the ordinance on Sept. 2 and, per the Forestry Board, voted to remove it, despite strong public support for keeping it. A consultant will look at code changes through December and a replacement may be considered.

grand-junction/3.title: Housing Affordability Code Task Force and code simplification
grand-junction/3.summary: The task force is reviewing the development code and TEDS street standards for housing costs, with consultant KLJ sorting possible amendments into four categories.
