Work is meant to wrap up, including hearings, in the first quarter of 2027, before the Comprehensive Plan update.

grand-junction/4.title: Housing Action Plan and Juniper Grove affordable homes at the Salt Flats
grand-junction/4.summary: Council reviewed a revised Housing Action Plan on Aug. 31, dropping a proposed Housing Advisory Board; the plan returns for a public hearing after state review. Council also took up selling about 3.3 acres of the city-owned Salt Flats at 450 28 Road to Grand Junction Homes for 48 for-sale affordable units (under 100% AMI), with the hearing continued to Sept. 16 and a funding agreement including $593,340 in water and sewer fee payments.

grand-junction/5.title: Galley Meadows rezone, 2590 Galley Lane and 675 26 Road
grand-junction/5.summary: Neighbors objected to the rezone of about 13.04 acres to RL-4 for Monument Homes and Cuesta Verde. They raised concerns over traffic, construction, lighting and the entrance location. The Planning Commission recommended approval and Council passed Ordinance 5341 on Sept. 16.

grand-junction/6.title: Annexations: 2911 D 1/2 Road and Redlands 360
grand-junction/6.summary: Council started annexation of 14.88 acres at 2911 D 1/2 Road, with Anthony Properties seeking MU-2 zoning, a Comprehensive Plan amendment and a circulation plan amendment; the hearing is set for Dec. 16. Council also began annexing rights-of-way around Redlands 360, whose planned development was expanded by about 29 acres to roughly 629 acres in August.

grand-junction/7.title: Materials Recovery Facility financing and Persigo sewer budget
grand-junction/7.summary: Council approved an additional $9.3 million in certificates of participation for the city's Materials Recovery Facility (Ordinance 5338). Separately, the proposed 2027 Persigo wastewater budget is $69.9 million, about $49.7 million of it capital, and Council moved toward a contract amendment for the plant's Phase 2 expansion.

grand-junction/8.title: Lincoln Park Barn and Certified Local Government
grand-junction/8.summary: The Historic Preservation Board discussed seeking Certified Local Government status, which could bring design review to historic districts. Members of the public asked the board to nominate the Lincoln Park Barn for designation, and members asked staff to schedule a special meeting on it. The board also commented to CDOT on I-70B impacts on historic resources.

grand-junction/9.title: Matchett Park Bike Park and parks capital funding
grand-junction/9.summary: A survey showed strong support for keeping the Matchett bike park. Given the city's budget problems, the parks board moved to hold off on further development there. Parks staff also warned that impact-fee revenue will drop from about $1.2 million to $758,000 in 2027.

grand-junction/10.title: Water supply planning and turf conversion vs. trees
grand-junction/10.summary: Staff presented a new Water Supply Element for the Comprehensive Plan required by SB 24-174, saying current supplies meet current and projected needs. The Forestry Board discussed how turf conversion can harm mature trees when owners stop irrigating.

grand-junction/11.title: 2324 Highway 6 and 50 rezone to commercial
grand-junction/11.summary: RAMS 1 Ho LLC asked to rezone 2.88 acres from I-1 to CG for a retail and office development in the 24 Road Overlay. The Planning Commission recommended approval, and Council set a hearing for Oct. 21.

grand-junction/12.title: Regional fire and EMS services and rural fire district
grand-junction/12.summary: Council discussed the long-term sustainability of the city's regional fire and EMS service. Staff plan to give the Rural Fire District the required two-year notice to renegotiate, and the city manager is pursuing a regional fire district.

grand-lake/0.title: 2027 Town budget and grant-funded contracts
grand-lake/0.summary: Trustees held a series of workshops on a preliminary 2027 budget built from the 2025 audit. It shows a General Fund deficit of about $589,184 after the Town's share of four grant contracts, with $2.87M of the $7.51M in General Fund revenue coming from grants. A public hearing is set for November 9 and final approval for November 23, 2026, with discussion of wages, benefits and a budget officer appointment.

greeley/0.title: Ballot measure for 0.60% sales tax for West Greeley and Civic Campus (Question 2F)
greeley/0.summary: Council moved to send voters a 0.60% sales and use tax increase (Jan 2027 through 2067) to fund capital projects tied to the West Greeley (Catalyst/Cascadia) and Civic Campus projects. Dozens of residents spoke against combining the projects with a tax, others supported a dedicated sales tax. Council reviewed legal advice in executive session and on Oct 6 considered a resolution supporting Question 2F on the Nov 3 ballot.

sources.body: West Greeley Project Citizen Oversight Committee

greeley/1.title: GlobalAI data center campus pre-annexation and interim water service
greeley/1.summary: Global AI (Colorado) LLC bought about 438 acres east of Highway 257 (former Kodak/Carestream campus) and is evaluating a data center. Council considered a pre-annexation agreement requiring annexation by March 31, 2028, and the Water and Sewer Board approved an interim water service agreement tied to it. Water service under the current agreement expires March 31, 2027.
greeley/1.where: East of State Highway 257, south of Eastman Park Drive

greeley/2.title: Great Western Industrial Park annexations and Windsor's reconsideration motion
greeley/2.summary: Council went into executive session to receive legal advice on Great Western Industrial Park annexations 1-15 and a Motion for Reconsideration from the Town of Windsor. Residents spoke at earlier meetings about the annexation's effects on services and a possible data center.

greeley/3.title: 2027 city budget, cuts and museum funding
greeley/3.summary: The City Manager's recommended 2027 budget (released Sept 4) followed a Sept 11 council retreat, with first reading Oct 20. It includes cuts, vacant positions eliminated and voluntary separations (67.75 FTE), a 25% reduction in capital maintenance, and proposed reductions to museum and Civic Center budgets. The Museum Board and Historic Preservation Commission objected to museum cuts, and residents raised budget concerns. A later note says $150,000 extra was added for CPRD museum funding.

sources.body: Union Colony Civic Center Advisory Board

greeley/4.title: Flock Safety license plate readers and police drones
greeley/4.summary: Residents repeatedly urged Council to end the Flock Safety ALPR contract, citing privacy, Fourth Amendment concerns, costs and no public vote. Council asked for a presentation, and a Sept 8 work session covered the police use of 17 Flock cameras with 30-day retention and the drones-as-first-responder program.

greeley/5.title: Civic Campus and Judicial Center redevelopment
greeley/5.summary: Council took up lease-purchase Certificates of Participation to finance the Civic Campus, a metropolitan district for West Greeley Commons, and a vacation of a public alley near 10th Ave, 11th Ave, 9th St and 10th St. Planning Commission reviewed subdivisions for the Judicial Center and Civic Campus, with a temporary juror lot and a new City Hall planned.
greeley/5.where: Downtown, between 9th and 10th Streets and 10th and 11th Avenues

greeley/6.title: Stormwater and water/sewer rates for 2027
greeley/6.summary: The Stormwater Board recommended a 10% increase for 2027 after staff showed 20% and 4.5% scenarios, amid downtown and 12th Street outfall work. The Water and Sewer Board reviewed a budget supporting a 4.5% water and 3.0% sewer increase, with the F Street facility delayed to limit rate impacts.

greeley/7.title: MERGE highway project and transportation safety
greeley/7.summary: The MERGE project (underpasses at 35th and 47th Avenues, roundabouts, over $50 million in federal grants) continues in design with significant property impacts, and a public art budget of up to $400,000 was proposed. The transportation committee also raised 16th Street speed transitions, crashes at US 34 and County Road 17, and the Safe Streets for All plan.

greeley/8.title: Arroyos del Sol annexation
greeley/8.summary: Planning Commission recommended approval of the roughly 999-acre Arroyos del Sol annexation northwest of Highway 257 and Weld County Road 19, with C-D conservation zoning, much of it under a conservation easement and planned for public recreation. A councilmember visited the new annexation area.
greeley/8.where: Northwest of State Highway 257 Spur, south of the Cache la Poudre River

greeley/9.title: Housing needs assessment, Prop 123 and federal housing funds
greeley/9.summary: Council considered a Housing Needs Assessment contract and a Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment. The Housing for All board reviewed the first CDBG/HOME cycle, noting unspent HUD funds hurt the city's entitlement, and the housing authorities took up voucher consolidation and 2027 plans.

greeley/10.title: Greeley Urban Renewal Authority and tax increment financing
greeley/10.summary: Council and GURA held a joint session on urban renewal law, TIF, bonding, and HB 1348 requirements, including possible links between the Greeley Mall TIF area and 17th Street. GURA later heard about a mobility hub and the Western Sugar multimodal project.

greeley/11.title: Halligan Water Supply Project legal action and water supply deals
greeley/11.summary: Council authorized the City Attorney to take legal action over the Clean Water Act Section 401 certification for the Halligan Water Supply Project. The Water and Sewer Board also took up groundwater rights adjudication, an augmentation lease and treatment plant master plans, and parks cut back watering at 13 sites.

greeley/12.title: 13th Street Quiet Zone and eminent domain
greeley/12.summary: Council considered an ordinance authorizing acquisition of property interests, including by eminent domain, for the 13th Street Quiet Zone project, along with 8th Street quiet zone work and a Sheep Draw Trail underpass grant at 83rd Ave.

green-mountain-falls/0.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption (Ordinance 2026-05)
green-mountain-falls/0.summary: The town introduced Ordinance 2026-05 on March 31 to meet a state mandate effective July 1, 2026, held a public hearing April 23, and approved it May 5 with a correction. In August the board approved changes replacing WUI references with the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. A resident objected to the penalties.

green-mountain-falls/1.title: Selling town land, open space rezoning and enclave annexation
green-mountain-falls/1.summary: The board has considered selling town properties, and in 2026 weighed rezoning town open space to park, which could make sales harder. The attorney presented a memo on annexing enclaves and the board sent it to the Planning Commission, with an update to the 1997 annexation plan on later agendas. A resident urged rezoning or an ordinance to protect open space.

green-mountain-falls/2.title: Sales tax increase ballot question for capital projects
green-mountain-falls/2.summary: Staff presented a 'Closing the Gap' plan for sidewalks, culverts, sewage, and pool, park and playground updates. On April 7 the mayor moved to put a 0.05% sales tax for four years on the ballot for the Capital Improvement Fund, with the old Marshal's building as a priority. Ballot and TABOR resolutions followed in May, and the general election was called in August.

green-mountain-falls/3.title: 2026 budget, fees, mill levy and 2027 draft budget
green-mountain-falls/3.summary: In December 2025 the town adopted the 2026 budget, fee schedule and mill levy certification. A March budget amendment raised Marshal's office wages and a 2026 fee schedule resolution was approved in May. Work sessions for the 2027 draft budget were being set up, with a draft on the October 8 agenda.

green-mountain-falls/4.title: Short-term rental tax and rules
green-mountain-falls/4.summary: In December 2025 the council took up Ordinance 2025-06 on a short-term rental tax and Ordinance 2025-09 amending short-term rental rules.

green-mountain-falls/5.title: Comprehensive Plan addendum and Community Redevelopment review
green-mountain-falls/5.summary: The town is updating its comprehensive plan with a 2026 addendum, with work sessions set for August 18 and further review on fall agendas. A CRA plan review was also scheduled in September. A resident stressed that the board should implement the plan's goals.

green-mountain-falls/6.title: Downtown parking, road base and paving
green-mountain-falls/6.summary: The town contracted for paving of about $96,000 focusing on parking near the Blue Moose and Lake Street. A Maple Street parking survey was pursued and trailhead parking raised. The paving was completed with 78 downtown parking spots.
green-mountain-falls/6.where: Downtown, Lake Street and Maple Street

green-mountain-falls/7.title: Wastewater, septic and drainage
green-mountain-falls/7.summary: The town discussed septic pumping near the Marshal's building and park at about $16,000, a wastewater feasibility study, and 2026 drainage improvements. Water rights attorney services were tabled until creek flows could be determined.

green-mountain-falls/8.title: El Paso trail property and Thomas Trail land sale list
green-mountain-falls/8.summary: The board requested an appraisal of the El Paso trail property and removed Thomas Trail from the land sale list. The mayor reported the Board of Health voted to remove the transfer of title resolution for El Paso, effective July 11.
green-mountain-falls/8.where: El Paso trail and Thomas Trail

green-mountain-falls/9.title: Election date change and Planning Commission role
green-mountain-falls/9.summary: The council approved Ordinance 2026-03 moving the election date from the first Tuesday of April. Ordinances 2026-01 and 2026-02 on Planning Commission and board responsibilities were discussed and tabled, after a resident asked that the commission be more involved.

green-mountain-falls/10.title: Pool, park restrooms and summer events
green-mountain-falls/10.summary: The board handled pool opening, Lake Street bathrooms, park restrooms, and event permits including Bronc Day fee waiver, 4th of July ($600 fee) and Green Box pool use ($1,200).

greenwood-village/0.title: Emergency permit parking districts near Cherry Creek High School
greenwood-village/0.summary: On August 3, 2026 Council passed emergency ordinances 08-26 and 09-26 expanding the Cherry Creek Village North permit parking district and creating one in Village on the Lake, ahead of a student parking shortage from the Cherry Creek High School rebuild. By October 5, police reported 88 warnings, 18 citations and about 125 households with permits, and Council discussed the districts again on October 19.
greenwood-village/0.where: Cherry Creek Village North and Village on the Lake neighborhoods

greenwood-village/1.title: 2027 budget and mill levy
greenwood-village/1.summary: Council held a public hearing on the 2027 budget and Capital Improvement Program, with Ordinances 12-26 (budget) and 13-26 (mill levy). First reading was October 19 and second reading was on the November 2 consent agenda. Staff presented an amended budget after the budget workshop, including $164,000 more for a citywide access control system.

greenwood-village/2.title: Grace Chapel special use permit at 8500 E. Orchard Road
greenwood-village/2.summary: Grace Chapel asked for a Special Use Permit and Site Development Plan to turn an existing building and parking lot into a place of worship, with 250 parking spaces and new LED lighting. The Planning and Zoning Commission recommended approval, staff found the criteria met, and Council held a quasi-judicial hearing on August 17.

greenwood-village/3.title: Electric vehicle charging station regulations
greenwood-village/3.summary: Staff asked Council whether to add EV charging rules to the Land Development Code, which currently has none. Options include screening of equipment and allowing chargers by right in most districts, and the discussion references state law HB24-1173. A proposal for four EV chargers at 7600 E. Orchard Road came before Planning and Zoning on September 15.

greenwood-village/4.title: Drone delivery regulations
greenwood-village/4.summary: Council was scheduled to discuss how to regulate commercial drone delivery on November 2. Staff surveyed other cities, including moratoriums in Castle Rock and Parker and special use permit rules in Northglenn, and options such as limits on parks and buffers around schools.

greenwood-village/5.title: Carson Park public art installation
greenwood-village/5.summary: The Arts and Humanities Council asked Council to approve fabrication and installation of three sculptures by Kevin Shaffer in Carson Park, tied to the park improvement project and the city's 75th anniversary. A public input meeting was held August 26, 2026, and the project was also on the October 15 Arts and Humanities Council agenda.

greenwood-village/6.title: High Line Canal irrigation phase two
greenwood-village/6.summary: Council considered a license agreement with Arapahoe County, which owns the land, for the second phase of irrigation along the High Line Canal, connecting to well water from Long Road to Steele to Garden Lane. Councilmembers asked about irrigating Curtis Park, which uses Denver Water and would need a large booster pump.
greenwood-village/6.where: High Line Canal, Long Rd to Garden Ln

greenwood-village/7.title: Side yard setback variances before the Board of Adjustments and Appeals
greenwood-village/7.summary: The board heard variance requests on side yard setbacks. One was a garage addition at a Monaco Heights PUD lot, where staff said the 20-foot setback applied and the request was not justified. Another was a north side yard addition on a 1959 home. A fence variance at 9150 E. Radcliff Ave was approved after a neighbor objected to a separate request.
greenwood-village/7.where: Monaco Heights PUD; 9150 E. Radcliff Ave

greenwood-village/8.title: Artificial intelligence use in city operations
greenwood-village/8.summary: Staff briefed Council on September 14 about a careful, staged approach to AI in municipal operations, focused on protecting sensitive information before any broader adoption.

gunnison-county/0.title: Lower Verzuh Ranch major impact sketch plan (LUC-25-00004)
gunnison-county/0.summary: Commissioners deliberated on the Lower Verzuh Ranch Subdivision sketch plan and whether to hold another public hearing. Commissioner Smith opposed a further hearing, while Commissioner Puckett Daniels wanted another hearing or more time; the board voted not to hold an additional hearing, and the decision was postponed to a later meeting.

gunnison-county/1.title: November 2026 ballot: 0.50% countywide sales tax for roads and bridges
gunnison-county/1.summary: On August 18 commissioners approved Resolution 2026-29 referring a 0.50% countywide sales tax to the November 3, 2026 ballot to fund roads, bridges and related transportation infrastructure. They also approved an agreement with the Clerk and Recorder for running the ballot question and said the funds would go only to road and bridge. The Road and Bridge budget was set for a work session on October 27.

gunnison-county/2.title: 2027 county budget draft and work sessions
gunnison-county/2.summary: On October 13 the chief finance officer presented the first draft of the 2027 budget. Commissioners asked for work sessions on Road & Bridge, Public Health, Human Services, the Housing Authority and Whetstone, and the Capital Improvement Plan. A public hearing was set for December 8 at 5:30 pm, and the board agreed to invite applications for a $10,000 late-night taxi request.

gunnison-county/3.title: Whetstone housing and Housing Authority budget amendment
gunnison-county/3.summary: The Housing Authority amended its 2026 budget and appropriation (Resolution 2026-005) for Whetstone because of how the bond documents work. Whetstone had permanent water onsite, and three units there are allocated to large family childcare. The Housing Authority and Whetstone business plan was also slated for a 2027 budget work session.

gunnison-county/4.title: Mineral Point property agreements
gunnison-county/4.summary: The Housing Authority and commissioners went into executive session on September 15 to get legal advice on proposed Mineral Point Property agreements and to develop negotiating strategy. No outcome is stated in the documents.

gunnison-county/5.title: Senior property tax exemption appeal (T. Haack)
gunnison-county/5.summary: On September 1 the Board of Equalization heard Teresa Haack's appeal of a denied senior property tax exemption. Staff said voter registration at another address determines primary residence, and the board voted to deny the appeal.

gunnison-county/6.title: Solid waste rate study
gunnison-county/6.summary: Commissioners approved awarding the Solid Waste Rate Study to Raftelis for $87,693 through Public Works.

gunnison-county/7.title: Cumberland Pass rehabilitation project grant application
gunnison-county/7.summary: Commissioners considered a resolution on a program application for the Gunnison County Cumberland Pass Rehabilitation Project, committing to implementation, matching funds and long-term commitments.

gunnison-county/8.title: Gunnison-Crested Butte Regional Airport pavement and contracts
gunnison-county/8.summary: The county approved a $719,737 airfield pavement maintenance construction agreement with Maxwell Asphalt, plus a contract change order, a Jviation amendment, and lease and concession amendments at the airport.

gunnison-county/9.title: Regional health, suicide prevention and early childhood programs
gunnison-county/9.summary: Commissioners heard updates on Whole Health Navigation, stigma reduction and the Regional Suicide Prevention effort, as well as early childhood scholarships that served 94 families. Human Services also discussed its fiscal year 2027 budget and reductions to meet federal guidelines.

gypsum/0.title: Automated license plate reader cameras and security cameras
gypsum/0.summary: Residents, including Eric Medina, pressed the Council on license plate reader cameras, asking for an independent investigation and raising possible legal claims. Staff presented on the Town's camera technology, the Council held a dedicated public comment period on ALPRs on Sept. 22, and a records request on the cameras came up in October. The contract with the Sheriff's Office was also discussed.

gypsum/1.title: Tower Center PUD amendment, Filing No. 2 plat and improvement agreements
gypsum/1.summary: Council approved Ordinance 10 amending the Tower Center PUD Guide after a public hearing on Aug. 11. Resolution 22 on the Filing No. 2 final plat and subdivision improvement agreements was tabled, then approved Aug. 25. Resolution 25 on assignment and assumption of the improvement agreement was approved Sept. 8.

gypsum/2.title: Lodging tax ballot question
gypsum/2.summary: Council approved Resolution 23 calling a special coordinated election on a Town lodging tax. Staff said it would replace the existing county tax rather than add a new one. A resident letter asked about the ballot measure and the ballot language was discussed.

gypsum/3.title: State collection of sales tax (Ordinance 11)
gypsum/3.summary: Council passed Ordinance 11 on first reading Aug. 11 and on second reading Aug. 25. It repeals and re-enacts the sales tax chapter to comply with state statutes and allow state collection of sales tax.

gypsum/4.title: 2027 budget and financial advisor
gypsum/4.summary: Staff are drafting the 2027 budget, and a resident asked that issues be considered in the upcoming budget talks. Council approved a Municipal Financial Advisor contract with UMB Financial Services for up to $50,000 and accepted the 2025 audit presentation.

gypsum/5.title: Siena Lake settlement with JPJG
gypsum/5.summary: A Denver resident, Rex Roberts, asked Council to consider a proposed settlement between the Town and JPJG related to the Siena Lake project.

gypsum/6.title: Changes to public comment policy
gypsum/6.summary: After the attorney reviewed the history and legal context, Council decided on Sept. 22 to move to a general public comment period at the start of each meeting. Mayor Green explained the changes Oct. 13, citing liability considerations.

gypsum/7.title: Clubhouse restoration change orders
gypsum/7.summary: Council approved Change Order 2 ($241,269.06) and Change Order 3 with A.J. Construction for the clubhouse renovation. By Sept. 8 the project was complete except for a final punch list.

gypsum/8.title: Water system: Cooley Mesa pump station generator and Mosher plant
gypsum/8.summary: Council awarded the Cooley Mesa Pump Station backup generator contract to Pinnacle Electric for $131,183.68. A lightning strike at the Mosher water plant was reported, and water use was reported down 20 percent from last year.
gypsum/8.where: Cooley Mesa Road; Mosher water plant

gypsum/9.title: I-70 Eagle Airport Interchange grant application
gypsum/9.summary: Council authorized an application to the FHWA PROTECT grant program for planning and design of the I-70 Eagle Airport Interchange project.

gypsum/10.title: Fire restrictions and wildfire planning
gypsum/10.summary: Council confirmed moving from Stage 2 to Stage 1 fire restrictions on Sept. 8, and approved another administrative order Oct. 13. Wildland fire officials are scheduled to give a fall update and 2027 plan.

gypsum/11.title: Amazon facility public improvements dedication
gypsum/11.summary: Council is scheduled to consider Resolution 30 accepting dedication of public improvements for the Amazon facility.

gypsum/12.title: Street chipseal and recycling center change orders
gypsum/12.summary: Council approved Change Order 2 with A-1 Chipseal ($14,570.63) for the 2025/26 street renovations. It also approved change orders 1-3 for the Recycling Center ($28,598.27, shared with Eagle County).

haxtun/0.title: Electric rate increase (Ordinance 2025-2)
haxtun/0.summary: Council adopted Ordinance 2025-2 amending Section 54.20 of the municipal code to raise residential and commercial electric rates, citing cost increases from MEAN and WAPA. All present voted in favor.

haxtun/1.title: 2026 budget and mill levy adoption
haxtun/1.summary: After a public hearing with no public comment, council adopted the 2026 budget and appropriations (Resolutions 2025-9 and 2025-10), including a general property tax levy and funds for water and sewer. Discussion touched on a crack-fill machine for streets and a supplemental fund to be handled once the generator project price is complete.

haxtun/2.title: MEAN wholesale power service agreement renewal
haxtun/2.summary: MEAN is restructuring its service contract procedures, requiring each municipality to sign a new agreement because current contracts expire January 1, 2026. Council voted to approve the new service agreement.

haxtun/3.title: 2026 employee health insurance increase
haxtun/3.summary: Public Sector Health notified the Town of an 18% rate increase for 2026 employee health insurance. Council acknowledged similar increases may recur and said alternative options may need to be considered next year.

hayden/0.title: Data center moratorium study and citizen committee
hayden/0.summary: Town Council said a citizen committee for the data center moratorium study will be announced shortly. Council also asked staff to draft letters to state and federal representatives about data center bills and related legislation.

hayden/1.title: Council endorsement of 2026 ballot measures (fire district, school district, CMC, regional transit)
hayden/1.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-14 endorsing Measure 6A (West Routt Fire mill levy override), 4B (annexing Hayden RE-1 into Colorado Mountain College District), 7A (half-percent sales tax for Yampa Valley Regional Transportation Authority) and 4A (Hayden RE-1 mill levy override). Councilmember Haight objected to the transit language and moved to remove it; a separate Resolution 2026-16 on Measure 7A also came up on Oct. 15.

hayden/2.title: 2027-2029 draft budget and property tax
hayden/2.summary: The Town Council, Housing Authority and Northwest Colorado GID were presented the 2027-2029 draft budget in October. Town budget materials show a 25.067 mill operating levy and 3.990 mill debt service levy, about $1.54 million in budgeted property tax revenue, and a forecast of sales tax near $2.35 million.

hayden/3.title: New road from business park to Highway 40 and hotel lot
hayden/3.summary: The Northwest Colorado GID heard about design work to start a new road from the business park to Highway 40. The GID is also closing on another business park lot intended for a hotel.

hayden/4.title: Pickleball court and 3rd Street Park
hayden/4.summary: The Parks and Recreation Board discussed creating an outdoor pickleball court, possibly splitting the court, with an estimated cost of $260,000 and a search for grants. 3rd Street Park updates were a recurring item.

hayden/5.title: Emergency fee schedule change and new animal ordinance
hayden/5.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-15 adopting an emergency fee schedule change, and held a second reading and public hearing on Ordinance 752 adopting new animal rules and conforming amendments to Section 14.20.040. No public comment was given at the hearing.

hayden/6.title: Housing Authority rents and grants
hayden/6.summary: The Hayden Municipal Housing Authority noted rent increases expected to start August 1 at $900, with grants pending.

hayden/7.title: Parks & Rec events and Hayden Center planning
hayden/7.summary: The Parks and Recreation Board reviewed event plans such as the farmers market (possible October pumpkin date), food trucks and vendor fees, along with a $5,000 grant and bylaws changes for members who move. The board also discussed budget ideas and Hayden Center updates.

hooper/0.title: 2026 budget, property tax levy and attorney contract
hooper/0.summary: At the December 3, 2025 meeting the Town held a public hearing on the 2026 budget. Trustees were also set to consider Resolutions 6, 7 and 8-2025 to adopt the budget, levy property taxes and appropriate funds. The agenda also listed an attorney contract rate increase and a legal services contract (Resolution 5-2025).

hooper/1.title: Town park safety concerns and 2026 park improvements
hooper/1.summary: Ramona Smith presented park safety concerns in December 2025. In March 2026 the Board planned to discuss a 2026 park grant led by Trustee Mimi Dolan, hiring a park and town maintenance employee, and placing a library box in the town park.

hooper/2.title: Public nuisance and ground fowl ordinances
hooper/2.summary: The March 18, 2026 agenda included Ordinance 1-2026 amending public nuisance provisions and Ordinance 2-2026 amending standards for ground fowl in the municipal code.

hooper/3.title: 2026 regular town election
hooper/3.summary: Resolution 4-2025 on the December 2025 agenda called the town's regular election.

hotchkiss/0.title: Drought restrictions, water moratorium and bulk water standpipe
hotchkiss/0.summary: In February the board passed an emergency ordinance (2026-01) pausing new out-of-town water taps and limiting sales from the town standpipe. In April and May it discussed drought restrictions, Resolution 2026-04, and raising bulk water rates to $12 per thousand gallons outside the 81419 ZIP code. Water rates and the standpipe were sent to a separate work session.

hotchkiss/1.title: Hiring a permanent Town Administrator and new Town Attorney
hotchkiss/1.summary: The board worked with KRW Associates on a search for a permanent Town Administrator, with executive sessions in May and June. Kimberly States was in the job by July, and Ordinance 2026-04 set out the office's powers. The board also sought proposals for a new town attorney and had the contract reviewed. Sarah Ross was serving as attorney by July.

hotchkiss/2.title: Proposed park on Bridge Street lots and skate park request
hotchkiss/2.summary: Don Foster proposed a park on the empty lots at 171 and 191 E Bridge Street, and the board agreed to form a working group in August. Resident Larry Wilkening opposed it and said the land should host a revenue-generating business. Tanner Wilson asked the town to consider a skate park, and the town offered a letter of support.

hotchkiss/3.title: Ordinance 2026-07 on demonstrations and special events in public rights-of-way
hotchkiss/3.summary: The board took up an ordinance setting content-neutral safety, access and permit requirements for demonstrations and special events on public rights-of-way. Residents commented, and the board approved it on August 27. In September the parade permit process had to change, and the board waived the permit for the North Fork Miners homecoming parade.

hotchkiss/4.title: Staff wage study and benefits
hotchkiss/4.summary: Graves Consulting presented a wage compensation study, with implementation proposed for June 1, 2026 and no increase to the 2026 budget. Staff also proposed more vacation time and insurance improvements costing $3,000 to $5,000. Trustee Sven Edstrom said there was too much information to decide on that night.

hotchkiss/5.title: Wildland-Urban Interface Code and wildfire planning
hotchkiss/5.summary: Ordinance 2026-03 adopting a Wildland-Urban Interface Code came to a public hearing in July, with a fire-risk map covering the whole town. The Western Slope Conservation Center presented a Wildfire Ready Action Plan in December. Staff also noted a wildfire near the town's water source could cut off supply, and talks are underway to fund a study.

hotchkiss/6.title: Variance requests: drive-thru lot and parking, sheds and fences
hotchkiss/6.summary: In November the board tabled a variance for a nonconforming lot at 6th Street for a drive-thru, sending the applicant back for a documented parking agreement with City Market. Neighbors raised parking concerns. In June it considered variances for a shed at 159 E Orchard, an 8-foot fence at 791 Barrow Mesa Road, and a 6-foot fence at 319 Knob Hill Circle Drive.
hotchkiss/6.where: 6th Street; 159 E Orchard; 791 Barrow Mesa Road; 319 Knob Hill Circle Drive

hotchkiss/7.title: Master Plan and housing
hotchkiss/7.summary: The town worked with Urban Rural Continuum on a new Master Plan, and the Planning Commission approved the final plan in April. Trustees also discussed the difficulty of finding housing in town.

hotchkiss/8.title: Sidewalk repair funding
hotchkiss/8.summary: A resident said no progress had been made on sidewalk repairs since a 2022 rating of sidewalks. He suggested a utility bill fee that would need voter approval.

hotchkiss/9.title: Police vehicles and Police Department policies
hotchkiss/9.summary: The board discussed transferring police vehicles in exchange for tuition at Technical College of the Rockies. It directed the chief to seek a contract amendment so the town avoids extra tuition costs. In September the board approved revisions to the Police Department vehicle use policy.

hotchkiss/10.title: Trustee compensation ordinance
hotchkiss/10.summary: After a work session discussion, the board passed Emergency Ordinance 2026-02 on trustee pay in March. It was set to take effect before the next election, with pay aligned with other valley towns.

hotchkiss/11.title: DMEA broadband franchise and telecom purchase
hotchkiss/11.summary: A franchise agreement with DMEA concerning broadband was planned for January. In July the board considered Ordinance 2026-05, a franchise agreement for the purchase of Delta County Tele-Com.

hudson/0.title: Prestige Builder Group settlement for Canterbury Meadows development
hudson/0.summary: Council held a public hearing on Resolution 26-118, a settlement of litigation and a multi-million-dollar claim with Prestige Builder Group over about 94.56 acres on Ravenna Street and Stow Road, to be developed as a 32-lot conservation subdivision. Neighbors and an attorney objected, citing water runoff, a high water table, and bypassing the Planning Commission. The Planning Commission has separately discussed the agreement and asked for its own legal counsel.

hudson/1.title: Clinton Crossing downtown redevelopment plan
hudson/1.summary: Council and staff are working toward a concept site plan for Clinton Crossing, with three refined plans, a market hall, and possible single-family, townhome and duplex housing. Some council members and residents oppose apartments. In October, council heard about financing tools including a TIF, New Community Authority, special or business improvement district and a downtown redevelopment district. The Planning Commission was to get an introduction to the concept plan.

hudson/2.title: Low-speed vehicle rules (Ordinance 26-113, Chapter 478)
hudson/2.summary: Council is amending Chapter 478 of the codified ordinances on low-speed vehicles such as golf carts. Residents objected that the draft bans travel on 35 MPH roads and questioned the rules on lights and equipment. The ordinance had its first reading on Aug. 11 and a second on Aug. 18, with further amendments proposed.

hudson/3.title: 2027 budget and 2027-2031 five-year capital plan
hudson/3.summary: Council reviewed the 2027-2031 capital plan and the 2027 capital budget, covering streets, stormwater, sidewalks, trails, debt service and many funds. Council also discussed which unfunded projects to prioritize, including Fiber-to-the-Home, stormwater and the Barlow Road sidewalk, as income tax revenue shifted after a business departure. Council also accepted the county Budget Commission's property tax rates.

hudson/4.title: Hudson Innovation Park at 996 Hines Hill Road
hudson/4.summary: Staff updated council on the innovation park site, including relocating the salt barn, excess soil on site, property tax abatement options, and improvements to Hines Hill Road. Council asked for a document on what an abatement would entail and estimated road costs. A resolution on excess soils from the public works facility was on a later workshop agenda.

hudson/5.title: Short-term rental rules (Ordinance 26-78, Chapter 876)
hudson/5.summary: Council is working on amendments to the short-term rental policy in Chapter 876, after workshops from March to May. The ordinance was postponed to a date certain of November 10, 2026, and a draft with a councilor's amendment was circulated.

hudson/6.title: Fiber-to-the-Home construction rules and broadband
hudson/6.summary: Council considered an ordinance on construction methods such as directional drilling, vacuum excavation and utility safety, with concern about added cost and delay to the Velocity Broadband schedule. A motion to suspend the rules failed, so the ordinance requires three readings. Fiber-to-the-Home also competes for funds in capital planning.

hudson/7.title: Fire and EMS full-time staffing and Senior Van
hudson/7.summary: Fire and EMS renovations and full-time staffing began in August, with 24/7 coverage starting the Monday after the Aug. 18 meeting. A Senior Van service was to start Sept. 2.

hudson/8.title: Downtown Phase II property financing and Maple Grove Park lease
hudson/8.summary: Council took up ordinances to issue $740,000 and $925,000 in bond anticipation notes tied to former Windstream properties at 94 and 100 Owen Brown Street bought for Downtown Phase II. Council also considered ending the lease with Summit Metro Parks for Maple Grove Park.
hudson/8.where: Owen Brown Street; Maple Grove Park

hudson/9.title: Townhome project at Clinton Street and Morse Road, 86 Owen Brown Street
hudson/9.summary: The Historic Board of Review reviewed a Fairmont townhome project, reduced from 22 to 18 units, and a denial of its design is being appealed to the Board of Zoning & Building Appeals. Staff also noted variances granted earlier.
hudson/9.where: 86 Owen Brown Street, Clinton Street and Morse Road

hudson/10.title: Appeal over unpermitted door at 88 N Main Street
hudson/10.summary: The property owner appealed a historic board decision over a door installed without a permit. His attorney challenged the legality of an executive session and sought a remand or continuance. The case returned to the Historic Board in September and October.

hudson/11.title: Standard Shop Company site plan nearing expiration
hudson/11.summary: The industrial business park project, approved in 2020 and still under construction, faces approval expiring in October 2026. Planning Commission members asked for proof of financing, a bond, and design fixes.

hudson/12.title: Brandywine Creek watershed study and stormwater projects
hudson/12.summary: Council reviewed the final draft Brandywine Creek Watershed Study, which ranks recommended capital projects. Stormwater work also includes Ellsworth Meadows golf course drainage and retaining wall projects.

hudson/13.title: Barlow Road sidewalk and railroad crossing exemption
hudson/13.summary: Council agreed to ask PUCO for an exemption for the W. Barlow Road railroad tracks. Staff also sought a contract with GAI Consultants to redesign the Barlow Road sidewalk, and council discussed the Walk and Bike Plan ranking.

huerfano-county/0.title: GroAway LLC conditional use permit (LU-26-000154)
huerfano-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on Sept. 10 on a conditional use permit for GroAway, LLC, then continued it twice to Oct. 8 and Oct. 22 while it weighed new materials, public comments received after the hearing and a Colorado Parks and Wildlife letter. The permit went to the county commissioners' Oct. 27 agenda; the documents do not state the outcome.

huerfano-county/1.title: Affordable housing: pre-approved home plans, Prop 123 down payment aid and revolving loan fund
huerfano-county/1.summary: The county is building housing tools. These include pre-approved single-family house plans (tiny home, barndominium, ranch and traditional), a Prop 123 Down Payment Assistance Program, an Affordable Housing Revolving Loan Fund with Impact Development Fund, and a resolution codifying the Housing Authority, which had been dormant since 2021. Commissioners approved Resolutions 26-43 and 26-44, and a land banking, acquisition and donation policy (26-45). A resident asked how the loan program and applications would work.

huerfano-county/2.title: Camping ordinance (Ordinance 26-04)
huerfano-county/2.summary: Commissioners took up Ordinance 26-04 regulating camping in the county, with discussion about the ordinance and camping rights. It was approved on first reading in August and on second reading Sept. 15.

huerfano-county/3.title: 2027 county budget
huerfano-county/3.summary: County Administrator Carl Young presented a preliminary 2027 budget with a 3.6% cost of living raise for all employees and market adjustments capped at $4,000 in Human Services and Road and Bridge. He warned that inflation, fuel prices and jail costs for housing prisoners elsewhere are straining County General and Road and Bridge. A balanced budget presentation was held Oct. 15.

huerfano-county/4.title: Recreation and cultural mill levy and voter survey
huerfano-county/4.summary: Magellan Strategies presented a county voter survey touching on parks and rec and jail renovation projects. Commissioners then approved Resolution 26-34 on a Recreation and Cultural Mill Levy, with Commissioner Wardell explaining the projects behind it.

huerfano-county/5.title: Gardner water augmentation, sewer project and Gardner revitalization plans
huerfano-county/5.summary: Commissioners approved lease-purchase financing for eight acre-feet of water augmentation for the Gardner Public Improvement District and three acre-feet for Road and Bridge. The Gardner Sewer Project bid tabulation was also before the board. Commissioners also approved the Gardner Main Street Revitalization Plan and the Rio Cucharas CRA Plan.

huerfano-county/6.title: Fox Theater Walsenburg loan guaranty
huerfano-county/6.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 26-41, guaranteeing a First Southwest Bank loan for the Fox Theater tied to tax credit sales, and a follow-up Resolution 26-48 guaranty on Oct. 20. A change order with McKinstry for the Fox Theater was also approved.

huerfano-county/7.title: Wildfire protection, fire restrictions and forest grants
huerfano-county/7.summary: The county moved from Stage 2 to Stage 1 fire restrictions in August and lifted Stage 1 in October. Commissioners approved the 2026 Community Wildfire Protection Plan, an amended Community Wildfire Defense Grant subaward, and letters of support for forest restoration and wildfire risk mitigation grants, including Blackhawk Ranch and the Huerfano Ember Shield Coalition.

huerfano-county/8.title: Cuchara Mountain Park: liquor license denial and ski pond dam study
huerfano-county/8.summary: The Liquor License Authority recommended against a special event liquor license for Cuchara Mountain Park. Commissioners also approved a $10,600 geotechnical services agreement for the Ski Pond Dam, with budget questions raised.

huerfano-county/9.title: Marijuana license for ISO99, LLC and water use concerns
huerfano-county/9.summary: A public hearing on Marijuana License ML-26-000008 for ISO99, LLC drew a citizen question about water restrictions and drought. The applicant provided proof of city water taps and past water bills, and the license was approved with conditions.

huerfano-county/10.title: School Creek Gravel Pit conditional use permit
huerfano-county/10.summary: The Planning Commission held a long public hearing on LU-26-000122, the School Creek Gravel Pit, and approved it with a recommendation to go to the county commissioners.

huerfano-county/11.title: Spanish Peaks Regional Airport projects and budget
huerfano-county/11.summary: The airport advisory board discussed the Turnaround Taxiway project, a 10-year capital improvement plan, possible land acquisition advised by the FAA, and an airport budget running in the red. Members also voiced frustration over commercial tax assessments.
huerfano-county/11.where: Spanish Peaks Regional Airport, County Road 101

huerfano-county/12.title: Tourism board budget, EV charger map and Enchanted Outpost ad
huerfano-county/12.summary: The Tourism Board reviewed lodging tax revenue, finalized the 2027 budget, approved a $3,560.75 Enchanted Outpost winter ad, and discussed an EV charger location map and the 2027 sponsorship program. Megan Rutter was appointed Director of Tourism and Bob Kennemer to the board.

huerfano-county/13.title: Trash dumping, Road and Bridge staffing and Gardner community center upkeep
huerfano-county/13.summary: The sheriff raised illegal trash dumping and the administrator discussed strengthening the ordinance; a resident asked about dumpsters. Road and Bridge also saw a superintendent change. Safe Streets and road conditions came up at the Raymond Aguirre Community Center board.

sources.body: Raymond Aguirre Community Center Advisory Board
Raymond Aguirre Community Center Advisory Board
Raymond Aguirre Community Center Advisory Board

hugo/0.title: Water restrictions and water share shortage
hugo/0.summary: Hugo went to Level One water restrictions to stay within its state water allocations, after LAWMA explained the Town owns only common shares. The Town leased two preferred shares, replaced the restriction ordinance (Ordinance 300), and passed emergency Ordinance 302 on watering hours and days after a resident objected to three-days-in-a-row watering. Restrictions lifted October 1.

hugo/1.title: Water system improvements, loans and grants
hugo/1.summary: The Town approved a Colorado Water Resources and Power Development Authority loan of up to $5,395,767 for water facilities. It also held CDBG and WPCRF hearings on the Water System Improvements Project, with design underway for water tank repairs, well pump replacements and other GMS-managed work. Board also approved a sewer lift station purchase for Roundhouse Estates and project draws.

hugo/2.title: Water, sewer and trash rates and 2027 fee schedule
hugo/2.summary: The Town is working with Colorado Rural Water Association on a rate study. Resolutions 2026-13 and 2026-14 would set water, wastewater and refuse rates and a fee schedule effective January 1, 2027. GMS also was approved to do a tap fee study and impact fees were discussed for new development.

hugo/3.title: Proposed 1% sales tax for pool, culture and recreation
hugo/3.summary: The Town held a community meeting on November 12 about a possible 1% sales tax for the pool, culture, recreation and capital improvements. It was slated for the ballot as Ballot Issue #2 in January discussions.

hugo/4.title: 2027 budget and strategic plan
hugo/4.summary: The Town scheduled a 2027 budget review and workshop for October 19 where the draft Strategic Plan will also be reviewed. A 2025 audit presentation was set for October 13.

hugo/5.title: Hugo Main Street program
hugo/5.summary: The Town is exploring running Hugo Main Street under the Town and recruiting board members. A steering committee works with Colorado Main Street and the Board approved a resolution supporting Hugo becoming an official Main Street Community.

hugo/6.title: New firehouse and Fire Protection District land
hugo/6.summary: A new firehouse plan was presented in March. The Board disconnected tracts owned by the Hugo Fire Protection District via Ordinance 301 and waived one water and one sewer tap at 5th Street and 9th Avenue. Earlier the Board declined to add the fire department driveway to the CDOT sidewalk project.

hugo/7.title: Code enforcement, trash and property ordinance updates
hugo/7.summary: Hugo adopted ordinances on penalties for violations and code enforcement authority, and contracted Willdan for code enforcement services. A trash ordinance revision is coming in August and staff are applying for a DOLA Local Planning Capacity Grant for an abandoned and dilapidated property ordinance. The Board also approved an automated vehicle identification system ordinance.

hugo/8.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code (Ordinance 295)
hugo/8.summary: The Board tabled Ordinance 295, which would adopt the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code by reference; a trustee said the town learned late about its effect.

hugo/9.title: Housing: Housing Authority, expedited review and new housing
hugo/9.summary: The Hugo Housing Authority sought grant help for plumbing repairs and is working toward compliance with new staff. The Board adopted Resolution 2026-07 on expedited review for affordable housing projects. County economic development reports on possible new housing and DOLA demo funding.

hugo/10.title: Street repair and CDOT sidewalk project
hugo/10.summary: A pavement study is planned to set a street maintenance plan, and the Board approved a pothole repair proposal from Millan Asphalt & Crushing. The CDOT Sidewalk Project was waiting on asphalt approvals.

hugo/11.title: Main Street Live building survey and geotechnical work
hugo/11.summary: The Board directed OLC to proceed with survey and geotechnical evaluation depending on the Colorado Historical Grant outcome; work was in progress by October.

hugo/12.title: Parks, playground and football field safety
hugo/12.summary: Staff are seeking quotes and grants for playground equipment, and the Board approved a BYO Recreation proposal. Concerns about children playing on a hard football field led to direction to the Clerk.

hugo/13.title: Backflow prevention program
hugo/13.summary: Colorado Rural Water Association reviewed the state backflow program, found many businesses were not inventoried, and a resident raised concerns about installing a device at the RV Park.

idaho-springs/0.title: Carlson Elementary / 1300 Colorado Blvd 50-unit affordable housing plan denied
idaho-springs/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on a Final Development Plan (FDP26-001) for a 50-unit affordable multifamily development at the old Carlson Elementary site. Residents wrote in and spoke about parking, building size and historic design standards. Council's Aug. 10 agenda included Resolution #15 formally denying the plan.

idaho-springs/1.title: Roberts Brothers Garage: Clear Creek Center for Arts & Education fee waivers and contributions
idaho-springs/1.summary: The arts center has a $1.538 million state grant that needs a 1:1 match and has about $700,000 in hand. It asked the city for in-kind contributions and fee waivers worth up to $729,307. Council took up Resolution #27 granting fee waivers for the 121 15th Avenue redevelopment. Parking arrangements and a parking fee-in-lieu request also came up, and Ordinance #20 would designate the property as historic.

idaho-springs/2.title: Recreational occupation tax on outdoor recreation providers
idaho-springs/2.summary: Council considered Ordinance #19 referring a ballot measure to voters for a new occupation tax on outdoor recreation outfitters, with revenue dedicated to impacts such as streets, parking, public safety and water. The tax could be up to $5 per customer and would be paid by the provider. Rafting businesses brought requests about the tax to Council in October.

idaho-springs/3.title: Downtown parking: paid parking moratorium, parking study and library parking
idaho-springs/3.summary: Council considered Ordinance #18, a temporary moratorium on permits for private paid parking facilities. Planning staff presented preliminary parking study results, and Council had a parking requirements study on its Sept. 28 agenda. Residents asked for free parking to be returned at the Library and for Disabled Veteran plates to get free managed parking. In October the parking enterprise's name and scope were being amended.

idaho-springs/4.title: Two-way traffic on downtown Miner Street
idaho-springs/4.summary: Council was asked on Oct. 26 to approve two-way vehicle traffic on downtown Miner Street. The Miner Street Market was scheduled to run through Halloween, with the street reopening to traffic Nov. 5.

idaho-springs/5.title: 2027 city budget
idaho-springs/5.summary: The proposed 2027 budget was described as extremely difficult to prepare. It moves community promotion costs to the Parking Fund and pauses some employee benefits, and General Fund revenue is projected to be only about $100,000 above 2024. The city's property tax share falls from $282,237 to $267,546 at the same 6.310 mill rate. The promotions board recommended a $211,109 baseline budget.

idaho-springs/6.title: Affordable and senior housing incentives, Prop 123 and Fair Housing code changes
idaho-springs/6.summary: Council worked on affordable housing incentives, an Affordable Senior Housing Project, and a DOLA predevelopment funding application. It also covered its Proposition 123 commitment for 2027-2029. Ordinance #17 amends the city code on housing for people with disabilities to conform with state and federal Fair Housing law, and a group homes code amendment was also discussed.

idaho-springs/7.title: 2026 Comprehensive Plan adoption
idaho-springs/7.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the draft and held a hearing on a resolution recommending the 2026 Comprehensive Plan. Council took it up again in a September discussion and approved it by resolution on Oct. 26.

idaho-springs/8.title: Noise ordinance with decibel limits
idaho-springs/8.summary: The city code sets no maximum decibel level, so police have no objective standard to enforce. Staff proposed adding decibel limits by zone, measured at the property line, with a professional dB reader. Council discussed this in August and September.

idaho-springs/9.title: Golddigger Park and Fieldhouse development park conveyance
idaho-springs/9.summary: Council considered accepting a new park conveyed by the Fieldhouse development, and Resolution #29 accepts Lot 3 of the former Golddigger Field subdivision as a city park named Golddigger Park. A related minor subdivision of Lots 1-12 to create a fourth lot was heard by the Planning Commission and Council. A neighbor also raised concerns about apartments at the Field House.

idaho-springs/10.title: Water use and city landscaping during restrictions
idaho-springs/10.summary: A resident told the Planning Commission the city should follow the residential water restrictions, citing the waterfall running, sprinklers on city property and water running down the street. She urged native plant landscaping.

idaho-springs/11.title: I-70 Floyd Hill project and Exit 240 agreement
idaho-springs/11.summary: Council received an I-70 Floyd Hill project update. It also considered Resolution #18 approving an agreement for a project near Exit 240, tied to a downtown RAISE planning grant.

idaho-springs/12.title: Stop signs and traffic complaints
idaho-springs/12.summary: A resident asked for stop signs at 16th Avenue and Colorado Blvd, citing increased traffic.

jefferson-county/0.title: Rezoning for up to 143 homes (case 25-122535RZ)
jefferson-county/0.summary: A request to rezone land from Agricultural-Two and Commercial-One to Planned Development for a maximum of 143 dwelling units went to the Planning Commission on Aug. 12. On Sept. 1 the commissioners approved it by majority vote (Resolution CC26-234) after staff, applicant and public testimony.

jefferson-county/1.title: Red Rocks Amphitheatre transportation hub
jefferson-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission was set to review a site plan for a transportation hub with 397 parking spaces, roadway improvements and grading to serve Red Rocks Amphitheatre on Oct. 14.
jefferson-county/1.where: 17355 Jurassic Road and 17900 Trading Post Road, Golden

jefferson-county/2.title: 2027 proposed county budget and 2026 supplemental appropriations
jefferson-county/2.summary: The commissioners received the 2027 proposed budget presentation on Oct. 27. They also handled August and September supplementary budget and appropriation resolutions for 2026, and reviewed budget practices in a closed legal session on Aug. 24.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Special Meeting

jefferson-county/3.title: Affordable housing, Prop 123 and private activity bonds
jefferson-county/3.summary: The county worked on a Proposition 123 unit-sharing agreement with Denver and Arvada, and assigned its 2026 private activity bond allocation for the Belveron project. Staff gave an annual update on the 15-year affordable housing plan, and a supplemental funding request for the Prop 123 expedited review incentive was briefed on Oct. 20.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/4.title: Lakewood Navigation Center operating costs agreement
jefferson-county/4.summary: On Oct. 13 the board unanimously approved an agreement on operating costs for the Lakewood Navigation Center and a memorandum of understanding with Arvada, Edgewater, Golden, Lakewood, Westminster and Wheat Ridge.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/5.title: Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport leases and Taxiway D project
jefferson-county/5.summary: The county approved the Winston Air hangar ground lease and the Premier Hangar Group ground leases, and amended its airport lease agreement policy. It also awarded Amrize West Central the Taxiway D Phase II reconstruction contract.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/6.title: Junction Urban Renewal Plan TIF revenue sharing
jefferson-county/6.summary: Commissioners held closed-door advice sessions and received a presentation on negotiating how tax-increment revenue from The Junction urban renewal plan would be shared.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/7.title: Positions on 2026 ballot measures
jefferson-county/7.summary: At a Sept. 23 special meeting the board took support and oppose positions on several state and local measures. These included support for Amendment 87 (graduated income tax) and the Front Range Passenger Rail District measure 7A, and opposition to Amendment 84 (mail ballot voter ID). Some resolutions passed by majority rather than unanimous vote.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Special Meeting

jefferson-county/8.title: Parks and open space projects
jefferson-county/8.summary: The county approved a Meyer Ranch Park forestry contract and a $3.2 million North Table Mountain Park improvement purchase order. It also handled easements, a West 32nd Ave and Kipling bus stop agreement with trails funding, and agreements at Van Bibber, Hildebrand Ranch and Long Lake parks.
jefferson-county/8.where: Meyer Ranch, North Table Mountain, Hildebrand Ranch and Van Bibber parks

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/9.title: Wildfire, pine beetle and hazard mitigation
jefferson-county/9.summary: Commissioners stressed wildfire resilience and evacuation planning, and hosted the statewide Ponderosa pine beetle task force. Staff briefed the 2026 Hazard Mitigation Plan for adoption on Oct. 27, and the board approved the Conifer and Elk Creek fire districts' 2024 fire codes.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/10.title: Head Start funding and expansion
jefferson-county/10.summary: The county approved Head Start policy updates and a continuation grant application, and commissioners backed the program's expansion in Lakewood. The board also prepared a public comment on proposed federal changes to Head Start performance standards.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/11.title: Preliminary and final plat hearing (case 24-114721PFP)
jefferson-county/11.summary: This plat was pulled from the consent agenda at the public's request. After staff, applicant and public testimony, the board unanimously approved Resolution CC26-266 on Sept. 29.

jefferson-county/12.title: Special district service plan (case 25-124167SV)
jefferson-county/12.summary: After continuing the case from July 28, the board unanimously approved a special district service plan on Aug. 18 following public testimony.

jefferson-county/13.title: Evergreen High School shooting anniversary
jefferson-county/13.summary: On Sept. 15 the sheriff and a congressional representative spoke on the one-year anniversary of the Evergreen High School shooting. The commissioners recognized the Evergreen community.

jefferson-county/14.title: County manager and county attorney appointments
jefferson-county/14.summary: The board appointed a county manager and approved her employment agreement on Aug. 11. It later approved a second amendment to the county attorney's contract on Oct. 13.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

johnstown/0.title: Property tax mill levy cut of 8 mills and the FY 2027 budget
johnstown/0.summary: Staff's preliminary FY 2027 budget keeps the full 23.947-mill levy, citing falling property tax revenue. Council then took up Ordinance 2026-299, which would permanently cut the levy by 8.000 mills in four annual steps of 2.000 mills, with any later increase needing voter approval. The 2027 proposed budget was on the Nov. 2 agenda, and a resident asked for trees at Clearview Park in it.

johnstown/1.title: Stormwater rate study and master plan
johnstown/1.summary: The Stormwater Utility fee has stayed at $5 per equivalent residential unit, with a $1,100/acre development charge, since the enterprise was set up in 2004. A consultant's master plan and rate study proposes rate increases to pay for a tiered list of capital projects.

johnstown/2.title: Repeated power outages and questions about AI data centers
johnstown/2.summary: Residents in Centerra and elsewhere in Johnstown complained to Council about constant power outages. Another resident asked about plans for future AI centers.

johnstown/3.title: Water supply, water rates and NISP
johnstown/3.summary: Council discussed the Northern Integrated Supply Project and later considered the Twenty-Second Interim Agreement for NISP participation. It also considered a Water System Master Plan update with J-U-B Engineers (up to $326,400), a Raw Water Transmission Project services agreement with Connell Resources, and the purchase of 15 CBT units. A resident commented on water usage at town facilities and on water rates.

johnstown/4.title: Senior Center construction
johnstown/4.summary: Residents spoke in support of continuing the Senior Center project. Council awarded the construction contract to Fransen Pittman Construction Co., Inc.

johnstown/5.title: Housing needs assessment and comprehensive plan updates
johnstown/5.summary: To comply with state Senate Bill 24-174, consultant ECOnorthwest drafted a Housing Needs Assessment and new Strategic Growth and Water Supply elements for the comprehensive plan. Planning and Zoning is to consider them Nov. 18 and Council is to consider adoption Dec. 2. A Housing Action Plan follows in mid-2027.

johnstown/6.title: I-25 East Frontage Road transfer from CDOT
johnstown/6.summary: Council held a public hearing on Ordinance 2026-297, which accepts part of the I-25 East Frontage Road between mile markers 253.2 and 257.1 and approves an intergovernmental agreement with CDOT. It passed first reading and came back on the Sept. 9 agenda.

johnstown/7.title: Downtown Development Authority plan and DDA fund
johnstown/7.summary: The DDA Plan of Development went to Planning and Zoning and to a Council public hearing. Ordinance 2026-298 sets up a DDA Fund, and a new DDA executive director was introduced.

johnstown/8.title: Town Attorney selection
johnstown/8.summary: Council interviewed law firms for the appointed Town Attorney position, including Hoffmann Parker Wilson & Carberry. It later considered a legal services agreement with Wilson Williams Fellman Dittman.

johnstown/9.title: Development approvals: Diamond Ridge Metro Districts, Lucky Star Monopine, Whitehall
johnstown/9.summary: Council was to consider a service plan for the Diamond Ridge Metropolitan Districts. Resolution 2026-40 covers the Lucky Star wireless Monopine, a Use by Special Review northeast of CR 42 and Colorado Blvd. Planning and Zoning also reviewed the Whitehall Filing No. 2 rezone and plat.
johnstown/9.where: CR 42 and Colorado Blvd; Diamond Ridge; Whitehall

johnstown/10.title: YMCA facility management agreement and settlement
johnstown/10.summary: Council considered an amended and restated Facility Management Agreement with the YMCA of Northern Colorado, tied to a settlement and release agreement and a reimbursement by the YMCA.

johnstown/11.title: Town land purchases: Quality Liquid Feeds and Gillam Development
johnstown/11.summary: Council considered a purchase and sale agreement with Quality Liquid Feeds, Inc., discussed in executive session, and a separate one with Gillam Development Corporation.

kersey/0.title: 6 P's annexation, industrial zoning and land-use map change on Highway 34
kersey/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission held a public hearing on annexing a 49.5-acre property at 24822 Highway 34, zoning it I-Industrial, and changing the Comprehensive Plan map from Agriculture/Tourism to an employment-oriented industrial designation. Neighbors who want to buy the property object to industrial use, and others raised traffic concerns. Annexing County Road 56 next to the site is also in play.
kersey/0.where: 24822 Highway 34, northeast of Kuner/Five Rivers feedlot

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/08.04.2026 Planning Commission Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202607311024090

kersey/1.title: Kersey Water Blueprint Plan
kersey/1.summary: The Board began the first of three working sessions with Brendle Group on long-term water supply, growth and funding. Northern Water now requires a native water supply at the tap for new development, and buy-and-dry transfers are accelerating, so Kersey's Colorado-Big Thompson water may not be enough. The $50,000 plan is paid for by a $37,500 DOLA grant, $10,000 from Northern Water and a $2,500 Town match.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/September 22, 2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202609221902470

kersey/2.title: Property tax ballot issues and 2027 budget
kersey/2.summary: The Board reviewed a preliminary 2027 budget and took up ballot measures on property tax. One ordinance would refer a measure fixing the rate at 12.000 mills. Ballot Issue 2B would extend the existing 17.205-mill levy for ten years (2028-2037) without raising the rate, and a resolution states the Board's support.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/October 13, 2026 Regular Meeting Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202610092015300
https://www.kerseygov.com/September 22, 2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202609221902470

kersey/3.title: Clark Street storm sewer project contract
kersey/3.summary: The Board awarded the Clark Street Storm Sewer contract to Mountain Constructors, Inc. after receiving 13 bids. Staff recommended the second-lowest bidder because of concerns about the lowest bidder. The bid came in well below the engineer's estimate, and the price is held for 180 days while the Town waits on FEMA funding. Other project costs will be incurred separately.

kersey/4.title: Adoption of the 2024 International Fire Code
kersey/4.summary: The Board introduced Ordinance 2026-0010 on August 11 and held the public hearing and second reading on September 8. It adopts the 2024 International Fire Code to match the Town's other 2024 codes. Platte Valley Fire District currently uses the 2018 code, and the new code addresses energy storage systems among other items. No public comment was given at the hearing.

kersey/5.title: Renaming duplicate streets in Berryman Farms
kersey/5.summary: Staff asked the Board to authorize renaming streets in Berryman Farms east of 1st Street because their names duplicate or resemble other Kersey streets. The concern is confusion for police, fire and EMS dispatch. Residents would need to update addresses, and staff would coordinate with residents, Weld County and emergency agencies.
kersey/5.where: Berryman Farms subdivision, east of 1st Street

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/08.25.2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202608211214270

kiowa/0.title: New 2026 Zoning Code replacing Chapter 16
kiowa/0.summary: The Planning Commission was asked to approve the 2026 Zoning Code Update as the town's official zoning ordinance (Resolution 2026-PC-01). On Oct. 13 the Board of Trustees holds a public hearing on Ordinance 2026-08, which would repeal and replace Chapter 16 and adopt a new zoning code.

kiowa/1.title: Proposed 2027 budget for the town and water authority
kiowa/1.summary: The Board of Trustees and the Kiowa Water and Wastewater Authority both have the proposed 2027 budget on their Oct. 13 agendas for discussion. The documents give no figures.

kiowa/2.title: Affordable housing commitment filing
kiowa/2.summary: Resolution 2026-19 would authorize the Town Administrator to file an affordable housing commitment with a state or other agency. The agenda excerpt does not name the agency.

kiowa/3.title: Floodplain permit fee
kiowa/3.summary: The Trustees have the town's floodplain permit fee, set by Resolution 2026-18, on their Oct. 13 agenda for discussion.

kiowa/4.title: Water authority contract with Gen-Tech, LLC
kiowa/4.summary: The Kiowa Water and Wastewater Authority is considering an agreement for professional services with Gen-Tech, LLC at its Oct. 13 meeting.

kiowa/5.title: Real property purchase discussions in executive session
kiowa/5.summary: The Trustees plan a closed session on Oct. 13 about the town's possible purchase or acquisition of real property, including negotiation strategy.

kit-carson-county/0.title: 2027 draft county budget public hearing
kit-carson-county/0.summary: The Board of County Commissioners scheduled a public hearing on the 2027 draft budget for 1:30 PM on October 28, 2026. The documents do not state the budget figures or any decision.

kit-carson-county/1.title: Engie Resources conceptual site plan
kit-carson-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission agenda for October 20, 2026 includes a conceptual site plan from Engie Resources, along with a separate request for a variance from setback requirements. The documents give no details on the project's location or outcome.

kit-carson-county/2.title: Letter to Colorado Parks and Wildlife on prairie dogs on public lands
kit-carson-county/2.summary: County commissioners had an item on the October 28 agenda about a letter to the Colorado Parks and Wildlife Commission concerning prairie dogs on public lands. The documents do not give the letter's contents.

kit-carson-county/3.title: Landfill leachate pump bids
kit-carson-county/3.summary: Commissioners were set to consider bids for a leachate pump and its installation at the county landfill.

kit-carson-county/4.title: ERTB grant-funded Catalis subscription for Clerk & Recorder
kit-carson-county/4.summary: Commissioners had an item for a $23,850 Catalis subscription fee for 2026-2027, tied to ERTB Grant #9, for the Clerk & Recorder's office.

kit-carson-county/5.title: Copier and printer rental agreement
kit-carson-county/5.summary: A rental agreement with Singlepoint LLC for copiers and printers at $4,352.45 per month was on the commissioners' October 28 agenda for the IT department.

kit-carson-county/6.title: 2027 rodeo association applications
kit-carson-county/6.summary: Commissioners had items on the 2027 PRCA application ($1,300) and WPRA application ($150) for the county rodeo.

la-junta/0.title: 2027 city budget, mill levy and utility rate changes
la-junta/0.summary: Finance Director Aliza Libby presented the 2027 budget on Sept. 8, and a public budget hearing was set. In October the Board of Utilities took up 2027 electric, water, wastewater and sanitation rate resolutions and its fund budgets. City Council then took up the budget resolution, the mill levy and the appropriation ordinance, with second readings set for Nov. 2. Mayor Ayala noted people say La Junta has the highest utility rates in Colorado.

la-junta/1.title: Pueblo sewage spill and Arkansas River safety
la-junta/1.summary: Water Director Tom Seaba briefed Council on a major raw sewage spill in Pueblo that reached the river near Confluence Park. Residents were told not to use untreated river or shallow well water for cooking or bathing. Local drinking water was reported safe, and reservoir releases were increased to help flush the river.

la-junta/2.title: Water loan and system extension on 24th Street
la-junta/2.summary: The city is extending its water system on 24th Street between Carson and Belleview to improve volume, flow and fire protection. An ordinance on first reading Nov. 2 would authorize a loan from the Colorado Water Resources and Power Development Authority for water distribution improvements. A water fund supplemental appropriation was also scheduled.

la-junta/3.title: Urban Renewal Authority Spark grants and blight funding
la-junta/3.summary: The URA tabled Sangre de Cristo Community Care's Spark Grant request for a storefront sign at 207 Colorado Ave. because the work was done before approval, and later told the applicant it would not be awarded. The URA approved a blight and safety grant for Arkansas Valley CASA's roof, and La Junta Associated Charities has an application pending. The URA also tabled its 2027 budget for a work session.

la-junta/4.title: Chestnut Apartments project delays
la-junta/4.summary: The URA reviewed the Chestnut Apartments project, which is about 52 days past its 180-day contract. Remaining work includes fire suppression, HVAC, plumbing and exterior doors. The board planned to hear from tenants about their experiences.

la-junta/5.title: New Economic Development Board
la-junta/5.summary: Council passed an ordinance on first and second reading creating a city Economic Development Board, run as an arm of the city like tourism rather than as a nonprofit, in part because of IRS issues. The City Clerk will call for letters of interest for board vacancies.

la-junta/6.title: Temporary event ordinance for side-by-sides and low-speed vehicles
la-junta/6.summary: Council passed on first and second reading a temporary ordinance allowing side-by-sides and other low-speed vehicles during events. Tarantula Fest and Early Settlers Day committee members use these vehicles, and the police chief was consulted.

la-junta/7.title: Street flooding and drainage at Lewis Avenue and 2nd Street
la-junta/7.summary: A Ward 1 resident told Council that recent rainstorms flooded the road at Lewis Avenue and 2nd Street and sent water into nearby basements. She said the area has only two drains.

la-junta/8.title: Arkansas Valley Emergency Communications authority agreement
la-junta/8.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement establishing an emergency communications authority among area towns and agencies, funded by a fee on cell phones in the state.

la-junta/9.title: Naming the field at Potter Park for Jim Sullivan
la-junta/9.summary: Residents asked to name the field Jim Sullivan Field at Potter Park, without renaming the park, under the city's naming procedure.

la-junta/10.title: Demolition of city-owned blighted property under the Copper Grant
la-junta/10.summary: Council approved a resolution on a city-owned 'junk' property tied to a larger brownfield-type grant called the 'Copper Grant.' Members discussed abatement costs and plans for four properties.

la-junta/11.title: Third Amendment to the Consolidation Agreement
la-junta/11.summary: Council was scheduled to consider a possible action on a third amendment to the Consolidation Agreement on Oct. 19. Earlier notes mention that conditions of the agreement were met for compliance.

la-junta/12.title: Industrial Park and golf course odor at wastewater plant
la-junta/12.summary: Water Director Tom Seaba addressed the smell near the Industrial Park and golf course and the wastewater treatment center. The wastewater work includes a new dewatering press, and the lagoons were also discussed.

lafayette/0.title: New Land Use Code and Old Town OTX-3 zoning
lafayette/0.summary: Council took up Ordinance No. 15, a rewrite of Chapter 26 with a new zoning map. First reading was Aug 18, a joint Council/Planning Commission workshop on Sept 9 covered Old Town Mixed-Use zoning, and second reading was set for Sept 15. Residents objected to OTX-3 along South Public Road south of Emma Street, including its 25,000 sq. ft. building footprint limit and building heights. Council generally agreed to move some changes into the second reading and others into a later ordinance.
lafayette/0.where: South Public Road south of Emma Street, Old Town

lafayette/1.title: Flock license plate readers and the 2027 budget
