lafayette/1.summary: Residents repeatedly objected to the city's Flock Safety license plate cameras and asked Council not to fund the contract. The 2027 budget came in two versions, one with and one without Flock funding (Resolutions 2026-24A/B, Ordinances 18A/B). Council also discussed a formal policy on automatic license plate readers and exempting surveillance contracts from administrative approval.

lafayette/2.title: 2027 budget, mill levy and fee updates
lafayette/2.summary: Staff presented a 2027 recommended budget with $128 million in revenue and no General Fund balance use. Sales tax is budgeted up 3% to $26.2 million. Council held the budget public hearing on Oct 6 and took up the fee ordinance (Ordinance 19), the 2027 pay plan and human services grants on later dates.

lafayette/3.title: Moratoria on data centers and advanced air mobility
lafayette/3.summary: Council considered potential moratoria on these land uses on Sept 15, then took up an 18-month moratorium on land use applications and building permits for data centers (Ordinance 21, second reading Oct 20). An emergency ordinance imposed a similar 18-month moratorium on advanced air mobility facilities.

lafayette/4.title: Boulder Ranch annexation and development
lafayette/4.summary: Residents wrote in against the proposed Boulder Ranch, a high-density development of about 78 acres off Burlington between Emma and Baseline Roads. They cited traffic on Baseline Road, open space and an intergovernmental agreement not to annex between cities, and said over 2,000 people signed petitions. On Nov 2 Council considered finding the annexation petition in substantial compliance and setting a hearing on eligibility.
lafayette/4.where: Southeast of Baseline Road and Nyland Way

lafayette/5.title: Church zoning in the new Land Use Code
lafayette/5.summary: Speakers raised concerns about how proposed zoning affects churches. Council amended its August 18 direction so that church parcels at Highway 287 and South Boulder Road be zoned consistently with Immaculate Conception (NC), and staff are to bring back related work.

lafayette/6.title: Naming the 701 S. Public Road pocket park
lafayette/6.summary: Many residents asked that the new pocket park be named for Rosebelle Lueras. A naming motion was on the Oct 20 agenda.

lafayette/7.title: LaMont Does Park tax extension and capital bond projects
lafayette/7.summary: Council put a ballot measure on the November ballot to extend an expiring property tax for LaMont Does Park, drawing both opposition and support. A Sept 22 bus tour reviewed capital projects including the water park, water treatment, and Baseline Road safety improvements. The city expects to issue $74 million in voter-approved bonds for the Recreation Center, Service Center and Civic Center, with a first tranche in October 2026, and Council also considered Ordinance 16 for G.O. bonds.

lafayette/8.title: Douglass Elementary School future
lafayette/8.summary: Residents asked the city to weigh in on BVSD's review of Douglass Elementary's future. Council directed staff to work with Councilor Jensen on a letter asking BVSD to consider whether it had a sufficient record of Lafayette family input.

lafayette/9.title: Inclusionary housing and affordable housing policies
lafayette/9.summary: Council took up an expedited review policy for affordable housing projects (Resolution 2026-26) and received inclusionary housing and affordable housing impact fee recommendations. It also approved assigning the city's 2026 private activity bond allocation to the Boulder County Housing Authority.

lafayette/10.title: Street racing near Avalon Flatirons and Flatirons Church
lafayette/10.summary: A resident wrote that street racers fill the church parking lot off South Public Road, with loud engines and speeding, and that police did not respond.
lafayette/10.where: South Public Road near Flatirons Church

lafayette/11.title: Oil and gas regulation workshop
lafayette/11.summary: Staff briefed Council on local authority over oil and gas under state law, after public comments about low-producing wells. The workshop was informational with no action requested.

lake-city/0.title: Phase 1 Hinsdale County/Lake City Comprehensive Housing Plan implementation
lake-city/0.summary: The town received six proposals to carry out Phase 1 of the housing plan and on Aug 19 accepted a Phase 1 implementation grant agreement and selected Collegiate Peaks Law & Mediation LLC. A professional services agreement was approved Sept 2. By Oct 7 and Oct 21 the consultant selection was back on the agenda, with a notice of award to Western Spaces LLC under discussion and action.

lake-city/1.title: DOLA ADU grant and pre-approved accessory dwelling unit designs
lake-city/1.summary: The council discussed a DOLA grant application, a reduced match request and incentive funding for accessory dwelling units. On Oct 21 it considered a $107,000 application with a 13% match of $13,910 for pre-approved ADU designs. The town also discussed ADU Supportive Jurisdiction certification.

lake-city/2.title: Elk Fire emergency response and disaster declaration
lake-city/2.summary: Town Manager Alexander Mulhall declared a local disaster on Aug 7 because of the Elk Fire on the town's border in unincorporated Hinsdale County, and council ratified it Aug 12. Council approved an emergency facilities and land use agreement with the USDA Forest Service for potable water and grey water disposal at $0.03 per gallon. Resolution 2026-13 to end the emergency was on the Oct 21 agenda, and the council also thanked Estes Park and Windsor for lending backup generators.
lake-city/2.where: Lake City and border with unincorporated Hinsdale County

lake-city/3.title: Flash flood cleanup and stormwater concerns
lake-city/3.summary: Council discussed flash flood cleanup and recovery in early August. On Aug 19 a resident raised concerns about loss of containment of stormwater, focusing on the depth and velocity of the water.

lake-city/4.title: 2027 budget, water and sewer rates, and health insurance
lake-city/4.summary: Council reviewed the 2027 draft budget, 2027 water and sewer rates, capital projects, and available money for donations. It appointed Town Manager Alexander Mulhall as 2027 budget officer and weighed alternate health insurance plans against keeping the current CEBT plan. It also discussed a request for proposals for the 2026 audit.

lake-city/5.title: Zoning amendments for MHR, CBD and GBD districts (Ordinance 2026-11)
lake-city/5.summary: Council held a public hearing and second reading on Ordinance 2026-11, amending sections of the town code covering performance standards in the MHR, CBD and GBD zoning districts.
lake-city/5.where: Medium-density residential, Central Business and General Business districts

lake-city/6.title: Lease of 8th Street right-of-way (Ordinance 2026-10)
lake-city/6.summary: Council held a public hearing and second reading on Ordinance 2026-10, which approves a lease of part of the town-owned 8th Street right-of-way.

lake-city/7.title: Wastewater treatment plant renovation change order
lake-city/7.summary: Council discussed and approved Ridgway Valley Enterprises electrical change order #3 on the WWTP renovation, for $23,331.11.

lake-city/8.title: Armory apartment rent and applicant criteria
lake-city/8.summary: Council discussed rent and applicant criteria for the apartment at the Armory in October.

lake-city/9.title: Dark Sky Community certification
lake-city/9.summary: Council discussed the requirements for certification as an International Dark Sky Community and the designation application.

lake-city/10.title: Colorado Ride 2027 tent camping in Memorial Park
lake-city/10.summary: Summit Cycle Solutions asked to use Memorial Park for tent camping Aug 11-13, 2027, with about 70 participants. Council approved the request and then Resolution 2026-12 permitting it.

lake-city/11.title: Wildfire resiliency code and pickleball court engagement
lake-city/11.summary: Council discussed CML and DOLA responses on adopting the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code and what it means for future grants. It also planned public engagement on pickleball courts for spring/summer 2027.

lake-county/0.title: Rural lodging and camping moratorium and new land code rules
lake-county/0.summary: After the Willow fire extended the timeline, the Planning Commission worked through rules for rural lodging, campgrounds and events: site selection, water, parking, emergency plans, conditional use permits and amendments. A public hearing on the moratorium rules was held Oct. 12 with resident questions, and the commissioners were to consider Resolution 2026-35 amending the Land Development Code on Oct. 20.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/1.title: E911 Authority restructuring, 2027 budget and PUC surcharge application
lake-county/1.summary: The E911 Authority has been working on a dispatch reorganization, hiring standards, a CentralSquare software agreement replacing the Motorola/Flex contract, and its 2027 budget. It also prepared an application to the Colorado PUC to raise the emergency telephone charge, with Resolutions 26-01 and 26-02 on the Oct. 2 agenda. The commissioners also looked at an offsite dispatch office.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions

lake-county/2.title: Leadville–Lake County fire rescue IGA and shared services with the City
lake-county/2.summary: The Fire Management Board reviewed fire budget figures and a draft intergovernmental agreement with the City of Leadville on funding and operating the fire department, including stations at 816 Harrison Ave and 141 County Road 10. The commissioners were to consider the IGA on Oct. 20, and the County and City held joint sessions on shared services and a possible joint task force.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/3.title: Lake County 2027 budget and capital requests
lake-county/3.summary: The commissioners held work sessions on budget priorities, elected officials' 2027 requests, department budgets, and capital requests including a Certificate of Participation. A preliminary 2027 budget was to be acknowledged Oct. 13.

lake-county/4.title: CMC employee housing project and affordable housing commitments
lake-county/4.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on a Colorado Mountain College housing project near existing roads and utilities, with 48 parking spaces. The statute exempts it from zoning review and members expressed support. Separately, the commissioners were to consider an amendment to the Proposition 123 affordable housing IGA and hear the Regional Housing Authority's semi-annual report.

lake-county/5.title: Willow Fire debrief and wildfire response
lake-county/5.summary: The commissioners held a debrief on lessons learned from the Willow Fire, which also delayed the moratorium schedule. Fire restrictions were rescinded in unincorporated areas by Resolution 2026-36.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings
Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions

lake-county/6.title: Aurora water deliveries and storage IGA
lake-county/6.summary: The commissioners were to consider an amended and restated IGA between Aurora and Lake County on water deliveries and storage, presented by the Water and Natural Resources Director.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/7.title: Comprehensive plan and strategic growth update
lake-county/7.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the draft strategic growth element from EPS and a final comp plan review, including a water augmentation plan. Adoption was expected in November. The 6663 Smuggler Backcountry site plan was also on the agenda.

lake-county/8.title: State highway safety and Gateway Mobility Plan
lake-county/8.summary: The commissioners discussed transportation and safety on state highways and the Lake County Gateway Mobility Plan.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions

lake-county/9.title: Animal shelter staffing, budget and IGA changes
lake-county/9.summary: The Animal Shelter Advisory Board discussed staffing, hours, budget, a partnership with Ark Valley, and changes to the shelter IGA.

lake-county/10.title: Onsite wastewater rules and public health items
lake-county/10.summary: The Board of Health discussed OWTS regulations and proposed amendments, the Public Health Improvement Plan, cottage food law expansion and the local tobacco ordinance.

lake-county/11.title: School safety MOU with PASS team
lake-county/11.summary: The commissioners were to consider an MOU with the school district's PASS team to formalize school climate and data work and meet grant requirements. It is a budgeted request.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lakewood/0.title: Ballot Issue 2G: half-cent sales tax for public and traffic safety
lakewood/0.summary: Council adopted Resolution 2026-58 on August 24 to put Ballot Issue 2G before voters on November 3, 2026. It would raise the sales and use tax rate by one-half of one percent, with all revenue dedicated to public safety and traffic safety improvements. On October 12 council considered a resolution formally supporting the measure.

lakewood/1.title: Automated license plate readers and proposed AVIS cameras
lakewood/1.summary: Police presented Lakewood's use of 17 fixed Flock Safety license plate cameras, in use in various forms since 2010. Council was asked to consider added safeguards and how the proposed Automated Vehicle Identification System relates to the existing readers. Policy PP-9126 bars a traffic stop based solely on an ALPR alert.

lakewood/2.title: Waste hauler licensing rewrite (Chapter 5.29)
lakewood/2.summary: Ordinance O-2026-30 would repeal and replace the hauler licensing chapter, adding definitions, a license review and approval process, and an enforcement framework that includes a hearing. License fees would move into rules and regulations. It aims to track tonnage and bring unlicensed haulers in, supporting the city's Zero Waste goal. It was on first reading August 10 and second reading August 24.

lakewood/3.title: Purchase of 1081 Vance Street for open space and park
lakewood/3.summary: Ordinance O-2026-32 authorizes the city to buy the property at 1081 Vance Street for municipal open space and park purposes. It had first reading September 28 and second reading with public hearing October 12.

lakewood/4.title: Rezonings at 2555 S. Kipling St. and 7201 W. Mansfield
lakewood/4.summary: Council took up first reading of two rezoning ordinances, O-2026-33 for 2555 S. Kipling St. and O-2026-34 for 7201 W. Mansfield.
lakewood/4.where: 2555 S. Kipling St. and 7201 W. Mansfield

lakewood/5.title: 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption
lakewood/5.summary: Council considered adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code with local deletions and amendments, on first reading August 24 and second reading September 28.

lakewood/6.title: Revised 2026 and proposed 2027 city and LRA budgets
lakewood/6.summary: Council held a study session September 14 on the revised 2026 and proposed 2027 city budget. The Lakewood Reinvestment Authority also reviewed its revised 2026 and proposed 2027 budget, with approval sought October 19. Council also approved 2027 budgets for the Alameda Corridor and West Colfax business improvement districts.

lakewood/7.title: Permanent police committee
lakewood/7.summary: Council considered amending Resolution R-2026-6 on establishing a permanent police committee and appointing a member to the ad-hoc committee working toward it.

lakewood/8.title: Neighborhood Participation Program funding and affordable housing
lakewood/8.summary: Council was asked to approve 2026 Neighborhood Participation Program projects for funding, which are small neighborhood-proposed improvements. A related resolution concerned the city's affordable housing stock by three percent.

lakewood/9.title: City manager contract
lakewood/9.summary: Council's August 24 agenda included a resolution on the city manager's contract.

lamar/0.title: Data center moratorium and community standards
lamar/0.summary: Council discussed data centers in September, including draft Community Benefit & Responsible Data Center Development Standards and interest from parties considering the Lamar area. On Oct. 12 residents voiced concerns, and council debated a proposed 24-month moratorium to give time to write regulations. The mayor said no nondisclosure agreements have been signed and no deals are in the works.

lamar/1.title: Possible SECPA purchase of Lamar Utility
lamar/1.summary: Council agreed to investigate an offer from SECPA to buy the Lamar Utility. A Utility Board member questioned the decision, and the mayor clarified that council is only investigating and lacks authority to sell a utility. Appointment to the Lamar Utility Board seat is on hold until outside counsel finishes a document and internal review.

lamar/2.title: Main Café Brownfield cleanup
lamar/2.summary: The city sought bids for EPA Brownfield grant cleanup of the Main Café site, holding a mandatory pre-bid walk-through in August. On Sept. 28 council awarded Bid 46-002 to Rockies Environmental for $483,299. A new assessment grant is also being set up.

lamar/3.title: Street repaving budget and 2026 paving list
lamar/3.summary: Annual asphalt paving was delayed by milling machine availability. Public Works said materials alone are estimated at $380,362 against a $400,000 budget, and urged a larger budget given rising asphalt costs. PMC will pay for materials to repave its parking lot, with the city providing in-kind work. The Willow Valley water line project is nearing completion, after which streets will be repaired.
lamar/3.where: Citywide, including Grant St. from Main to 6th and Willow Valley

lamar/4.title: 2027 budget preparation and revenue outlook
lamar/4.summary: The treasurer began budget work, with director meetings starting the week of Aug. 17 and a council work session on revenue projections on Aug. 24. Sales tax is up 5% year to date, and insurance renewals came in lower than feared. A federal funding application through Senator Bennett's office is still pending.

lamar/5.title: Tyler software rollout
lamar/5.summary: The city is moving finance and other functions to Tyler software, with sales tax, accounts receivable, court, parks and recreation, cemetery and utility billing modules still being finished. Project accounting went live Aug. 10.

lamar/6.title: Subdivision regulations amendment (Ordinance 1287) and Valco annexation
lamar/6.summary: Council approved on second reading Ordinance No. 1287 amending Chapter 22 Subdivisions of the municipal code. Planning and Zoning discussed an upcoming annexation of the Valco property.

lamar/7.title: Parks and recreation fields and facilities
lamar/7.summary: Residents and councilmembers raised concerns about the youth soccer field's grass and divots and the community building's worn carpet. Escondido Field was topsoiled, reseeded and treated for weeds and fungus. The city will look for grants for ADA-accessible playground equipment.
lamar/7.where: Escondido Field, youth soccer field, community building

lamar/8.title: Colorado State Patrol Taser donation
lamar/8.summary: Council accepted Taser X26P units and equipment donated by the Colorado State Patrol, worth about $50,000.

lamar/9.title: Ward I council vacancy filled
lamar/9.summary: Robert 'Bob' Seay was the only applicant for the Ward I vacancy. After an open-session interview and executive session, council appointed him to serve until November 2027.

limon/0.title: 2026 budget and property tax levy
limon/0.summary: Council held a November 18 budget workshop, then a December 10 public hearing and votes on the 2026 budget, the property tax levy and the appropriation ordinance (No. 648). A December 29 hearing covered a supplemental appropriation to the 2025 budget.

limon/1.title: Water and sewer projects report and recommendations
limon/1.summary: Council took up a GMS report and recommendations for water and sewer projects on April 2, with a follow-up report on the projects on August 6. The documents do not state the decisions.

limon/2.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption
limon/2.summary: Council held a public hearing on March 5 on Ordinance 649, which would adopt the 2025 edition of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. The ordinance appeared again on the April 2 agenda.

limon/3.title: Municipal code changes on vehicles, licenses and penalties
limon/3.summary: Council considered ordinances to enforce state vehicle rules (No. 650), require a valid license or permit while driving (No. 651) and amend municipal penalties (No. 652).

limon/4.title: E-bike regulation (Ordinance 646)
limon/4.summary: Council had Ordinance 646 on e-bike regulation on its November 6 agenda. The agenda does not say what the rules are.

limon/5.title: Irrigation water rights ordinance (Ordinance 647)
limon/5.summary: Council considered Ordinance 647 on irrigation water rights at its November 6 meeting.

limon/6.title: Affordable housing project review policies
limon/6.summary: On June 4 council considered Resolution 26-06-12, which would establish review policies for affordable housing projects. A Housing Authority board appointment followed on August 6.

limon/7.title: Limon Municipal Airport and transfer of entitlements
limon/7.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-04-07 on April 2 to transfer airport entitlements to Archuleta County. An airport presentation was scheduled for August 6.

limon/8.title: Street chip sealing and Limon Events contract
limon/8.summary: On May 7 council considered a proposal from A-1 Chipseal to chip seal designated streets. On July 2 it took up a contract with Big Sandy Builders for work at Limon Events.

limon/9.title: Tamarack Golf Club user rates
limon/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-03-06 on March 5, which would set user rates for the Tamarack Golf Club.

littleton/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center applications
littleton/0.summary: On Oct. 20, 2026 council took up Ordinance 22-2026 on first reading, which would pause acceptance, processing and approval of data center applications while staff study and recommend land use regulations.

littleton/1.title: Geneva Village site redevelopment
littleton/1.summary: Council discussed process options and advisory services for redeveloping the Geneva Village site in August, and on Oct. 27 was set to hear the Redevelopment Advisory Team's recommendation.

littleton/2.title: Utility rate study and South Platte Renew governance
littleton/2.summary: Council reviewed Part 2 of the utility rate study results and analyzed governance model options for South Platte Renew, the wastewater plant shared with Englewood.

littleton/3.title: Economic partnership incentives for Mineral area retail (RIG Mineral, Scheels)
littleton/3.summary: Council considered an updated Economic Partnership Incentives Policy and agreements with RIG Mineral LLC, including a sales tax share-back amendment and a new agreement involving Scheels.

littleton/4.title: E-bike and e-motor safety ordinance
littleton/4.summary: Council discussed a draft ordinance on e-bike and e-motor safety on Aug. 25.

littleton/5.title: 25 mph speed limit ordinance and Safer Streets
littleton/5.summary: Ordinance 17-2026 would set a maximum lawful speed of 25 mph; it passed first reading Aug. 18 and came up for second reading Sept. 1. Council also received a Safer Streets update on Sept. 8.

littleton/6.title: Street projects and transportation planning
littleton/6.summary: Council approved contracts for the 2026 Mill & Overlay and surface sealing projects, studied the Elati Street corridor, and approved a consultant agreement for the Transportation Master Plan update.

littleton/7.title: Hauler licensing and waste diversion rules
littleton/7.summary: Council discussed hauler licensing and an Equal Space Ordinance proposal, then took up Ordinance 19-2026 amending Title 3 on Oct. 20, tied to the South Metro Waste Diversion Plan. A Circular Action Alliance subaward was also on consent.

littleton/8.title: Sign variances for 2450 W Main Street
littleton/8.summary: The Appeals & Adjustment Commission was to hear seven variance requests for signs at 2450 W Main Street, including a marquee sign projecting 6 ft, extra height, and exposed bulb lighting.

littleton/9.title: Historic review of Main Street facade remodels
littleton/9.summary: The Historical Preservation Commission was to consider certificates of appropriateness, including a restaurant facade remodel at 2589 W Main Street.

littleton/10.title: Land use code update and Main Street investment
littleton/10.summary: Planning Commission looked at transition standards and previewed the Unified Land Use Code update, and council discussed a Main Street investment strategy and joint study session priorities.

logan-county/0.title: Rural Health Transformation Program grant for Sterling Fire/EMS ($2.1 million)
logan-county/0.summary: Sterling Fire and the County are contracting for a federal Rural Health Transformation Program grant through the State, totaling $2,105,514, to advance EMS services including interfacility transports. The Board and staff reviewed the contract in October, noted that planned wellness funding for community paramedic and medical director positions was omitted, and raised audit and confidentiality questions. A special meeting was set for October 27 to sign it.

logan-county/1.title: Prairie dog policy and Colorado Parks and Wildlife petition
logan-county/1.summary: Commissioners discussed a petition before the Colorado Parks and Wildlife Commission on prairie dogs, which will be taken up at CPW's November meeting. Speakers raised concerns about damage to ranchland, lack of compensation, and whether local voices are heard. Residents were encouraged to submit written comments through Engagecpw.com.

logan-county/2.title: Summit Carbon Solutions pipeline and carbon sequestration resolution
logan-county/2.summary: Summit Carbon Solutions told the Board it hopes to build as much of its route as possible through voluntary landowner agreements, with surveys starting and construction not expected until mid- to late-term. The County has recently adopted new pipeline fees and setbacks, and the Board reviewed a revised carbon sequestration resolution 2026-32 in October.

logan-county/3.title: County Road 26 bridge and bridge grants
logan-county/3.summary: The Board weighed applying for a bridge planning and engineering grant for the CR 26 bridge, but decided against pursuing the grant and not to close the bridge for a multi-year project. It decided to hold a public meeting about the bridge's future and discussed other narrow, old bridges near Proctor/Crook. Off-system bridge grants also came up earlier.

logan-county/4.title: Sterling sales tax ballot question for road repair
logan-county/4.summary: Sterling officials asked the Board to support a ballot question raising the city sales tax from 3% to 4% for five years, dedicated to road maintenance in the city. A similar measure failed last year. The County Attorney will draft a resolution, since the Board can encourage votes but not spend public money.

logan-county/5.title: 2027 EMS and county budget planning
logan-county/5.summary: Sterling Fire EMS staff sought guidance on the 2027 budget, including moving a $14,000 RETAC training grant, building up capital funds for an ambulance grant (a CDPHE grant needing about $40,000 match on a $337,000 ambulance), and how to split costs with the City, which wants a 3% cost-of-living raise. Sheriff vehicle replacement and $233,000 in hail-damage proceeds for Road and Bridge vehicles also feed into next year's budget.

logan-county/6.title: Underground fire-suppression water tank at CR 70 and CR 11
logan-county/6.summary: The Centennial Soil Conservation District won a $30,000 state resiliency grant to bury a 10,000-gallon water tank for wildfire fighting in the northwest corner of the county, where hauling water is a long trip. The Board agreed to maintain County Road 11, including snow removal, and help as much as possible.

logan-county/7.title: County comprehensive plan update and DOLA grants
logan-county/7.summary: A DOLA representative said state grant prospects are weak but a possible $50,000 housing planning award for a joint City of Sterling and County comprehensive plan would require a County match. The current plan dates to 2013 or earlier and predates battery storage and data centers.

logan-county/8.title: Battery storage and wind projects: Niyol Wind road use
logan-county/8.summary: Niyol Wind representatives asked to temporarily remove signs at County Roads 67 and 24 to replace blades on two turbines, with no road improvements planned. Commissioners also looked at a battery energy storage facility's setbacks and fire suppression.

logan-county/9.title: Fairgrounds improvements and Fair Board decisions
logan-county/9.summary: The fairgrounds needed a corrected Public Service Company easement for new transformers, and the fairgrounds manager sought direction on the master plan and capital spending for the 2027 budget. The Fair Board is considering ticket price increases, gate cameras, and expiring bull riding and demo derby contracts.

logan-county/10.title: Permit Gateway online oversize/overweight permits
logan-county/10.summary: Road and Bridge staff proposed adopting Permit Gateway, a free system where carriers pay a service fee, to automate oversize and overweight permits and route trucks away from restricted roads and bridges. The Board indicated support for moving forward.

logan-county/11.title: Colorado River, Perkins County Canal and water issues
logan-county/11.summary: Commissioner Yahn reported on the Colorado Water Congress, including shortage cuts and a Nevada lawsuit against the federal government over Colorado River cuts. Commissioners also asked about the Perkins County Canal and a diversion structure on the South Platte.

logan-county/12.title: County employee health insurance rates
logan-county/12.summary: The County Health Pool rates dropped after the county moved down a band, and dental is switching to Ameritas. Staff requested separate employee, plus-one and family rates; the county pays 65% of family premiums and a retiree stipend idea was discussed.

lone-tree/0.title: Brick wall construction management contract with Alfred Benesch
lone-tree/0.summary: Council reviewed an update and communications plan for the city's brick wall project. It also took up a professional services agreement with Alfred Benesch & Company for construction management. The documents do not state the outcome.

lone-tree/1.title: City Administration building renovation contractor
lone-tree/1.summary: Council considered awarding a general contracting services contract for the City Admin renovation project at the October 6 study session and regular meeting.
lone-tree/1.where: Lone Tree Civic Center, 8527 Lone Tree Parkway

lone-tree/2.title: Douglas County School District mill levy override and Ballot Issue 5A
lone-tree/2.summary: Council heard a presentation on the Douglas County School District mill levy override. It also considered Resolution 26-46 supporting a yes vote on the district's 2026 Ballot Issue 5A.

lone-tree/3.title: Off-highway and low-speed electric vehicle rules (Ordinance 26-08)
lone-tree/3.summary: Council held a public hearing on second reading of Ordinance 26-08. It would amend Chapter 8 of the municipal code to regulate off-highway vehicles and low-speed electric vehicles.

lone-tree/4.title: Proposition 123 implementation
lone-tree/4.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-43 on how the city will implement Proposition 123, the state affordable housing program.

lone-tree/5.title: Happy Canyon Trail connection deed from Schweiger Ranch Foundation
lone-tree/5.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-45 to accept a special warranty deed from Schweiger Ranch Foundation for the Happy Canyon Trail connection project.

lone-tree/6.title: Snow removal agreement with Douglas County
lone-tree/6.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-42, an intergovernmental agreement with Douglas County for 2026-2027 snow removal on certain city streets.

lone-tree/7.title: Southwest Village plan and parks master plan amendments; Fidelity office site plan
lone-tree/7.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled public hearings on the Southwest Village Preliminary Plan Amendment and Parks Master Plan Amendment. It also scheduled a hearing on the Fidelity Office Building site improvement plan.
lone-tree/7.where: Southwest Village; Fidelity Office Building site

lone-tree/8.title: Unified Development Code overview
lone-tree/8.summary: Council held a strategy session on October 26 for an overview and preliminary discussion of a Unified Development Code.

lone-tree/9.title: Parks master plan, Entertainment District Park and High Note Park
lone-tree/9.summary: The Recreation Advisory Committee discussed the Parks, Open Space, and Trails Master Plan, the South Suburban strategic plan, Entertainment District Park and a High Note Park update.

lone-tree/10.title: Council strategy sessions on staffing, police, capital projects and community development
lone-tree/10.summary: Council's October 5 strategy session covered compensation and a 5-year staffing plan, the Police Department, the 5-year capital projects plan and community development. An earlier session continued discussion of topics from an August 19 retreat.

longmont/0.title: Public safety tax increase and charter amendments on the November 3 ballot
longmont/0.summary: Council referred a city sales/use tax and property tax increase for public safety (police, dispatchers, firefighters) to voters, along with Home Rule Charter amendments on ranked choice voting and requiring voter approval to sell open space. Council also considered resolutions urging 'Yes' votes on the public safety tax and open space measures, and on a Boulder County property tax ballot issue.

longmont/1.title: 1st and Main urban renewal area, transit center and parking garage
longmont/1.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority took up tax increment revenue agreements with the City, Boulder County, Northern Water, St. Vrain Valley School District and the Downtown Development Authority for the 1st and Main plan area. Council considered the urban renewal plan, lease-purchase financing for a parking garage, and a development agreement with Main Street Tebo, LLC for the 1st and Main Transit Center and transit-oriented project.

sources.body: City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners

longmont/2.title: 2027 proposed budget and 2027-2031 Capital Improvement Program
longmont/2.summary: Staff presented the 2027 proposed budget and five-year capital program, with public hearings on Sept. 29 and Oct. 6 and final council direction. Council also took up the tax levy ordinance for the 2027 fiscal year.

longmont/3.title: Annexations: Dry Creek, 8513 St. Vrain Road, Gateway Northwest and 8979 Nelson Road
longmont/3.summary: Council moved through several annexations: Dry Creek (Airport Road and Clover Basin Drive, zoned R-MN), 8513 St. Vrain Road (east of Airport Road), and Longmont Gateway Northwest (Hwy 287 and Park Ridge Avenue). A neighborhood meeting was noticed for annexing a 0.88-acre church parcel at 8979 Nelson Road, and another for 10930 Airport Road amendments for new single-family homes.
longmont/3.where: Airport Road, St. Vrain Road, Hwy 287 and Park Ridge Ave, 8979 Nelson Road

longmont/4.title: Composting subsidy and sanitation rate structure
longmont/4.summary: Council discussed a possible subsidy for composting services and compost rate proposals, and asked the Sustainability Advisory Board for feedback on the sanitation rate structure. Council members also wanted rates aligned with policy goals ahead of a waste rates conversation, and staff reported on solid waste collection issues in alleys.

longmont/5.title: Water exchange with St. Vrain & Left Hand Water Conservancy District and drought conditions
longmont/5.summary: The Water Board reviewed a one-year exchange of 148.8 acre-feet of the district's Colorado-Big Thompson water for Longmont water, helping keep more storage in Ralph Price Reservoir; the district's supply could run out by 2028 if drought continues. The board also reviewed Ralph Price Reservoir water rights management and the Dry Creek Fire near Button Rock.

longmont/6.title: Extraterritorial water service for Hygiene Fire Protection District
longmont/6.summary: Council considered ordinances directing staff to process applications for a larger tap and an additional water service for the Hygiene Fire Protection District's fire house and fire suppression system. The Water Board was asked for a recommendation.

longmont/7.title: Airport future vision and monitoring systems
longmont/7.summary: Council held an Airport Vision Session on a new vision, governance models, and rebuilding community trust, and heard options for implementing airport monitoring systems. RTD's Longmont-to-airport bus was also reinstated.

longmont/8.title: Longmont Housing Authority: Briarwood Apartments, bonds, vouchers and budget
longmont/8.summary: The Housing Authority discussed Briarwood Apartments, resigned as property manager at Zinnia, and considered multifamily housing revenue bonds and a private activity bond allocation. It also took up the voucher program plan, payment standards, 2027 budgets and a review of the countywide affordable housing tax.

sources.body: Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners Meeting
Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners

longmont/9.title: Inclusionary housing fee-in-lieu and human services funding
longmont/9.summary: The Housing and Human Services Advisory Board heard an update on the inclusionary housing ordinance, which requires 12% affordable units or a fee, and set a two-tier scoring system for funding. It then held agency funding hearings through October.

sources.body: Housing and Human Service Advisory Board
Housing and Human Service Advisory Board
Housing and Human Service Advisory Board
Housing and Human Service Advisory Board
Housing and Human Service Advisory Board

longmont/10.title: Contractor's shops in MU-E zone and Avis rental at 206 S. Main
longmont/10.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission reviewed a citizen-initiated request to allow contractor's shops in the MU-E zone, with the hearing possibly continued to Nov. 18. A proposal would locate Avis Car Rental behind 206 S. Main Street, requiring conditional use review adjacent to a greenway.
longmont/10.where: 206 S. Main Street; MU-E zone districts

longmont/11.title: Short-term rental at 607 Emery Street
longmont/11.summary: An owner seeks conditional use for intermittent short-term rental at 607 Emery Street; another rental already exists at 619 Emery on the same block segment.

longmont/12.title: Show cause hearing on liquor license at 333 Main Street
longmont/12.summary: The Local Licensing Authority scheduled a show cause hearing on a liquor license at 333 Main Street over alleged disturbances, noise and open container violations; it was continued to a date to be determined, then set for Oct. 2.

sources.body: Local Licensing Authority- CONTINUED TO DATE TBD

louisville/0.title: Centennial Valley General Development Plan amendment for future housing and parks
louisville/0.summary: Council took up an amendment to the Centennial Valley GDP for Lot A of Filing No. 8 (Ordinance 1935, second reading with public hearing), and a related Centennial 8 Replat B combining 1006 Honeysuckle Lane. A resident letter says the plan would grow Louisville's housing units by 12% while its parks, trails and open space are inadequate. OSAB approved a resolution with a trail addition and sent it to council, and PPLAB held a hearing on the park components.
louisville/0.where: Centennial Valley Business Park, Lot A / 1006 Honeysuckle Lane

louisville/1.title: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance update (Ordinance 1936)
louisville/1.summary: Council considered amendments to Title 17 on inclusionary housing, with second reading and public hearing on Aug 18 and a further hearing on Sept 15. Strong Towns Louisville urged by-right incentives, exemptions for small 10-12 unit projects, and zoning reform first; another resident worried new market-rate units could raise prices.

louisville/2.title: 2027-2028 budget, mill levy and capital plan
louisville/2.summary: Following the July 22 budget retreat, staff reported an operating deficit and a General Fund gap. The City Manager gave an initial budget presentation Sept 1, a final one with a public hearing Oct 20, and budget and mill levy adoption was scheduled Nov 2. Capital plan refinements, the Xcel franchise fee and the northeast water loop (pulled from the budget) were among the items discussed.

louisville/3.title: Sustainability funding, bag tax and climate action
louisville/3.summary: At a joint meeting, the Sustainability Advisory Board proposed funding ideas including renegotiating the Xcel franchise agreement, expanding the bag tax, a dedicated tax or fee, and development impact fees. Residents asked about a climate impact fee, urban heat island strategies and bag tax transparency, and others urged electrification. LSAB also worked on electrification rebates and commercial sustainability rebates.

louisville/4.title: Golf course and recreation center 2027 fees
louisville/4.summary: The Recreation Advisory Board reviewed golf fee models showing green fee increases alone cannot cover projected deficits, and recommended 2027 golf fees and pass rates to council. It also approved 3% resident and 7% non-resident increases for Rec and Senior Center admission, which went into the City Manager's 2027 fee update.
louisville/4.where: Coal Creek Golf Course, Recreation/Senior Center

louisville/5.title: Parks, Recreation and Open Space (PROS) plan and Trails Plan
louisville/5.summary: A draft PROS Guidebook (Long Range Plan and Trails System Plan) went through OSAB, PPLAB and council discussion. Friends of Louisville open space groups asked for Charter-based changes, including removing Trail 18 and larger ecological buffers. Council adopted a PROS-related resolution on Nov 2 agenda. Residents also asked for bocce court investment.

louisville/6.title: Fire Smart Louisville and wildfire mitigation
louisville/6.summary: Council considered funding the Fire Smart Louisville neighborhood wildfire-risk program led by volunteers and Boulder Watershed Collective, matching Wildfire Partners rebates. An agreement with Boulder Watershed Collective for $100,000 for wildfire work was on the Oct 20 consent agenda.

louisville/7.title: Avista hospital helipad and Redtail Ridge development
louisville/7.summary: A final PUD, special review use for a helicopter pad and development agreement for the hospital were before council (Resolution 66). A councilmember's questions noted the hospital is exempt from LEED requirements and the agreement reduces the overall solar obligation for Redtail Ridge.

louisville/8.title: Grain Elevator and Grain Yard revitalization funding
louisville/8.summary: The Revitalization Commission worked on a Grain Elevator tax increment financing agreement, Grain Yard facade and property improvement funding, and reallocating $344,400 in unspent 2025 property improvement funds. Council also approved a conditional assignment of the preservation grant for the Grain Elevator at 540 County Road. Concern was raised about Front Street construction effects, and a construction impact grant for about 12 eligible businesses was discussed.
louisville/8.where: Grain Elevator, 540 County Road / Front Street

louisville/9.title: Comprehensive Plan and Development Code update
louisville/9.summary: Planning Commission reviewed the Comprehensive Plan with growth estimates and place types; residents raised concerns about population growth, traffic, water, evacuation routes and wildfire risk. Council accepted a DOLA grant and approved agreements for the Development Code update, which residents asked to include climate strategies.

louisville/10.title: Affordable housing: senior concept plan and expedited review
louisville/10.summary: Council reviewed a concept plan for Centennial Drive affordable senior housing, a Housing Strategic Framework from Trestle Strategy Group, multifamily housing revenue bonds, and resolutions for expedited review of affordable projects and a state affordable housing commitment.

louisville/11.title: Real estate purchases: Empire Road, 1155 Pine Street, Gateway Open Space
louisville/11.summary: Council approved a contract to buy 1501 Empire Road and the easterly part of 1303 Empire Road (zoned Industrial) and later extended it. It also considered extending a lease-purchase of 1155 Pine Street and an agreement to buy the Gateway Open Space property. The city bought 101 Cherry St.

louisville/12.title: E-bike and e-moto regulations
louisville/12.summary: Council scheduled a discussion on e-bike and e-moto regulations and traffic safety strategies. Park advisory members noted e-bikes are accelerating erosion and social trails in parks.

louisville/13.title: Business assistance agreements for local companies
louisville/13.summary: Council considered incentives including $208,400 for Arsenal Health, $281,114 for Infleqtion Quantum (consumer-use-tax rebates capped at $189,900), and an amendment for Louisville Cyclery's sales tax rebate.

louisville/14.title: Historic preservation tax and landmark grants
louisville/14.summary: Council placed a Historic Preservation Tax measure on the 2026 ballot and reviewed landmark designations and grants, including the Caranci, Giorzelli, James and Mudrock houses (613 Grant Avenue) and a Methodist Church at 741 Jefferson.

lyons/0.title: Planet Bluegrass annexation and PUD zoning at 19617 and 19661 N. St. Vrain Drive
lyons/0.summary: Planet Bluegrass has asked to annex two parcels near Eagle Canyon and zone them as a PUD. The Utilities board, Economic Vitality, Sustainable Futures, Ecology and Parks commissions all reviewed the referral. The Utilities board backed an impact statement with notes. Ordinances 1225 and 1226 were continued, with a request to move them to 12/7/26, and the Parks commission recorded community concerns.

lyons/1.title: 2nd & 3rd Avenue stormwater project and bond vote
lyons/1.summary: The $3.8M stormwater and sidewalk project lost its FEMA BRIC grant. The town planned a 20-year loan and found that a bond requires a ballot vote. A ballot measure failed 3–2, and a roughly $4M state-loan version may return in November 2027. The board also moved ahead with a Safe Routes to School sidewalk grant.

lyons/2.title: Electric rates, time-of-use billing and meter collar policy
lyons/2.summary: The town is moving to time-of-use electric tiers. Transmission costs from Southwest Power Pool rose 50%, and staff project a 9% rate increase for 2027. Local businesses such as Main Stage raised concerns about too little consultation. A meter collar policy for solar customers, and net-metering billed at nameplate capacity, is still under discussion. Further TOU rate changes are expected in March.

lyons/3.title: Water, sewer and stormwater rate increases and 2027 budget
lyons/3.summary: Trustees held public hearings on Resolutions 2026-64, 65 and 66, which raise stormwater, water (indexed to CPI) and wastewater rates. The 2027 budget workshops, supplemental 2026 items and a 5-year capital plan ran alongside. Infrastructure is the board's priority.

lyons/4.title: Flock license plate reader cameras
lyons/4.summary: Trustees discussed automated license plate readers and a Flock Safety agreement in September and again on Nov. 2. The packet included the law enforcement agreement and police budgets.

lyons/5.title: Wastewater treatment plant upgrade
lyons/5.summary: The treatment facility has a separate $5.8M need, with about $2.5M saved and a $1.7M federal grant decision expected in January. The board saw a 60% design update, and the Utilities board reviewed options such as a screw press and aeration improvements while awaiting CDPHE approval.

lyons/6.title: Wildfire mitigation rules and fire code
lyons/6.summary: Lyons has used the state fire code since July 1, requiring fire-resistant roofing, and issued permits after the hailstorm. A town hall on fire risk was held and a wildfire mitigation ordinance is being drafted, with historic properties a question. Mitigation work is under way along trail extensions.

lyons/7.title: Strategic growth and water supply element of the comprehensive plan
lyons/7.summary: The town is adding a state-required (SB24-174) strategic growth and water supply element to the comp plan. Staff say water supply has ample surplus, and state housing projections recommend preparing for 87 more units. The planning, utilities, historic and ecology boards and trustees reviewed it, and historic commissioners asked for stronger infill language.

lyons/8.title: Water rights cash-in-lieu for 402 Main Street
lyons/8.summary: Roots to Revival asked to dedicate Lake McIntosh shares and pay cash in lieu for additional water at 402 Main Street. 1.4 shares at about $12k each came to $16.8k, and trustees ratified it by Resolution 2026-62.

lyons/9.title: Sundance Film Festival visitors, SELL lodging ordinance and task force
lyons/9.summary: Ordinance 1222 created special event lodging licenses, which opened Aug. 1 and require $1M liability insurance. The task force shifted toward private events and curated experiences, planned community sessions and shuttles, and is considering moving under a nonprofit. The town directed $5,000 for beautification along the route.

lyons/10.title: Special event and park fee waiver policy
lyons/10.summary: Trustees considered a policy on fee waivers for special events and park use, based on a Parks and Recreation Commission recommendation. The Economic Vitality Commission discussed local versus non-local entities and administrative approval.

lyons/11.title: Vacant to Vibrant downtown incentive program
lyons/11.summary: The Economic Vitality Commission is designing a rebate program to fill vacant downtown storefronts. Ideas include up to 75% of projects under $5,000 and about 10% for up to $25,000; none is approved.

lyons/12.title: Flagstone culvert repairs and historic review
lyons/12.summary: A roughly $482,000 DOLA grant funds repairs to the Flagstone culvert near 4th and 5th Streets. The Historic Preservation Commission reviewed the investigation and drafted comments for DOLA and History Colorado on impacts to the historic sandstone structure.

lyons/13.title: Moss Rock hotel and Roots to Revival redevelopment agreements
lyons/13.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority received updates on the Moss Rock hotel at 343-347 Main Street, with a third amendment to its agreement, and on a reimbursement agreement for 402 Main Street. It also reviewed its 2027 budget.

lyons/14.title: Boulder County housing projects and Prop 123
lyons/14.summary: Trustees received a Boulder County Housing Authority update covering Carter Court and Seward Street, and the town considered opting into Prop 123 building permits.

manzanola/0.title: 112 S. Canal brownfield cleanup and demolition
manzanola/0.summary: CDPHE awarded a Targeted Brownfields Assessment for 112 S. Canal, and the town later applied for grants. By spring 2026 the demolition was out for bid, and Earth Services & Abatement was named contractor, with the grant contract still to be awarded.

manzanola/1.title: Water plant storage study, Well #2 testing and water system mapping
manzanola/1.summary: Engineers GMS (Tom McClernan) have been working on a water plant storage study, which moved to a PER with flow and chemical tests on Well #2. The town is also considering a $15/month Diamond Maps system from Colorado Rural Water to map valves, meters and hydrants. A report noted 84% water loss in April 2026.

manzanola/2.title: MMOF/CDOT sidewalk grant of $474,041
manzanola/2.summary: The town received a $474,041 CDOT MMOF grant for sidewalks. The contract is budgeted for Colorado's 2029 budget year, and a related council resolution was held until the grant amount was known.

manzanola/3.title: Southeastern Water Conservancy District Conduit vault at water plant
manzanola/3.summary: The council asked Congress for support of the Conduit and heard from SECWCD's Hunter Willits on placing a conduit vault at the water plant, for Valley water. It remained on agendas through October 2026.

manzanola/4.title: Drought water restrictions and project water release
manzanola/4.summary: The council took up Resolution 2026-02 on drought water restrictions in April 2026. In July it discussed a 100 acre-foot project water release on 6/30/2026.

manzanola/5.title: Second Street repair and chip seal
manzanola/5.summary: Otero County was to repair Second Street for about $1,000 in mid-2026. A chip and seal of the street is planned for 2027 at about $10,000.

manzanola/6.title: Solar tax credit refund
manzanola/6.summary: The IRS sent a November 3 letter saying a tax credit refund is coming on the town's solar project.

manzanola/7.title: Federal procurement and grant compliance policies
manzanola/7.summary: In March 2026 the council took up a package of procurement policies, including 2 CFR 200 compliance and requirements for federally funded projects.

manzanola/8.title: Budget approval and insurance renewal
manzanola/8.summary: The council approved the budget and its resolutions in December 2025. It also considered the Gallagher insurance renewal at $36,216.

manzanola/9.title: Weed and tree removal ordinance, senior housing parking lot, and surplus vehicles
manzanola/9.summary: The council considered Ordinance 2026-05 on emergent weed and tree removal. It also discussed paving the Park Street Senior Housing parking lot and whether to sell or scrap a 2012 Dodge police car and a jetter truck.
manzanola/9.where: Park Street Senior Housing and Townwide

manzanola/10.title: Charter franchise agreement
manzanola/10.summary: A Charter franchise agreement was on the February 2026 agenda.

mead/0.title: Mead Police Facility: site plan, groundbreaking and financing
mead/0.summary: The town approved the Mead Police Department site plan (Ordinance 1118) and held a groundbreaking for the new facility in the Liberty Ranch subdivision on Chaparral Street. Urban Renewal Authority commissioners heard about a DOLA grant and Piper Sandler's financing plan, and discussed a cooperation agreement with the town for the project.

mead/1.title: 2027 budget and mill levies
mead/1.summary: The Town presented its proposed 2027 budget on Sept. 28 and set public hearings for Oct. 26 on the town budget (Resolution 71-R-2026). The Urban Renewal Authority and the Highway 66/I-25 and Elevation 25 General Improvement Districts held hearings the same day on their own 2027 budgets and mill levies. The town also amended the 2026 Municipal Facilities Impact Fee Fund budget.

mead/2.title: Data center moratorium
mead/2.summary: The Board of Trustees adopted a twelve-month moratorium on data centers at its Aug. 31 meeting. Staff told the Planning Commission the town has received no data center proposals so far.

mead/3.title: Public Facilities zoning and the Ordinance 1121 reconsideration
mead/3.summary: The Planning Commission recommended Public Facilities (PF) zoning for the town-owned Valdez annexation property and other town-owned properties. The Board took up the zoning map amendment (Ordinance 1121) on Oct. 26. An Oct. 29 agenda lists options to reconsider Ordinance 1121 or pursue a conditional use permit.
mead/3.where: Town-owned properties, including the Valdez annexation

mead/4.title: Waterfront Filing No. 2 preliminary plat
mead/4.summary: The Planning Commission recommended conditional approval of the preliminary plat for Waterfront Filing No. 2, a proposed mixed-use development. Commissioners focused on traffic capacity, road improvements and trail connections. They also called for broader coordination of transportation improvements across nearby developments.

mead/5.title: Ariet's Grove Filing No. 1 preliminary plat
mead/5.summary: The Planning Commission considered conditional approval of the Ariet's Grove Filing No. 1 preliminary plat. It then went to the Board of Trustees for a public hearing on Oct. 26.

mead/6.title: 1785 Weld County Road 32 annexation and Valdez annexation zoning
mead/6.summary: The Planning Commission recommended initial zoning for two annexations: Public Facilities zoning for the town-owned Valdez property and initial zoning for 1785 Weld County Road 32.

mead/7.title: Urban Renewal Authority tax increment incentive policy
mead/7.summary: The Mead Urban Renewal Authority considered a formal policy for evaluating requests for tax increment financing reimbursement of public improvement costs. It sets eligibility thresholds, three evaluation criteria and a small project track, and keeps the board's full discretion. The board took up the policy as Resolution 03-URA-2026 on Oct. 26.

mead/8.title: I-25 sewer relocation and Safe Routes to School construction contracts
mead/8.summary: The Board considered awarding the I-25 Sewer Relocation Project bid to SMH West LLC and the Mead Safe Routes to School bid to Colorado Paving. It also considered a common use agreement with CDOT for the sewer relocation.
mead/8.where: I-25 corridor and Mead school routes

mead/9.title: High Plains Boulevard road project
mead/9.summary: Construction of two miles of High Plains Boulevard (WCR 9.5) between WCR 32 and WCR 36 is nearly complete. It includes two travel lanes, bike lanes, roundabouts at CR 32 and CR 34, and a ten-foot detached sidewalk. A celebration was planned in October.
mead/9.where: High Plains Blvd between WCR 32 and WCR 36

mead/10.title: New Mead library and Parks, Recreation, Open Space and Trails Master Plan
mead/10.summary: The town celebrated the new High Plains Library District Mead Library on Chaparral Street and gave conditional acceptance of its public improvements. The Board also adopted the Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Master Plan.

meeker/0.title: Circle Park water rights discussion
meeker/0.summary: The Council's October 6 agenda includes a discussion of water rights for Circle Park, along with a final water report from Micheal Erion. The documents give no details on the outcome.

meeker/1.title: Draft Town of Meeker 2026 budget
meeker/1.summary: The Council is scheduled to see a presentation of the draft 2026 town budget on October 6. A presentation from Pioneers Medical Center is also on the same agenda.

meeker/2.title: Short-term rental conditional use permit at Chase Rule's property
meeker/2.summary: The Council held a public hearing on February 23 on a conditional use permit for Chase Rule to run a short-term rental. The street address is cut off in the agenda.

meeker/3.title: Setback variance requests (891 3rd Street, 325 Curtis Creek Drive, 390 Market Street)
meeker/3.summary: The Council heard variance requests to reduce setbacks. Theodore and Jana Dawson asked for a side yard setback of about 6 feet at 891 3rd Street. Renninger Investments asked for a 0-foot front yard setback at 325 Curtis Creek Drive. Training Grounds, LLC asked for a reduced side yard setback at 390 Market Street.
meeker/3.where: 891 3rd Street; 325 Curtis Creek Drive; 390 Market Street

meeker/4.title: Sign and fence variances (43904 Highway 13 and 172 Water Street)
meeker/4.summary: On August 3 the Council took up two variance requests. David Bradfield asked to put up a sign larger than the maximum at 43904 Highway 13. Jessica and Matt Franks asked to build an eight-foot fence at 172 Water Street.

meeker/5.title: Home occupation and right-of-way encroachment requests
meeker/5.summary: On July 13 the Council considered a home occupation conditional use for Tevin Pelloni at 440 Garfield Street. It also considered an encroachment request from Rebekah and Justin Grant to access the town's right-of-way in Sanderson Hills Subdivision.

mesa-county/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center applications in unincorporated Mesa County
mesa-county/0.summary: On Sept. 29 the commissioners were to consider a temporary moratorium on accepting, processing and approving land use applications for data center facilities in unincorporated Mesa County. It would also suspend negotiation of county inducements for such facilities. The documents do not state the outcome.

mesa-county/1.title: Appeal of short-term rental approval at 123 Mesa Vista Road
mesa-county/1.summary: The commissioners were to hear the Parentice appeal of an administrative approval (RES2026-0224, Beatrice Estate) that would allow a short-term rental at 123 Mesa Vista Road, owned by Passion Project, LLC, in an RSF-4 zone. The hearing was set for Sept. 15.
mesa-county/1.where: 123 Mesa Vista Road, south of South Broadway, Grand Junction

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing

mesa-county/2.title: 32 1/2 Road Phase II roadway improvement project
mesa-county/2.summary: The county moved on the 32 1/2 Road project through a property purchase and deed in August. In September it took up a new agreement with Housing Resources of Western Colorado for a regional stormwater detention facility, replacing a 2008 agreement, and a memorandum of understanding with Clifton Water District. It also considered a $4,606,193.95 construction contract with Mountain Valley Contracting.

mesa-county/3.title: Grand Junction Regional Airport FAA grants and runway replacement
mesa-county/3.summary: The county accepted and ratified several FAA Airport Improvement Program grants as co-sponsor with the Airport Authority. They cover terminal improvements and the runway replacement program, including a $13,265,445 grant for runway transition and taxiway conversion.

mesa-county/4.title: 2027 county budget and special district budgets
mesa-county/4.summary: Staff briefed the commissioners on Mesa County's proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 6. They also briefed on the proposed budgets for the Mesa Community Center, Lower Valley, Whitewater and Upper Grand Valley Pest districts. A supplemental 2026 budget resolution was also considered Sept. 22.

mesa-county/5.title: Board of Public Health budget, finances and legal counsel
mesa-county/5.summary: The Board of Public Health reviewed its financial status and the 2027 budget in work sessions and meetings. It repeatedly met on engaging legal counsel, including conflict counsel, and on an intergovernmental agreement with Mesa County. Outcomes are not stated in the documents.

sources.body: Board of Public Health Work Session
Board of Public Health Special Meeting

mesa-county/6.title: Flock camera presentation by Sheriff's Office
mesa-county/6.summary: The Sheriff's Office gave a presentation on Flock cameras to the commissioners on Aug. 18. The documents give no detail on what was presented or decided.

mesa-county/7.title: Stormwater Management Manual contract changes
mesa-county/7.summary: The county considered change orders with Wright Water Engineers for the Stormwater Management Manual, including an $87,214 second change order. The work covers cost-impact analysis, community outreach, training and technical updates.

mesa-county/8.title: Justice Center projects
mesa-county/8.summary: The commissioners considered a $2,223,684 contract with Comfort Air of Grand Junction to replace rooftop units at the Mesa County Justice Center. They also considered a $15,000 change order for architect Roth Sheppard on the design of the Justice Center North Addition.

mesa-county/9.title: Land use hearings: rezones, vacation of rights-of-way and PUD extension
mesa-county/9.summary: The commissioners heard the Serrano Estates rezone of 4.1 acres at 825 26 Road, the Bailey rezone of 7 acres at 1083 20 Road near Fruita, and a five-year extension of the Experius Community PUD plan to Dec. 17, 2031. They also heard the Smith vacation of Patterson and Burbank Street rights-of-way in Loma and an easement extinguishment at 223 Elberta Drive.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing
Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing
Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing

mesa-county/10.title: Wildfire mitigation and trails grant applications
mesa-county/10.summary: The county considered an $840,000 Forest Restoration and Wildfire Risk Mitigation grant application for the Mesa Creek Cross-Boundary Wildfire Mitigation Project. It also considered a Colorado Parks and Wildlife Trails Stewardship Grant application. In October it supported a federal Forest Health and Wildfire Risk Reduction Act.
mesa-county/10.where: Mesa Creek area and county trails

mesa-county/11.title: Federal land and legislative support letters
mesa-county/11.summary: The commissioners approved letters to the Bureau of Land Management on wilderness characteristics in land use planning. In October they considered letters supporting federal bills on forest health, geothermal energy and snow water forecasting, and a Waters of the United States definition update. They also considered a resolution supporting Grand Junction as the western terminus of new state rail service.

milliken/0.title: Water bills, new smart meters and rate increases
milliken/0.summary: Residents told the Board that water bills jumped after the Metron smart meter replacement (about a $1.25 million project) and tiered rates; one resident cited a 30,000-gallon bill and another asked for 2024 vs 2025 rate comparisons. The interim administrator said rate adjustments averaged about 35% with the baseline up about 14%, and that next year's rates come from a five-year cost-of-service study, with rates usually adopted in December.

milliken/1.title: Paving County Road 44 in the 2027 budget
milliken/1.summary: Residents of CR 44, including Katie VanDeraa at 9102 CR 44, asked the Board to remove proposed paving from the 2027 budget, citing traffic, speed, cost and the road's rural character. The proposal is part of the 2027 budget review that continued through October.

milliken/2.title: 2027 Town budget process
milliken/2.summary: The Board held budget retreats and repeated review sessions on the General Fund and proposed 2027 budget. The first public budget hearing is set for October 14, with final adoption at the November public hearing.

milliken/3.title: New Town Administrator hire: Greg Brinck
milliken/3.summary: The Board approved a Town Administrator employment agreement offered to Greg Brinck after interviews and negotiations, and a September resolution appointing him was on the agenda. By October he was reporting to the Board as Town Administrator.

milliken/4.title: Town Hall rental program fees and hybrid model
milliken/4.summary: Staff proposed raising hourly Town Hall rental rates under a hybrid model, keeping a tiered structure with reduced rates for residents and nonprofits and higher rates for non-residents. The Board discussed it August 12 and again August 26 before fee schedule amendments are prepared.

milliken/5.title: Water Supply Element of the Comprehensive Plan
milliken/5.summary: The Board approved a contract with Ayres Associates, not to exceed $17,500, to prepare the Water Supply Element required by state Senate Bill 24-174. Staff reported kicking off the update in September.

milliken/6.title: Milliken Housing Authority budget, Prop 123 and strategic plan
milliken/6.summary: The Housing Authority drafted and approved its 2027 budget, which projects a balance of about $140,720 on Jan 1, 2027. It also worked on its strategic plan, Prop 123 meetings with the Community Development Director, and Dove Valley operating costs and water bill questions, and planned a presentation to the Town Board in November.
milliken/6.where: Dove Valley and Housing Authority, 1101 Broad Street

milliken/7.title: HWY 257 noise complaint
milliken/7.summary: The Board took up discussion and direction on a noise complaint about Highway 257 on August 12. The documents do not state an outcome.

milliken/8.title: Food truck park and student home construction at 1398 Irene
milliken/8.summary: The Board scheduled discussion of a possible food truck park and of a student home construction partnership at 1398 Irene. It also considered an encroachment agreement with the Meadow Farms HOA.

milliken/9.title: Social media and communications policy
milliken/9.summary: Trustees asked that the town's social media policy be added for discussion, and it came back in September and October as a communications and social media policy discussion.

milliken/10.title: Sidewalk and ADA project and Little Thompson River project
milliken/10.summary: The Board considered the CDOT-funded Milliken Sidewalk and ADA Project in October. Staff also reported on the Little Thompson River project, with documents approved by CDOT and construction bidding expected in August.

minturn/0.title: Minturn shooting range grant and USFS special use permit
minturn/0.summary: The Town was awarded a $225,000 Colorado Parks and Wildlife grant to improve its shooting range and address long-standing issues. It is seeking in-kind help from Eagle County and a Forest Service special use permit, targeted for Spring 2027. A council item on the range was pulled and continued on Oct. 7, and a status update was on the Oct. 21 agenda.

minturn/1.title: Police services contract with Eagle County Sheriff's Office
minturn/1.summary: Council is negotiating a police services contract with the Eagle County Sheriff's Office beginning in 2027. Talks cover service levels, costs, contract terms and community concerns about automated license plate readers. Proposed terms will return to the full Council for approval.

minturn/2.title: Speed bumps and traffic calming on Main Street and neighborhood streets
minturn/2.summary: Residents in the Boulder and Pine Street area asked for traffic calming, and residents spoke about speeding and missing speed bumps. Staff is studying a Main Street speed camera and evaluating speed bumps, speed tables and radar feedback signs for the FY 2027 budget.
minturn/2.where: Main Street and Boulder/Pine Street area

minturn/3.title: Water moratorium and downtown water improvements
minturn/3.summary: Council took up the second reading of Ordinance No. 11 amending the town's water moratorium. It also considered Resolution No. 50 repurposing CDS funds for downtown water improvements. Water Treatment Plant work and line relocation are ongoing.

minturn/4.title: Historic Preservation Plan update
minturn/4.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission finalized the 2026 Historic Preservation Plan, with amendments to goals on objects and cultural resources. Members discussed asking Council about a historic district and a budget line item for preservation. They also elected Ken Halliday chair and Dan Brown vice chair, and gave an update on the Meyer's Barn project.

minturn/5.title: Regional housing authority and employee housing
minturn/5.summary: Council discussed the Regional Housing Authority in a joint meeting with Eagle County, where housing costs, unoccupied homes and employee housing were raised. Participants noted the RHA is still taking shape and past ballot measures lacked a specific plan.

minturn/6.title: Land use code rewrite and definitions
minturn/6.summary: The Planning Commission worked through draft definitions and standards for the land use code, including permeability of decks and parking areas, bulk plane illustrations, and how uses in the Bolts Lake zone districts are separated under a settlement agreement.

minturn/7.title: DDA Investment and Incentive Policy
minturn/7.summary: The Downtown Development Authority board considered Resolution No. 02 adopting an Investment and Incentive Policy. It covers a small project matching grant program, large redevelopment and catalyst projects, and strategic property acquisition.

minturn/8.title: 2027 budget and sales tax
minturn/8.summary: Staff and council began 2027 budget talks, with sales tax about $10K down year to date. Capital wish-list items include traffic calming, a Beach Park retaining wall and other projects.

minturn/9.title: Main Street parking study
minturn/9.summary: A planning intern presented parking study findings. Council members suggested a winter study around plowing restrictions, later evening counts of resident vehicles, and marking parking spaces on Main Street if permitted.

minturn/10.title: Xcel Energy power outages and reliability
minturn/10.summary: Town staff met with the Colorado Energy Office and Xcel Energy about outages and system reliability. The Town sent formal correspondence at Xcel's recommendation and is monitoring its response.

minturn/11.title: Ballot Issue 5B for Education Foundation of Eagle County
minturn/11.summary: Council heard a presentation from the Education Foundation of Eagle County and considered Resolution No. 51 on Ballot Issue 5B.

minturn/12.title: ERWSD Main Street siphon rehabilitation
minturn/12.summary: Eagle River Water & Sanitation District is rehabilitating the Minturn siphon, with sewer bypass pumping starting by Aug. 14 and traffic control on US 24/Main Street.

moffat-county/0.title: Data center moratorium and regulations
moffat-county/0.summary: Residents, Pure-Green Colorado (Trapper Reborn project) and Yampa Valley Electric spoke on a proposed data center moratorium (Resolution 2026-103) on Sept 8, mostly opposing it. The Planning & Zoning Commission took up rulemaking and public panel meetings were held in early October. On Oct 13 Commissioner Bohrer called for a motion to adopt the moratorium and got no response, so it died.

moffat-county/1.title: 2027 County Budget public hearing
moffat-county/1.summary: A public hearing was held Oct 13 to present and adopt the proposed 2027 Moffat County budget, as required by state statute. The documents excerpted do not state the final vote.

moffat-county/2.title: Term limits referendum on November ballot
moffat-county/2.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-100 referring a term limits question to voters, plus an intergovernmental agreement with the Clerk's Office to place it on the November ballot. Both passed 3-0.

moffat-county/3.title: Craig skatepark funding and design
moffat-county/3.summary: The Craig Skatepark Alliance and county staff won approval to apply for $25,000 grants each from the Laura Jane Musser Fund and El Pomar Foundation toward construction. The group plans a GOCO application in January, and a services agreement with Grindline Skateparks was on the Oct 13 consent agenda.

moffat-county/4.title: Loudy-Simpson Park Master Plan
moffat-county/4.summary: Staff presented a Logan Simpson proposal for a master plan for Loudy-Simpson Park, and the contract was on the Sept 22 consent agenda.

moffat-county/5.title: Echo Park Road (CR 156) closure after flash flooding
moffat-county/5.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-120 temporarily closing County Road 156 in Dinosaur National Monument because of flood erosion. The Park Service has archaeological concerns to investigate before road repairs can begin.
moffat-county/5.where: County Road 156 (Echo Park Road), Dinosaur National Monument

moffat-county/6.title: Road & Bridge snow bank payment policy
moffat-county/6.summary: A Road & Bridge employee, George Miner, asked commissioners to examine inconsistencies in the snow bank payment policy and followed up on Sept 8 about his earlier request.

moffat-county/7.title: Vermillion/Great Divide shop project
moffat-county/7.summary: The county approved a contract amendment with Charchalis Construction for the Vermillion Shop and later took up fuel tank removal testing and consultation for the Great Divide/Vermillion Shop project.

moffat-county/8.title: Employee Health Insurance Advisory Board reinstated
moffat-county/8.summary: Commissioners were asked to reinstate the Employee Health Insurance Advisory Board and appoint five employee-elected members to recommend improvements to the plan. Bohrer moved to appoint the five members.

moffat-county/9.title: Wolf Creek Reservoir jurisdictional determination
moffat-county/9.summary: A request for a new approved jurisdictional determination for the Wolf Creek Reservoir Project was on the consent agenda on Sept 22.

montrose-county/0.title: Gold Mountain Fire response and FEMA support
montrose-county/0.summary: The county activated an Emergency Operations Center for the 2026 Gold Mountain Fire, with Road and Bridge crews supporting the response. The county leased the Wells Basin property to stage fire mitigation crews, and the Chair signed a letter asking the President for FEMA support.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/1.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code agreements with fire districts
montrose-county/1.summary: The county considered intergovernmental agreements with the Montrose Fire Protection District and the Norwood Fire Protection District to share administration and enforcement of the county's adopted Wildfire Resiliency Code.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/2.title: Ordinance banning non-native wildlife and wildlife resolutions
montrose-county/2.summary: A public hearing was set for Oct. 28 on proposed Ordinance 2026-01, which would prohibit the intentional introduction or release of non-native wildlife species in unincorporated Montrose County. The board also considered resolutions opposing a citizen petition to ban lead ammunition for hunting and opposing proposed Colorado Parks and Wildlife changes on prairie dogs.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/3.title: 2027 proposed county budget and 2026 supplemental appropriation
montrose-county/3.summary: The 2027 proposed budget was presented to commissioners at a public hearing on Oct. 14. Finance also brought a first supplemental appropriation to the 2026 budget to a work session, along with a follow-up on community partnership funding.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/4.title: $75,000 emergency funding for West End Family Link
montrose-county/4.summary: At a special meeting in Nucla, the commissioners heard a presentation and public comment on an emergency funding request from West End Family Link. Commissioner Pond moved to fund the request at $75,000.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/5.title: Kinikin Road and county road work
montrose-county/5.summary: Public Works gave Kinikin Road updates at two work sessions, and a County Road Education session was scheduled. Road and Bridge also responded to the 6400 Road flood, and the county contracted for B-24 bridge rail replacement ($487,333) and for asphalt overlay work with the Town of Olathe.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/6.title: Housing needs assessment grant and private activity bonds
