montrose-county/6.summary: Planning and Development discussed a grant application for a Housing Needs Assessment related to SB24-174. The county also assigned $1,573,936 of its 2026 private activity bond allocation to the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/7.title: Montrose Regional Airport projects and leases
montrose-county/7.summary: The county handled several airport matters: hangar lease changes, geotechnical design work for apron and taxilane reconstruction, an AWOS installation retainage release, a law enforcement reimbursement agreement of $54,750, and baggage delivery permits.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/8.title: Rural health grants, behavioral health contracts and safe sleep program
montrose-county/8.summary: The county sent support letters for Family Connects Colorado and Basin Clinic's Rural Health Transformation Program applications. It also approved core mental health service agreements with Axis Health Systems and H.O.P.E. Counseling, and discussed a Rocky Mountain Health Plans Safe Sleep Incentive Program.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/9.title: Montrose/Ouray county line discussion
montrose-county/9.summary: A work session item on Oct. 26 covered a Montrose/Ouray County line discussion. The documents give no further detail.

montrose/0.title: Charter amendments for the November ballot (election date, term limits, council oversight of police chief and city clerk)
montrose/0.summary: Council took up Ordinances 2727-2730 to put charter changes on the ballot: moving municipal elections to November, an 8-year lifetime term limit for the at-large seat, and council approval rights over appointing and discharging the police chief and the city clerk. Earlier proposed amendments (he/she language, ranked choice) were dropped, and residents spoke both for and against the remaining measures.

montrose/1.title: City manager separation and interim city manager
montrose/1.summary: Council went into executive session about a confidential memo and possible independent counsel, then approved a mutual separation agreement with City Manager Bill Bell on Sept 1. On Sept 15 it ratified the agreement, appointed Ann Morgenthaler as interim city manager under an open-ended agreement during recruitment, and named her Montrose Urban Renewal Authority executive director. Council had to ratify the decisions because the original action was not specifically noticed.

montrose/2.title: Council vacancies: District IV and At-Large seats
montrose/2.summary: The District IV seat was vacated Sept 7 and the charter requires an appointment within 30 days. Council appointed Adam Woodden to District IV on Oct 6, which opened the At-Large seat; applications ran Oct 7-21, and John Brown, Danielle Godt and Cindee Williams were up for appointment Nov 2.

montrose/3.title: Locust Road Addition annexation (1815 Locust Road)
montrose/3.summary: A 4.2-acre annexation at 1815 Locust Road, including part of the road right of way, with requested R-2 low-density zoning. Planning Commission recommended approval of the zoning and discussed improving pedestrian infrastructure and eventually rebuilding Locust Road. Council set a Sept 15 hearing and took Ordinance 2731 on second reading Oct 6.

montrose/4.title: Data center moratorium request
montrose/4.summary: A resident urged council to enact a moratorium on new data centers until regulations are in place.

montrose/5.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing opt-in and Shepherd's Hand shelter funding
montrose/5.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-16 committing to increase affordable housing units under Proposition 123, and a $28,597 expenditure tied to the housing effort. It also reviewed a funding request for The Shepherd's Hand shelter. The state also requires a housing needs assessment and housing action plan as part of the comprehensive plan update.

montrose/6.title: Comprehensive plan update and growth concerns
montrose/6.summary: Staff are doing a five-year update of the Envision 2040 comprehensive plan and land development code, including state-mandated housing, water supply and strategic growth planning, with approval targeted by year's end. Residents urged council to make growth pay its own way and stick to the plan on subdivisions.

montrose/7.title: 2027 fee schedule revisions
montrose/7.summary: Proposed fees effective Jan 1, 2027 include higher cemetery lot and open/close fees, a higher school land dedication fee-in-lieu, a higher memorial bench fee, a $75 park shelter electricity fee, and a $50 building reinspection fee. Resolution 2026-18 to adopt the schedule was set for Nov 2.

montrose/8.title: Rotary Park pump house replacement
montrose/8.summary: Council considered a $514,011 contract with FCI Constructors to replace the 1980s irrigation pump house at Rotary Park, which is at the end of its useful life. This is $14,011 over the $500,000 budget, covered by savings from other 2026 Public Works capital projects.

montrose/9.title: Landfill agreement extension with Bruin Waste Management
montrose/9.summary: Staff recommended a one-year extension of the landfill agreement with Bruin Waste Management, LLC, scheduled for council action Nov 2.

montrose/10.title: Student parking on residential streets near the high school
montrose/10.summary: Residents asked council to reinstate permit-only parking on residential streets near the high school and to increase police presence.

montrose/11.title: Miami Road electronic speed sign
montrose/11.summary: Residents asked for an electronic traffic speed indicator sign on Miami Road near Cedar Creek.

montrose/12.title: Subdivision and zoning hearings at Planning Commission
montrose/12.summary: Planning Commission reviewed the Star Court Lot 8 townhomes plat (739-749 E. Star Court), the Chelsi Lane townhomes PD amendment (reducing units from 24 to 23), the Chipeta Lake 2 annexation zoning (1.14 acres, requested Public zoning), and the Spruce Point amended preliminary plat.
montrose/12.where: 739-749 E. Star Court; Chelsi Lane; Chipeta Road; Sanctuary Drive

monument/0.title: Monument 2040 Comprehensive Plan and Downtown Master Plan
monument/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on the draft Monument 2040 Comprehensive Plan and Downtown Master Plan, the product of nearly two years of outreach. Residents worried that conceptual downtown redevelopment renderings don't fit Monument's historic small-town character, and asked about participation levels. The Town Council was scheduled to hold a public hearing on adopting it (Resolution 78-2026) on Nov. 2.

monument/1.title: Use tax increase ballot issue
monument/1.summary: The Town is referring a ballot issue to raise its use tax on construction and building materials (Ordinance 19-2026), with potential construction use tax revenue of about $2.2M. Raising the motor vehicle use tax to 3.5 would add about $500K. Council considered Resolution 77-2026 expressing support, and the advisory committee questioned the earlier lack of attention to motor vehicle use tax.

monument/2.title: 2027 town budget
monument/2.summary: The finance director presented the preliminary and draft 2027 budget to the Citizens Service Levels Advisory Committee and Town Council. Topics included the Traffic Impact Fee and Park Fee funds, four new police positions funded by police impact fees, stormwater impact fee study, park vandalism, a pavilion at Monument Lake and water system cybersecurity. Council asked for more information on the 2F and Police Department funds.

monument/3.title: Jackson Creek Parkway growth and traffic
monument/3.summary: Advisory committee members raised concerns about traffic from growth, including a Target (completion October 2028), apartments near Walmart, and a possible Costco, and whether widening Jackson Creek Parkway to four lanes is enough. Traffic impact fees can be used on the parkway. Council was to get an improvements update Nov. 2, and a resident raised traffic on Old Denver Road.
monument/3.where: Jackson Creek Parkway and Old Denver Road

monument/4.title: Commercial PUD approvals: 7 Brew, Native Sun, Karl Malone Powersports, Conexus
monument/4.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed several development plans. These include 7 Brew Drive Thru Coffee at 15822 Jackson Creek Parkway, a Native Sun Construction amendment at 15010 Woodcarver Road with a deceleration lane and 66 new trees, and a 30,000 sq ft Karl Malone Powersports RV sales and service site. Council took up ordinances for 7 Brew and Native Sun on Sept. 8. Conexus Lot 1 Filing 2 (312 apartments) was also reviewed, and Council later acted on a Conexus property transfer and temporary easement.
monument/4.where: 15822 Jackson Creek Pkwy; 15010 Woodcarver Rd; Conexus

monument/5.title: Falcon Commerce Center Phase 2 PUD amendment
monument/5.summary: Council re-introduced Ordinance 15-2026, which would approve a major amendment to the preliminary PUD for the south 43 acres of Falcon Commerce Center. It was continued from Aug. 3 and staff gave a timeline of events.

monument/6.title: Appeal of use classification at 309 Woodworth Street
monument/6.summary: The Planning Commission heard an appeal of the Planning Director's use classification determination for 309 Woodworth Street (Case BOA-02-2026).

monument/7.title: Prohibited motorized devices ordinance
monument/7.summary: Council considered Ordinance 25-2026 regulating certain prohibited motorized devices, presented by police. Council members supported its educational components and a motion was made to approve it.

monument/8.title: Water quality, water attorney and water taps
monument/8.summary: Council heard a presentation on water testing and sampling to maintain water quality, and appointed Nazarenus Stack & Wombacher as the Town's water attorney (Resolution 71-2026). A council member asked for a water workshop, and Resolution 68-2026 authorized a new tap.

monument/9.title: Police fee schedule and handgun purchase
monument/9.summary: Council approved revisions to the police department services fee schedule effective Oct. 1 (Resolution 72-2026). Council also considered buying Shadow Systems handguns for on-duty officers (Resolution 63-2026) on the consent agenda.

monument/10.title: Snowplow agreement with El Paso County and road grant
monument/10.summary: Council considered an intergovernmental agreement with El Paso County reaffirming the snowplow agreement, including the newly built section of Beacon Lite Road. Council also authorized a Federal Lands Access Program grant application (Resolution 67-2026).

monument/11.title: Small business and nonprofit funding requests
monument/11.summary: The advisory committee weighed a funding proposal from the Small Business Development Center Network, with members critical of the $250 consulting fee and the impact. Silver Key asked Council to consider a $25,000 contribution.

morgan-county/0.title: Data center zoning regulations
morgan-county/0.summary: The county commissioners have been working on new data center rules for Chapter 4 of the zoning regulations. The Planning Commission recommended approval in April 2026, and the commissioners' hearing opened May 5 and was continued repeatedly, through August 4, for staff revisions. Open points include new definitions (edge, large and accessory data centers), setbacks, closed-loop cooling only, and decommissioning and emergency plans.

morgan-county/1.title: Fortress solar and battery project: road work enforcement hearing
morgan-county/1.summary: The county issued a Notice of Intent to Take Enforcement Action and Order to Show Cause against Fortress over its three-phase solar and battery project. The notice alleges violations of its special use permits and the Public Improvements Agreement for paving County Roads Q and R, including paving before county inspectors could observe roadbed preparation. Fortress responded in writing ahead of the October 23 hearing and said it will crush and rebuild the road.

morgan-county/2.title: Jail expansion and county financial report
morgan-county/2.summary: The 2025 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report was presented August 18. It notes that the commissioners are targeting a County Jail expansion funded partly by an Energy Impact Assistance Fund grant and a Jail Capital Improvement Fund set up in 2008. The county may also ask the cities and towns to help pay.

morgan-county/3.title: Home Rule Charter and special election
morgan-county/3.summary: On September 1 the commissioners heard a presentation on a Home Rule Charter from Charter Commissioner Brian McCracken. They also considered Resolution 2026 BCC 38 calling a special election.

morgan-county/4.title: Planning and building fee schedule changes
morgan-county/4.summary: The commissioners considered Resolution 2026 BCC 40 adopting new fees for planning services and building inspection on September 1. A revised 2026 county fee schedule for Planning, Zoning and Building Inspection came up again September 29.

morgan-county/5.title: Zoning enforcement process amendments and junk ordinance
morgan-county/5.summary: On September 29 the commissioners considered Resolution 2026 BCC 42, which cleans up the zoning regulations' enforcement processes and adds continuing county jurisdiction over permits. On September 15 they took up Ordinance No. 2, Series 2026, a first reading on county prohibitions on junk and refuse deposited in unapproved sites in unincorporated areas, with an exemption for operating junk yards.

morgan-county/6.title: Temporary RV housing special use permit near Wiggins
morgan-county/6.summary: A special use permit hearing on August 4 concerned temporary residential use of RVs at 18975 County Road 1 while manufactured home placement permits are obtained. Once the homes are in place, the RVs would no longer be allowed as residences. The permit is meant to bring the property into compliance with county zoning.

morgan-county/7.title: Farm stand special use permit on County Road 19
morgan-county/7.summary: The commissioners heard a special use permit for a small family farm stand at 16255 County Road 19 on August 4, in an Estate Residential zone. Resolution 2026 BCC 33 approving it was on the August 18 agenda, following a Planning Commission recommendation of approval on July 13.

morgan-county/8.title: Solar lease amendment and wastewater plant road use agreement
morgan-county/8.summary: On October 6 the commissioners considered a second amendment to a 2024 solar energy system lease and easement covering about 17 acres. They also considered a road use agreement with Glacier Construction for the expansion of Fort Morgan's wastewater treatment plant.

morgan-county/9.title: Justice Center security fence and Proposition 123 presentation
morgan-county/9.summary: On October 20 the commissioners considered awarding a bid for a security fence project at the Morgan County Justice Center and East Point Building. They also heard a presentation on Proposition 123 from the United Way.
morgan-county/9.where: Morgan County Justice Center, Fort Morgan

morgan-county/10.title: Mission Goldwing Solar Project comments
morgan-county/10.summary: The county was asked for comments on the Mission Goldwing Solar Project in Adams County near the county line. It was on the September 1 agenda.

morrison/0.title: The Fort extraterritorial water and sewer agreement and Farm at the Fort annexation
morrison/0.summary: The Board considered an agreement to provide water and sewer service to The Fort and an adjacent parcel for Morrison RE Development, LP. It would allow up to 75 EQRs (50 residential), $2.5 million in impact fees and a public improvement fee on restaurant sales. Separate notices set August 18 public hearings on annexing about 59.36 acres known as the Farm at the Fort and on initial zoning (RE and MX-N). The agreement notes the developer intends to withdraw its annexation and zoning applications.
morrison/0.where: The Fort / Farm at the Fort, unincorporated Jefferson County near Morrison

morrison/1.title: Green Tree Metro District extraterritorial sewer service
morrison/1.summary: The Board approved a term sheet for extraterritorial sewer service with Green Tree Metro District and held executive sessions on negotiations. A Green Tree Metro District sewer service agreement was on the October 20 agenda.

morrison/2.title: Downtown and overnight parking concerns
morrison/2.summary: Residents told the Board that new downtown businesses should not be permitted without adequate parking. The Board discussed overnight parking (discussion only) and interstate parking, and sought community direction on parking issues.

morrison/3.title: Lodging tax changes and November ballot questions
morrison/3.summary: Ordinance 562 aligns the lodging tax exemption with the 2012 voter-approved ballot language, effective October 1, 2026. Two ballot questions would remove the small-lodging exemption (+$125,000) and raise the rate from 6% to 8% (+$500,000), starting January 1, 2027.

morrison/4.title: 2027 draft budget
morrison/4.summary: The draft 2027 budget includes a 15.85% health insurance renewal increase, a 3.6% cost-of-living raise, and a new full-time position under consideration. Lodging tax is expected to become the second-largest tax revenue source, and a hotel uses the sales tax incentive program (ESTIP). The first of two hearings was set for November 4.

morrison/5.title: Water and sewer code rewrite and drought watering restrictions
morrison/5.summary: Ordinance 565 repealed and replaced Title 8 of the municipal code to clarify water and sewer requirements, including backflow rules. Mandatory outdoor watering restrictions (two days per week, none 10am-6pm) have applied since April 2, 2026 because of drought.

morrison/6.title: Town Manager transition
morrison/6.summary: The Board approved an interim Town Manager employment agreement effective August 14, 2026, held executive sessions on the manager's exit interview, and later took up a Town Manager employment agreement and the manager application process.

morrison/7.title: East Planning Area agreements
morrison/7.summary: The Board held closed negotiations on development of the East Planning Area and on October 6 approved a pre-development agreement tied to it.

morrison/8.title: Zoning code amendments: garden sheds, motels, floodplain
morrison/8.summary: Ordinance 566 permits garden sheds up to 120 sq ft as an accessory use, adds motels in the HD district, requires structures elevated two feet above base flood elevation, and revises the definition of substantial improvement.

morrison/9.title: Nuisance abatement on public property
morrison/9.summary: Ordinance 567 allows the Town to abate nuisances on public property without notice. The Board adopted it October 6.

mountain-view/0.title: R3 and R4 zoning district update
mountain-view/0.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission is set to consider recommending adoption of an R3/R4 zoning update on October 7, 2026. It includes general plan amendments, a zoning map change applying R4 in 14 change areas and new R3-A, R3-B and R3-C districts, and an environmental impact report certification.

mountain-view/1.title: 36-unit rowhouse project at 924-940 San Rafael Avenue
mountain-view/1.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission will hear a gatekeeper project on October 21, 2026. It would rezone two parcels from industrial (MM) to R3-2 and replace two industrial buildings with 36 rowhouses under state density bonus law. It also needs a general plan amendment, a vesting tentative map, and removal of two heritage trees.

mountain-view/2.title: LinkedIn development agreement amendment
mountain-view/2.summary: Council introduced an amendment to LinkedIn's development agreement on October 13, 2026, and an adoption was on the October 27 consent agenda. A $1.6 million public benefit fee would go to the Mountain View Affordable Housing Fund once the funds are received.
mountain-view/2.where: 700-810 East Middlefield Road and 1100-1200 Maude Avenue

mountain-view/3.title: Historic Preservation Ordinance and Historic Register update
mountain-view/3.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission reviewed the update to the historic preservation ordinance and the zoning map amendment on August 19, 2026. Council second reading to adopt them was on the October 13 agenda. Public comments are attached to the staff materials.

mountain-view/4.title: Rengstorff Complete Streets Study and Active Transportation Plan
mountain-view/4.summary: The Bicycle/Pedestrian Advisory Committee heard the Rengstorff Complete Streets Study (Project 25-39) and voted 5-0 on August 18 to recommend the final Active Transportation Plan. It asked for added language on smaller-scale projects and for Los Altos schools on the maps. The Council Transportation Committee took up both items on August 31.

mountain-view/5.title: Affordable housing financing: 96 West El Camino Real and 334 San Antonio Road
mountain-view/5.summary: Council considered accepting $388,515 in state Permanent Local Housing Allocation funds, with money directed to the 96 West El Camino Real affordable project and a homeownership assistance pilot. It also considered tax-exempt bond financing for 96 West El Camino Real and for 334 San Antonio Road.
mountain-view/5.where: 96 West El Camino Real; 334 San Antonio Road

mountain-view/6.title: Heritage tree removal appeals
mountain-view/6.summary: The Urban Forestry Board denied the 961 Eichler Drive appeal and approved the appeal for a heritage tree at 777 San Carrizo Way, overturning staff. An appeal for 1473 Tyler Park Way is set for October 14. Commissioners asked for coordination on the Heritage Tree Ordinance update, which is also on the October 14 agenda. Other hearings involve tree removals at an affordable housing site and 26 trees at a mobile home park.
mountain-view/6.where: 961 Eichler Drive; 777 San Carrizo Way; 1473 Tyler Park Way

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Commission and Urban Forestry Board
Parks and Recreation Commission and Urban Forestry Board

mountain-view/7.title: Rent stabilization appeals
mountain-view/7.summary: The Rental Housing Committee upheld a tentative appeal decision on a landlord-tenant petition on August 27, 2026. It also discussed the one-time utility adjustment petition process. Another appeal (Petition C25260032) is scheduled for October 22.

mountain-view/8.title: Shoreline athletic fields and Google environmental reimbursement
mountain-view/8.summary: Council acting as the Shoreline Regional Park Community board considered an $880,000 Tetra Tech contract for athletic field renovations. It also considered agreements with Google for reimbursement of past environmental work and for ongoing monitoring, with $4,968,700 appropriated.

mountain-view/9.title: SR 237/Middlefield Road interchange and Public Safety Building
mountain-view/9.summary: Council was asked to approve the design concept for the State Route 237 and Middlefield Road interchange improvements (Project 19-65). It also considered authorizing pre-qualification of bidders for Package 2 of the Public Safety Building (Project 20-49).
mountain-view/9.where: SR 237 and Middlefield Road; Public Safety Building

mountain-view/10.title: Ambulance billing fees and Pathways to Housing progress report
mountain-view/10.summary: Council considered revised ambulance billing and user fees for the Fire Department on October 13, 2026. It also considered accepting the first annual progress report on the Pathways to Housing homeless response strategy.

mountain-view/11.title: Downtown Castro Street and pedestrian mall
mountain-view/11.summary: The Downtown Committee was to get updates on downtown development, Castro Street and the Business Improvement Area renewal. Its members listed future topics including vacant storefronts, parking and restrooms. The Bicycle/Pedestrian Advisory Committee was to review the concept for interim pedestrian mall improvements at Castro and California Streets (Project 23-49).

mountain-view/12.title: All-electric construction zoning exceptions
mountain-view/12.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission was to consider a zoning amendment allowing exceptions to development standards in R1 and R2 districts for single-family and duplex homes that voluntarily build all-electric.

nederland/0.title: Rezoning 242 & 252 E 5th St from General Commercial to Medium Density Residential
nederland/0.summary: LandShark Investments LLC asked to rezone two vacant lots on E. 5th Street so it can build two roughly 2,100 sq ft A-frame single-family homes, arguing the slope and site make commercial use impractical. After a public hearing on Oct. 21, the Planning Commission found the application met the code criteria and moved to recommend approval of Ordinance 895. A neighbor raised concern about losing GC flexibility in the area, and another resident spoke in support.

nederland/1.title: Temporary use permits (Ordinance 893)
nederland/1.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a draft ordinance creating staff-reviewed temporary use permits, generally limited to 90 days and revocable if a use creates health or safety problems. A processing fee would be set by resolution, and staff could require neighbor notification when a use might significantly affect neighbors. A resident submitted public comment.

nederland/2.title: Allowing outdoor sales, eating and drinking (Ordinance 894)
nederland/2.summary: The Planning Commission considered amending the use group table to allow outdoor sales, eating and drinking and other outdoor commercial activities, with safety standards near roadways. A commissioner moved to recommend approval of Ordinance 894, and a resident spoke in support at the Oct. 21 meeting.

nederland/3.title: Moving Board of Zoning Adjustment duties to the Planning Commission (Ordinance 896)
nederland/3.summary: Ordinance 896 would dissolve the separate Board of Zoning Adjustment and give its variance functions to the Planning Commission. Commissioners cited the low number of variance applications and the difficulty of keeping a separate volunteer board filled.

nederland/4.title: Flex zoning for housing and redevelopment
nederland/4.summary: The Planning Commission began discussing 'flex zoning,' a concept in the Comprehensive Plan and Downtown Subarea Plan, to allow more housing types, mixed uses and affordable-housing incentives. The industrial Wolf Tongue area and General Commercial properties near East Street Garage and Mountain Auto were discussed as possible candidates, with limited infrastructure noted as a challenge.
nederland/4.where: Wolf Tongue industrial area; East Street Garage and Mountain Auto area

nederland/5.title: ADU code amendments (Ordinance 892)
nederland/5.summary: The Planning Commission moved to recommend approval of draft Ordinance 892, which amends section 16-33 of the municipal code on accessory dwelling units.

nederland/6.title: Chipeta Park playground replacement and PROST update
nederland/6.summary: The parks advisory board continued discussing a vision, grant opportunities and priorities for replacing the Chipeta Park playground. It also worked toward final revisions of the PROST (parks, recreation, open space and trails) update and reviewed strategic goals for the Board of Trustees.

sources.body: PROSAB - Nederland Parks, Recreation, and Open Space Advisory Board

nederland/7.title: Town property purchase for recreational activities (executive session)
nederland/7.summary: The Board of Trustees scheduled executive sessions on Oct. 20 and Oct. 29 to discuss the Town's purchase of property and operations for recreational activities. No details or decisions appear in the documents.

nederland/8.title: Planning Commission strategic goals 2026-2027
nederland/8.summary: The Planning Commission discussed its strategic planning goals for 2026-2027 as part of the Town's planning priorities.

new-castle/0.title: Comprehensive Plan update (last adopted 2009)
new-castle/0.summary: The Town Attorney briefed Council on the legal process for updating the Comprehensive Plan, which was adopted May 27, 2009 and never updated. The discussion is an initial step to understand requirements and options and to pick next steps.

new-castle/1.title: Plastic bag fee fund, Community Market recycling and compost, and cleanup days
new-castle/1.summary: The Climate and Environment Commission is using the plastic bag fee fund, with about $12,000 remaining, to pay for compostable cups and recycling at the Community Market and for the Dump Day and fall cleanup. The commission is also planning a plastic pledge, a parade float in the Burning Mountain Festival, a business sustainability award and the October 10 trash pick-up day.

new-castle/2.title: Proposed Garfield County School of Innovation charter school
new-castle/2.summary: Garfield County School of Innovation presented its plan to open a charter school in New Castle in 2027, with an application filed with the Garfield County Re-2 School Board and awaiting review. Council also has on its agenda a letter of support for the Re-2 ballot issue.

new-castle/3.title: 2027 budget and trash and recycling fees
new-castle/3.summary: Council is discussing the 2027 budget and Council initiatives, with monthly bills at $760,381.54 in October. Mountain Waste is gathering landfill data that will drive 2027 trash and recycling fees and will present upcoming changes.

new-castle/4.title: Development and building update: apartments, Archwood, New Castle Center
new-castle/4.summary: The Town Planner reported that 40 of 80 expected apartment units have been permitted, that the Coal Seam hotel/restaurant was approved April 7, and that Archwood approval was anticipated September 1. The New Castle Center (Walters Center) amended PUD is expected to be submitted in fall 2026, with TC Midwest planning road and infrastructure work.
new-castle/4.where: Lakota, Castle Valley Ranch and New Castle Center

new-castle/5.title: Police Department update on training and priorities
new-castle/5.summary: Chief Curry briefed Council on training and professional development, largely funded through Colorado POST grants and regional training. The update feeds into the Council retreat on priorities and resources.

new-castle/6.title: Canyon Senior Housing residents' concerns
new-castle/6.summary: A speaker raised residents' concerns at Canyon Senior Housing and asked about town ordinances that might apply. Administrator Reynolds said Council can discuss it at an upcoming work session.

new-castle/7.title: EV charging station guidelines
new-castle/7.summary: Council is to consider guidelines for electric vehicle charging stations at its October 20 meeting.

new-castle/8.title: Historic preservation: survey grants, videography project and CLG audit
new-castle/8.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission is working on historical survey grant applications, a videography project and the annual Certified Local Government report. It is also handling the Highland Cemetery designation plaque.

new-castle/9.title: Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act and library ballot committees
new-castle/9.summary: Council took up a discussion of the Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act and heard presentations from the Re-2 ballot issue committee and the Maintain Our County Libraries committee.

norwood/0.title: Town-wide 15 mph speed limit
norwood/0.summary: The board discussed lowering the speed limit in April and June. A July ordinance would set a 15 mph limit on all town streets unless otherwise posted, and the item returned in August. The documents do not state the final vote.

norwood/1.title: Moratorium on medium and large scale development and land use code rewrite
norwood/1.summary: In January the board discussed extending the emergency temporary moratorium on medium and large scale development (Ordinance 0813, 2025). It has since worked on a KLJ land use code contract, a Land Use Code amendment ordinance in October, and a KLJ master plan contract and update.

norwood/2.title: Norwood Public School property purchase and rezone at 2028 Maverick Way
norwood/2.summary: The board took up an update on buying the Norwood Public School property in January. In May it held a public hearing on rezoning 2028 Maverick Way from Agriculture to a Public zoning district.

norwood/3.title: Pocket park at 1575 Grand Ave
norwood/3.summary: The board handled a bid from RMC Builders, updates, signage and the park's address. A dedication was scheduled for September.

norwood/4.title: Employee compensation and retention incentives
norwood/4.summary: In May the board considered a legal review of employee compensation. In June and July it took up a resolution and ordinance authorizing additional compensation and retention incentives for employees.

norwood/5.title: Water commission, raw water and water treatment plant land
norwood/5.summary: The board and Water Commission met in executive session in March on State Land Board property for the water treatment plant. Later items covered Raw Water Board rules, water commission terms and appointments, a drainage study by SGM, and a joint work session on the raw water subcommittee.

norwood/6.title: Short-term rental rules
norwood/6.summary: Short-term rentals were on the agenda in July, September and October for discussion.

norwood/7.title: CDOT Safer Sidewalks to School project and school traffic
norwood/7.summary: The board approved job bids for the CDOT Safer Sidewalks to School project and an MOU with CDOT in June. In October it discussed school traffic and the sidewalk project.

norwood/8.title: Wildlife and wildfire ordinances, fireworks and dark sky rules
norwood/8.summary: The board repeatedly discussed draft wildlife and wildfire ordinances in early 2026. It also discussed fireworks, streetlight and Dark Sky compliance, and updated Dark Sky Coalition rules.

norwood/9.title: 2027 draft budget and mill levy
norwood/9.summary: The board set the mill levy and amended the certificate of mill levies in January. A 2027 draft budget was presented in October.

norwood/10.title: Removal for cause hearing
norwood/10.summary: In August the board adopted a resolution setting a public hearing on removing an official for cause. It was amended in September, and the hearing was cancelled in October.

norwood/11.title: Town building leases and EV charging stations
norwood/11.summary: The board considered updated lease agreements for 1110 Lucerne St and 1475 S Pine St, the latter with an option to purchase and right of first refusal. It also discussed EV charging station rates and install budget.

nunn/0.title: North Weld Water Services Agreement and water system planning
nunn/0.summary: The Town attorney has been reviewing and amending a water services agreement with North Weld County Water, with several areas still needing clarification as of April. Water loss remains a problem, the Board is looking at more meters, and it picked a bid for a Master Water Plan in August. In October the Board is to discuss a water committee, an excess water usage ordinance and tap approvals.

nunn/1.title: CDBG grants for Senior Center and Community Center/Town Hall improvements
nunn/1.summary: The Town pursued a CDBG grant for the Senior Center, with asbestos abatement bids ranging from $56,000 to $161,000 against $56,000 budgeted in the grant. In June the Board reviewed the $206,739 approved grant total, which includes a $17,500 engineering contract and contractor bids for painting and a trophy case. A project manager for the grant was approved in August, and a second CDBG project manager vote is on the October 15 agenda.

nunn/2.title: Clayton Homes development and 1467 4th Street variance
nunn/2.summary: Clayton Homes wants to build 18 homes. The Board said it needs to discuss plant investments, tap fees and future large developments. Permits for lots 2 and 3 of the RLD subdivision were processed in August. A September public hearing covered a variance at 1467 4th Street, where a lot line adjustment would give 13 feet to 1457 4th Street, whose home was placed too close to the line.

nunn/3.title: Sunrise Solar Project permit at CR 29.5
nunn/3.summary: The Board reviewed a permit application for a 20-acre solar project at 49600 CR 29.5, with a 10-foot fence with aluminum slats. The Town wants written commitments on dust mitigation, truck routes during construction, an eco plan and contingencies. A 50% plan is expected in mid-August.

nunn/4.title: Building code and Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption
nunn/4.summary: The Town adopted Ordinance 329 adopting the 2024 International Building Code in April. The Board has been reviewing the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code and plans to adopt it in September, but the fire district must first review specific pages. An October update is on the agenda.

nunn/5.title: Blue Spruce Development on 4th Street
nunn/5.summary: The Town attorney is working on a development agreement with Blue Spruce Development on 4th Street. The developer must provide water shares.

nunn/6.title: Safer Streets grant, speed study and Master Drainage Plan
nunn/6.summary: The Town hired an engineering firm for the Safer Streets grant and comprehensive safety plan, with outreach to seniors, youth and at Nunn Days. The Safer Streets and Master Drainage plans are to be posted online for 30 days for public comment.

nunn/7.title: Weld County roads, CR 31 and 2027 budget
nunn/7.summary: The Town plans an important discussion with Weld County about CR 31 and county road assistance and costs. The October 8 agenda includes the initial 2027 budget draft, and the Board noted the fuel budget needs to increase for 2027.

nunn/8.title: Police equipment: pepper ball guns, tasers and vehicle lease
nunn/8.summary: The Police Department asked to buy pepper ball guns at $969 each, which were not in the budget. Other items include new tasers, a $1,800 taser battery charger, police car repairs and a vehicle lease or purchase this year.

nunn/9.title: Marijuana facility licenses and manufacturing application
nunn/9.summary: The Town's Marijuana Licensing Authority reviewed an applicant for a manufacturing facility, who still needed state approval. It also reviewed renewals for NOCO Farms, SPCY Canna and Ace's Place cultivation and manufacturing licenses.

nunn/10.title: 2026 budget, mill levy and fee schedule
nunn/10.summary: The Town previewed the 2026 budget, received the final mill levy, and adopted resolutions levying property taxes, adopting the budget and appropriating funds in December. It also adopted the 2026 town fee schedule and municipal court fees in January.

nunn/11.title: RV ordinance and Antelope Run concept plan
nunn/11.summary: The October 8 agenda includes a review of an RV ordinance for the Town and a preliminary concept plan for Robert Kearny's 20 acres, formerly Antelope Run.

oak-creek/0.title: New 2% sales tax chapter for capital improvements (Ordinance No. 678)
oak-creek/0.summary: The Town Board discussed an ordinance adopting a new Chapter 3.02 of the municipal code covering the town's 2.0% sales tax, to be used for construction and rehabilitation of capital improvements. It was discussed in August and September and Ordinance No. 678 was up for approval on October 8, 2026.

oak-creek/1.title: Lot 15, Sierra View Subdivision development agreement with MACOGA, LLC
oak-creek/1.summary: The board was asked to approve a development agreement for Lot 15, Sierra View Subdivision on October 8, and on October 22 it held a legal-advice session and considered a Development Improvement Agreement with MACOGA, LLC. The new agreement would terminate and replace an April 2025 improvements agreement, and requires a $5,000 deposit from the developer.

oak-creek/2.title: Sheriff Dam enlargement and reservoir project
oak-creek/2.summary: The board considered a Special Use Permit for the enlargement and rehabilitation of Sheriff Dam, as approved by the state Division of Water Resources, along with an agent authorization form for the Sheriff Dam Reservoir Project.

oak-creek/3.title: Law enforcement agreements with Routt County Sheriff's Office
oak-creek/3.summary: The August 13 meeting included a hearing on two draft law enforcement service agreements with Routt County and an off-duty overtime reimbursement agreement with the Routt County Sheriff's Office.

oak-creek/4.title: 2027 budget first draft
oak-creek/4.summary: The board reviewed the first draft of the town's 2027 annual budget on October 8, 2026.

oak-creek/5.title: Bulk water dispensing station upgrades
oak-creek/5.summary: The board discussed upgrades to the bulk water dispensing station, then took up buying a new control panel and a proposal to build a new shell for the station.

oak-creek/6.title: Trash hauling rate increases from Apex Twin Enviro
oak-creek/6.summary: Apex Twin Enviro was scheduled to discuss with the board its trash hauling rate increases beginning in November 2026.

oak-creek/7.title: Dog park proposal and flow trail grant
oak-creek/7.summary: The SOROCO Youth Action Council sought a letter of support for a grant and presented a proposed dog park in town. Separately, the board considered a resolution to apply for a $125,000 Colorado Parks and Wildlife trail grant to complete a downhill flow trail in Oak Creek Mountain Park.

oak-creek/8.title: South Routt Medical Center health service plan expansion
oak-creek/8.summary: The Planning Commission and Town Board held public hearings on an application to add 880 square feet of institutional space to the existing South Routt Medical Center facility.

oak-creek/9.title: Street and drainage projects: Sharp Avenue, Oak Ridge, Bell Avenue
oak-creek/9.summary: The board considered an asphalt patching project on Sharp Avenue and Oak Ridge and a bid for the Bell Avenue drainage improvement project. It also considered buying a $135,364 sewer jetter.
oak-creek/9.where: Sharp Avenue, Oak Ridge, Bell Avenue

oak-creek/10.title: South Routt Housing Authority funding request
oak-creek/10.summary: The South Routt Housing Authority asked the town for $13,000 in operations funding.

oak-creek/11.title: School running track condition and nuisance abatement
oak-creek/11.summary: The board planned to discuss the condition of the running track with the South Routt school district, and later discussed nuisance abatement actions in town.

ophir/0.title: Ban on short-term rentals (Ordinance 2026-7)
ophir/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission recommended 3-0 an ordinance amending Section 303.1 of the Land Use Code to make leasing short-term rentals unlawful, citing impacts on town services, neighbors and the town's limited housing stock. P&Z also discussed what minimum rental length should count, with one member suggesting anything under 63 days, and was to review a full draft from the Town.

ophir/1.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and new exterior material rules
ophir/1.summary: Ophir must adopt the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code under state law (deadline noted as May). P&Z has reviewed wildfire-resistant siding, such as wood-styled cement board, and in October considered new exterior material requirements for siding, garage doors, decking and fences that comply with the code.

ophir/2.title: Revegetation ordinance for soil disturbance
ophir/2.summary: A draft ordinance would require a revegetation plan before any soil disturbance, including construction, septic, utility and road work, to protect native plants and pollinators, with penalties for non-compliance. P&Z recommended approval 5-0 in March, with the construction fencing requirement removed, after discussing an approved seed list.

ophir/3.title: Dark Sky and lighting ordinance
ophir/3.summary: A draft Dark Sky/Lighting Ordinance was reviewed by P&Z, which recommended approval 5-0 in March 2026.

ophir/4.title: Variance for side setbacks and 2/12 roof pitch on Aurum Street
ophir/4.summary: An applicant requested a variance to cut required side yard setbacks from 15 feet to 10 feet and to allow a 2/12 roof pitch for new construction on Lots 1 and 2, Block 2 on Aurum Street. The applicant presented the request to P&Z in March 2026, and approval would also involve the General Assembly.

ophir/5.title: Fence rules and the Bobtail Street fence
ophir/5.summary: P&Z considered whether a fence on Lots 5 and 6, Block 4 is a permitted accessory use to the residence on Lots 7 and 8, and decided new fencing needed neither a variance nor a Special Use Permit. It then took up fencing materials for a new fence at 112 Bobtail Street, and earlier discussed whether neighbor permission should be required for fences.

ophir/6.title: Residential building plan reviews
ophir/6.summary: P&Z reviewed building plans for the Aplin and Kondracki home on Bobtail Street, the Croke residence on Granite Street (recommended 4-0) and the Cooper residence on Aurum Street. Reviews check setbacks, parking, exterior materials and fire safety.

ophir/7.title: Low Energy and Carbon Code presentation
ophir/7.summary: EcoAction Partners was scheduled to give P&Z a 30-minute presentation on a Low Energy & Carbon Code in June 2026.

ophir/8.title: Wood stove permits and parking rules
ophir/8.summary: P&Z discussed requiring permits for replacement wood stoves, with free application and review. It also discussed parking spaces placed where roofs shed snow, and limiting parking of vehicles and boats to spaces or town rights-of-way.

ordway/0.title: Toni Evans annexation and zoning
ordway/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on Aug. 10, 2026 on a petition by Toni Evans to annex land into Ordway, and the trustees adopted resolutions on eligibility and the petition. A second reading of the annexation and zoning ordinances (#673 and #674) followed on Oct. 5. A separate 'Addies' annexation was also recommended and approved to move forward.

ordway/1.title: Water moratorium and water restrictions
ordway/1.summary: Council denied a water restrictions resolution in April, then approved Resolution 2026-07 in June placing a moratorium on additional water services. Water reports, well output and a town water restructuring were also discussed.

ordway/2.title: CIRSA coverage and settlement over former town attorney's contract change
ordway/2.summary: Documents in August include a CIRSA coverage letter and a settlement agreement, release and assignment. They concern losses the Town says began in 2022 after the former town attorney amended a water-rate contract and allegedly failed to advise the Town correctly. A malpractice lawsuit and a receivership are mentioned.

ordway/3.title: Historic preservation, Certified Local Government status and cemetery board
ordway/3.summary: Council advanced ordinances to establish a Certified Local Government and a Historic Preservation Advisory Authority, and created a cemetery board. A further historic preservation ordinance (#675) had a first reading in October, and a cemetery grant is moving forward.

ordway/4.title: 428 E. 3rd Street town-owned property sale and foreclosure
ordway/4.summary: Council considered resolutions in March authorizing the sale of town-owned property, including 428 East 3rd Street. In May and June it discussed the property in executive session and talked about restarting foreclosure.

ordway/5.title: Tax certificates, demolition and property requests on Arkansas, Idaho and E. 3rd
ordway/5.summary: In October the board approved negotiating tax certificates for 305, 317 and 319 Arkansas and 326 Idaho. It approved a demolition application at 318 E 3rd and an extension request for 215 E 4th Street. Discussion of 629 Idaho was postponed. An agreement on future affordable housing development was also on the agenda.

ordway/6.title: Street improvements, comprehensive plan and Old Pharmacy
ordway/6.summary: The town held a kickoff with the State for street improvements and is updating its comprehensive plan. It also discussed extending 1st Street, a master plan for the Old Pharmacy building, and a Stantec visit.

ordway/7.title: Fire department invoices and funding
ordway/7.summary: In June the town discussed a county invoice to the fire department, which will pay past due invoices with a subsidy. Workers' compensation for the fire department and Air Med Care membership were also discussed.

ordway/8.title: Budget, raises and health insurance
ordway/8.summary: The town held a preliminary budget work session on Oct. 19, approved a health insurance company, and approved 3% personnel raises in August.

ordway/9.title: Community library agreement
ordway/9.summary: Council approved a revised Community Library intergovernmental agreement in September after library discussion in April.

ouray-county/0.title: Land Use Code rewrite: definitions, ADUs and special use permits
ouray-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission is working through a multi-section rewrite of the county Land Use Code under Resolution 2024-029. Drafts address accessory dwelling unit size and distance limits (including a 'bonus ADU' concept), agricultural structures needing building permits, and new or revised Special Use Permits for guest lodges, guest ranches, event venues, campgrounds and commercial outdoor recreation. Staff plan to finish Section 2, move to Section 3 (Zoning), and hold a public hearing after revised drafts of Sections 3 and 13.

ouray-county/1.title: Fire flow and water supply definitions for subdivisions and PUDs
ouray-county/1.summary: Staff proposed a broader definition of 'water supply' for PUDs and subdivisions, with minimum fire flow as a narrower requirement. Tri-County Water has said its existing hydrants may not meet minimum fire flow pressure and flow recommendations.

ouray-county/2.title: Water-wise landscaping and artificial turf rules in Zoning Section 3.11
ouray-county/2.summary: Draft Section 3.11 adds state-driven 'water-wise' landscaping requirements for new development, including a broad invasive plant species definition and limits on artificial turf with an exception for athletic fields of play. Staff say the field-of-play wording needs further clarification.

ouray-county/3.title: Yurt limits and Colona zone changes in the zoning draft
ouray-county/3.summary: Staff suggested the Planning Commission and county commissioners consider limiting yurts to one per parcel in the Alpine zone or all zones, to prevent multiple yurts claiming building code exemptions. The draft also adds a 'Commercial Storefront' special use to the Colona Zone.

ouray-county/4.title: Curry subdivision at 1615 County Road 1
ouray-county/4.summary: The Planning Commission holds a public hearing on Kilpin and Sandra Curry's combined preliminary and final development plan to subdivide the parcel into 2 lots. The commission is to make a recommendation to the county commissioners.

ouray-county/5.title: Pastor subdivision exemption at 6549 County Road 24
ouray-county/5.summary: The Planning Commission hears Clifford Pastor's request for an exemption to divide a parcel into 2 lots and will make a recommendation to the county commissioners.

ouray-county/6.title: Joint planning agreement with the City and zoning map updates
ouray-county/6.summary: Staff say 2022 changes to the Joint Planning IGA on annexation authority raised legal and planning concerns that Section 3 may need amending quickly. Staff also proposed keeping overlay district designations off the official zoning map because amending it is a lengthy hearing process.

ouray-county/7.title: Tribal consultation for renewable energy projects
ouray-county/7.summary: Code changes respond to state law on Tribal consultation for renewable energy projects. Staff have contacted the Tribes and will shape the proposed language depending on their replies.

pagosa-springs/0.title: Data center moratorium (Ordinance 1037)
pagosa-springs/0.summary: Council passed a 6-month moratorium on accepting or processing permit and land development applications that include a data center. The Land Use Development Code has no data center use class, and staff want time to watch development in Colorado and write rules. The moratorium would need renewal every 6 months to reach the two years Council asked for.

pagosa-springs/1.title: 2027 budget, fee schedule and capital plan
pagosa-springs/1.summary: Council held a public hearing and adopted Resolution 2026-21 on Oct. 6, setting the 2027 budget across seven funds, with a mill levy of 1.561 expected to raise $173,145. The fee schedule has changes, and the 5-year capital plan includes the community center roof, vehicles and park improvements. The Sanitation district also took up its own 2027 budget and fee schedule.

pagosa-springs/2.title: Sewer system repairs and new wastewater treatment plant
pagosa-springs/2.summary: The Sanitation district is finishing the McCabe Creek sewer replacement on Florida Street and moving to Rosita Street. It approved surge tank and pump purchases, applied for a $900,000 grant for the 1st Street lift station, and is seeking an owner's advisor for the new wastewater treatment facility, with an award expected Nov. 3. Sewer line replacements reduced infiltration by about 15%.
pagosa-springs/2.where: McCabe Creek, Florida Street, Rosita Street and 1st Street lift station

pagosa-springs/3.title: Project 64 workforce housing and Housing Action Plan
pagosa-springs/3.summary: Staff prepared talking points for Project 64 (formerly Project 102), where the Town won a bid for grants for renovation and purchase, with COPs to be obtained. Grants could lower the rents needed to cover COP payments. Housing also appears in a joint Town/County Housing Action Plan session and a Proposition 123 affordable housing credits agreement.

pagosa-springs/4.title: Ponderosa Mountain planned development and subdivision
pagosa-springs/4.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the Ponderosa major subdivision sketch plan and planned development agreement. Ordinance 1042 on the planned development agreement and zoning map amendment had a first reading on Oct. 6 and was continued to Oct. 20.

pagosa-springs/5.title: Talisman Drive area rezoning to Multi-unit Town Center (Ordinance 1040)
pagosa-springs/5.summary: Council approved Ordinance 1040 on first and second reading, rezoning Cornerstone Lofts and Talisman Pointe units on Talisman, Eaton and Village drives to Multi-unit Town Center. The Planning Commission recommended approval on Aug. 25.
pagosa-springs/5.where: Talisman Drive, Eaton Drive and Village Drive

pagosa-springs/6.title: G&I Sanitation trash franchise and rates (Ordinance 1039)
pagosa-springs/6.summary: Council granted G&I Sanitation Services a five-year franchise for refuse collection using town streets and alleys. Ordinance 1039 passed first reading Sept. 15 and second reading Oct. 6. A public hearing was held on the company's proposed rates, as the charter requires.

pagosa-springs/7.title: Traffic, parking and truck complaints near San Juan Alley and the library
pagosa-springs/7.summary: A resident repeatedly told Council that truckers park overnight in the library lot, that the jake brake ordinance is not enforced, and that San Juan Alley is heavily used. Staff reviewed a speed dip on San Juan Alley between 8th and 10th streets and found it not recommended based on residential feedback. A traffic calming policy and ordinance is being drafted.
pagosa-springs/7.where: San Juan Alley (8th to 10th Streets) and library parking lot

pagosa-springs/8.title: Parks: San Juan River Park, master plan and Yamaguchi bike park
pagosa-springs/8.summary: Council named the town-owned former Bob's LP/Basin Coop property at 1040 E US 160 "San Juan River Park." The parks master plan survey and facility inventory continue, Yamaguchi South Bike Park is under construction, and an astronomy shed proposal is under review. Staff also reported a Forest Legacy Program application.

pagosa-springs/9.title: Dark Sky Lighting Management Plan
pagosa-springs/9.summary: The Dark Sky Steering Committee is working on a Lighting Management Plan that would exceed current Land Use Development Code standards. It sets limits like lights out by 11 p.m., no flashing lights, and unlit trails, and has been through work sessions and review meetings.

pagosa-springs/10.title: Town Manager contract extension
pagosa-springs/10.summary: After an executive session on his evaluation and employment agreement, Council voted to extend Town Manager David Harris's contract. Council Member Martinez and Mayor Pierce will help craft the extension.

pagosa-springs/11.title: Tourism board strategy, 2027 budget and flood discussion
pagosa-springs/11.summary: The Area Tourism Board held a strategic retreat Aug. 14, is developing a third-party market study, discussed a draft 2027 budget, and is managing state tourism grants for river access kiosks and wayfinding signage. A 2026 flood discussion is on its Oct. 28 agenda.

pagosa-springs/12.title: Main Street board expansion and post-construction plans
pagosa-springs/12.summary: The Main Street Advisory Board is expanding from 10 to 11 members as highway reconstruction nears completion. The coordinator plans to update the transformation strategies, possibly with DOLA funding, and to close out the Business Assistance Grant Fund.

palisade/0.title: Draft 2027 Town of Palisade budget
palisade/0.summary: Staff presented the draft 2027 budget to the Board of Trustees as required by state law. The board was asked to set the public hearing to adopt the final budget for November 10, 2026.

palisade/1.title: 2027 special event calendar and blackout dates (Resolution 2026-17)
palisade/1.summary: The Board of Trustees was to consider Resolution 2026-17, approving the 2027 special event calendar and blackout dates.

palisade/2.title: Watershed wildfire mitigation presentation from Colorado State Forest Service
palisade/2.summary: The Colorado State Forest Service was scheduled to present on watershed wildfire mitigation and coordination with the town.

palisade/3.title: Tourism Advisory Commission interviews and appointment
palisade/3.summary: The board was to interview candidates and appoint a commissioner to the Tourism Advisory Commission by roll call vote.

palisade/4.title: Fall Town Cleanup Day and Trick-or-Treat Street events
palisade/4.summary: Fall Town Cleanup Day is Saturday, October 17 from 8 am to noon at the Riverbend Park parking lot, or until dumpsters are full. Trick-or-Treat Street and Touch a Truck is Friday, October 30.

palmer-lake/0.title: Temporary data center moratorium (Resolution 31-2026)
palmer-lake/0.summary: The Board of Trustees had Resolution 31-2026 on its September 10 agenda for discussion and possible action on a temporary moratorium on data centers. The documents shown do not state the outcome.

palmer-lake/1.title: Town-wide bear-proof trash rules and Bear Mitigation Ordinance 6-2026
palmer-lake/1.summary: The Planning Commission discussed a mandatory town-wide bear-proof container ordinance, certified receptacles and CPW grants, and a resident urged strict enforcement. By October 22 the Board had Bear Mitigation and Enforcement Ordinance 6-2026 on its agenda for possible adoption.

palmer-lake/2.title: Water restrictions and stage one water emergency
palmer-lake/2.summary: The town remains under a stage one water emergency with an outdoor watering ban that cut demand by 25% and allowed a shift to the Denver well. Monument Creek is too low to be a production source and there is no firm end date to the water call. A resident criticized town communications about the restrictions, and Columbine Park plantings were put off until spring because of the restrictions.

palmer-lake/3.title: 2027 budget, spending freeze and department consolidation
palmer-lake/3.summary: Town Administrator Patrick Davidson began 2027 budget projections and froze non-essential spending and new capital projects. Budget workshops were scheduled in late September and October, and a draft 2027 budget and 2026 amended budget were on the October 22 agenda. A proposal would consolidate the Water, Road/Streets and Parks departments, and a possible ballot measure on fire protection services with Monument Fire is being researched.

palmer-lake/4.title: Buc-ee's annexation withdrawal and landowner negotiations
palmer-lake/4.summary: An executive session was set to discuss negotiations with the landowner's counsel and counsel for Buc-ee's following withdrawal of the annexation request. Details are not public in the documents.

palmer-lake/5.title: Lakeview lots conservation easement and town lease with option to purchase
palmer-lake/5.summary: The Board agenda included a conservation easement and donation of about 140 platted lots in Lakeview. Executive sessions were also set for October 22 on a proposed lease with option to purchase town property.

palmer-lake/6.title: Trustee Moseley hearing officer process and legal costs
palmer-lake/6.summary: The town has retained a hearing officer and is finalizing an agreement with a presenting officer to schedule hearings concerning Trustee Roger Moseley. Trustees also discussed CORA request procedures and legal service costs.

palmer-lake/7.title: Parks and Trails projects: Centennial Park, Elephant Rock pavilion, fences and weeds
palmer-lake/7.summary: The commission discussed the Elephant Rock pavilion renovation, Centennial Park pickleball court flooding and curbing, dogs in the courts, and the Crawford memorial fence repair. It decided against no-fishing zones at Centennial Park Lake, and also covered poison hemlock and noxious weed control, wildlife-feeding signs, a playground inspection and Awake the Lake ideas.
palmer-lake/7.where: Centennial Park, Glen Park, Elephant Rock

palmer-lake/8.title: Motorized vehicles on Palmer Lake trails
palmer-lake/8.summary: The Parks and Trails Commission put motorized vehicle use on town trails on its September 8 agenda, and trustees were told restrictions on trails were being discussed.

palmer-lake/9.title: Creek Week and Fountain Creek Watershed cleanup
palmer-lake/9.summary: The Fountain Creek Watershed District presented on its restoration projects and the 9-day cleanup running Sept 26 to Oct 4, 2026. The Board proclaimed Creek Week, with a joint cleanup event planned in Palmer Lake.

palmer-lake/10.title: New town policies: agenda setting, social media, snow removal, 2026 fee schedule
palmer-lake/10.summary: The Board was to consider resolutions adopting agenda-setting, social media and snow removal policies (37, 38, 39-2026). Resolution 34-2026 amends the 2026 Master Fee Schedule.

palmer-lake/11.title: Fowler Branch land use, plat amendment and Calverts sign application
palmer-lake/11.summary: The Planning Commission's September 16 agenda included the Fowler Branch land use item, a plat amendment adjusting Lot 8 to be larger within a PUD, and a sign application for Calverts. The applicant on one item requested a continuance.

paonia/0.title: Short-term rental regulation (Common Ground Ordinance)
paonia/0.summary: An ad hoc committee has met repeatedly since August to review a draft Common Ground Ordinance for registering short-term rentals. It has discussed registration fees, no numerical cap, three-year registrations, owner-occupancy verification, self-certification of safety, tax compliance, liability insurance, neighbor notification and complaint-based enforcement. Survey responses and written comments were mixed, and the Board of Trustees will set final requirements and fees.

paonia/1.title: Stage 2 water restrictions and water supply concerns
paonia/1.summary: After unusually high water use drained the treated-water storage tank, the Board adopted Stage 2 restrictions in Resolution 19-26 on Aug. 18, allowing hand or drip watering of gardens. Residents commented on fire risk from dried lawns, alternating schedules and penalties. The Board asked for regular updates on tank levels and production, and later rescinded the restrictions with Resolution 22-26. A water attorney briefed the Board in executive session on water rights, and the Planning Commission is looking at water moratorium and tap availability processes.

paonia/2.title: Raw Water Monitoring Project engineering amendment
paonia/2.summary: The Board considered Amendment #2 to the RESPEC agreement for pre-construction award and construction engineering services on the Raw Water Monitoring Project. It is funded within the project budget and includes meters to better track water production. A resident commented asking for clarification, and Trustee Hunter moved approval.

paonia/3.title: Estate zoning density changes and related ordinances
paonia/3.summary: Staff found an inconsistency in the estate zoning table (Table 16-2) and recommended allowing 1.5 to two acres per dwelling to support Comprehensive Plan housing-density goals. The Board sent the matter to a work session and a revised ordinance. A re-zoning application from David Warren also had a public hearing continued from Aug. 25.

paonia/4.title: Accessory dwelling unit (ADU) rules and new subdivision sidewalks
paonia/4.summary: The Planning Commission is discussing adding ADU provisions to Chapter 16, since the 2025 Comprehensive Plan lists ADUs as a key housing strategy. Questions include where ADUs are allowed, utilities, parking, owner occupancy, fees and separate sale. It will also discuss sidewalk requirements in new subdivisions based on lot size.

paonia/5.title: Emergency sewer tap fee waiver for septic users
paonia/5.summary: The Board discussed waiving sewer tap fees for septic tank users and took up Ordinance 02-26, later titled an emergency sewer tap fee waiver, on Sept. 8 and Sept. 15. The documents do not state the outcome.

paonia/6.title: New police chief appointment
paonia/6.summary: The Board appointed Sergeant Henderson as the new Chief of Police on Oct. 27. Residents spoke in support of him during public comment.

paonia/7.title: Town Administrator search
paonia/7.summary: The Board considered proposals from executive search firms in August (RFP 26-03) and approved a search firm profile for Town Administrator on Sept. 30. An interim administrator is currently serving.

paonia/8.title: 2027 budget
paonia/8.summary: The 2027 budget was presented Oct. 27 after a work session on Oct. 21 and another on Oct. 28. The Board asked for weekly budget work sessions. Employee insurance benefits were also on a September agenda.

paonia/9.title: West Fourth Street overlay IGA with Delta County
paonia/9.summary: Public Works proposed an intergovernmental agreement with Delta County for a two-inch asphalt overlay on West Fourth Street. The county's project limit of about $25,000 means the entire street may not be completed. Trustee Brown moved to enter the IGA.

paonia/10.title: Town Hall roof, solar panel removal and public works trucks
paonia/10.summary: The Board took up a Town Hall roof replacement bid, a quote to have Empower remove the solar panels from Town Hall, and the final price for three public works trucks. A police patrol truck purchase was also considered Sept. 30.

paonia/11.title: Recycling service with Recyclops
paonia/11.summary: The Board heard a presentation on Colorado's Extended Producer Responsibility program and considered a proposal with Recyclops to provide free recycling service. Recyclops representatives said they want to work with local recyclers.

paonia/12.title: Street lights and dark skies
paonia/12.summary: The Board discussed removing street lights in September and dark skies and trail lights in October.

paonia/13.title: New town ordinances: tobacco sales, solid waste, animals and meeting procedures
paonia/13.summary: The Board considered Ordinance 01-26 on solid waste disposal rules, Ordinance 03-26 repealing sidewalk for business use, and Ordinance 04-26 amending the animal code. It adopted Ordinance 06-26 on cigarette and tobacco sales and Ordinance 07-26 on meeting procedures, and moved the regular meeting start time to 5:30. Staff also proposed combining the juvenile loitering and curfew rules and creating a single nuisance ordinance.

parachute/0.title: Data center regulations (Ordinance 838-2026)
parachute/0.summary: Town Council is set to consider Ordinance No. 838-2026, which would amend Title 15 of the municipal code to regulate data centers and technology facilities. It was on the October 15, 2026 agenda with a cover memo; the documents do not state an outcome.

parachute/1.title: Prop 123 expedited review for affordable housing (Ordinance 837-2026)
parachute/1.summary: The Council is considering a Title 15 amendment adding Section 15.02.214 to create expedited review for affordable housing under Prop 123 and updating the land use review procedures chart. The Planning Commission recommended approval. In July the council also heard a regional housing needs assessment from an Aspen analyst.

parachute/2.title: 2026 and 2027 town budget
parachute/2.summary: Council held a 2026 budget workshop in late 2025, including an employee benefits package assessment. A 2027 budget kickoff took place in September 2026, and the draft 2027 budget with a 2027-2031 capital improvement plan was presented October 15. Council also discussed sales tax ballot initiative options in February.

parachute/3.title: Highway 6 and 1st Street "Parachute Moves" reconstruction project
parachute/3.summary: Council backed multiple grant applications for the Highway 6 and 1st Street mobility, revitalization, reconstruction and safety project, including a USDOT BUILD grant, congressionally directed spending, and HUD funding. The town was later noted as recipient of a $600,000 CDBG grant for the 1st Street project, and committed local match dollars to a federal grant in October.

parachute/4.title: Water system: raw water tank, loan refinance and Stage 2 restrictions
parachute/4.summary: Council supported a DOLA grant for the raw water tank replacement and approved a loan amendment on the water enterprise loan with Alpine Bank (Ordinance 833-2026). Stage 2 water restrictions remained in place in May 2026. Council also celebrated the Shoshone instream flow agreement and later considered a resolution on the Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act with a water consultant report.

parachute/5.title: Town purchase of 147 1st Street from Qwest/Lumen
parachute/5.summary: Council considered Ordinance 834-2026 approving a contract to buy the property at 147 1st Street from Qwest Corporation. By May 2026 the town reported the purchase had closed and it was town-owned.

parachute/6.title: Parachute Area Transit System and bus service
parachute/6.summary: Council approved a services agreement with Glenwood Downtowner for public transit operations and a license agreement with Flix Bus for a bus stop. It also supported a state transit grant application and a regional transit planning grant in June 2026. Riders can use the ridepats.com app.

parachute/7.title: Community center and Senior Center future use
parachute/7.summary: The Valley Senior Center president asked Council in February to make the Senior Center more of a community center and noted the need for funding. In July 2026 Council reviewed a draft Community Center Management Plan with a rental agreement and liability waiver.
parachute/7.where: Parachute Community Center / Valley Senior Center

parachute/8.title: Wildland Urban Interface fire code and landscaping turf rules
parachute/8.summary: Council took up Ordinance 836-2026 revising and adopting the Wildland Urban Interface Fire Code in Title 15. Earlier, Ordinance 835-2026 added restrictions on nonfunctional artificial turf and invasive plant species in development projects.

parachute/9.title: Household pet limits ordinance (831-2025)
parachute/9.summary: Council approved Ordinance 831-2025 on animal rules and impound fines, amended to remove any household pet limits.

parachute/10.title: 6670 Transmission Line rebuild and Xcel easement
parachute/10.summary: Council held a special use review hearing for reconstruction of a public utility transmission line (6670 Transmission Line). In July it also considered a temporary construction easement for Xcel Energy. A solar project expansion of 50 acres at Straight Bottom Ranch was also noted.

parachute/11.title: Fun House Kids special use review at 201 East 1st Street
parachute/11.summary: Council scheduled a public hearing on Resolution 2026-39, a special use review for Fun House Kids LLC at 201 East 1st Street.

park-county/0.title: County manager terminated; resolution ratified and corrected
park-county/0.summary: After an executive session on a personnel matter, commissioners ratified Resolution 2026-47 terminating the county manager on Sept. 1. On Sept. 8 they passed Resolution 2026-48 to correct statutory citations. A discussion of delegating duties between administration and the commissioners was also on the Sept. 8 work session.

park-county/1.title: 2027 county budget
park-county/1.summary: Commissioners held work sessions on the 2026 budget and the proposed 2027 budget, with department presentations in October. The 2027 proposed budget was adopted on Oct. 15 by a 2-0 vote. The Land and Water Trust Fund board also reviewed its own 2027 budget for recommendation.

sources.body: Land and Water Trust Fund Board
Land and Water Trust Fund Board

park-county/2.title: Regenerative agrotourism camp at 634 County Road 62, Grant
park-county/2.summary: A conditional use permit (A26-0021) for an agrotourism business with commercial camping, cabins and bell tents drew environmental concerns about wildlife, wetlands, water rights and Geneva Creek flooding. Commissioners recommended conditional approval with conditions including water rights, a septic review and a flood evacuation plan, and adopted Resolution 2026-50 on Oct. 6. Related setback variances and a minor subdivision (Down to Earth, 1525 Venture Road) were also handled.

sources.body: Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments
Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments

park-county/3.title: Lostfork PUD amendment at 49355 Hwy 285 and 373 County Road 62
park-county/3.summary: The applicant sought to merge its PUD lot with an adjacent lot at 373 County Rd 62. Commissioners approved adding the second parcel on Oct. 20 with conditions including a Geneva Creek review, no buildings on wetlands, a CDOT road evaluation and a septic permit. A resolution was scheduled for Oct. 27.

sources.body: Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments
Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments

park-county/4.title: Emergency culvert repairs: CR 43 and Deer Creek
park-county/4.summary: Commissioners approved emergency replacement of twin 72-inch culverts at County Road 43 and used Land and Water Trust Fund discretionary money for an emergency Deer Creek culvert repair (Resolution 2026-49). Emergency road work in Harris Park was funded at $500,050 in August. CR 43 repairs were also on a later agenda.
park-county/4.where: County Road 43 and Deer Creek; Harris Park

sources.body: Land and Water Trust Fund Board

park-county/5.title: Land and Water Trust Fund: landfill contingency and bylaws
park-county/5.summary: The trust fund board reviewed bylaws, a landfill application and other grants. Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-44 raising the landfill contingency from $1,750,000.

sources.body: Land and Water Trust Fund Board
Land and Water Trust Fund Board

park-county/6.title: Environmental blight ordinance (Ordinance 6)
park-county/6.summary: Commissioners advanced and gave final approval on Sept. 1 to Ordinance 6 (2026), which prohibits accumulation of environmental blight in unincorporated areas and replaces the 1991 ordinance.

park-county/7.title: Property tax abatements and valuation appeals
park-county/7.summary: The Board of Equalization finalized 2026 valuation decisions, upholding all but one parcel. Commissioners heard abatements for the Cooks, Circle C Ranch Tarryall LLC and Zesiger, granting the 2024 and 2025 abatements for Circle C.

park-county/8.title: Overlook St right-of-way vacation, Harris Park Estates
park-county/8.summary: A request by the county and Michael Fleming to vacate 14 feet of the 30-foot right-of-way at 128 Overlook St was sent back to the Planning Department for review.
park-county/8.where: 128 Overlook St, Harris Park Estates Unit 2

park-county/9.title: Bailey Water and Sanitation District site at 19 County Road 64A
park-county/9.summary: Commissioners approved a conditional use permit (Resolution 2026-45) and a minor subdivision (Resolution 2026-46) for the district's property.

park-county/10.title: Paris Mill preservation and heritage projects
park-county/10.summary: Commissioners weighed a construction agreement with High Country Haulers for Paris Mill work, approved Oct. 6. The heritage board also reported on the old courthouse basement work, a preservation plan update and a Dark Sky designation effort centered on Eleven Mile State Park.

sources.body: South Park National Heritage Area Board

park-county/11.title: Planning fee schedule and development applications
park-county/11.summary: A resolution amending land use application fees was postponed. Planning also had several pending cases: the McMillan rezoning (continued to Nov. 17), the Camp Sycamore conference and event venue for up to 250 people, and plat amendments.

sources.body: Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments
Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments

park-county/12.title: Planning Commission member removal and Chaffee jail agreement
park-county/12.summary: A public hearing on removing a county-appointed planning commission member was held in October. Commissioners also had an agreement with Chaffee County to house Park County inmates.

parker/0.title: Axon drone-as-first-responder and license plate reader program
parker/0.summary: Police are researching Axon's countywide Drone as First Responder and License Plate Reader programs, which would add about $175,000 a year to the Axon contract. Council discussed transparency, accountability and video retention. A resident separately asked the Town to remove Flock cameras around Parker.

parker/1.title: Nine-month moratorium on drone dispatch and delivery facilities
parker/1.summary: Council affirmed on second reading an emergency ordinance, first passed July 20, 2026, suspending applications for land use approvals or building permits for commercial drone dispatch and delivery facilities for nine months.

parker/2.title: 2027 budget, property tax levy and related funds
parker/2.summary: Council held a budget workshop on Oct. 2 and a study session on the 2027 proposed budget, which was published Oct. 13. First reading covered the 2026 property tax levy, the 2026 revised budget, and new special funds for risk management and the My Mainstreet General Improvement District. Budget adoption is set for Nov. 16, after a Nov. 2 public hearing. Staff are also proposing a redesign of property and liability insurance with a reserve.

parker/3.title: Parker 2050 Comprehensive Plan and Three-Mile Area Plan
parker/3.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on the 2050 Comprehensive Plan, and Council adopted it by Resolution 26-060 on Sept. 21. The Planning Commission also took up the 2026 Three-Mile Area Plan in October.

parker/4.title: Salisbury Regional Park Phase 2
