parker/4.summary: Phase 2 of the 91-acre Salisbury Regional Park advanced. Council approved a water pipeline easement to Parker Water and Sanitation District, and the Planning Commission and Council took up the site plan amendment southeast of Motsenbocker Road and Todd Drive.
parker/4.where: Salisbury Regional Park, Motsenbocker Road and Todd Drive

parker/5.title: Speeding, drag racing and Mainstreet safety
parker/5.summary: Residents complained about teens speeding and causing damage at O'Brien Park and drag racing on Victorian Drive and Longs Way, and asked for a traffic study on Mainstreet between Jordan Road and Twenty Mile Road. Others proposed making Mainstreet pedestrian-only.
parker/5.where: O'Brien Park, Victorian Drive, Longs Way, Mainstreet

parker/6.title: School resource officers for American Academy
parker/6.summary: Council discussed American Academy's request for a school resource officer and then approved an amended and restated intergovernmental agreement for SRO services for the 2026-2027 school year.

parker/7.title: Security guard and massage facility licensing rules
parker/7.summary: The Town is rewriting its security guard ordinance (Chapter 5.06, last amended in 2004) and the merchant patrol rules, including fees and background checks. Chapter 5.10 on massage facilities was repealed and readopted under a new state law, and license fees were set by Resolution 26-070.

parker/8.title: Sign enforcement and Land Development Ordinance changes
parker/8.summary: Council and the Planning Commission considered changes to sign enforcement and temporary sign rules in the Land Development Ordinance, with enforcement amendments moving through readings in August and September.

parker/9.title: Wildlife exclusion fencing for plant nurseries
parker/9.summary: A plant nursery asked to install deer fencing, which is typically eight feet high, taller than the six feet the Land Development Ordinance allows. Council showed general support and staff returned Oct. 19 seeking direction on amending the ordinance.

parker/10.title: Twenty Mile Road improvements and Parker Road/Hilltop intersection
parker/10.summary: Council introduced an ordinance stating the Town's intent to acquire property interests to build and improve Twenty Mile Road. It also awarded a $1,339,679.75 contract to Denver Dirt Works for the Parker Road and Hilltop Road intersection and added $607,070 to the 2026 resurfacing contract.
parker/10.where: Twenty Mile Road; Parker Road and Hilltop Road

parker/11.title: Parker Heritage Center reimagining and tribal history
parker/11.summary: Council reviewed an Interpretive Plan to reimagine the Parker Heritage Center with Douglas County and Parker History, with $100,000 budgeted for 2026 plus a $7,500 grant. Council also discussed ways to honor the area's tribal history, and an amendment to the partnership agreement came up Nov. 2.

parker/12.title: Parker Senior Center feasibility study and improvements
parker/12.summary: Council received an update on the Senior Center's feasibility study and facility needs including drainage, flooring and parking lot repairs. No funding was requested.

parker/13.title: Downtown Parker and Chambers business improvement district 2027 budgets
parker/13.summary: The two business improvement districts presented 2027 operating plans and budgets, and resolutions to approve them were scheduled for Oct. 19.

phillips-county/0.title: Regulations for wind, solar, battery storage and data center facilities
phillips-county/0.summary: The county commissioners had an agenda item on regulations for wind energy, solar, battery energy storage and data center facilities on Aug. 20. A Land Use Code public hearing was cancelled that day. The documents do not state what was decided.

phillips-county/1.title: 2027 county budget work sessions
phillips-county/1.summary: The commissioners scheduled 2027 budget work sessions after their meetings on Sept. 9, Sept. 29, Oct. 9, Oct. 19 and Oct. 30. A 2027 sales tax MOU for control of confidential data also came up on Sept. 29.

phillips-county/2.title: Floodplain ordinance
phillips-county/2.summary: A floodplain ordinance had its first reading on Oct. 19 and its second reading on Oct. 30.

phillips-county/3.title: Housing needs assessment and water supply element
phillips-county/3.summary: On Oct. 9 the commissioners considered a request for qualifications for a housing needs assessment and water supply element. On Oct. 30 they took up Proposition 123 recertification, which relates to affordable housing commitments.

phillips-county/4.title: Landfill equipment purchase and landfill rates
phillips-county/4.summary: The landfill manager presented an equipment purchase on Aug. 20, and landfill rates were on the Aug. 31 agenda.

phillips-county/5.title: Viaero roadway occupancy agreements
phillips-county/5.summary: Roadway occupancy agreements with Viaero were on the agenda on Aug. 31 and again on Oct. 9.

phillips-county/6.title: Road and Bridge propane contracts and equipment
phillips-county/6.summary: Road and Bridge brought a CHS propane contract on Sept. 29, propane contracts on Oct. 9, and a cutting edges equipment purchase on Sept. 29.

phillips-county/7.title: Minor land use change hearing for Jason Roberts
phillips-county/7.summary: A public hearing on a minor land use change requested by Jason Roberts was scheduled Sept. 21. The documents do not state the outcome.

phillips-county/8.title: Brightwater Cattle Co. and County Road 38
phillips-county/8.summary: An item concerning Brightwater Cattle Co. and County Road 38 was on the Oct. 30 agenda.

phillips-county/9.title: Human services contract and carpet bids
phillips-county/9.summary: The Department of Human Services director presented a contract on Aug. 20, and DHS carpet bids were considered on Sept. 21.

pitkin/0.title: 2026 Zoning Code rewrite, RV parks and Planned Development
pitkin/0.summary: The Board went through the zoning code update page by page in November, held a public hearing in January, and took up adoption of the 2026 Zoning Code in February. Residents debated an RV park use and the Planned Development wording, and the Board agreed to strike the RV Park section and the "mixed uses" language. In April the Zoning Board was set to review more code wording on May 4.

pitkin/1.title: Western Slope Towers radio tower lease with Gunnison Met Rec
pitkin/1.summary: The Board has been negotiating a lease for the town's tower site, where Western Slope wants 18 months at no charge. The mayor thought the proposed amount was too low, and the lease lists 2,500 square feet at the site. Residents commented, and the Board wanted a clause requiring site cleanup if no tenant remains. The agreement was discussed again in February, and the contract came up again in April.

pitkin/2.title: 2025 budget amendment, 2026 budget and mill levy
pitkin/2.summary: The Board held a public hearing on the 2025 budget amendment (street maintenance raised by $7,000) and the 2026 budget, then waited on county mill levy figures. On Dec. 11 it adopted Resolution 7 (amended 2025 and 2026 budgets) and Resolution 8 (levying 2026 property taxes). April financials showed a large increase in sales tax.

pitkin/3.title: Pay for town officials and board members
pitkin/3.summary: Trustees discussed paying the Environmental Health Agent about $550 for classes, the Streets/Ditches Commissioner $300 a month, and Zoning Board members $50 per meeting (about $3,000 a year for a full board). Resolution 6 on coverage with CIRSA was also passed, and Ramon Reed was paid for his time as Trustee.

pitkin/4.title: Onsite wastewater (OWTS) regulations update
pitkin/4.summary: After a public hearing on Nov. 19, the Board adopted Ordinance 1 of 2025 updating on-site wastewater treatment system regulations, as required by state Regulation 43. Josh Ackerman was appointed the town's Environmental Health Agent.

pitkin/5.title: Wildfire resiliency, energy and building codes
pitkin/5.summary: The town held a work session on a Wildfire Resiliency Code in October and planned public hearings on the Zoning, Wildfire, Energy and Building codes starting in January 2026. A wildfire mitigation seminar was noted in April.

pitkin/6.title: Fire/irrigation ditch cleaning and pond maintenance agreement with CPW
pitkin/6.summary: The Board took bids to clean and dig about 600 feet of fire and irrigation ditches. It also considered a 5-year operations and maintenance agreement with Colorado Parks and Wildlife for a pond. The mayor heard concerns that the pond could be drained into the ditch.

pitkin/7.title: Two open Board seats and Zoning Board vacancy
pitkin/7.summary: Resolution 4 of 2026 declared two Board member positions open, and the Board posted an open Zoning Board seat since the mayor's term there expires at the end of April. Cory Nasso was named Mayor Pro Tem and the Town Clerk and Attorney were reappointed.

pitkin/8.title: Fence permit at 428 State Street
pitkin/8.summary: The Board reviewed a previously denied fence permit request for 428 State Street and approved it in April.

platteville/0.title: Housing needs assessment, expedited affordable housing review and Proposition 123 commitment
platteville/0.summary: The Oct. 20, 2026 agenda lists three housing items: Resolution 2026-20 adopting a Housing Needs Assessment (with a public hearing), Resolution 2026-21 on expedited review policies for affordable housing projects, and Resolution 2026-22 on the town's Proposition 123 commitment for 2027-2029. The documents do not state the outcome.

pueblo-county/0.title: Aspen Acres Fire disaster emergency and flood recovery
pueblo-county/0.summary: The Board renewed its local disaster emergency declaration week after week for the Aspen Acres fire, which began June 29, 2026. The fire affected over 101,965 acres and destroyed about 240 homes and 9 businesses. The county has moved to burn-scar flooding and debris-flow recovery, including an $18.3 million USDA watershed grant, engineering contracts with Wilson and Company ($300,000) and Rocksol, a $500,000 mitigation MOU, federal assistance applications and a FEMA office lease.

pueblo-county/1.title: Stage-2 open fire ban in unincorporated Pueblo County
pueblo-county/1.summary: The Board adopted a Stage-2 open fire ban for unincorporated areas due to high fire danger and the active wildfire. It bans campfires, fireworks, explosives, off-road vehicle use and chainsaws without spark arresters.

pueblo-county/2.title: Data center zoning standards
pueblo-county/2.summary: The Planning Commission held work sessions on August 19 and September 16 on draft use-specific standards for data centers, which are a special use in the county code. Staff added requirements for infrastructure cost-sharing, road use agreements and decommissioning within 12 months. The goal is a code amendment for Planning Commission and Commissioner review.

pueblo-county/3.title: 2026-2027 county budget cuts and layoffs
pueblo-county/3.summary: The county is dealing with a budget shortfall. Executive sessions covered personnel and operating cuts affecting the Assessor, District Attorney, Treasurer, Sheriff and Clerk offices. The Board eliminated BOCC receptionist positions, with the effective date later moved to Dec. 19, 2026. A 2026 budget amendment hearing was held and the 2027 proposed budget was presented. The county also adopted a 2027 pay plan and employee benefits, redesignated TABOR reserve property, and discussed certificates of participation and a revitalization authority.

pueblo-county/4.title: Honors Energy and 3 Corners Connector 1041 permits
pueblo-county/4.summary: The Board considered a second 24-month extension of Honors Energy's HB 1041 permit for a project on about 1,390 acres. It also took up a 1041 permit request from 3 Corners Connector LLC on October 8.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use

pueblo-county/5.title: Solar agreements and stormwater maintenance
pueblo-county/5.summary: Executive sessions covered potential agreements with Solon Solar and AES Solar. The Board approved stormwater facility maintenance agreements with Highland Solar I and Thunder Wolf II.

pueblo-county/6.title: Pueblo West roads sales tax oversight
pueblo-county/6.summary: The Board appointed members to the Pueblo West Roads Sales Tax Oversight Committee for the 1% temporary sales tax under Ballot Question 6C. It also discussed the roads IGA with the Pueblo West Metropolitan District.

pueblo-county/7.title: Land use cases: rezonings, permits and zoning violations
pueblo-county/7.summary: The Board and Planning Commission handled rezonings, special use permits abandoned or rescinded, a vehicle sales permit for Toby and Rose Miller, a Fremont Paving gravel and asphalt permit review, cell tower permits including 4800 North Creek Road in Beulah, and legal action against zoning violators including 46911 Fields Road in Avondale. A fire hydrant impact fee for Pueblo Rural Fire Station 2 was also considered.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use
Board of County Commissioners Land Use

pueblo-county/8.title: Runyon Sports Complex lease
pueblo-county/8.summary: The county negotiated a lease with the Runyon Sports Complex Commission, discussed in executive sessions, and approved a lease agreement on October 22. Contracts for bleachers and artificial turf were also discussed.

pueblo-county/9.title: Jail construction contract with JE Dunn
pueblo-county/9.summary: Executive sessions addressed the jail construction contract between the county and JE Dunn, along with a Sheriff's Office collective bargaining agreement and inmate health services agreement.

pueblo-county/10.title: New County Attorney and administrative changes
pueblo-county/10.summary: The Board appointed Brendan Hursh as County Attorney on Sept. 22 after he served as interim since June 9. It also removed directors of the county capital construction corporation and transferred a property, appointed the CAO to the PEDCO board, and delegated personnel authority under the chief executive model.

pueblo-county/11.title: Marijuana excise tax funding and scholarships
pueblo-county/11.summary: The Board discussed a marijuana excise tax agreement with the Pueblo Hispanic Education Foundation for scholarships and a potential amendment.

pueblo-county/12.title: Pueblo Area Council of Governments transportation planning
pueblo-county/12.summary: PACOG considered its FY2027 budget, TIP amendments including highway safety funds of $618,750, the Medal of Honor Blvd. trail project, the Bicycle and Pedestrian Master Plan, Bustang expansion and Carbon Reduction Program projects.

pueblo/0.title: Automated speed camera enforcement program
pueblo/0.summary: Police Traffic Division presented a plan for speed safety cameras on residential streets, park frontages and designated traffic safety corridors, estimating $302,400 to $504,000 in monthly citations depending on pay rate. On Oct. 13 Council took up a first-reading ordinance on automated enforcement and a staffing ordinance amendment for the Police Department.

pueblo/1.title: Black Hills Energy electric rate increase
pueblo/1.summary: Council discussed the 2026 Black Hills Colorado Electric rate case and then considered a resolution opposing the proposed increase and the added ratepayer costs of its 2026 Electric Resource Plan and Clean Energy Plan (PUC Proceeding No. 26A-0333E). Certified copies would go to the Public Utilities Commission.

pueblo/2.title: 2027 city budget
pueblo/2.summary: Departments presented 2027 budgets to Council in August and October work sessions (Police, Fire, Public Works, IT, Law, Finance, Parks). The Mayor's recommended budget totals $117,785,907, with sales tax (3.7% rate) making up 66.8% of general taxes. A public hearing on the proposed 2027 budget was set for Oct. 26.

pueblo/3.title: Leonardo da Vinci Museum funding and economic development partner
pueblo/3.summary: Council reviewed a funding request from the Leonardo da Vinci Museum of North America from the 1/2-cent sales tax fund, which has already approved $14.4 million for the project that replaced the Professional Bull Riders university. Council also followed up on an economic development partner RFP and held closed-door talks on projects including Tortuga, Falcon, Manta and St. Charles Industrial Park.

pueblo/4.title: Lime Road and St. Charles Industrial Park infrastructure
pueblo/4.summary: Staff reviewed the 1.4-mile, two-lane concrete Lime Road, the only route into St. Charles Industrial Park, which needs frequent repairs. Reinforced concrete is estimated at about $20M versus about $5M for asphalt, against $8M already moved to design Lime Road and wastewater improvements. A resident also spoke about capital improvements on Limon Road.
pueblo/4.where: Lime Road, St. Charles Industrial Park

pueblo/5.title: EPA smelter cleanup in Eilers and Bessemer
pueblo/5.summary: An EPA project manager briefed Council on the cleanup of former smelter contamination in Eilers and Bessemer, including residential properties, parks and Benedict Park. The public comment period closed Oct. 15 and EPA is preparing a responsiveness summary.
pueblo/5.where: Eilers and Bessemer neighborhoods, Benedict Park

pueblo/6.title: Annexations and Jackson Ranch zoning
pueblo/6.summary: Council found valid the petition to annex the 89.93-acre Pueblo Masterplan Communities Annexation No. 1 and sent it to Planning and Zoning for review. On Sept. 14 it began zoning of Jackson Ranch annexation parcels of 250.1, 65.7 and 225.66 acres, including agricultural zoning.
pueblo/6.where: Jackson Ranch annexation area; Pueblo Masterplan Communities

pueblo/7.title: Moratorium ordinance on new applications
pueblo/7.summary: On Sept. 14 Council took up a first-reading ordinance imposing a 24-month moratorium on accepting applications for and issuing certain new permits or licenses; the type is not fully shown in the documents.

pueblo/8.title: Pueblo Mountain Park next steps and city parks
pueblo/8.summary: Council scheduled a work session on next steps for Pueblo Mountain Park, and a resident spoke about city parks and Mountain Park at the Oct. 13 meeting. Council also awarded a $148,337.95 contract for concrete improvements at Elmwood Golf Course.
pueblo/8.where: Pueblo Mountain Park; Elmwood Golf Course

pueblo/9.title: Airport projects and Aviation Asset Defense funding
pueblo/9.summary: Council created a project for Aviation Asset Defense with a $300,000 transfer from the airport grant match project, formed an Airport Policy Advisory board, and approved taxiway/hangar contingencies. The Aviation Asset Defense resolution was then brought back for a motion to reconsider on Oct. 5, and an airline operating agreement was introduced.

pueblo/10.title: Emergency sewer and storm sewer repairs
pueblo/10.summary: Council ratified emergency contracts including $210,648.29 for a sewer repair at 109 Vernon Pl, $295,504.20 for storm sewer repair at 10th and Conley streets, and smaller sewer repairs at Marian Dr and Bryan Cir. It also awarded a $134,265 manhole rehabilitation contract.
pueblo/10.where: 109 Vernon Pl; 10th St and Conley St; 132 Marian Dr; 31201 Bryan Cir

pueblo/11.title: Pueblo Library District funding and regional transportation authority
pueblo/11.summary: A library presentation stressed that the library's mill levy approved in 2019 is not a new tax or rate increase. Council also reviewed a draft steering committee structure for forming a Regional Transportation Authority, including voting seats and technical advisors.

pueblo/12.title: Dangerous building demolition cost at 125 E. 7th Street
pueblo/12.summary: Council held a hearing and passed an ordinance assessing demolition and removal costs for dangerous buildings at 125 E. 7th Street, amending the interest rate from 7% to 10%.

pueblo/13.title: BATTLE grant and blighted property acquisition
pueblo/13.summary: Council considered grant funding for a police BATTLE team (project PS2605) and a CREATE emergency and trauma education grant. Closed sessions covered acquiring blighted properties under a housing Section 108 project.

rangely/0.title: Geothermal energy campus and proposed data center
rangely/0.summary: Council repeatedly took up the Energy Campus Development & Municipal Participation Study (stage 2 of Rangely geothermal development). Residents including Tanner Nielsen and Camille raised concerns about a possible data center, water use, noise, NDAs and transparency, and Nielsen suggested a moratorium and a solar partnership with CNCC. A proposal was raised to bar officials from signing NDAs for economic development.

rangely/1.title: Water shortage, Stage 3 restrictions and White River water supply
rangely/1.summary: The Town went into Stage 3 water restrictions as river flow dropped, with the water conservancy district releasing 10 cfs from Kenney Reservoir; it later returned to Stage 1. Council took up Resolution 2026-07 declaring a municipal water urgency and authorizing negotiation, but not signing, of a conditional storage agreement for the White River Regional Water Supply Project. Council also dealt with bulk water customers under Emergency Ordinance 707.

rangely/2.title: Water and wastewater plant repairs
rangely/2.summary: Staff reported the wastewater pond liner needs replacement, with other lagoon liners also needing work and grants being sought. The water plant has structural problems including corrosion, and the middle zone water tank re-coating project was proposed for delay. Repairs to chlorine pumps and the water softener were also reported.

rangely/3.title: 2027 budget and capital projects
rangely/3.summary: Council held budget and capital project work sessions, including a possible Main Street beautification project. On Oct 13 it considered approving the draft 2027 budget as presented, and revised the Housing Assistance Fund budget.

rangely/4.title: Town Manager's outside employment and oversight
rangely/4.summary: A resident, Jack Richens, raised concerns about the Town Manager, and council discussed Jonah's employment outside the Town in a conversation reported at the Sept 22 meeting. The documents do not state an outcome.

rangely/5.title: Independent hearing officers for employee grievances
rangely/5.summary: A virtual special meeting on Oct 29 considered Resolution 2026-08, creating two to three independent hearing officers to hear grievances over discipline and terminations by the Town Manager, and amending personnel rules. The Town Council would no longer sit as the hearing body.

rangely/6.title: Police leadership and services
rangely/6.summary: Interim Chief of Police Joseph McGuire was sworn in, with two police openings reported earlier. Council also amended the 2026 fee schedule for certified VIN inspections, and an SRO change was noted.

rangely/7.title: Bell Street crosswalk and no-parking changes
rangely/7.summary: Residents and council discussed the Bell Street crosswalk sign and a no-parking area extended 50 ft at the park. Council member Tim Webber worried about the effect on parking during events.

rangely/8.title: Asbestos abatement on Birch Street
rangely/8.summary: An asbestos project on Birch is starting, and additional asbestos was found. The grant is expected to cover it.

rico/0.title: Letter of support for Montelores Bridge restoration trail grant
rico/0.summary: The Dolores Ranger District asked the Town of Rico for a letter of support for its 2027 Colorado Parks and Wildlife Non-Motorized Trail Grant application, seeking about $80,000 to repair the Montelores Bridge. The Forest Service wants letters by September 15, 2026, and the Town's support would be limited to endorsing the project. The Council was set to consider approving the letter on September 2, 2026.

ridgway/0.title: Beaver Creek Diversion Restoration and infiltration gallery
ridgway/0.summary: The Town amended its RESPEC engineering contract to $657,312 in January 2026 to redesign the infiltration gallery. The project is funded by NRCS grants and a CWCB loan of up to $8,080,000, with total cost near $4 million. In June 2026 Council awarded the gallery work to Meridian Contracting for no more than $641,386.

ridgway/1.title: Wastewater Treatment Plant renovation and siting
ridgway/1.summary: Council reviewed the needs assessment for renovating the wastewater treatment plant in May 2026. Siting and treatment options were slated for discussion at the September agenda and the October 31 budget retreat. A resident asked that the new plant be built to last 50 to 60 years.

ridgway/2.title: Housing Action Plan and regional affordable housing services
ridgway/2.summary: The Town is preparing a Housing Action Plan required under state law (SB 24-174) with five goal areas, including ADUs, land banking and workforce housing. A resolution adopting it was on the October 14 agenda, along with Proposition 123 participation and the Home Trust of Ouray County's housing services work. The Home Trust also gave the Council a right-of-first-refusal decision on a home at 683 Frederick St.

ridgway/3.title: 2026 and 2027 budgets, sales tax decline and capital plans
ridgway/3.summary: The 2026 budget was adopted in December 2025 after workshops. Staff noted sales tax receipts were down 22.64% from 2024, with 2.4% pay movements proposed. The draft 2027 budget was presented in October with a budget retreat on October 31 covering pay, capital projects and funding requests from the Home Trust and EcoAction Partners.

ridgway/4.title: Lodge converted to workforce housing and tourism strategy
ridgway/4.summary: The Town's move of a lodge to workforce housing cut lodging tax revenue by about $40,000 and reduced sales tax. The Council received a tourism strategy report and a destination marketing plan, and signed a visitor and business engagement agreement.

ridgway/5.title: Water supply planning and drought restrictions
ridgway/5.summary: Council reviewed the Draft Water Supply Element of the Master Plan amendment. It considered rescinding Stage 2 mandatory water restrictions and fire restrictions, and a modified Water Conservation and Management Plan. A resident asked how growth is being planned against water supply.

ridgway/6.title: Lawsuit over land use code
ridgway/6.summary: In March 2026 Council considered filing a Complaint for Declaratory and Injunctive Relief, discussing the importance of defending the land use code and not setting a precedent.

ridgway/7.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and building code update
ridgway/7.summary: Council introduced Ordinance 03-2026 adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code and other codes by reference, with 25 of 26 staff amendments forwarded by the Planning Commission.

ridgway/8.title: Vehicle idling ordinance
ridgway/8.summary: An ordinance to limit vehicle idling was presented for adoption in December 2025. In July 2026 a resident asked Council to reconsider addressing the proposed idling ordinance.

ridgway/9.title: Street closures for events and Council meeting procedures
ridgway/9.summary: Council weighed closures of Clinton Street and other streets for events, and a business owner complained of insufficient notice. Council also discussed adopting rules of procedure and decorum, including time limits on comment.

ridgway/10.title: Athletic Park Bike Park and development applications
ridgway/10.summary: The Athletic Park Coalition asked for Town funds for design of a bike park. Council also had a site plan for Riverbend Townhomes on Liddell Drive and plat applications.

rifle/0.title: Data center / Bulk Resource Consumer conditional use permit rules
rifle/0.summary: Community Development drafted a conditional use permit framework for data centers and other "bulk resource consumers" limited to industrial districts. It would require utility, water, noise, fiscal, emergency response, thermal, housing and decommissioning analyses and let the city deny projects that can't show net public benefit. The Planning Commission discussed it Aug. 25 and Sept. 29, and City Council took it up Oct. 14.

rifle/1.title: Draft 2026 Comprehensive Plan update
rifle/1.summary: Planning Commission reviewed a partial draft of the first comprehensive plan update since 2019, which will guide development for the next 5-10 years. The state-required strategic growth and water supply elements are still being prepared, and staff asked for feedback on direction.

rifle/2.title: Municipal code amendments: ADUs, warehouses, site plans and variances
rifle/2.summary: Staff proposed multiple text amendments to the Rifle Municipal Code, including ADU size requirements, splitting warehouses into Local and Regional categories (with size limits and zones), height requirements, lot line rules, site plan requirements and variance applications. An ADU ordinance had a public hearing before City Council Oct. 21.

rifle/3.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment and housing needs study
rifle/3.summary: Council was asked to consider the city's Proposition 123 commitment of affordable and attainable housing units, and the Planning Commission was to consider an amended 2025 Rooted in Rifle Housing Needs document.

rifle/4.title: Business Incubator Center Rifle branch funding
rifle/4.summary: The city asked the Grand Junction Business Incubator Center to price a Rifle branch to support startups and downtown vitality. The budget line was $100k, and the finalized proposal requests $137k, for Council's Oct. 21 budget workshop; a USDA grant request is also mentioned.

rifle/5.title: 2026 Water System Improvements bid
rifle/5.summary: Council was asked to award the bid for the Rifle 2026 Water System Improvements Project to Martinez Western Constructors Inc. A water rights report was also on the Oct. 14 agenda.

rifle/6.title: GRIT downtown grants, facade improvements and wayfinding
rifle/6.summary: The GRIT board approved four grants totaling $22,200 for local events, and considered facade grants for 126 W. 4th Street and ProMex at 233 Railroad Ave. It also reviewed the 2027 GRIT budget, a downtown wayfinding consultant, a Third Street shade structure (about $20,000-$30,000 for ~400 sq ft) and a participatory budgeting pilot funded by lodging tax.

sources.body: Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board
Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board
Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board

rifle/7.title: Rifle Community Foundation restructuring under the city
rifle/7.summary: After the resignation of board president Kasey Nipsel, the foundation discussed becoming a city board rather than a separate 501(c)(3), focused on grant decisions. It reviewed about a dozen grant requests, including $30,000 for Discovery Cafe, and a new online application and city webpage.

rifle/8.title: Parks and Recreation plans, budget and Rifle Mountain Park requests
rifle/8.summary: The advisory board considered the 2027-2028 Strategic Plan, a 2027 budget request, weather closure policy for the Metro Pool, a skate park comment, a Centennial Park riparian restoration grant letter of support, and a Rifle Mountain Park recognition plaque request near an apple tree between the ice caves under the naming policy.
rifle/8.where: Rifle Mountain Park, Centennial Park, Metro Pool

rifle/9.title: Planning applications: 799 Buckhorn, 758 Railroad Ave, 1317 E 17th St, and a Tourist-district rezone
rifle/9.summary: Planning Commission held hearings on a conditional use permit for 799 Buckhorn, a variance for 758 Railroad Ave, a minor subdivision of 1317 E 17th St, and rezone PLN 2026-023 from Tourist.

routt-county/0.title: Yampa Valley Gravel Pit special use permit (PL20260026)
routt-county/0.summary: The county is reviewing a special use permit to expand the permit boundary of the Old gravel pit on the north side of County Road 65. It went to the Planning Commission on Sept 17, and the commissioners considered it Sept 29 and then took up the permit for the Chair's signature Oct 13. A written public comment from Drew Kolbe is in the Sept 29 packet.

routt-county/1.title: 2027 county budget and health insurance costs
routt-county/1.summary: Commissioners heard 2027 budget presentations from Public Works, Facilities Management and the District Attorney, reviewed the proposed budget on Sept 21-22, and looked at county dues and outside funding requests. They also reviewed the 2027 health and dental insurance plan and the insurance pool budget, and the Tri-County District Attorney personnel budget.

routt-county/2.title: Nottingham Ranch conservation easement and Purchase of Development Rights projects
routt-county/2.summary: The PDR Board recommended $3,000,000 toward a conservation easement on Nottingham Ranch (PDR Project 222), which commissioners considered on Sept 8 after an executive session. Projects 224 and 225 were also under Tier I and II review in October. The PDR Board also met with Planning about how conservation easements affect development and subdivision design under the county's development code.

sources.body: Purchase of Development Rights Board Meetings
Purchase of Development Rights Board Meetings

routt-county/3.title: Small modular reactor proposal and electrical needs
routt-county/3.summary: The Planning Commission discussed the electrical needs of a small modular reactor (SMR) proposal after the project application was re-submitted. The documents give little further detail.

routt-county/4.title: Milner wastewater matter
routt-county/4.summary: Commissioners went into executive session on Sept 8 and Sept 22 over the Milner wastewater notice. The documents do not state the outcome.

routt-county/5.title: Stage 1 fire restrictions
routt-county/5.summary: The county returned to Stage 1 fire restrictions under Ordinance 2026-001 in September. Commissioners then moved to rescind them on Sept 29.

routt-county/6.title: Yampa Valley Airport west terminal expansion grant
routt-county/6.summary: Commissioners considered Amendment #3 to the FAA Airport Improvement Program grant for the west terminal expansion at Yampa Valley Regional Airport. The Airport Commission also continues to receive capital, infrastructure and budget updates.

routt-county/7.title: Affordable housing bonds: YVHA and CHFA private activity bond delegation
routt-county/7.summary: Commissioners handled the Routt County and Yampa Valley Housing Authority delegation agreement with CHFA and an inducement resolution (2026-062) involving private activity bond volume cap for housing.

routt-county/8.title: Regional water quality plan and instream flow proposals
routt-county/8.summary: Commissioners ratified comments on the draft NWCCOG Regional Water Quality Management Plan ("208 Plan"). The state Colorado Water Conservation Board was also scheduled to present proposed instream flow water rights on Lost Dog Creek and Butcher Creek on Oct 19.
routt-county/8.where: Lost Dog Creek and Butcher Creek

routt-county/9.title: County Annex HVAC problems
routt-county/9.summary: On Oct 27 commissioners discussed HVAC problems recently found in the Annex building and a replacement proposal, seeking direction from facilities staff.

routt-county/10.title: Sheriff's office and detention center: body scanner, remodel and officer training fund
routt-county/10.summary: Commissioners considered a contract for a body scanner purchase and detention center remodel (RFP 899) and a Peace Officer Training and Support Fund resolution. Two Sheriff's Office training agreements with CMC were also on the Sept 22 agenda.

routt-county/11.title: Lodging tax tourism marketing funding panel
routt-county/11.summary: The Advertising and Marketing Local Tourism Panel is setting up how lodging tax money will be awarded, including funding cycle, applicant eligibility, evaluation criteria and scoring.

sources.body: Advertising and Marketing Local Tourism Panel
Advertising and Marketing Local Tourism Panel

routt-county/12.title: Heritage grants and Certified Local Government designation
routt-county/12.summary: The Museum and Heritage Advisory Board considered fall grants, including $48,500 for a South Routt historic survey, $10,711.55 for Hayden Heritage Center and $3,646 for Oak Creek and Phippsburg. The Historic Preservation Board is finalizing a resolution to become a Certified Local Government and reviewing a permit at 54200 CR 62.

routt-county/13.title: North Routt recreation strategic plan and trail grants
routt-county/13.summary: Commissioners approved a consultant for the North Routt County recreation strategic plan (RFP 891) and ratified a letter of support for a Colorado Parks and Wildlife non-motorized trails grant by Routt County Riders.

routt-county/14.title: Public health work session: school vaccination rates and tobacco ordinance
routt-county/14.summary: A Sept 14 work session covered school vaccination data, an update on a tobacco coalition ordinance, and a SAMHSA grant.

rye/0.title: Water tank inspections, cleaning and updates
rye/0.summary: Council held a special session on Nov. 3 to review water tank inspections and cleaning. Updates on Water Tanks #1, #2 and #3 were on the November and December agendas.

rye/1.title: Sewer main line replacement project
rye/1.summary: The sewer main line replacement capital project was an ongoing update item on the November and December agendas, alongside water treatment plant and infrastructure updates and a brainstorm on removing silt and reeds from the inlet.

rye/2.title: 2026 budget and supplemental appropriation
rye/2.summary: Council began 2026 budget preparation in November. In December the agenda included a 2025 supplemental budget and appropriation (2025-7) and adoption of the 2026 budget (2025-8).

rye/3.title: Intergovernmental agreements with Pueblo County and Colorado City Metro
rye/3.summary: Council took up an agreement with Pueblo County on road maintenance. It also considered a three-party agreement with Pueblo County and Colorado City Metro for a satellite office.

rye/4.title: Safer Routes to School grant
rye/4.summary: Council received an update on the Safer Routes to School grant in November.

rye/5.title: Wildlife-protection refuse ordinance and animal control rules
rye/5.summary: Council reviewed Ordinance 2020-11 on wildlife protection through refuse disposal, including an update on Account #87. It also planned to review the Pueblo County Animal Control Ordinance.

rye/6.title: Lien for unpaid ordinance violation fees (Account #69) and dumpster right-of-way fees
rye/6.summary: Council considered placing a lien on Account #69 for nonpayment of 2022 ordinance violation fees. December's agenda also had dumpster right-of-way service fees.

rye/7.title: EV charging stations and CERT program presentation
rye/7.summary: Matt Akers was scheduled to present on EV charging stations and the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) program on Nov. 12.

salida/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center applications
salida/0.summary: Council held the second reading and public hearing on Ordinance 2026-19, which would impose a temporary moratorium on submitting, accepting, processing and approving data center applications in Salida. No one spoke at the hearing.

salida/1.title: Short-term rental residency and active use requirements
salida/1.summary: Ordinance 2026-22 changes the residency and annual active use requirements for short-term rental licenses. At the Sept. 1 hearing, Paula Givan and Nancy Wallace spoke about the active use requirement. Council moved to approve the residency amendment and remove the active use amendment.

salida/2.title: 1st & D affordable workforce housing project with Trellis Housing Partners
salida/2.summary: Council took up an MOU with Trellis Housing Partners for the 1st & D Space-to-Create affordable workforce rental housing project. A resolution authorizing the sale of city property for it is on the Nov. 2 agenda, subject to an upcoming ordinance.
salida/2.where: 233 E. First Street and 102 D Street

salida/3.title: Regional housing needs assessment and Proposition 123 collaboration
salida/3.summary: Council reviewed preliminary housing needs assessment results and later considered approving the regional assessment and final findings. It also considered MOUs on regional Proposition 123 affordable housing collaboration with Buena Vista, Poncha Springs, Chaffee County and the Chaffee Housing Authority. Earlier, it approved a Chaffee Housing Trust fee transfer for 8 deed-restricted units in the Two Rivers development.

salida/4.title: Land Use Code amendments and follow-up work
salida/4.summary: Council held the second reading of Ordinance 2026-21, a comprehensive set of Land Use Code amendments. Planning Commission then began a work session on leftover issues, including how to define and regulate cottage housing and co-housing.

salida/5.title: Energy code adoption and regional sustainability work
salida/5.summary: Council gave first reading to Ordinance 2026-23 amending adoption of the 2021 International Energy Conservation Code. Several residents spoke at the Sept. 15 hearing. Staff also updated Council on grant-funded regional sustainability work, including EV readiness, greenhouse gas inventory and possible recycling and waste hauler rules.

salida/6.title: 2027 budget and community budget survey
salida/6.summary: Council discussed a community budget survey, then held several sessions on the 2027 preliminary budget. One session included a treasurer's comparison of the 2026 and 2027 budgets. Earlier, it approved a financial condition monitoring and revenue response policy.

salida/7.title: Mountain Mail building renovation at 125 E. 2nd Street
salida/7.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission considered a Major Certificate of Approval from Shavano Holding Co. LLC for exterior renovation of the old Mountain Mail building. The plan includes a rooftop patio, two upper-floor residences, ground-floor retail and demolition of a deteriorated rear structure. The building is non-contributing to the historic district.

salida/8.title: Comprehensive plan update and water supply and growth elements
salida/8.summary: Planning Commission is to discuss comprehensive plan amendments for a Water Supply Element and a Strategic Growth Element. Council also considered supporting a Local Planning Capacity grant application for the 2027 Comprehensive Plan update.

salida/9.title: Historic Preservation Commission alternate members
salida/9.summary: Ordinance 2026-24 would allow up to two alternate members on the Historic Preservation Commission. It passed first reading and was set for a second-reading public hearing.

salida/10.title: Mesa Tank project and city utility projects
salida/10.summary: Council considered awarding the Mesa Tank Project, which was pulled from the consent agenda for separate discussion. Final settlements for the CR105 bridge area river restoration and the 2026 utility replacement project were also on the agenda.

salida/11.title: 610 Walnut Street dangerous building notice
salida/11.summary: Council went into executive session about potential contracts tied to the Chaffee County Building Safety Department's Notice to Vacate and Notice of Demolition of Dangerous Building at 610 Walnut Street.

salida/12.title: US-50 and SH-291 intersection letter to CDOT
salida/12.summary: Council considered approving a letter to CDOT about intersection improvements at US-50 and SH-291.

san-juan-county/0.title: Stage Two fire ban (Resolution 2026-07)
san-juan-county/0.summary: The council agenda for June 29, 2026 includes Resolution 2026-07 to put a Stage Two fire ban in place. The agenda gives no further detail on the restrictions or the outcome.

san-miguel-county/0.title: Natural resources land use code rewrite: forestry, oil & gas, deep geothermal
san-miguel-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed new Land Use Code rules for forestry practices (logging tiers by board feet, streamlined wildfire mitigation review), oil and gas operations, and deep geothermal, with Sheep Mountain Alliance commenting on forestry. The county commissioners scheduled public hearings on Resolutions 2026-40 through 2026-43 for October 21 to adopt the new Article 6 sections and related amendments.

san-miguel-county/1.title: Housing Code Update and affordable housing land use changes
san-miguel-county/1.summary: The county is rewriting its land use code to make affordable and workforce housing easier to build, funded by a Proposition 123 planning capacity grant. Stakeholder roundtables discussed density bonuses tied to deed-restricted workforce housing, ADUs, and streamlined review, and the county sought an amendment to its Local Planning Capacity grant after expedited review approval from DOLA. The Planning Commission also took up a Qualified Developer amendment to the affordable housing rules.

san-miguel-county/2.title: Employee Housing Impact Mitigation Fee
san-miguel-county/2.summary: Commissioners discussed the county's Employee Housing Impact Mitigation Fee, which applies to new construction and additions in the unincorporated Telluride R-1 school district area and funds housing purchases and projects like Sunnyside. Materials compare it with the Town of Telluride's gap fee of $902 per square foot.
san-miguel-county/2.where: Unincorporated county, Telluride R-1 school district

san-miguel-county/3.title: Mountain Village affordable housing project: fee waiver and setback variance
san-miguel-county/3.summary: The commissioners held a hearing on waiving land use application fees for the Town of Mountain Village affordable housing project. The Board of Adjustment considered reducing the setback from County Road 63L from 20 feet to 7 feet on a 56.34-acre parcel, to keep homes away from the riparian corridor and wetlands. Staff recommended a five-year approval.

san-miguel-county/4.title: Land use code amendments: natural medicine and nonconforming lots
san-miguel-county/4.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a new Section 5-31 setting where and how natural medicine businesses may operate, including distance from daycares. It also reviewed amendments allowing uses on nonconforming lots, where attorneys and other speakers commented.

san-miguel-county/5.title: 2027 county budget and community support funding
san-miguel-county/5.summary: Commissioners reviewed the 2027 preliminary budget and considered 2027 Community Support Funding, including a $12,000 request from West End Family Link. The Open Space Commission also worked toward a November 9 budget deadline, and a voter-approved county excise tax bill was discussed.

san-miguel-county/6.title: Lawson Hill Connector Trail
san-miguel-county/6.summary: The county approved an agreement with the Lawson Hill Property Owners Association to build trail improvements and sought CDOT concurrence to award the Lawson Hill Connector Trail Project (#26003). Commissioners later ratified the agreement for construction.

san-miguel-county/7.title: Bridal Veil Falls water flow and black swifts
san-miguel-county/7.summary: Citizens raised concerns that water diversion dropped flow at Bridal Veil Falls to about 1 CFS versus the 6.5 CFS required, threatening nesting black swifts. The commission noted no formal management prescriptions exist, pointed to the Forest Service and US Fish & Wildlife, and considered it resolved for now as birds migrate.

san-miguel-county/8.title: Open Space and parks projects: Galloping Goose Park, new manager, Gunnison sage grouse
san-miguel-county/8.summary: Galloping Goose Park is targeted for completion by an October 29 deadline, with a governor's visit possibly tied to a sculpture unveiling. The commission is hiring a Parks and Open Space Manager (J.D. Wise introduced later), wants Gunnison sage grouse on the work plan, and discussed a management plan and fire mitigation for a county property.
san-miguel-county/8.where: Galloping Goose Park and Down Valley

san-miguel-county/9.title: Noxious weed enforcement and grant funds
san-miguel-county/9.summary: The Noxious Weed Advisory Board discussed enforcement options and how to allocate a $5,800 Colorado Department of Agriculture Noxious Weed Fund grant. Past work includes tamarisk removal in Dry Creek Basin funded by America the Beautiful grants.

san-miguel-county/10.title: Down Valley and Placerville issues: Highway 145 multimodal, Station 3, Down Valley plan
san-miguel-county/10.summary: Commissioners followed up with Sawpit and Placerville residents on multimodal improvements with CDOT, signage near Juniper Village Road, the Down Valley Master Plan RFP, fire mitigation on county land, and a Telluride Fire Protection District update on Placerville Station 3.

san-miguel-county/11.title: Telluride Pines water system CDBG application
san-miguel-county/11.summary: Commissioners considered co-sponsoring a Community Development Block Grant public facilities application for the Telluride Pines HOA to restore safe and reliable water.

san-miguel-county/12.title: Gas pipeline spill and regional county discussion
san-miguel-county/12.summary: Five southwest counties planned an informal discussion with the Southern Ute Indian Council about a gas enterprise pipeline spill.

severance/0.title: Annexation petitions: Berrado Holding, Buffalo Creek and Ridgegate
severance/0.summary: On Oct. 27 the Town Council took up three resolutions finding annexation petitions in substantial compliance, starting annexation proceedings and setting public hearings under the Municipal Annexation Act for the Berrado Holding, Buffalo Creek and Ridgegate annexations.
severance/0.where: Berrado Holding, Buffalo Creek and Ridgegate annexation properties

severance/1.title: 2027 budget, rates and fee schedule
severance/1.summary: Council reviewed the 2027 proposed rates, fee schedule and budget on Oct. 27, after an Oct. 13 town hall on 2027 town projects and budget. An audit services agreement for 2026 was also on the Sept. 22 agenda.

severance/2.title: 2027 Capital Improvement Program
severance/2.summary: Council discussed the final draft of the 10-year CIP, of which only 2027 projects will be funded in the 2027 budget. New or increased items include a 2036 Police Department addition, more money for the 2027 water acquisition program, and added funds for Town Park improvements including a restroom.

severance/3.title: Metropolitan district service plans: Bower North and Northgate Lakes
severance/3.summary: Council held public hearings on Sept. 22 on ordinances approving consolidated service plans for the Bower North and Northgate Lakes metropolitan districts. On Oct. 27 a resolution confirmed that the Northgate Lakes ordinance (2026-12) took effect.
severance/3.where: Bower North and Northgate Lakes districts

severance/4.title: Oil and gas setbacks aligned with Weld County rules
severance/4.summary: The Planning Commission took up a Land Use Code amendment to align Severance's oil and gas setbacks with Weld County regulations. Council then considered Ordinance 2026-14 amending section 16.8.80 on Oct. 27.

severance/5.title: Land use code changes: setbacks, early grading, application suspensions and electric infrastructure
severance/5.summary: The Planning Commission handled several code amendments. They cover Town Core and Development Node setbacks, early grading permit rules, procedures for suspending applications at an applicant's request, and electric service infrastructure for new development. Council considered ordinances on early grading and setback tables on Oct. 27.
severance/5.where: Town Core and Development Node zone districts; Townwide

severance/6.title: Council power to adopt time-sensitive code amendments
severance/6.summary: Legal staff proposed letting Town Council adopt time-sensitive Land Use Code text amendments without waiting for a Planning Commission recommendation, while keeping a noticed public hearing. The Planning Commission reviewed Resolution PC 2026-02R in September and October.

severance/7.title: Comprehensive Plan update and community engagement
severance/7.summary: The Comprehensive Plan Advisory Committee reviewed the current 2020 plan and an engagement plan and schedule meant to build trust and gather resident input on land use, transportation, parks and growth.

severance/8.title: Severance High School After Prom grant
severance/8.summary: The school's After Prom program requested a $2,000 community grant for its 2027 event, after receiving $1,000 in February 2026. The Citizen Advisory Board reviewed it and it went to Council on the Oct. 27 consent calendar.
severance/8.where: Severance High School, 1200 Hidden Valley Parkway

severance/9.title: Interim town attorney appointment
severance/9.summary: Council considered a resolution appointing an interim town attorney and amending the engagement agreement.

severance/10.title: Mobile food vendor licensing
severance/10.summary: The Citizen Advisory Board discussed mobile food vendor licensing with the Town Attorney, along with an overview of town licensing and permits.

sheridan/0.title: 2027 budget and 2026 budget amendment
sheridan/0.summary: Council reviewed the 2027 proposed budget in work sessions (revenues, capital, open spaces, stormwater, general fund) and held a Sept. 28 public hearing where no one spoke. Ordinances 14-2026 (2026 amended budget) and 15-2026 (2027 budget) were up for second reading Oct. 12. The Redevelopment Agency also held hearings on its amended 2026 and 2027 budgets (Resolutions 4 and 5-2026).

sheridan/1.title: 0.50% sales and use tax increase referred to voters
sheridan/1.summary: Ordinance 13-2026 on second reading Aug. 24 would refer a 0.50 percentage point increase in the city sales and use tax to city voters for a public purpose.

sheridan/2.title: Bear Creek Trailhead rezoning at 3600 S. Federal Blvd.
sheridan/2.summary: Council held a public hearing Aug. 10 on rezoning 3600 S. Federal Blvd. to Parks and Recreation District to allow a public trailhead and park. The city acquired the property in 2024 in partnership with the Mile High Flood District. Planning Commission unanimously recommended approval, and no members of the public came forward to testify.

sheridan/3.title: Subdivision plats at 2200 W. Radcliff Ave. and 2500 W. Hampden Ave.
sheridan/3.summary: Planning Commission held hearings Sept. 2 on preliminary and final plats for both properties. Council heard the 2200 W. Radcliff case Sept. 28: four industrial parcels never legally subdivided, platting is needed before permits, no development is proposed, and the applicant would dedicate 19 more feet of right-of-way.
sheridan/3.where: 2200 W. Radcliff Ave. and 2500 W. Hampden Ave.

sheridan/4.title: Housing: Sheridan Housing Implementation Plan, Housing Authority and state ADU law
sheridan/4.summary: Planning staff updated on compliance with state ADU law HB24-1152, with code amendments to return later in the year. A consultant, Matrix Design Group, will present final Sheridan Housing Implementation Plan (SHIP) recommendations in October. Council work sessions in October took up the Sheridan Housing Authority.

sheridan/5.title: Trash and recycling equal space ordinance
sheridan/5.summary: Sustainability Coordinator Mel Englund is expected to introduce a potential equal space ordinance for trash and recycling, with a Planning Commission discussion scheduled Oct. 21.

sheridan/6.title: Crisis services contract with AllHealth Network
sheridan/6.summary: Council's Oct. 26 agenda includes Resolution 28-2026 approving an agreement with AllHealth Network for crisis services.

sheridan/7.title: Roads, Comcast franchise and regional items
sheridan/7.summary: Residents raised road concerns, and a council member noted the city's limited authority over them. The city manager reported the Comcast cable franchise agreement expired in 2024. A council member said DRCOG wants to advance congestion measures and E-470 expansion.

sheridan/8.title: Flying Saucer RV Park subdivision and brownfields grant
sheridan/8.summary: Planning staff reported on the Flying Saucer RV Park subdivision application, a federal EPA Brownfields Grant award, the renewed South Metro Enterprise Zone and South Santa Fe planning projects.

silver-cliff/0.title: Workforce housing agreement with Westcliffe and affordable housing project
silver-cliff/0.summary: The Board considered a Workforce Housing intergovernmental agreement (IGA) with Westcliffe in September and October 2026, with a draft going back to the attorney for edits. Trustee Troy Bomgardner gave workforce housing updates, and the Planning Commission took up an affordable housing interior lot line request with site plans for five buildings. The board also acted on Resolution 06-2026 on Prop 123 in June.

silver-cliff/1.title: Park improvements: playground, pickleball and Silver Cliff Park lot lines
silver-cliff/1.summary: The town sought proposals in June 2026 for park work including dirt work, concrete curb and handicap parking at the playground, and pickleball site preparation, and the board was asked to award the contract. A part-time park employee was proposed, the GOCO grant account is being tracked, and the Planning Commission will look at vacating lot lines in Silver Cliff Park in October. The board also signed a release for the old playground equipment.

silver-cliff/2.title: Excessive noise ordinance (Ordinance 01-2026)
silver-cliff/2.summary: Ordinance 01-2026 amending Sec. 10-9-30 on excessive noise had a first reading in April, was tabled, and then went through second reading and a public hearing for consideration in June 2026.

silver-cliff/3.title: Zoning code rewrite and Title 16 changes
silver-cliff/3.summary: The Planning Commission has been working on a municipal code update through a rezoning committee and on Title 16 Zoning. The Board had a first reading of Ordinance 03-2026 amending Title 16 in June, and discussed state wildfire-resiliency building code requirements for the wildland-urban interface.

silver-cliff/4.title: Dutch Pantry additional parking and rezoning request
silver-cliff/4.summary: Matt Hershberger asked about buying land for additional employee and customer parking for Dutch Pantry. The property is zoned R3 and would need rezoning to B1 commercial.

silver-cliff/5.title: 2027 budget and budget workshops
silver-cliff/5.summary: The proposed 2027 budget was presented on October 6, 2026 with no discussion or decisions, and the board set about scheduling budget workshops. The Altitude Fitness funding request is to be taken up at the workshop.

silver-cliff/6.title: Board meeting quorum and attendance rules (Ordinance 02-2026)
silver-cliff/6.summary: After discussion of poor meeting attendance, the Board moved Ordinance 02-2026 amending Sec. 2-2-90 on meeting quorum through readings and a public hearing in June 2026. Trustees discussed requiring notice to the Town Clerk of absences.

silver-cliff/7.title: CloudBreak decommissioning bond
silver-cliff/7.summary: The board considered approving the CloudBreak decommissioning bond in April 2026. The documents give no further detail.

silver-cliff/8.title: Cemetery regulations update (Ordinance 05-2026)
silver-cliff/8.summary: The board had a first reading of Ordinance 05-2026 amending the 2021 cemetery regulations in fall 2026.

silver-cliff/9.title: Grants: Black Hills Energy and incentive award
silver-cliff/9.summary: The town received a grant award from Black Hills Energy and considered Resolution 05-2026 to accept it, plus Resolution 04-2026 accepting another grant. In October it considered Resolution 08-2026 on an incentive award grant.

silver-plume/0.title: Camping ordinance for Silver Plume town limits
silver-plume/0.summary: Camping within town limits is not defined in the Land Use Code (Ordinance 340) as allowed or prohibited. A resident asked for an ordinance after reports of overnight activity near an apartment building, with people looking for bathrooms and residents feeling unsafe. Staff will gather model ordinances, and a public hearing on a camping ordinance is on the Sept. 14 agenda.

silver-plume/1.title: 2027 budget and water and sewer rate increases
silver-plume/1.summary: The Budget Committee began 2027 budget work in August, with work sessions on Sept. 5 and Oct. 3 and a proposed budget on the table. The preliminary budget is due to the Board by October and the final by Dec. 31, 2026. Staff say water and sewer rates will need to rise because those fees have not increased in many years.

silver-plume/2.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and Ordinance 359
silver-plume/2.summary: The Town is considering adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code through Ordinance 359. A public hearing for second and final reading is on the Sept. 14 agenda.

silver-plume/3.title: Main Street sidewalk concerns
silver-plume/3.summary: A resident raised problems with the sidewalks on Main Street between Jefferson and Silver Street, including a dumpster along the sidewalk. Sidewalk work is on the Town's priority list but comes after a water treatment tank repair, and the Road and Bridge committee is to discuss it.
silver-plume/3.where: Main Street between Jefferson and Silver Street

silver-plume/4.title: Cemetery forms, expansion and cleanup
silver-plume/4.summary: The Town reviewed new cemetery forms, including a contract replacing the old deed, an open/close request, a monument application and a transfer request. Officials discussed opening a new section for plot sales, possibly a non-resident section at market value, extending the access road, cleanup logistics and the cemetery gate.

silver-plume/5.title: Town shop electrical and door quotes
silver-plume/5.summary: The Board continued discussing quotes for electrical work and doors at the Town shop, with one quote around $20,500. The Clerk has contracted services from two firms, PME and MBIE.

snowmass-village/0.title: Ritz Carlton (Viewline) redevelopment sketch plan
snowmass-village/0.summary: Elevate Snowmass, LLC's sketch plan would rebuild the Ritz Carlton lodge (about 167 units), redevelop the Wildwood area with about 125 workforce housing units, and add a 252-space subgrade parking garage. The Planning Commission has held several lodge, housing and conference/commercial discussions and a draft resolution is set for Oct. 7. Residents including Alan May raised concerns about height, massing, traffic, parking, deliveries and pedestrian safety on Fall Lane. The Part-Time Resident Advisory Board worried about overdevelopment like Base Village.

snowmass-village/1.title: Employee housing mitigation rate and nexus study update
snowmass-village/1.summary: After raising the housing mitigation rate from 60% to 100% (Ordinance No. 1, 2026), Council is reviewing an EPS study of employee generation rates and fee-in-lieu. Council generally agreed to update rates, add residential remodels as an activity requiring mitigation, and use a fee based on $945/SF for a 750 sf unit at 1.75 employees per unit. It asked for more information on residential operations and maintenance employees. A housing mitigation ordinance first reading is on the horizon.

snowmass-village/2.title: Draw Site workforce housing project
snowmass-village/2.summary: Council reviewed next steps as owner of the Draw Site workforce housing project, which carries $76.1 million in construction in the 2027 budget. Council was to give staff direction on next steps on Oct. 19.

snowmass-village/3.title: 2027 town budget
snowmass-village/3.summary: Staff presented a proposed 2027 budget described as exceptionally tight after the low-snow 2026 ski season, with capital project funds depleted. Total spending includes $107.96 million in capital projects. Council reviews on Oct. 12 and 19, with adoption by resolution expected Nov. 4. The Financial Advisory Board and Tourism board weighed in, and Tourism projected $14.8 million in marketing and lodging tax revenue.

snowmass-village/4.title: Cavern Springs mobile home park funding and Workforce Housing Advisory Board
snowmass-village/4.summary: Council took up Ordinance 15 appropriating funds for the Cavern Springs Mobile Home Park, plus Resolution 23 on an IGA, housing covenants and a grant agreement. It also considered Ordinance 16 creating a Workforce Housing Advisory Board; both were set for second reading Oct. 5.

snowmass-village/5.title: Daly Lane employee housing sketch plan
snowmass-village/5.summary: The Snowmass Village Community Foundation applied to build workforce housing on the Daly Lane SRA site, with a joint Council and Planning Commission sketch plan review on Aug. 17. Feedback from the March pre-sketch meeting included adding on-site parking because town lots are insufficient.

snowmass-village/6.title: Snowmass Mall transit center project
snowmass-village/6.summary: A possible new transit center at the Snowmass Mall is estimated at $42M to $60M depending on scope and parking. The Part-Time Resident Advisory Board broadly supports improvements but questioned cost, funding partners, and timing given the Ritz redevelopment, and prefers modest targeted upgrades. It planned a letter to Council.

snowmass-village/7.title: Wildfire mitigation and Fire Authority agreement
snowmass-village/7.summary: Council considered a memorandum of understanding with Roaring Fork Fire Rescue Authority on wildfire mitigation. A rebate program (about $1,000 for homeowners) would be administered by the RFV Wildfire Collaborative since the fire district lacks capacity for assessments.

snowmass-village/8.title: Pesticide and noxious weed spraying on trails
snowmass-village/8.summary: The Environmental Advisory Board raised concerns about trail spraying and lack of signage. Council held a pesticide application discussion on Sept. 8, and parks staff promised a more detailed noxious weed spraying plan.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board

snowmass-village/9.title: Highway 82 congestion fee proposal
snowmass-village/9.summary: A presentation outlined a plan to cut Highway 82 traffic using incentives, roadway improvements, enhanced transit and a phased congestion-reduction fee on up-valley trips. The fee would raise an estimated $10–20 million per year; it is described as an initial strategy open to feedback. The EOTC also held budget and workplan hearings and debated broadening use of transit tax funds.

snowmass-village/10.title: Entryway roundabout project
snowmass-village/10.summary: Council asked the Snowmass Arts Advisory Board for recommendations on the Entryway Roundabout project, with a joint meeting planned.

snowmass-village/11.title: Town Park playground renovation
snowmass-village/11.summary: The Parks board is working with a vendor on a playground renovation capital project, with discussion of theming such as the Mt Daly stripe, nature or hot air balloons.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board
Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board
Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board

snowmass-village/12.title: Liquor licensee sales tax delinquency hearing
snowmass-village/12.summary: The Liquor Authority scheduled a show cause hearing over Il Poggio's delinquent sales tax payments, which could lead to suspension or revocation of its license.

sources.body: Liquor Authority Hearing & Local Marijuana Licensing Authority Hearing

starkville/0.title: Crypto currency data center special exception on Industrial Park Road
starkville/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission held a public hearing on SE 26-08, a request to use a site in an industrial zone as a "Data Center - Crypto Currency Generation Facility." The site is on the east side of Industrial Park Road, about 350 feet south of Miley Road. The documents do not state the outcome.
starkville/0.where: Industrial Park Road, about 350 feet south of Miley Road

starkville/1.title: Chronic nuisance property ordinance
starkville/1.summary: The Board of Aldermen called a first public hearing on adopting a chronic nuisance property ordinance on Aug. 4. A second public hearing and vote on adoption were on the Sept. 15 agenda.

starkville/2.title: Leisure and Recreation District ordinance amendment
starkville/2.summary: The board scheduled hearings to amend the Leisure and Recreation District ordinance to add specific language. A first hearing was called in August and a second hearing was on the Sept. 15 agenda.

starkville/3.title: 2026-2027 city budget, tax millage and pay raises
starkville/3.summary: Aldermen called public hearings on the 2026-2027 budget and tax millage in August. They also took up proposed 2027 budgets for outside agencies, including the Oktibbeha County Economic Development Authority. Pay raises for all departments were on the Sept. 15 agenda.

starkville/4.title: Jackson 128 mixed-use development downtown
starkville/4.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission heard SE 26-06 for a mixed-use development at 128 South Jackson Street. The applicant sought five special exceptions, including a fifth story. A citizen, Steve Langston, spoke in favor.

starkville/5.title: Sterling Ridge phased preliminary plat
starkville/5.summary: The Planning Commission and then the Board of Aldermen considered PP 26-01, a phased preliminary plat for the Sterling Ridge subdivision. It is at the southwest corner of Mockingbird Road and Highway 182.

starkville/6.title: Airport runway extension and hangar grants
starkville/6.summary: The board took up state matching grants and FAA projects to extend the runway, taxiway and lighting. Later items covered change orders and grant applications for Corporate Hangar #3 and Phase III of the runway extension and overlay.

starkville/7.title: Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East multi-dwelling development
starkville/7.summary: The Board of Adjustments considered a variance (VA 26-07) and the Planning Commission a special exception (SE 26-11) for a multi-dwelling residential development near Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East.
starkville/7.where: Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East

starkville/8.title: Hotel development parking reduction on Mill Street
starkville/8.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled a hearing on SE 26-12, a request to reduce minimum parking for a proposed hotel east of Mill Street, directly east of the Cotton Mill Road intersection.
starkville/8.where: Mill Street near Cotton Mill Road

starkville/9.title: Skate park construction
starkville/9.summary: A skate park item was on the Sept. 15 agenda. On Oct. 6 the board considered a low quote of $46,190.78 from Econ Construction for skate park work.

starkville/10.title: Fire Department staffing and restructuring plan
starkville/10.summary: The board considered hiring three additional firefighters and approving a Fire Department staffing and organizational restructuring plan.

starkville/11.title: Southwire rail spur crossing easements and CC Clark Road
starkville/11.summary: The board considered crossing easements over the rail spur to Southwire for a roadway connection to CC Clark Road.
starkville/11.where: CC Clark Road / Southwire rail spur

starkville/12.title: Extension of tourism and restaurant/hotel taxes
starkville/12.summary: The board considered a resolution asking the 2027 Mississippi Legislature to extend the economic development, tourism and convention taxes on non-alcoholic beverages and the hotel/motel tax.

starkville/13.title: Electric Department projects and rates
starkville/13.summary: A Sept. 11 work session included a presentation on electric department projects and rates.

starkville/14.title: Police department to sell abandoned-property firearms to buy sighting and light devices
starkville/14.summary: On the September 1, 2026 Board of Aldermen agenda, the Starkville Police Department asked for approval to convert abandoned property firearms into sales so it could purchase sighting and light devices. The firearms would go to The Southern Connection, which gave the higher of two bids.

steamboat-springs/0.title: 2027 city budget and 6-year capital improvements program
steamboat-springs/0.summary: Council held a 6-year Capital Improvements Program work session on Sept. 8 and a 2027 budget retreat on Oct. 6 that included general fund operations, the capital projects fund and a public comment slot. On Oct. 20 the 2027 budget ordinance came up for first reading, along with an eighth supplemental appropriation for 2026.

steamboat-springs/1.title: Slate Creek / Brown Ranch development and annexation
steamboat-springs/1.summary: The Slate Creek Steering Committee met Oct. 2 and Oct. 9 to discuss the Slate Creek development roadmap and the phases of the development process. Agendas tie the work to the Brown Ranch plan and annexation proposal and invite public comment.

steamboat-springs/2.title: Base area redevelopment, URA budget and Gondola Transit Center agreement
steamboat-springs/2.summary: The Redevelopment Authority reviewed its 2026 project activity plan and a preliminary 2027 budget, then moved to adopt its budget on Oct. 20. An executive session covered negotiations on the Gondola Transit Center and public improvements with Steamboat Ski & Resort Corporation. The advisory committee tracked Complete Streets Segment 4B Phase II and Mount Werner Road/Circle.

steamboat-springs/3.title: The Forge at Burgess Creek preliminary plat
steamboat-springs/3.summary: Planning Commission reviewed a preliminary plat and major variance for 2.32 acres of unplatted land in the 1900 block of Burgess Creek Road on Oct. 8. Council then took up a resolution approving the plat and variance on its Oct. 20 consent calendar.

steamboat-springs/4.title: Child care centers in commercial zones code change
steamboat-springs/4.summary: A Community Development Code text amendment would allow large and small child care centers in commercial zones. Planning Commission heard it Oct. 8 and an ordinance amending the code went to Council for first reading on Oct. 20.

steamboat-springs/5.title: Automated license plate readers update
steamboat-springs/5.summary: Council held a work session on Sept. 8 to get an update on the city's automated license plate readers, with public comment accepted.

steamboat-springs/6.title: Yampa Valley regional transit sales tax ballot question
steamboat-springs/6.summary: Council considered a resolution supporting the Yampa Valley Regional Transportation Authority ballot question for a one-half percent sales tax.

steamboat-springs/7.title: Crowell-Marshall House permanent placement and Rodeo Grounds tax refund
steamboat-springs/7.summary: Council was asked to direct staff to approve a building permit for the permanent placement of the Crowell-Marshall House, following Ordinance 3036 that allowed its temporary storage. The Historic Preservation Commission also took up a sales tax refund certification for rehabilitation projects at the Rodeo Grounds.

steamboat-springs/8.title: Water supply element and downtown plan text amendment
steamboat-springs/8.summary: Planning Commission held a policy work session on Oct. 26 to hear the Water Supply Element and a text amendment implementing the Downtown Plan.

steamboat-springs/9.title: Easement vacations and rezoning ordinances
steamboat-springs/9.summary: Council moved ordinances vacating a portion of an easement, a water and sewer line and fire hydrant easement, and rezoning lots through readings in September. An ordinance for a Yampa River riprap easement agreement followed on Oct. 20.

steamboat-springs/10.title: Golf course 2027 rates and overhead allocation
steamboat-springs/10.summary: The Golf Management Committee discussed allocated overhead and 2027 golf rates on Sept. 23.

sterling/0.title: Rezoning 917 Hamilton Street from R-3 to Community Business
sterling/0.summary: J-Tab Rentals, LLC asked to change the zoning at 917 Hamilton Street from High Density Residential (R-3) to Community Business (CB). The Planning Commission reviewed it in August. Council took first reading of Ordinance No. 10 on Aug. 25 and held the second-reading public hearing on Oct. 13, with no public comment.

sterling/1.title: Allowing veterinary clinics as a conditional use (Copper Gate Animal Clinic)
sterling/1.summary: Porche Robison wants to open the Copper Gate Animal Clinic at 625-627 Holly Drive, but veterinary clinics are not permitted in the Medical Services zone. The Planning Commission suggested a map or text amendment. Council took up Ordinance No. 8 to allow veterinary clinics as a conditional use, with first reading Aug. 11 and a second-reading public hearing Sept. 8.

sterling/2.title: Proposed street improvement sales and use tax on the Nov. 3 ballot
sterling/2.summary: Council considered Resolution 8-2-26 to refer a 1% sales and use tax question to the Nov. 3, 2026 election. Residents John Tyson and Lee Roth spoke about the proposed street improvement tax, asking for more information, raising a sunset clause and exceptions, and asking that the $400,000 already budgeted for street repair be combined with any new tax revenue.

sterling/3.title: 2027 city budget
sterling/3.summary: A tentative budget workshop was set for Sept. 25 at 8:00 AM. Council held a public hearing on the proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 27.

sterling/4.title: Waterline replacement projects
sterling/4.summary: Council accepted a bid from Hard Rock Civil, LLC for the 2026 Waterline Replacement Project #26-001. It later approved a change order with Hard Rock Civil for the North 10th Avenue waterline project, and a change order with Concrete Specialties and Utilities Construction for the 2025 Waterline Replacement Project #25-006.

sterling/5.summary: Council considered Resolution 9-3-26 approving a professional engineering design services agreement for renovating and expanding the Police Department Armory.

sterling/6.title: DOLA grant to update the city Master Plan
sterling/6.summary: Council considered Resolution 9-4-26 authorizing a funding request to the Colorado Department of Local Affairs Local Planning Capacity Grant Program to update the city's Master Plan.

sterling/7.title: Hotel Tax Fund spending: holiday garland and downtown
sterling/7.summary: Council considered spending up to $45,000 from the Hotel Tax Fund on lighted holiday garland wraps and a storage container for West Main Street. A separate item considered up to $10,000 from the fund. A council member also asked for an update on the downtown sidewalks.

sterling/8.title: Resident concerns: chicken permits, shipping containers, speeding, loud mufflers
sterling/8.summary: Lisa LeFevre asked Council to revisit the chicken code and clarify the building permit process. Richard Bedford said the new shipping container rules have unintended problems with community business zoning. Residents also raised loud mufflers at night and speeding near Pioneer Park, and the city manager said he would pass the muffler complaint to police.

sterling/9.title: Sober living conditional use and garage conversion on McKinley Street
sterling/9.summary: The Planning Commission was to review a conditional use request from Milestone Community Wellness to operate a sober living facility, and a variance request from Jesse Mull to convert a garage to a home at 728 McKinley Street.

sterling/10.title: Marijuana regulations discussion at Planning Commission
sterling/10.summary: Colin Mudd of Jay's Downtown Dispensary discussed marijuana regulations with commissioners. They agreed to table the discussion to give dispensary owners time.

sterling/11.title: Intergovernmental agreement with Logan County and radio station lease
sterling/11.summary: Council considered Resolution 7-5-26 approving an intergovernmental agreement with Logan County. It also considered Resolution 9-1-26 leasing city-owned land in the Platte Addition to Media Logic Radio, LLC.
