summit-county/0.title: Quikrete concrete and asphalt batch plant appeal at 28755 State Hwy 9
summit-county/0.summary: Commissioners heard an appeal of the Lower Blue Planning Commission decision on PLN26-004, a Class 4 conditional use permit for milling and concrete and asphalt batch plant operations on a 151-acre portion of a 605-acre A-1 parcel. Public comments, a stormwater plan, and a landscape plan were in the packet. The documents do not state the outcome.

summit-county/1.title: Verizon Wireless tower appeal at 6631 Heeney Road
summit-county/1.summary: Commissioners held a public hearing on an appeal of the Lower Blue Planning Commission decision on PLN26-009 and PLN26-010, a conditional use permit and site plan for a new Verizon Wireless telecommunication facility. Public comments received through 9/23/26 were in the packet. The documents do not state the outcome.

summit-county/2.title: 2027 county budget
summit-county/2.summary: The county reviewed the 2027 draft budget across work sessions and a regular meeting. Sessions covered the Assessor, Capital Projects, Road & Bridge, Lodging Tax, Coroner, and Human Services budgets, plus a District Attorney budget amendment. A public hearing for comment on the proposed 2027 budget was set for 10/27.

summit-county/3.title: Purchase of historic mining claims and mill sites
summit-county/3.summary: Commissioners were asked to exercise option agreements to buy the Pirate, Canadian, and Manerva mill sites in the Snake River Basin. They were also asked to exercise an option for the Summit Gulch claims in the Upper Blue Basin.
summit-county/3.where: Snake River Basin and Upper Blue Basin

summit-county/4.title: Soda Creek Proposition 123 housing credits IGA with Keystone
summit-county/4.summary: The county discussed in work session and then considered an intergovernmental agreement with the Town of Keystone on allocating Proposition 123 housing units and credits for the Soda Creek project.

summit-county/5.title: Positions on November 2026 ballot measures
summit-county/5.summary: Commissioners considered resolutions supporting Amendment 87, Proposition 137, Proposition NN and Referred Measure 4A. They also considered resolutions opposing Amendments 81, 82 and 85 and Proposition 136.

summit-county/6.title: SCRAP fee analysis and rate study
summit-county/6.summary: A special work session reviewed a rate study and fee analysis for SCRAP. A rate study Q&A and comparison with other agency rate factors followed on 10/27.

summit-county/7.title: County Road 506 full maintenance
summit-county/7.summary: Commissioners considered a resolution on whether the county should provide full maintenance on CR 506 for 2026.

summit-county/8.title: Background checks for massage facility personnel
summit-county/8.summary: Commissioners considered a proposed resolution requiring background checks for massage facility personnel.

summit-county/9.title: Head Start and community services grants
summit-county/9.summary: The county considered the Head Start continuation application for 2027 and a supplemental Head Start grant application. It also considered the Community Services Block Grant 3-year community needs assessment.

summit-county/10.title: Property tax abatements for Highlands Riverfront tracts
summit-county/10.summary: Commissioners considered abatement requests on 2025 property taxes for Highlands Riverfront Subdivision future development tracts A, T and U.

superior/0.title: Marshall Fire Remembrance Project and 5-year anniversary event
superior/0.summary: The Town is designing a Marshall Fire memorial with a place to gather, pet remembrance and dispersed elements. Colorado Gives is acting as fiscal sponsor, and Louisville is committing $25,000. On Oct 26 Council took up agreements with Colorado Gives and Make Philanthropy Work as fundraising advisor. A resilience celebration is planned for Dec 18 at the Community Center.

sources.body: Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)

superior/1.title: 2027 budget, fee schedule and property tax levy
superior/1.summary: Council held budget review sessions in Aug-Sept and on Oct 12 adopted the 2027 budget, fee schedule and property tax levy, along with budgets for the SMID, SURA and Metro District No. 1. Mid-year reports showed vehicle use tax down 17.1%, permit revenue down about 31% and sales tax roughly flat.

superior/2.title: Zaharias property PUD amendment (7500 S 88th Street)
superior/2.summary: Planning Commission held a hearing on the Twenty-Fifth Amendment to the Rock Creek Ranch PUD for the Zaharias property, proposed by Garrett Companies. Resident Natasha Flyer commented. A motion to recommend approval was made, and Council held a public hearing on Sept 14.

superior/3.title: Water conservation, turf reduction and water supply
superior/3.summary: A draft water conservation plan was put out for survey, and Council adopted a Waterwise Landscape Transformation Roadmap and a non-functional turf reduction prioritization tool. Council also approved a Northern Water Southern Water Supply Project allotment amendment. Water usage is up 17.4% in 2026, including a 9.5% rate increase.

superior/4.title: Pirate Park playground renovation
superior/4.summary: Council approved a design-build contract with Altitude Recreation for the Pirate Park playground renovation. The Parks and Recreation Advisory Committee and Council have received project updates.

superior/5.title: Coyote Ridge trails, prairie dog and wildlife management plans
superior/5.summary: The Open Space Advisory Committee reviewed Pointe Strategies' draft Coyote Ridge trail recommendations, a prairie dog management plan, a town wildlife management plan, wildfire mitigation and the open space master plan. The master plan review is planned for October. A CPW trail grant submission and PARC support for the McCaslin multi-use trail grant also came up.
superior/5.where: Coyote Ridge and Town open space

superior/6.title: 2024 International Fire Code adoption
superior/6.summary: Council took up first reading of an ordinance adopting the 2024 International Fire Code, with a presentation from Mountain View Fire Protection District's Deputy Chief. Second reading was continued and Ordinance 80 was approved Sept 28.

superior/7.title: Town building physical security assessment
superior/7.summary: Wold Architects & Engineers presented a physical security assessment of Town buildings and offices to Council.

superior/8.title: 88th Street bicycle and pedestrian improvements
superior/8.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement with CDOT for the 88th Street Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvements Project. Construction updates on Rock Creek Parkway, the Community Center and pools were also given.

superior/9.title: Boulder County child care mill levy and co-responder program
superior/9.summary: Council discussed the Boulder County Child Care Investment Initiative and approved a resolution supporting the county's early childhood care and education mill levy increase ballot measure. Council also heard a presentation on the Boulder County co-responder program.

superior/10.title: Proposition 123 housing agreement and affordable housing funding
superior/10.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement with Boulder County Housing to implement Proposition 123. The Town also received a $1M Boulder County grant for affordable and attainable housing, and approved a rebate agreement with the Impact Development Fund.

superior/11.title: Park spraying concerns and Vargas landscape maintenance contract
superior/11.summary: A resident raised concerns at ACES about herbicide spraying in a park near a pond. At the Oct 26 Council meeting speakers backed the Vargas landscape maintenance contract.

superior/12.title: ARTery public art and CAPS purchases
superior/12.summary: The arts committee is expanding the ARTery through Circle Park with benches and utility box art. It is seeking Council approval of purchases of about $12,000 for art and two swing benches at $12,000 each, which Council took up on Oct 26.

sources.body: Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)

teller-county/0.title: Ordinance 23: short-term rental regulation and tax administration
teller-county/0.summary: The commissioners took up Ordinance 23 on regulating short-term rentals in unincorporated Teller County, with first reading on Aug. 6 and second reading scheduled Sept. 10. On Sept. 24 they were to ratify an agreement with Neumo Group, LLC for short-term rental tax and license administration. Residents have raised STR concerns in Four Mile, including STR owners taking seats on HOA boards.

teller-county/1.title: Quantum Tech compliance agreement over revoked permit at 10180 West
teller-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission revoked a 1995 conditional use permit for a construction storage yard on Quantum Tech's property on May 12, 2026, and the Board of Adjustment took up the matter on July 9. A compliance agreement gives Quantum 90 days to remove the non-permitted operations while office use continues, and any future permit would need a new application. The commissioners were asked to approve it Sept. 2 and ratify it Sept. 10.

teller-county/2.title: Cripple Creek & Victor Gold Mining Amendment 14
teller-county/2.summary: Commissioners held a work session on Oct. 27 about the mine's Mining Development Plan Amendment 14. It covers a proposed employee parking lot along County Road 821 and a temporary unpaved access road built in Grassy Valley. State regulators conditionally approved it on Oct. 1, 2025, and county staff recommend approval with conditions. Public comments are included in the packet.
teller-county/2.where: Cripple Creek Mining Overlay District, County Road 821 and Grassy Valley

teller-county/3.title: NETCO impact fee study and housing costs
teller-county/3.summary: The county received an impact fee study from NETCO and is seeking public comment on the proposed fees, which would help fund fire districts. One commissioner warned the fees will raise housing costs, while acknowledging the fire districts' need for funding.

teller-county/4.title: 2026 budget amendments and 2027 proposed budget
teller-county/4.summary: Commissioners held budget work sessions in August and September, covering the capital plan. They presented the 2027 proposed budget on Oct. 8, and passed resolutions amending the 2026 General, Jail, Social Services and Road and Bridge budgets. Another amendment was on the Oct. 22 agenda, and the 2027 insurance renewal was discussed Oct. 27.

teller-county/5.title: Stage II fire ban eased to Stage I
teller-county/5.summary: Teller County remained under a Stage II fire ban during fire season. On Sept. 2 the commissioners considered a resolution to move to Stage I, and the Sept. 10 agenda included ratifying it. The Forest Service has lifted its recreational shooting restriction.

teller-county/6.title: Teller County building code and contractor license changes
teller-county/6.summary: A work session on Aug. 25 covered proposed changes to the county building code. These include contractor license categories and fees, such as $50 specialty licenses and $150 licenses for septic (OWTS) cleaner and related contractors.

teller-county/7.title: Jail underground repair contract increase
teller-county/7.summary: A change order raised the Mid-Colorado Construction contract for jail underground repair investigation and logistics from a not-to-exceed $40,000 to $100,000 and extended it to June 30, 2027. It was on the Oct. 8 agenda for ratification.

teller-county/8.title: Lot line adjustments: Moore/Corporate Wellness and Pollock-Kenyon
teller-county/8.summary: Commissioners reviewed two amended final plats with staff recommending approval. One adjusts the line between Lots 21 and 22 in Ranch Resorts of Colorado Subdivision No. 2 to extend power. The other adjusts the line between Lots 3 and 4 in Highland Meadows Filing 1, where a residence encroached.
teller-county/8.where: Ranch Resorts of Colorado No. 2; Highland Meadows 1 (Floresta Drive and Floresta Place)

teller-county/9.title: Victor water pipe leak and road funding (Initiative 175)
teller-county/9.summary: A water pipe leak left the City of Victor without water. It has been fixed and the city is looking for grants. Commissioners also discussed Initiative 175 and House Bill 260, which would require highway funds to go to roads and bridges, and a possible state ballot measure on TABOR surplus.

teller-county/10.title: Public health, childcare facility rules and emergency programs
teller-county/10.summary: Public health staff reported a rise in suicides among men ages 45 to 64 and updates on the Rural Health Transformation Grant and a non-emergent oxygen program. Reflective address signs were funded by grant. The board also discussed childcare facilities and Special Use Permits, and said some recent public information on the regulations was inaccurate.

telluride/0.title: Carhenge and Shandoka redevelopment projects
telluride/0.summary: The Carhenge Redevelopment Project (Lots 34 and 34B, Backman Village) has three large-scale applications for Buildings A-E before HARC, continued from July and August and back on Sept. 30. The Shandoka Lot Redevelopment (Lot L, Backman Village) has a preliminary PUD before P&Z and a large-scale application before HARC, both continued without discussion, with HARC pushed to Nov. 18. On Oct. 27 Council also considered a resolution on a preliminary subdivision consolidating Lots 34 and 34B.
telluride/0.where: Backman Village (Carhenge parking lot and Shandoka)

telluride/1.title: Affordable housing waitlist and Housing Authority policies
telluride/1.summary: The Housing Authority and its subcommittee are reworking the employee rental housing waitlist rules in sections 105 and 106.1, after a recent suspension of the waitlist. They also adopted a policy on primary residency for children of multiple custodial parents, are considering a partial 2027 rental rate increase, and are amending deed restrictions on town-built units at 215 E. Colorado Ave. Bedroom size standards and exceptions for households in multi-bed units are also under discussion.

telluride/2.title: 2027 town budget, fees and rates
telluride/2.summary: Council held a budget workshop on Oct. 13 covering enterprise funds, open space, affordable housing and 12 smaller funds requesting $12.11M in revenue and $16.11M in spending. The Open Space set-aside of $4.79M would be drawn down by $4.25M, the Transportation Fund needs a $290,000 larger transfer, and lodgers' tax is budgeted to rebound. A water and sewer rate study and draft 2027 fee schedule were also presented, and adoption is set for Nov. 17. An ordinance to suspend part of the real estate transfer tax for the 2027 budget year had first reading Oct. 27.

sources.body: Commission for Community Assistance, Arts & Special Events

telluride/3.title: License plate reader (Flock) cameras
telluride/3.summary: Town Council discussed automated license plate reader cameras, including Flock, on Oct. 6 with a staff memo. A resident, McKenzie, submitted public comment.

telluride/4.title: Ethics code and code of conduct for councilmembers
telluride/4.summary: After an ethics complaint against a councilmember's conduct at a public meeting, the Ethics Commission weighed adding a code of conduct to the ethics code or adopting a stand-alone one. Council held second reading of an ordinance amending the ethics code general guidelines (section 2-4-30) on Oct. 6.

telluride/5.title: Telluride school district employee housing
telluride/5.summary: P&Z held a work session on proposed employee housing at the northwest corner of the Telluride Middle-High School site, under an intergovernmental agreement with the school district. A separate work session covered potential Land Use Code amendments.
telluride/5.where: Telluride Middle-High School site, northwest corner

telluride/6.title: Gondola replacement project funding
telluride/6.summary: SMART considered an FY27 amendment to the Gondola Project Development IGA and an update on the gondola replacement. Town Council was asked to approve the Fourth Supplement to the cost-sharing agreement for the 2027 gondola development budget.

sources.body: San Miguel Authority for Regional Transportation

telluride/7.title: Two-night concert proposed for Town Park
telluride/7.summary: Council discussed a proposed major two-night concert in Town Park on Oct. 27 and reviewed 2026 special events on town property. Combined public comment was included in the packet.

telluride/8.title: Campground and shower fee increases for 2027
telluride/8.summary: The Parks & Recreation Commission considered 2027 Town Park campground fee increases of $2-$5 per night (about 8% average), projecting $203,304 in revenue versus $192,866 budgeted for 2026. Shower fees would rise to bring in $62,500, up 25% from $50,000. The commission also discussed the 5-year capital fund and Town Park Oval improvements.

telluride/9.title: Ban on fuel-burning landscape equipment and Climate Action Plan update
telluride/9.summary: The Ecology Commission discussed a draft ordinance banning gas-powered landscaping equipment, a step called for in the 2022 Climate Action Plan, and will connect with town staff who use such equipment. It is also working on the 2027 Climate Action Plan update and a regional dark sky initiative.

telluride/10.title: Historic review of pergola, 510 W Columbia and other properties
telluride/10.summary: HARC considered a pergola built without a permit on a rated structure near the historic depot at Swede Finn Hall, with staff not supporting approval. Other items include payment-in-lieu of parking and a lot line vacation at 510 W Columbia/129 N Townsend, 208 S Fir, Primrose Lane, 461 Dakota, 448 Tomboy Road, and a Phoenix Market extension. The Stender residence appeal on North Aspen Street was continued.
telluride/10.where: 510 W Columbia Ave, 208 S Fir St, Primrose Lane, Dakota Ave

telluride/11.title: Telluride Energy Mitigation Program updates
telluride/11.summary: Council had first reading of an ordinance amending the Telluride Energy Mitigation Program (TEMP) in municipal code section 15-9-40.

thornton/0.title: Data center moratorium discussion
thornton/0.summary: City Council discussed a possible data center moratorium at the Aug. 25 council update and again at the Sept. 1 planning session, with a data center presentation each time. The documents do not state a decision.

thornton/1.title: Creekside Gardens Annexation and zoning
thornton/1.summary: Council held a public hearing on Aug. 25 on annexing about 26 acres at the southwest corner of East 140th Avenue and Washington Street into Ward 4. The second reading of the annexation and of the zoning amendment with a development plan followed on Sept. 8.
thornton/1.where: Southwest corner of East 140th Avenue and Washington Street

thornton/2.title: Bellflower Annexation, zoning and site plan
thornton/2.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled on Oct. 20 to hear the annexation of about 39 acres near East 120th/140th Avenue and Holly Street. The same hearing covered a zoning amendment and a conceptual site plan for a residential development on about 38 acres. Council also designated an annexation plan for land in Adams and Weld Counties on Oct. 13.
thornton/2.where: East of Holly Street, north of East 140th Avenue

thornton/3.title: Welby Station zoning amendment
thornton/3.summary: A zoning amendment for about 55 acres at the northeast and northwest corners of East 88th Avenue and Welby Road went to the Planning Commission on Sept. 15. It then went to a Council public hearing on Oct. 13.

thornton/4.title: 2027 city budget, pay plans and tax levy
thornton/4.summary: Council reviewed the preliminary 2027 budget in September planning sessions. On Oct. 27 it held public hearings on adopting the 2027 budget, pay plans and appropriations, and a first reading of the property tax levy. Related budgets were also on the agenda for TASHCO, the Thornton Development Authority and the 136th Avenue General Improvement District.

thornton/5.title: 2027 water, sewer and stormwater rates and water revenue bonds
thornton/5.summary: Council reviewed proposed 2027 utility rate and fee adjustments for water, sewer and stormwater, effective Jan. 1, 2027. It also had a first reading of an ordinance authorizing Series 2026 Water Enterprise Revenue Bonds.

thornton/6.title: Interim City Attorney and City Attorney recruitment
thornton/6.summary: Council held several executive sessions in August on interviewing internal candidates and negotiating a potential employment agreement for the Interim City Attorney position. In October it met on selecting a vendor for the City Attorney recruitment and on performance of the interim attorney, municipal judge and city manager.

thornton/7.title: Parks and Recreation Master Plan and Arts and Culture Master Plan
thornton/7.summary: The Parks, Recreation and Community Programs Master Plan and the Arts and Culture Master Plan 2026-2030 were presented on Sept. 8. Council considered a resolution adopting the Parks and Recreation Master Plan on Sept. 22.

thornton/8.title: Parterre subdivision legal strategy
thornton/8.summary: Council met in executive session on Sept. 8 for legal advice and negotiator instructions about developing the Parterre subdivision.

thornton/9.title: Small-lot housing and residential design standards
thornton/9.summary: Council held a planning session on Oct. 20 on residential housing and design standards, including small-lot housing. The Planning Commission also took up housekeeping amendments to the development code in Chapter 18.

thornton/10.title: Station area plans and Thornton Parkway multimodal path
thornton/10.summary: Council discussed visioning for the York at 144th and North Thornton at CO 7 station areas. The Thornton Development Authority took up conveying property to the city for the Thornton Parkway multimodal path from I-25 to Grant Street.
thornton/10.where: Thornton Parkway, I-25 to Grant Street; 144th and CO 7 station areas

thornton/11.title: Marijuana licensing code amendments
thornton/11.summary: Council reviewed potential amendments to the city code on marijuana licensing at the Oct. 27 council update.

thornton/12.title: Redevelopment Request for Qualifications negotiations
thornton/12.summary: Council met in executive session on Sept. 22 and 29 to set negotiation strategy on responses to the city's Request for Qualifications for a redevelopment project.

thornton/13.title: Old Hire Fire Pension cost-of-living request
thornton/13.summary: The Old Hire Fire Pension Board asked that a cost-of-living adjustment be included in the 2027 budget recommendation. Council reviewed the request at the Aug. 18 planning session.

timnath/0.title: Peanut Park (Timnath Ranch North Park) master plan and $6 million funding
timnath/0.summary: The PROST Committee reviewed the master planning process for Peanut Park, including a resident poll on amenities and challenges such as drainage and the park's size. By October the draft master plan from Ayres and Associates was on the agenda, and the five-year Capital Improvement Plan includes $6 million for next year, which is not guaranteed until the budget is approved. The park will need to be built in phases.

timnath/1.title: 2027 Town budget and five-year capital plan
timnath/1.summary: Town Council held work sessions on the 2027 draft budget, which includes a five-year capital improvement plan and cash flow projections tied to the Strategic Plan. Projects listed include a parking lot reconfiguration at the police department, a parks maintenance facility, and security cameras at Timnath Community Park. The August compensation study findings are also expected to feed into the budget.

timnath/2.title: Timnath Landing GID bond issuance (Series 2026A and 2026B)
timnath/2.summary: The Timnath Landing General Improvement District Board took up an ordinance authorizing Limited Tax General Obligation Bonds, Series 2026A and subordinate Series 2026B. The bonds would fund public improvements approved by district voters, reimburse the developer and the Town, and cover issuance costs. The ordinance is being re-authorized because the board approved it in December 2025 and the timeline has since been extended. First reading was October 13 and the public hearing was set for October 27.

sources.body: Timnath Landing General Improvement District Board
Timnath Landing General Improvement District Board

timnath/3.title: Ban on new on-site wastewater and graywater treatment systems
timnath/3.summary: Town Council held a public hearing on Ordinance 16, which would add a municipal code prohibition on new on-site wastewater treatment systems and graywater treatment works.

timnath/4.title: Land Use Code amendments 25 and 26, including flood maps
timnath/4.summary: Council held public hearings on Ordinances 17 and 18 adopting Amendments 25 and 26 to the Land Use Code. Amendment 25 relates to the Larimer County Flood Insurance Rate Maps and Flood Insurance Study.

timnath/5.title: Timnath Town Center Expansion and recreation center construction
timnath/5.summary: Council considered a construction agreement with GH Phipps Construction for the Town Center Expansion Project. The recreation center project finished schematic design and is being reviewed by Adolfson & Peterson Construction and a third-party architect before moving into design development.

timnath/6.title: Timnath Parkway project and road safety
timnath/6.summary: Council received an October 2026 Timnath Parkway project update and a Safety Action Plan report. A construction contract with Noraa Concrete Construction was also on the consent agenda.

timnath/7.title: Timnath Elementary and school funding discussion
timnath/7.summary: Town Council listed a possible discussion of Timnath Elementary and school funding at its October 30 meeting, along with an executive session on negotiations.

timnath/8.title: Ladera Business Improvement District budget and 2027 operating plan
timnath/8.summary: Council considered resolutions approving the Ladera BID's amended 2026 budget and its 2027 operating plan and budget.

timnath/9.title: Town employee compensation study
timnath/9.summary: A work session presented compensation study findings from Graves, reviewing the Town's defined labor market. Staff plan to incorporate the recommendations into the budget.

washington-county/0.title: Landfill resolution (Resolution 34-2026)
washington-county/0.summary: The county scheduled a 2:30 landfill resolution discussion on Aug. 18, and Resolution 34-2026 on the landfill was on the Sept. 1 consent agenda. The agendas do not state what the resolution does.

washington-county/1.title: Wind moratorium extension (Resolution 49-2026)
washington-county/1.summary: The county considered Resolution 49-2026 to extend its moratorium on wind development on Sept. 29. The agenda gives no further detail.

washington-county/2.title: County Comprehensive Plan RFP
washington-county/2.summary: The county repeatedly took up a draft request for proposals for a comprehensive plan from August to October. On Oct. 27 it was set to open and discuss the bids received.

washington-county/3.title: RAISE grant RFP and bid opening
washington-county/3.summary: The county drafted a request for proposals tied to a RAISE grant (a federal transportation grant program) in August and September. It opened and discussed the bids on Oct. 6 and Oct. 20.

washington-county/4.title: County clinic roof and clinic construction bids
washington-county/4.summary: The county approved an APEX agreement for the clinic roof on Aug. 25. It then opened and discussed RFP bids for the clinic on Oct. 6 and Oct. 20, with a clinic bids discussion on Oct. 27. A clinic capital purchase also appeared on the Aug. 4 agenda.

washington-county/5.title: Courthouse and EMS building surveillance system
washington-county/5.summary: On Aug. 18 the commissioners were to discuss and decide on proposals for a surveillance system at the courthouse and EMS building. A CamNet service contract followed on Sept. 8.

washington-county/6.title: 2027 county health benefits and health pool rates
washington-county/6.summary: The county reviewed 2027 health pool rates on Sept. 22. Resolution 50-2026 on 2027 health benefits came up on Sept. 29 and on four later agendas through Oct. 27.

washington-county/7.title: PILT agreement and conflict waiver
washington-county/7.summary: In October the county discussed a conflict waiver and a PILT (payment in lieu of taxes) agreement. The PILT agreement was on the Oct. 20 agenda. The agendas do not give the terms.

washington-county/8.title: Telecom utility agreements with Level 3 and Williams Communications
washington-county/8.summary: On Oct. 20 the county took up Resolutions 52-2026 and 53-2026 for two communications companies, Level 3 Communications LLC (UAA26-01) and Williams Communications, Inc. (UAA26-02). These appear to be utility accommodation agreements, though the agenda does not say.

washington-county/9.title: Planning and zoning fee schedule (Resolution 48-2026)
washington-county/9.summary: The county considered Resolution 48-2026, a Washington County fee schedule for planning and zoning, on Sept. 1.

washington-county/10.title: Nursing Home and Housing Authority board vacancies
washington-county/10.summary: In October the county discussed letters of interest for the Nursing Home Board and Housing Authority Board. It also considered nursing home purchases, including a vehicle, a dishwasher and landscaping.

weld-county/0.title: Weld County Justice Center construction and financing
weld-county/0.summary: The county approved a construction manager/general contractor bid for the Weld County Justice Center (Block 66), then signed a contract with J.E. Dunn Construction Group. It also handled stormwater responsibility, a temporary parking lot, parking garage plan review and Emergency Ordinance #264 on a ground lease and lease-purchase financing.

weld-county/1.title: Rule Farm Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3 service plan
weld-county/1.summary: The commissioners accepted the service plan filing for the proposed Rule Farm Metropolitan District, referred it, and held a hearing on September 23. The service plan (MET26-0001) was later approved. The district is north of County Road 2 and east of County Road 21.
weld-county/1.where: North of County Road 2, east of County Road 21

weld-county/2.title: Code rewrite of zoning, administration and areas of state interest (Ordinance 2026-04)
weld-county/2.summary: The board moved Code Ordinance #2026-04 through second and final reading in August. It repeals and re-enacts parts of Chapter 2 (Administration), Chapter 21 (Areas and Activities of State Interest) and Chapter 23 (Zoning) of the county code.

weld-county/3.title: BURNCO gravel mining permit amendment and water enterprise
weld-county/3.summary: A first major amended Use by Special Review permit tied to BURNCO Colorado and the Water Activity Enterprise of the Groundwater Management Subdistrict was heard on August 19 and approved on August 24. The site lies near County Road 58, Weld County Parkway and County Road 49.
weld-county/3.where: North of County Road 58, west of County Road 49

weld-county/4.title: Solar farms and Latham Solar Farm annexation deed
weld-county/4.summary: On October 21 the commissioners heard two Use by Special Review permits for solar energy facilities (USR26-0007 near County Road 35 and AA Street, and USR26-0015 near County Road 46). Earlier, in September, they approved a quit claim deed for the Latham Solar Farm annexations.
weld-county/4.where: County Road 35/AA Street and County Road 46

weld-county/5.title: Oil and gas leases, 1041 permits and dissolution of the Department of Oil and Gas
weld-county/5.summary: The board held oral auctions for large-tract oil and gas leases, approved a lease of 40.685 acres, and extended other leases. It approved road maintenance agreements for Noble Energy 1041 WOGLA permits and named a backup hearing officer. On September 30 it considered dissolving the county Department of Oil and Gas.

weld-county/6.title: Housing Choice Voucher program transfer to Greeley Housing Authority
weld-county/6.summary: The county Housing Authority Board considered a voluntary transfer of the Housing Choice Voucher program to the Housing Authority of the City of Greeley. The commissioners approved it on August 26.

weld-county/7.title: CDBG 2026-2030 Consolidated Plan and local agreements
weld-county/7.summary: A public hearing on August 10 took input on the Community Development Block Grant five-year plan and 2026 action plan. The plan covers infrastructure, public facilities, services and housing rehabilitation, and the board approved it. Intergovernmental agreements with towns to run the program followed, including Firestone.

weld-county/8.title: Regional dispatch agreements with local police and fire agencies
weld-county/8.summary: The county signed public safety communications services agreements with many fire districts and police departments (including Frederick, Hudson, Kersey, LaSalle, Lochbuie and Milliken). In September it also approved dispatch agreements with Eaton, Greeley, Johnstown, Mead and Windsor.

weld-county/9.title: Road projects: High Plains Boulevard, roundabout, and bridge replacements
weld-county/9.summary: The board approved gas pipeline agreements with Xcel for the High Plains Boulevard (CR 9.5) project and the SH 392/CR 37 intersection. It approved street lights for a County Road 31 and 74 roundabout and a traffic signal at SH 52 and CR 37. It also awarded bridge replacement construction, including Bridge 19/46.5A.

weld-county/10.title: Tax incentive agreements and urban renewal revenue sharing
weld-county/10.summary: The board considered tax incentive agreements, an amendment to tax increment revenue sharing for the Colliers Hill Urban Renewal Plan, and the county incentives program. It also considered a proposed area for state economic development designation and private activity bonds for residential facilities.

weld-county/11.title: Cistern usage and right-of-way permit ordinances (2026-12 and 2026-13)
weld-county/11.summary: Code Ordinances #2026-12 (cistern usage permit criteria) and #2026-13 (right-of-way use permit) went through first reading on September 28, second reading on October 12, and final reading on October 26. A further ordinance (#2026-19) on liquor code updates, dance licenses and fees had first reading October 26.

weld-county/12.title: Mineral resource and gravel permit enforcement hearings
weld-county/12.summary: The board held show cause or probable cause hearings on compliance with special review permits, including a mineral resource site (PCSC26-0007), a water-skiing lake facility (PCSC23-0011) and PCSC21-0008. It also considered a major amended permit to expand a mineral extraction site near County Road 22.5.
weld-county/12.where: Various sites incl. County Road 22.5 and County Road 64

wellington/0.title: Flock license plate reader cameras and Sheriff's Office contract
wellington/0.summary: Larimer County Sheriff's Office presented on Flock automated license plate readers at five Wellington locations, including Highway 1/County Road 9 and 6th Street/Cleveland Avenue. The Town set aside $17,000 after a grant was not awarded. By October 13 the Board had asked to remove ALPRs from the 2027 LCSO budget, and a resident thanked them for it.

wellington/1.title: FY2027 budget and sewer fund interfund loan
wellington/1.summary: The Board worked through the 2027 budget in a workday on October 2 and a public presentation on October 13, including department reductions and delayed capital projects. A $2,000,000 loan from the General Fund to the Sewer Fund, through 2040, would delay a sewer rate adjustment and was set for a resolution vote on October 27.

sources.body: Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board

wellington/2.title: Cleveland Avenue downtown construction project
wellington/2.summary: The signature downtown project adds street and sidewalk lighting, more on-street parking and a new storm drain in Cleveland Avenue and 5th Street. It relies on grants including $1.8 million Revitalizing Main Street and $1.35 million MMOF money that must be spent by 12/31/2026. Coulson Excavating is the contractor, and crews have dealt with waterline and sewer service conflicts.

wellington/3.title: Water supply agreements, water master plan and utility fees
wellington/3.summary: On October 27 the Board was to consider a water supply agreement with North Poudre, a storage and carriage operations agreement, and the 2025-2026 Water Distribution System Master Plan. It also had new town fees and capital investment (tap) fees for water and wastewater connections on the agenda. A resident asked the Board in August to look at water options beyond reliance on Lake 3.

wellington/4.title: Economic development incentive policy
wellington/4.summary: The Board gave direction in August on a framework for incentives aimed at commercial development, with public benefit matching the incentive and caution about waiving tap fees. Resolution 36-2026 adopting the policy was considered August 25 and discussed affordable housing gains.

wellington/5.title: Metropolitan district model service plan and review policy
wellington/5.summary: The Board held work sessions on a model service plan and review criteria for metro district proposals. Topics included what counts as sufficient public benefit, single versus multi-district plans, and mill levy limits such as a 60-mill combined cap.

wellington/6.title: Housing needs assessment and affordable housing
wellington/6.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a technical memorandum updating the Housing Needs & Affordability Assessment with new data, ahead of a Housing Action Plan expected in 2027. The NoCo Foundation also briefed the Board on regional housing needs and down payment assistance.

wellington/7.title: Parks master plan, community center and park improvements
wellington/7.summary: The Parks board toured east-side parks, worked on implementing the PROST Master Plan and community center feasibility study, and discussed signage and fundraising. A Girl Scout proposed an accessible playground at Sunrise Park or Park Meadows.
wellington/7.where: Sunrise Park, Park Meadows, Wellville Park, Harvest Park

sources.body: Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board
Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board
Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board

wellington/8.title: Floodplain code amendments
wellington/8.summary: The Planning Commission recommended and the Board adopted Ordinance 13-2026 updating the floodplain rules in Chapter 15 to align with FEMA model standards. The changes affect properties newly mapped into the floodplain and the flood insurance program.

wellington/9.title: 2024 building and fire code adoption
wellington/9.summary: Ordinance 11-2026 updates the Town's building, residential and fire codes, with local amendments to align with the Wellington Fire Protection District's 2024 Fire Code. It includes electric-ready and solar-ready provisions, which prepare buildings for future solar rather than requiring panels.

wellington/10.title: Xcel power shutoffs and wildfire mitigation
wellington/10.summary: Xcel Energy briefed the Board on Public Safety Power Shutoffs and wildfire risk mapping, with undergrounding planned. The Town's water and wastewater plants are treated as critical facilities.

westcliffe/0.title: Data center moratorium (Ordinance 2-2026)
westcliffe/0.summary: After a June discussion of data centers straining the electrical grid and water supply, the Town drafted a moratorium. First reading was July 21, and the Council approved Ordinance 2-2026 on Aug. 18 as an emergency ordinance, effective immediately. No one spoke at the public hearing.

westcliffe/1.title: Main Street parking, safety and crosswalk
westcliffe/1.summary: The Mayor raised closing Main Street between 2nd and 3rd in summers because of over-length vehicles and people crossing outside crosswalks. A workshop is planned. The Town bought two signs (up to $1,000) for the Rosita Street lot and approved a temporary painted crosswalk near 104 Main St. A permanent crosswalk is to be budgeted next year. A stop sign at Main and Adams Blvd is also on the October agenda.
westcliffe/1.where: Main Street between 2nd and 3rd Streets; Rosita lot; Main St. and Adams Blvd

westcliffe/2.title: Prop 123 affordable housing, Housing Needs Assessment and IGA with Silver Cliff
westcliffe/2.summary: The Town considered the final Housing Needs Assessment. It approved an intergovernmental agreement with Silver Cliff on Prop 123 so Westcliffe can count some of Silver Cliff's affordable housing numbers, since it missed the three-year requirement. Residents asked numerous questions about the Prop 123 grant in September, and a Custer County workforce housing report is on the October agenda.

westcliffe/3.title: Water/sewer expansion south of town and reservoir project
westcliffe/3.summary: The Council approved a public statement for trustees and staff to use when residents ask about the water/sewer expansion south of town. It says the project improves the chance private lots get built on. In August the reservoir project was awarded to Mountain Valley Excavation, starting in September with completion hoped by May. The wastewater pilot study was 70% complete.

westcliffe/4.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code rejected and wildfire plan adopted
westcliffe/4.summary: The Council adopted the Custer County Community Wildfire Protection Plan in January, replacing a 2007 plan. In March it denied Ordinance 1-2026 adopting the state Wildfire Resiliency Code. The Fire Department, Silver Cliff and the County had not adopted it, and the attorney noted possible insurance and permitting risks.

westcliffe/5.title: Park shade structures instead of tree planting amid drought
westcliffe/5.summary: Because of drought and water shortage concerns, the Council dropped 2026 tree planting. It approved up to $40,000 for shade structures of about $3,000-$4,000 each. Bids for Memorial Park structures were moving forward in August.

westcliffe/6.title: Overnight camping ordinance update
westcliffe/6.summary: A trustee wants to revamp the Town camping ordinance to match Silver Cliff's, citing more overnight camping linked to rising homelessness. The current ordinance refers only to parks.

westcliffe/7.title: Tourism funding: Highway 69 welcome signs and holiday decor
westcliffe/7.summary: The Council gave $5,000 for Highway 69 welcome signs to get travelers to stop in town, with Mr. Shy opposed and approval contingent on the auditor. It also gave $3,500 for the holiday wreath contest and business holiday decor. The attorney said a statutory town cannot donate to the Altitude Fitness pool resurfacing and it must go through the grant process.

westcliffe/8.title: 2026 budget and mill levy
westcliffe/8.summary: After a public hearing with no comment, the Council approved the 2026 budget, appropriation and mill levy ordinances (5, 6 and 7-2025) in one motion on Dec. 9. A 2027 budget workshop was set for Aug. 28.

westcliffe/9.title: Façade Grant program
westcliffe/9.summary: The Council approved 2026 Façade Grant awards, cutting the Wildflower Hotel's award to $3,542. It rewrote application rules: reimbursement only, in-town business license, brick-and-mortar, and signs capped at $1,000. It also let a 2025 recipient finish work past the deadline.

westcliffe/10.title: Street sweeper purchase and town truck replacement
westcliffe/10.summary: The Council approved buying a street sweeper after a trial period, with discussion of renting it to businesses. Earlier the public works lead sought to buy a truck to replace aging Town trucks.

westcliffe/11.title: Farmer's Market at Jess Price Park and Bluff Park observatory hours
westcliffe/11.summary: The Council approved Resolution 4-2025 supporting the Farmer's Market on Town land at Jess Price Park, drafted as a resolution to avoid creating a leasehold. It also approved an MOU for extended Bluff Park hours at the Smokey Jack Observatory.

westminster/0.title: Data center zoning and neighboring-jurisdiction data centers
westminster/0.summary: After Resolution No. 20 (July 27, 2026) backed an interpretation that data centers are a prohibited use in Westminster, Council held an Oct. 19 study session on writing stronger data center language into the Unified Development Code. Council also discussed concerns about water use and utility service for data centers proposed just outside city limits.

westminster/1.title: Automated license plate readers (Flock cameras) discontinued
westminster/1.summary: Police presented on automated license plate readers at an Oct. 5 study session. On Oct. 26 Council took up Resolution No. 46 on discontinuing the technology, and residents spoke against Flock cameras citing data retention, cybersecurity and privacy.

westminster/2.title: 2027 city budget
westminster/2.summary: Council reviewed the proposed 2027 budget, held a public hearing Sept. 14 and took second reading of the budget on Oct. 26. The charter requires adoption by Oct. 26. Related hearings covered the Westminster Economic Development Authority budget and the General Improvement District budgets and mill levies.

westminster/3.title: Affordable housing definition, density bonus and down payment assistance
westminster/3.summary: Council moved ordinances amending the 2040 Comprehensive Plan to add an affordable housing density bonus, a revised definition and parking provisions (Councillor's Bills 39 and 36). Staff also presented a proposed Down Payment Assistance Program offering up to 20 percent of the purchase price, with an RFP that closed Sept. 3. Other items included Housing LIFT agreements, right-of-first-refusal agreements for multifamily housing, and Proposition 123 expedited review policies.

westminster/4.title: Water, sewer and stormwater rates and fees
westminster/4.summary: Council considered 2027 and 2028 single-family water rates, water, sewer and reclaimed water rates and fees (Councillor's Bill 40), and stormwater fee changes (Bills 43). It also revisited the non-residential roadway improvement fee.

westminster/5.title: Event center moratorium and new ordinance
westminster/5.summary: Council enacted a six-month moratorium on new event centers in multi-tenant commercial developments or within 300 feet of residential areas, citing impacts on public safety, water and sewer, parking and traffic. Staff presented revised recommendations for Councillor's Bill No. 19 on Oct. 5 after meeting with operators.

westminster/6.title: Jefferson County homelessness and navigation center agreements
westminster/6.summary: Council authorized intergovernmental agreements with Jefferson County and several cities on homelessness and a navigation center in Lakewood, and received a homelessness prevention and response update. A resident urged consideration of a navigation center closer to Westminster.

westminster/7.title: Kaiser North redevelopment and Mountain Range High School appeal
westminster/7.summary: Council held a public hearing on the Kaiser North Comprehensive Plan amendment and Preliminary Development Plan amendment. It also heard an appeal of the denial of an Official Development Plan for the Mountain Range High School Nutrition Center.
westminster/7.where: Kaiser North; Mountain Range High School

westminster/8.title: Economic development agreements and Holly Park sale
westminster/8.summary: Council approved economic development agreements with Mi Pueblo Market and Digantara U.S. and a scratch kitchen and food warehouse at 12450 Delaware Street. The Economic Development Authority considered selling Holly Park property to Pumpkin Ridge Holdings, LLC.

westminster/9.title: Business tax modernization and online filing
westminster/9.summary: Staff proposed requiring online filing and payment of business tax returns starting Jan. 1, 2027, with exceptions for taxpayers without internet. About 94 percent of 77,424 returns in 2025 were filed online. An ordinance moved through readings in September.

westminster/10.title: Childcare market study and property tax rebate
westminster/10.summary: A market study found a need for licensed childcare spaces for 3,695 children. Council considered a Child Care Provider Property Tax Rebate Program (Councillor's Bill 51).

westminster/11.title: Rental housing conditions and rising rents
westminster/11.summary: A Westminster renter spoke about rising rents and mold in rental housing, and urged healthy housing standards. Council also took up adoption of a residential property maintenance code.

westminster/12.title: Trails master plan and park projects
westminster/12.summary: Council authorized a Trails Master Plan contract with Logan Simpson, work on the Eaton Greenline project, England Park Corridor engineering, pool replastering and Foxshire Park playground replacement. Dog park volunteers also announced an event at Westminster Hills Dog Park.
westminster/12.where: Eaton Greenline, England Park, Foxshire Park, Westminster Hills Dog Park

windsor/0.title: 2027 utility rate increases for water, sewer and stormwater
windsor/0.summary: Stantec's 2027 rate study was presented to the Water and Sewer Board (Oct 14) for a recommendation to the Town Board, then to the Town Board on Oct 26. The proposed plan includes a 20% sewer rate increase in 2027 and water increases of 12.5% annually through 2028, driven by the new wastewater treatment plant (about $154M Windsor share) and NISP costs.

windsor/1.title: 2027 budget, revenue shortfall and staffing requests
windsor/1.summary: Staff presented 2027 revenue estimates, staffing requests and operations budget worksessions. Property tax declines mean general fund positions got heavy scrutiny; a Deputy Chief of Police, Deputy Town Attorney and Transportation Planner/Engineer are not recommended. Sales tax is split 67% general fund and 33% capital projects.

windsor/2.title: Crossroads/Colorado Blvd roundabout construction phasing
windsor/2.summary: Contractor AB Underground asked to fully close Crossroads Boulevard east of Colorado Boulevard during Phase 2, rather than keeping two-way traffic, citing constrained work area, winter conditions and a potentially faster schedule. The Town Board reviewed the request and a detour plan; the project also involves a NISP water casing.

windsor/3.title: Data center concerns near Windsor
windsor/3.summary: A joint board work session on data centers was held Aug 3, concerning a proposal in unincorporated Weld County, outside Windsor and Greeley. Main concerns are electricity and water use, written comments are being accepted, and a public hearing is expected in a couple of months unless annexation is requested; Town Board discussions are ongoing.

windsor/4.title: Hollister Lake Metropolitan District service plan
windsor/4.summary: The Town Board reviewed a presentation on the Hollister Lake Metropolitan District and then took up an ordinance approving its service plan and an intergovernmental agreement on Oct 26.

windsor/5.title: Sign code rewrite
windsor/5.summary: Planners presented a draft update of the town's sign code to implement the 2024 Comprehensive Plan, with measurement, permitting and master sign plan changes. A public hearing draft is due in September, Planning Commission hearing in October/November and Town Board adoption in early December.

windsor/6.title: Windsor Lake Road / WCR 70 extension and 7th Street roundabout land acquisition
windsor/6.summary: The Town Board accepted right-of-way dedications and temporary construction easements for the Weld County Road 70 extension (Windsor Lake Road) connecting Hollister Lake Road to SH 257, and for the 7th Street 'dogbone' roundabout at Garden Drive.
windsor/6.where: Windsor Lake Road / SH 257 and 7th Street at Garden Drive

windsor/7.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment and housing discussions
windsor/7.summary: The Town Board considered a resolution expressing intent to commit to Proposition 123 for affordable housing on Oct 26. Board members also reported on Housing Literate Leaders sessions, the NoCo Housing Fund and the Windsor Housing Authority.

windsor/8.title: Glade Inlet Canal / NISP grant and water supply
windsor/8.summary: The NISP Enterprise is applying for a $3,000,000 Bureau of Reclamation grant for Glade Inlet Canal Diversion improvements. Windsor holds about 15 percent, so a successful grant would save the town about $450,000.

windsor/9.title: GWIP property annexation
windsor/9.summary: The Town Board held a public hearing on annexation of the Great Western Industrial Park (GWIP) property, which drew public comment; the mayor said the board listens to all comments.

windsor/10.title: Wireless tower and conditional use permit rules, plus site plans
windsor/10.summary: Planning Commission considered a 50-foot stealth silo wireless tower at Timberline Church, 22918 County Road 17, along with code amendments on conditional use permits and Chapters 14 and 15. Site plans for a fire training facility, Firestone Complete Auto Care and a medical office building also came forward.

windsor/11.title: Downtown parking management plan
windsor/11.summary: Staff reported on 2025 and 2026 parking utilization studies showing downtown occupancy under 85%, with peak demand near Main and Walnut Streets, and proposed code updates under the Downtown Parking Management Plan adopted June 2025.

windsor/12.title: Recreation center ballot tax survey and parks projects
windsor/12.summary: A Magellan survey found 48% approval of a 0.8% tax for a new rec center and 50% for 0.5% if partnered with Severance, so the town will wait a year or two. Parks also bought about 70 acres of open space and received bids for North Campus Park.

windsor/13.title: Flood insurance rate map adoption
windsor/13.summary: Ordinance amending municipal code to adopt updated FEMA flood maps for Larimer County portions of Windsor advanced from Planning Commission to Town Board; staff found no parcels affected adversely.

windsor/14.title: American Legion Post 109 funding request for ADA improvements
windsor/14.summary: American Legion Forbes-McKay Post 109 asked the town for financial help with ADA access improvements to its building at 624 Ash Street, where the main floor sits about five feet above grade.

windsor/15.title: Backyard chicken rules
windsor/15.summary: The town proposed eliminating the $10 chicken permit and allowing coops up to 10 feet tall, consistent with accessory structure rules; the ordinance moved from Planning Commission to the Town Board.

winter-park/0.title: Urban Renewal Authority tax increment agreements (East Grand Fire and Cooper Creek Village)
winter-park/0.summary: The Winter Park Urban Renewal Authority took up Resolution 25, a tax increment revenue agreement with the East Grand County Fire Protection District No. 4, and Resolution 26, a professional services agreement with Northland Securities. It also scheduled a closed session on negotiating a tax increment sharing agreement with the Cooper Creek Village Metro Districts. The agenda does not state outcomes.

winter-park/1.title: Downtown Aerial Transit System (ATS) portal design
winter-park/1.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority received a presentation on the design of the downtown portal for the Aerial Transit System.

winter-park/2.title: Downtown Design Guidelines 75% draft
winter-park/2.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the 75% draft of the Winter Park Downtown Design Guidelines on September 22. It also discussed its 2026 priorities list.

winter-park/3.title: 2027 Transit Operating Budget
winter-park/3.summary: The Transit Advisory Committee reviewed the 2027 transit operating budget at its September 14 meeting and held a further meeting October 5.

winter-park/4.title: Rendezvous at Winter Park Filing 2C final plat
winter-park/4.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on the final plat for Rendezvous at Winter Park Filing No. 2C (PLN26-024).

winter-park/5.title: ROAM Neighborhood Park
winter-park/5.summary: The Planning Commission discussed the ROAM Neighborhood Park on August 25.

winter-park/6.title: Setback variance at 23 Maple Road
winter-park/6.summary: The Board of Adjustment will hear a setback variance request for 23 Maple Road (PLN26-076) on September 8, with draft resolutions for both approval and denial prepared.

winter-park/7.title: Site plan reviews: Bear Trail, Lupine Lane, Ski Idlewild Road, Trademark Drive, Arrow sign program
winter-park/7.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed minor site plans for 373 Bear Trail, 405 Lupine Lane, 40 Ski Idlewild Road, and 100 Trademark Drive (which includes a retaining wall plan). It also reviewed a master sign program for Arrow at Winter Park, 78746 US Highway 40.
winter-park/7.where: 373 Bear Trail; 405 Lupine Lane; 40 Ski Idlewild Road; 100 Trademark Drive; 78746 US Hwy 40

winter-park/8.title: Turkey Trot special event permit
winter-park/8.summary: Town Council scheduled a public hearing on a special event permit application for the Turkey Trot on October 20.

woodland-park/0.title: 209 E. Midland (Vos Building) historic landmark designation and dangerous-building appeal
woodland-park/0.summary: The Historical Preservation Committee considered recommending that City Council designate the Vos Building at 209 E. Midland a Local Historic Landmark, with four letters of support and one public comment received. Separately, owner Andrew Nguyen appealed a Dangerous Building Notice and Notice to Vacate issued May 28, 2026 to the Board of Review. His representative said the building has been vacant since 2019 and the 60-day permit deadline is not feasible, and the Historical Preservation Committee later discussed the appeal.

woodland-park/1.title: Eagle Fire Lodge rezoning and multi-family conditional use permit
woodland-park/1.summary: Cedarwood Development, for owner Woodland Capital, asks to rezone 777 E. US Highway 24 from Planned Unit Development to Multi Dwelling Urban Residential and to get a Conditional Use Permit for multi-dwelling housing. The Planning Commission hearing is Oct. 8, with a City Council hearing to follow.

woodland-park/2.title: New 'Public Safety Facilities' use in the Unified Development Code
woodland-park/2.summary: The city is amending the Unified Development Code to add and define 'Public Safety Facilities' as a use allowed through the Special Use Permit process. The Planning Commission discussed it in September and October, and Council was to consider Ordinance No. 1536 on initial posting Oct. 15.

woodland-park/3.title: 116 W. Lake Avenue historic landmark request
woodland-park/3.summary: Applicant Steve Plutt and owner Murray WP Cabin, LLC asked to designate 116 W. Lake Avenue a Local Historic Landmark. The Historical Preservation Committee held a hearing Sept. 1, and a City Council public hearing is set for Oct. 1, 2026 at 6:00 PM.

woodland-park/4.title: Downtown Development Authority 2027 budget and micro-grants
woodland-park/4.summary: The DDA reviewed its 2026 micro-grant program (about $197,517 total, with final reports approved for several businesses) and discussed its 2027 budget. The flower budget line may drop from $250,000 to $50,000, and a downtown walkability study, holiday promotion and 2027 grants were discussed. The board will see the budget in October, and a member noted City Council may dissolve the DDA.

woodland-park/5.title: City 2027 budget, sales tax and school funding presentations
woodland-park/5.summary: The Oct. 15 City Council agenda included a 2027 budget presentation, an August sales tax update and a school district funding presentation explaining how property taxes interact with state school funding.

woodland-park/6.title: Historic preservation projects: Junction House, Templeton Cemetery, Bergstrom Park
woodland-park/6.summary: The Historical Preservation Committee tracks the Junction House/Roberts House grant (a possible Brownfields grant handled by the city), the Templeton Cemetery restoration plan, the preservation plan, and the Bergstrom Park Reimagined design, which a council member said is already agreed upon. The committee is also preparing a 2027 work plan and budget.
woodland-park/6.where: Junction House, Templeton Cemetery, Bergstrom Park

woodland-park/7.title: Boy Scouts Reservoir presentation
woodland-park/7.summary: Utilities Director Wiley was scheduled to give City Council a presentation on the Boy Scouts Reservoir on Oct. 15.

wray/0.title: Zoning and subdivision code rewrite (Ordinances 656 and 657)
wray/0.summary: Council gave first reading in May to Ordinances 656 and 657, which amend and repeal parts of the zoning code (Title 18) and subdivision regulations (Title 16). The Planning Commission recommended both, and they grew out of the Innovative Housing Strategies Grant project. A public hearing on the amendments was held April 21, and second readings were on the June 9 agenda.

wray/1.title: Affordable housing planning and DOLA grant for the southern district
wray/1.summary: Council approved a request to amend DOLA Local Planning Capacity Grant #25-085, adding $50,000 to focus on affordable housing plans for the Wray southern area. Council also appointed two members to the Wray Housing Authority Board in February.

wray/2.title: Wray Civic Center construction contract
wray/2.summary: The June 9 agenda included a draft construction contract (guaranteed price) and possible award of RFP 139-2025 for Wray Civic Center construction. Council was also updated in May on a $2.1 million Congressional Directed Spending request tied to the project.

wray/3.title: Amphitheater revitalization
wray/3.summary: The Amphitheater Advisory Board presented a strategic plan for revitalizing the amphitheater, which Council adopted by resolution in January. In April Council approved a memorandum with the University of Colorado Denver and the Colorado Center for Community Development to help design improvements.

wray/4.title: Electric rates and power supply
wray/4.summary: Council received notice of an electric rate increase in January and held a public hearing in March before approving Resolution 15-2026 establishing electric rates. In April it approved a contract amendment with Western Area Power Administration so MEAN can keep handling power purchases, and in February it signed a consent related to the Sandhills Energy solar project.

wray/5.title: South Business and Residential District project and DOLA grant
wray/5.summary: Council accepted a DOLA Energy and Mineral Impact Assistance Fund grant of up to $800,000 with a local match for the South Business and Residential District Project.

wray/6.title: Industrial park lot sales and listings
wray/6.summary: In January Council approved Ordinance 655 selling Lot 10 of the Wray East Industrial Park to PR Transportation, LLC. In June it considered exclusive right-to-sell listing contracts for Lots 2 and 3 of the East Industrial Park and Lots 1-6, Block 1 of the Golf Course Commercial Addition.
wray/6.where: Wray East Industrial Park and Golf Course Commercial Addition

wray/7.title: Traffic code adoption, e-bike enforcement and traffic safety grant
wray/7.summary: Council adopted the 2024 Model Traffic Code through Ordinance 659, with second reading and a public hearing on June 9. Council approved applying for a $9,038 CDOT safety grant for the Power to Be Safe program with local schools, and discussed police enforcement of electric bikes and scooters and possible changes to the UTV ordinance.

wray/8.title: Procurement policy ordinance (Ordinance 658)
wray/8.summary: Council approved Ordinance 658, which codifies the city's current procurement practices into a formal policy and procedure.

wray/9.title: Airport funding transfer
wray/9.summary: Resolution 21-2026 ratified the City Manager's signature on a transfer of $150,000 in Airport Improvement Program entitlement funds.

yuma-county/0.title: Moratorium on data centers through 2026
yuma-county/0.summary: On March 17, 2026 the commissioners approved a resolution placing a moratorium on data centers in the county until 12/31/2026, along with a companion resolution adopting rules. The documents give no further detail on the rules.

yuma-county/1.title: County Road 39 repaving project
yuma-county/1.summary: The commissioners approved Simon Construction's proposal for repairs on County Road 39 in March. Work was expected to start in late July 2026; by mid-August paving was done from County Road G to M, with grinding next from Highway 59 to County Road G.

yuma-county/2.title: County Road M railroad approach and asphalt repairs
yuma-county/2.summary: Repairs on County Road M near the BNSF railroad crossing were delayed while the county sorted out flagger costs and permits, and were tied to the County Road 39 work to avoid doing it twice. In August the commissioners approved a $410,050 Simon Construction estimate to remove and replace asphalt on County Road M.
yuma-county/2.where: County Road M near the BNSF tracks

yuma-county/3.title: December 2025 windstorm and wildfires
yuma-county/3.summary: After a severe windstorm with 60-70 mph gusts and fires that burned over 14,000 acres, the commissioners declared a local disaster emergency on Dec. 19, 2025. Road crews logged overtime fighting the fires, DOLA matching grants for Eckley's generator were discussed, and crews have been clearing blown sand from roads in the burn scar.
yuma-county/3.where: Countywide, burn scar area and Town of Eckley

yuma-county/4.title: Road and Bridge staffing, supervisor hire and blade coverage
yuma-county/4.summary: The county interviewed for a new Road and Bridge Supervisor and offered the job to David Lee at $76,000 a year. The department is short-staffed, so blade operators cover larger areas and roads may be bladed more slowly. Commissioners discussed adding blade operator positions to the 2027 budget and approved several salary authorizations.

yuma-county/5.title: Expedited review for affordable housing projects
yuma-county/5.summary: The commissioners approved Resolution 11-25-2025D establishing expedited review policies for affordable housing projects. Land use code updates and a fire resilience code were also discussed.

yuma-county/6.title: 2026 budget hearing and revised mill levy certification
yuma-county/6.summary: The commissioners held a public hearing in December 2025 on 2026 budgets for the county, landfill and Water Authority. After the Assessor's Office notified local governments of a required change in January, the board approved a revised Certification of Mill Levies and Revenue for tax year 2025 and budget year 2026.

yuma-county/7.title: South Spur Solar Project and utility permits
yuma-county/7.summary: The South Spur Solar Project is expected to begin in early 2027, and the Road and Bridge supervisor plans to work with the company so county roads are restored afterward. A Viaero underground utility permit was moved to the south side of County Road 38, and exposed fiber on County Road 18 needed a utility locate.
yuma-county/7.where: County Roads 38 and 18; South Spur Solar site

yuma-county/8.title: Sale of the Idalia House
yuma-county/8.summary: The county approved a listing contract for the Idalia House in December 2025. In February 2026 an inspection found the water heater only needed lighting, and the board took $2,500 off the purchase price.

yuma-county/9.title: Dreher Pit and gravel supply
yuma-county/9.summary: Staff contacted the Dreher Pit landowners again about the county's gravel supply, and the board approved purchasing a Grizzly rock screen because the current screen is wearing out. A mining reclamation form was also sent to the state.

yuma/0.title: Historic designation of four properties on South Main Street
yuma/0.summary: The City Council scheduled a public hearing and four resolutions (Series 2026) to give historic designation to properties at 300, 301, 113 and 401 South Main Street. A fifth address, 320 S. Main Street, also appears in the agenda. The documents do not state the outcome.
yuma/0.where: South Main Street (300, 301, 113, 401 S. Main St.)

yuma/1.title: Council five-year goals, survey and strategic plan
yuma/1.summary: Council discussed five-year goals, a community survey and a strategic plan guide between April and June 2026. In September, members planned to attend a strategic planning workshop on teamwork, communication and council priorities.

yuma/2.title: 2026 budget proposal
yuma/2.summary: The December 2025 agenda included a proposal for the 2026 budget, along with grants and donations including the Workman Memorial. No figures or decisions appear in the documents.

yuma/3.title: Library 2026 plans and five-year plan
yuma/3.summary: In January 2026 Council scheduled a discussion of the library for 2026, including a five-year plan. Details are not given in the agenda.

yuma/4.title: June 14 event and Old Threshers event planning
yuma/4.summary: Council met in June 2026 to finalize planning for an event on June 14 and to discuss an event during Old Threshers.
